# Phase F5b: the SDL standalone's audio and MIDI as packages - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** `packages/native/sdl/main.cpp` stops owning the audio device and the MIDI ports. Both become packages behind
interfaces a second implementation fills: PortAudio, SDL2 audio and `null` for audio; RtMidi and an in-process fake for
MIDI. The MIDI stream (today's `MidiIo`) is written once over the interface and serves the SDL app and the CLI; the
Launchpad pack drops its own smaller port seam and its hand-kept copy of the port filters; the CLI's MIDI facet becomes
a provider. What the device, driver and ports are called stops being PortAudio's or RtMidi's vocabulary and becomes
names a saved file can carry: audio settings become a stamped section of `config.json`, MIDI selection becomes a section
of the project. **F5b changes no audio in the engine, no graph document, no plugin file and no saved file's shape but
the two new sections.** Strict parity, the kit and render baselines, `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the `buildGraph` and
role goldens, the protocol and script digests, `edio-golden.json`, the registration golden, the device-check and box
image hashes and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes hold unmodified, and no behaviour moves but the fourteen edges of the
design's section 8 (E1 to E14). Exactly one record moves: the recorded menu matrix's three audio/MIDI seam cases (Task
5). Task 7 is the acceptance run; Tasks 1 to 6 are one commit each.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md), whose sections 1 to 12 are
corrected in place to what the prototype built and whose section 13 records how and every departure. Task 1 merges
`feature/sdl-standalone` (the `MidiIo` ring fix, its test, `docs/sdl-release-readiness.md`) so the ring's fix exists
when the stream is rewritten around it. Task 2 lands `packages/midi`: `MidiBackend` / `MidiPort` / `systemMidi()` /
`rtMidiBackend()`, one copy of the port filters, `MidiStream` (`MidiIo`'s policy over the interface, its receive ring,
and the published output set with the `seq_cst` epoch handshake that lets a change cost no audio stop),
`FakeMidiBackend` as test support, the facet as a provider (`rp_midi_provider`) with the CLI and the headless host
mounting it, and the Launchpad pack onto the backend. Task 3 lands `packages/audio`, `packages/audio-portaudio` and
`packages/audio-sdl`: the `AudioBackend` / `AudioStream` contract, `AudioHost` (open/start/stop/reconfigure once, the
`null` fallback with a status, a lost device and a no-pull watchdog as the same fallback, render-ahead, per-thread
real-time tuning, the stats line, the log line in today's form), the `audioBackend` manifest item and `AUDIO_BACKENDS`
with its configure refusals, and the engine-graph re-rate equality case. Task 4 splits `main.cpp` into `app.hpp` and
five translation units, a pure move. Task 5 lands the TypeScript half: `definePackage({ configSections })` and the
config-section rules (verbatim keep, refuse-newer, the re-read write, an absent key not invented), the `audio` and
`midi` sections, `portMatch`'s tiers, the `AudioDevice` and `MidiDevice` host groups, the audio and MIDI rows moved
into their packages, the startup rendezvous, and the menu matrix's three seam cases re-recorded. Task 6 lands the
SDL-audio leg of `sdl:pipewire`, `tools/check-audio-linkage.sh`, the tracked `/dev/snd` guard under
`tools/sdl-audio-guard/`, the harness rewrites and the docs (AGENTS.md, spec/05-07 and spec/13,
`docs/sdl-standalone.md` and `docs/sdl-release-readiness.md`), and the design's as-built section.

**Tech stack:** no new third-party dependency: PortAudio and RtMidi are the tree's existing submodules (PortAudio's
`add_subdirectory` moves to root scope), SDL2 audio is the SDL2 the root already requires, TypeScript (the workspace
packages under `packages/`), the F1 package generator (`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`) and the boundary
check, esbuild through the tree's bundle tools, pnpm's workspace links, CMake 3.28 (the `audioBackend` manifest item,
`AUDIO_BACKENDS`, the generated `rp_product_audio_backends.hpp`, the refusals) and the existing native tree. The
lockfile moves in three tasks, and only by workspace links: Task 2 adds the `packages/midi` importer and the two edges
to it, Task 3 the three audio importers and the shell's `@retroplug/audio`, Task 5 `packages/audio`'s
`@retroplug/testing` devDependency. Each is `pnpm install --offline` with the lockfile diff quoted whole, never a bare
re-resolve that prunes another platform's optional packages.

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (`793c655fd`).** The design's section 13 lists all twenty-three
departures; this plan follows what was built. In short:

- **The `midi` package.** `MidiBackend` owns its client name (`clientName()`, `withClientName()`; a virtual-port open
  takes none), so a session that wants another name is given another backend. `MidiStream` gained
  `Apply { Diff, Reopen }`, `openedInputs()` / `openedOutputs()`, `setLogSink`, the virtual output in the published set,
  a Debug-only single-sender assert, a `seq_cst` handshake and a wait until the epoch CHANGES (never "while odd": a
  pinned core never returned). `retroplug-host` names `midi` in `PROVIDERS` too (the design named the CLI only).
  `retroplug-midi` is an unlisted library target, the fake is test support behind an INTERFACE target, and every new
  native target is on `_rp_werror_targets`; `check:boundaries` learned a dependency's own library targets, with `-`,
  `.` and `+` part of a name. `portMatch` is TIERS (exact; ALSA's `<client>:<port>` stripped; RtMidi's trailing index
  stripped), each of which must find exactly one port, and the `N- ` rule is dropped.
- **The `audio` packages.** `packages/audio` declares no `node-sdk` (`AudioHost` never names the Engine). The contract
  grew `AudioStream::start(std::string& error)`, `AudioBackend::driverLabel()` and `devicesListableFor()`, and
  `AudioHost` gained `backendDrivers()`, `live()`, `setLogSink`, `RunOverrides` and `applyRunOverrides()`. `describe()`
  enumerates only the backend IN FORCE (a sibling is asked for on the explicit "More drivers..." step, and the native
  hook returns `[]` under a pin). `AudioClient::prepare` hands the engine back at its end; the ring, its counters and
  the renderer are set up before `start`; a refused start is an open failure; `sameChoice` compares the backend; the
  watchdog's clock starts at `start()` and is stamped at pull exit, its bound is max(250 ms, 4 x the longer of the
  render block and the device quantum), a trip stays muted until an apply (which is the retry), and `tuneAudioThread`
  runs per thread and only on a real device's thread. SDL: a stale device warns and falls back like PortAudio's, a
  driver switch is refused while a device is open, `dummy` and `disk` are hidden, and a wide request on its PipeWire
  driver warns that the node shows 2 ports. `AUDIO_BACKENDS` has six manifest-level fixtures and four product-level
  cases, and `tools/check-audio-linkage.sh` is the design's 5.7(4) check as a standing leg.
- **The split.** Its own stage (Task 4), in the namespace `retroplug::sdl`; `MidiClockSync` is in `app.hpp`;
  `restoreControlSurface` became `waitForUiStartup` (it waits on the audio apply too); `bootControlPlane` and
  `readReady` are `main.cpp`'s.
- **Config, settings and startup.** Six hooks (`__rp_audioDescribe` with `overrides`, `__rp_audioBackendDrivers`,
  `__rp_audioApply`, `__rp_audioStatus`, `__rp_midiDescribe`, `__rp_midiApply(sel, mode)`) replace the eight;
  `ConfigModel { core, sections, raw, written }` keeps a contributed block this session did not set, and survives a
  shell-field write; an absent key is not invented; `setSection` computes over the re-read file; `CORE_CONFIG_KEYS` is
  derived from the schema; `ProjectHost.revision()` and `MenuBuilder.onOpen` are new contract members; the MIDI
  service re-resolves on EDGES and never on a render; `--audio-backend` replaces only the backend and keeps a saved
  driver and device when the section names the same backend; the audio apply RECORDS the request in the rendezvous and
  the device opens at the app's old point, after `midi.open()` and the providers' restore (no new edge).
- **Harnesses, kit and process.** `sdl:smoke` exports no `SDL_AUDIODRIVER` (null is pinned) and gained the E7, E12,
  startup-order and `RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_MENU` legs; the `/dev/snd` guard is tracked under `tools/sdl-audio-guard/` and
  all three harnesses source it; the kit gained `tsanmidi`, `tsanaudio`, `audiolink`, `pipewire` and `nosnd`;
  `sdl:pipewire` gained an Auto leg, an SDL-audio mode with a live-menu leg and counted skips, and its ALSA-fallback
  leg holds the clean degradation, not an ALSA open. `check-doc-links` reports a dead link inside a `*-plan.md` record
  as a warning. Six stages, not five; `sdl:pipewire` ran at S4, not S2.

**One claim in the design's as-built text is not backed, and it is not a departure either.** Section 13.1 (and the

**The behaviour edges** (design section 8, each with what was found). None changes audio, a graph document, the plugin
or a saved file's shape but the two sections.

- **E1. `audio.json` and `midi.json` are ignored; settings reset once.** Nothing reads them after Task 5; they are not
  deleted, not imported (the SDL app never shipped). The harnesses that wrote them are rewritten in Tasks 5 and 6.
- **E2. MIDI ports are per project; a fresh project has none** (the virtual ports only, which is what an unconfigured
  install had). A user who had picked a hardware input re-picks it once per project; the selection travels with the
  file, matched by name on another machine.
- **E3. Inputs and outputs are multi-select**: the old single `input` / `output` become lists, merged into the one host
  MIDI in and mirrored to every selected output. A hardware input is still never opened unless chosen.
- **E4. The Driver row names the backend, and SDL audio can be picked.** "Auto (PortAudio: PipeWire)", "PortAudio:
  ALSA", and, after the explicit "More drivers..." step, "SDL: pipewire". PortAudio's log line is byte-identical to
  today's; SDL's is the same form.
- **E5. A MIDI change or a Launchpad claim no longer stops audio.** `reconfigureMidi`, `onReserveMidi` and
  `onSuspendInputs` lose their `stopAudio` / `startAudio`; the claim's log line stands, and `sdl:controller`'s leg 2
  now holds that the claim precedes `] running ` and that the claimed port is NEVER opened as a hardware input by the
  stream (the virtual ports open before the claim now).
- **E6. A failed or lost device shows "Muted: <reason>".** A failed open, a refused start, a lost device and a
  watchdog trip are the same fallback, with the reason in the status the Settings row shows; Apply stays enabled while
  the status carries an error (that is the retry), and a trip stays muted until the next apply.
- **E7. The clock tempo is saved in the project** (`midi.clockBpm`); a project switch applies the new project's tempo;
  the transport still starts stopped.
- **E8. `config.json` gains `audio`; `controlSurface`'s bytes are unchanged** (its owner is the Launchpad pack now); the
  file-level `schemaVersion` stays 3.
- **E9. A project saved in the standalone carries `midi`, which the plugin keeps verbatim**; a fresh project written by
  the plugin has no `midi` block.
- **E10. On Windows the stream logs what is true.** `MidiIo` printed two RtMidi WinMM warnings and then announced
  virtual ports that did not exist; `supportsVirtual()` is false there now, no virtual port is attempted and the line is
  not printed. Linux and macOS are byte-identical.
- **E11. The CLI's `midiOpen(client, "")` opens every hardware input again** (it read none since the input default
  changed to None), as the contract says and as `n8-bridge` with no `--midi-in` expects. A named input opens that one.
- **E12. `--block-size`, `--render-ahead` and `--audio-backend` override the saved choice for that run.** Before, a
  saved `audio.json` won over `--block-size`. The Settings rows say "This run: ...", and the muOS launcher's
  `--block-size 4096` now always wins.
- **E13. Startup builds cores before the device is open**: cores are built at the default rate and re-rated once at
  `prepare`, held by the engine-graph re-rate equality case (Task 3).
- **E14. On Windows PortAudio's Auto prefers WASAPI**, where it resolved to MME. The Windows agent verifies it, and a
  saved `driver` still wins; the prototype found that without `paWinWasapiAutoConvert` a mismatched rate moves Auto to
  the SDL backend, not to MME (recorded, unverified off this box).

**The record, and nothing else.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
`RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE` or `RP_SKIP_BASELINE_UPDATE`. One variable is set in
the whole phase, and it is named in its step: `RP_MENU_MATRIX_UPDATE=standalone-start,standalone-instance,standalone-scan`
for the recorded menu matrix's three audio/MIDI seam cases (Task 5). The jump is too large to quote as a diff, so the
record is DERIVED: the recorder run is the step, and `git hash-object` on the file must print the prototype's blob
(quoted there). Every other record holds: strict parity (30 files, 250 cases: the suite's own count, the per-file
lines' sum, while the baseline directory holds 197 entries in 26 groups), the kit and render baselines, `render-chunks`,
`render-cli`, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the protocol and script digests, `edio-golden.json`,
`product-registrations.json`, both device images and the pack's bytes are this phase's proof that nothing moved, and
each task's suites step runs them. The skip baseline does not move at all (its counts stay the baseline's; only a
moved file's slug changes, and F5b moves no suite file). Every changed existing test is quoted as its diff with the
reason the design or the stage report gives. A golden, parity or digest change is a bug to find, never a re-record.

**HARDWARE SAFETY. A real NES with an Everdrive N8 Pro, a Pico box, a probe, a Zoom L6 and MIDI interfaces are wired
in, and this container's ALSA `default` IS the Zoom L6 (there is no PipeWire server and no ALSA config). No step in this
plan may touch any of them, and these rules are absolute:**

- **Never touch the NES, the N8 cart, the Pico box or the probe**, by serial port, by USB, by a flash tool or by hand.
  The N8 tools (`n8-load`, `n8-play`, `n8-bridge`, `n8-sync`) are exercised only by their existing fake-backed tests
  (`pnpm test:n8` over fake port factories, and the native tool tests over scripted backends). Every device step here
  happens on a **build**: `pnpm device:check` and `pnpm device:box` compile their images and run the check's plan in an
  arena, built and never flashed.
- **NO step runs `retroplug-sdl`, `pnpm sdl:smoke`, `pnpm sdl:controller` or `pnpm sdl:pipewire`, or any
  `pnpm reaper:*` / `tools/run-reaper-*` check, except under the `/dev/snd` guard, with `NOSND_LOG` set and (for the
  SDL legs) the `null` audio backend pinned** - that is `LD_PRELOAD` of the guard (`tools/sdl-audio-guard/` from Task 6,
  `.superpowers/verify/nosnd.so` before it), `NOSND_LOG=<a file>` and `RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND=null` (which the
  smoke and the controller set themselves from Task 3 on). **The guard a run preloads must be one an earlier step of
  that task actually built**: before Task 6 the kit's copy (`test -s` checked, built from its `nosnd.c` if absent), and
  from Task 6 `/tmp/f5b-guard/nosnd.so`, built there by `tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh /tmp/f5b-guard`. ld.so
  ignores a missing preload object with a warning, so a stale path leaves the run UNGUARDED while it looks guarded.
  `sdl:pipewire` is the exception that guards itself: it runs PortAudio and SDL audio on its PRIVATE PipeWire server
  with its ALSA-fallback leg pointed at a private ALSA config whose default is the null PCM, and it sources the guard
  itself, so it never opens a card. **A null-pinned run's `NOSND_LOG` must be EMPTY**; a non-empty log is a finding to
  report, not something to clean up. A Reaper run's `NOSND_LOG` is its own proof: card CONTROL-node refusals only (the
  prototype's: 32 `controlC*` nodes from jackd's ALSA probe) and NO `/dev/snd/pcm` line.
- **Before Task 3 lands (S2), `sdl:smoke` and `pnpm sdl:controller` are NOT run at all**: they open the L6 through
  PortAudio, which is why Task 2's kit run sets `TV_SKIP_SDL=1` and runs neither.
- **Nothing that lists or opens a system MIDI port may run, with one exception.** `pnpm sdl:controller`
  (`tools/run-sdl-controller.sh`) is that exception: it sets `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` itself, from its two ALSA fakes'
  full port names, refuses a caller that preset the variable, lists before it claims anything, and fails the run when a
  listed port is not one of its fakes. Run it as `pnpm sdl:controller`, never with the variable preset, and never any
  other MIDI-port-enumerating harness. **Never touch the Zoom L6 or any MIDI interface.**
- **`pnpm sdl:smoke` runs under a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` with `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`, which
  matches nothing** (an EMPTY list means every port). It sets that itself; do not remove it or export a list of your
  own.
- **Never run `amidi`, `aconnect`, `aseqdump`, `aplaymidi`, `aplay`, `arecord` or `speaker-test` against this machine**,
  and never build or run with a saved enabled `controlSurface` in the real `~/.config/retroplug`: a saved, enabled pair
  is claimed at startup and its close bytes go out at quit, which is why the SDL tools take a scratch config dir.
- **`pnpm test`, `test:plugin`, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `device:check`, `device:box` and the CLI legs open no
  port and initialise no audio library**: their MIDI fakes are scripted openers in C++ and TypeScript, and the audio
  cases drive `FakeAudioBackend` only. If a run seems to be waiting on MIDI or audio, stop and report it rather than
  reaching for a queueing tool.
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (two tracked patches). That is expected; never stage, reset or
  stash it, and never touch any submodule (`deps/dpf.js` and everything under it included).

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 7 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own, named for what it fixes). A commit message is a subject line, a blank line, then the body, and the
  prototype's bodies are quoted whole: use `git commit -F -` as the blocks show. No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated
  with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code, the specs, and a tool's own output
  a diff quotes): leave those be. The prototype's own passes removed every emdash from an added line but the wide-output
  warning's, which is written as the bytes it always was.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself. Never bare `git stash`, never switch branches with uncommitted work in the tree, and never `rm -rf build` to
  fix CMake: investigate.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a
  `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not
  just something that applies. The temporary `patch` blocks are the RED proofs that need the old code: each is applied,
  run, and reversed by the step after it.
- **Task 1 is a merge, and its blocks are the merge's own:** the two conflicting files are resolved as the prototype
  resolved them (`git checkout HEAD -- <path>` and then the prototype's diff of the file), the other six are what the merge
  carried, and the hashes of all eight are the proof that the resolution is the prototype's.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,consoles,protocol,
  scriptNodes,placers}.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/generated/{menus,views}.ts`,
  `packages/retroplug/cli/generated/tools.ts`, `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.host-modules.json`,
  `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.paths.json`, `packages/retroplug/.products/` and `build/products/` are written by the
  generator and gitignored, and the runners, `pnpm typecheck` and the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages[-<product>]` targets
  regenerate them. A worktree a prototype build ran in holds all of them, untracked and ignored (this one does); no
  `git status` list below shows them. If one ever does, `.gitignore` is wrong: stop and report it.
- **The lockfile moves in THREE tasks, and only by workspace links.** Task 2 adds `packages/midi` and the two edges to
  it, Task 3 the three audio importers and the shell's `@retroplug/audio`, Task 5 `packages/audio`'s
  `@retroplug/testing` devDependency; each runs `pnpm install --offline` (the prototype's command: **not**
  `--frozen-lockfile`, and never a bare re-resolve that prunes another platform's optional packages) and quotes the
  whole `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff. Tasks 1, 4 and 6 move no dependency and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`.
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with three exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` reports a total that moves from run to run (its threaded cases assert in loops), and so
  do `retroplug-launchpad-test`'s and the ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must match
  and the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which the
  quotes below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s final line counts FILES; a case total is counted from the run's TAP lines
  (or quoted from a report) and is not the runner's own line, and the `jobs=N` a runner prints is the pool it was
  given (the kit's caps), not a figure to match.
- **The Catch2 binaries, `retroplug-render-host-test` and the device images are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the
  default build:** `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before
  a run (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first, and the render-host tool is built by
  name). **A manifest change, a CMake list change or a new package needs `cmake -S . -B build` first** (the
  generator's inputs, the product lists and every new target are configure-time), which is why Tasks 2, 3 and 6
  configure before they build.
- **The scratch root, and one filesystem rule.** Every scratch path this plan writes is under `/tmp/f5b-accept`,
  `/tmp/f5b-tree-<n>` or `/tmp/f5b-v*`; none is inside the repository. The per-task and fresh-archive recipes run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` in the tree and give the pure runner the worktree's tjs binary through
  `RETROPLUG_TJS`; **a task's extracted tree never links this worktree's `build/`**, because a run that wrote there
  would write into this worktree. Do not `cp -al node_modules` into a scratch tree either.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build recompiles what changed and
  regenerates the generated modules; that is expected. Task 6's build also rebuilds `retroplug-sdl` and the device
  images and hashes them from the dirs it made.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose
  failing file, case or target is the one predicted but whose wording differs (the red steps say which are predicted);
  and a device script's trap-probe lines, whose object path and offsets are this devcontainer's and this binutils' (the
  device scripts judge a probe by its own object and the two symbol names, `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`). Never
  edit code, a test or a golden to make a step pass. In Tasks 1 to 6 each task's tree must equal its prototype commit,
  so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a fix belongs to a commit of its own after the plan.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does
  not show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote: Task 7 states the owed items, and no step below builds on Windows. macOS
  and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either. **No step below needs a real device, and none may touch one.**

Design section 3 and the design's stage S0. Five commits on `feature/sdl-standalone` (`b9105a004` the release-readiness
checklist and its pointer, `e059a7862` the `MidiIo` input ring's producers serialised on a `pushMutex_` with its test,
`71d7b8ff4` and `d51c4a4ef` doc ticks, `1304e33a3` the review follow-ups) come onto `feature/modularize` BEFORE anything
else, so that the ring's fix and its case exist when Task 2 rewrites the code around them. It is one merge commit with
two parents, and the design predicted the two files it conflicts in (the controller's `git merge-tree` dry run agreed):
`packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, where this branch's own edit of the same block added the Launchpad pack's include
root, and `packages/retroplug/scripts/run-plugin-tests.mjs`, whose header the F5a docs pass had already reworded.

The resolution is the merge's own content: for the six files that merge cleanly it is what git produces, and for the two
conflicts it is this branch's side plus the branch's additions (keep both). The step below reproduces all eight as one
diff of the prototype's, applied after the eight are put back to this branch's side, so the commit's tree is provably
the prototype's and the two resolved hunks are the diff's own hunks.

+# SDL standalone: release readiness checklist
+
+Everything that has to be dealt with before `retroplug-sdl` replaces the DPF standalone (`retroplug-jack`)
+in `release.yml`. Assessed 2026-10-06 against `main@cfeb80e0`. **Keep this file current:** tick an item
+(`- [x]`) in the same commit that fixes it, and add the commit hash. New findings go in the right section.
+
+Status at assessment: `./build.sh` exit 0, `pnpm sdl:smoke` 8/8, `pnpm sdl:pipewire` 8 passed / 0 failed
+(wide-output leg skipped: no wireplumber in the container).
+
+Background: [sdl-standalone.md](sdl-standalone.md) (feature history; its parity list predates most of this),
+[audit-2026-09-20.md](audit-2026-09-20.md) (items marked *audit* below were first raised there).
+
+## 1. Bugs (fix first)
+
+- [x] **MidiIo ring has multiple producers.** *Fixed in `e059a786` (review follow-ups `1304e33a`): producers serialize on `pushMutex_`,
+  `poll()` stays lock-free; guarded by the ring case in `retroplug-midi-test` (plain build aborted/segfaulted
+  3/3 without the fix, TSan clean with it).* Original finding: `MidiIo.hpp` documented an SPSC ring with
+  one producer, but the virtual `RetroPlug In` port and every hardware `RtMidiIn` each run their own
+  callback thread into `pushRing` (`MidiIo.cpp`). Any hardware input pick (or All Devices) gives two or more concurrent
+  producers: torn slots, lost messages, possible heap corruption from two threads assigning one slot's
+  vector. Fix: serialize the producer side (spinlock / mutex in `pushRing`; consumer stays lock-free), or
+  one ring per port. Add a TSan run that drives two producers.
+- [ ] **Pa_StopStream / Pa_StartStream used as a lock.** `reconfigureMidi`, the Launchpad
+  `setOnLinkChanged` and `setOnScanBusy` callbacks in `sdl/main.cpp` stop and restart the stream to
+  quiesce the audio thread. On PipeWire `StopStream` calls `pw_stream_disconnect`, so hand-patched routing
+  (wide outs in qpwgraph) is lost and a new node appears; every case is an audible gap. Fix: a pause
+  handshake with the callback (request flag + ack) instead of a stream restart.
+- [ ] **Dead audio device = frozen app.** The emulator only advances inside the audio callback. A device
+  that disappears (USB unplug, PipeWire node removed, suspend) freezes everything; nothing watches stream
+  health (`Pa_SetStreamFinishedCallback` / `Pa_IsStreamActive`). *audit:* `Pa_StartStream` /
+  `Pa_StopStream` return values are ignored, so a failed restart leaves a live-looking app with a dead
+  emulator and an undrained command ring. Fall back to the headless pump (or reopen) on failure.
+- [ ] **Bad persisted audio config = muted forever.** If `audio.json` holds params the device rejects,
+  `openAudio` mutes on every launch with no fallback to defaults, and `__rp_getAudioConfig` has no
+  status field, so the UI can't say the device failed to open. Retry with defaults; expose
+  open/muted/error to Settings > Audio.
+- [ ] **RT tuning applies once per process** (*audit*). `paCallback`'s `static std::atomic<bool> tuned`
+  latches on the first stream. On ALSA (the handheld) each `StartStream` spawns a new thread, and because
+  of the stop/start lock above that now happens in ordinary use, so the audio thread loses SCHED_FIFO +
+  core pinning. On PipeWire the same call sets SCHED_FIFO 80 and pins PipeWire's shared data-loop thread,
+  overriding rtkit. Re-tune per callback thread (compare `pthread_self()`), and only on ALSA.
+
+## 2. Parity gaps vs the DPF standalone
+
+- [ ] **System > Render missing.** `__rp_startRender` / `__rp_cancelRender` / `__rp_dismissRenderJob` /
+  `__rp_getRenderJobs` are bound only in `plugin/PluginUI.cpp` (around `RenderJobRegistry g_renderJobs`).
+  That code is not DPF-specific; lift it into a shared binder (see section 5) and bind it in SDL.
+- [ ] **No file watcher.** SDL never calls `svc.host.enableWatching(...)` nor pumps `__rp_pumpWatcher`
+  (the plugin does both: `PluginDSP::activate`, `PluginUI::uiIdle` every 15 ticks). `config.json` /
+  bindings edits and ROM-rebuild hot reload are dead in the standalone.
+- [ ] **Right-click instance menu dead; every button is a left click.** SDL never emits the `"mouse"`
+  bus (`[button, press, x, y]`, consumed in `App.tsx` for right-click-to-open), and
+  `handleEvents` sets `input.mouseDown` for any button, so right/middle click acts as a left click on
+  LVGL. Map SDL buttons to DPF's (left=1, right=2, middle=3), emit `"mouse"`, and only drive the pointer
+  indev from the left button.
+- [ ] **No HiDPI.** No `SDL_WINDOW_ALLOW_HIGHDPI` and a software renderer: blurry on Retina and fractional
+  Wayland, no DPI awareness on Windows. The DPF host uses `getScaleFactor()`.
+- [ ] **MIDI-in sub-block timing.** `renderAudioBlock` stages everything at frame 0 and RtMidi timestamps
+  are discarded (`MidiIo::onMidiIn` ignores `timeStamp`; `Message.seq` is never turned into an offset).
+  Up to one block of jitter: 10.7 ms at 512 frames, 85 ms at the handheld's 4096. The plugin carries
+  `e.frame`.
+- [ ] **MIDI clock is tempo-only, no phase lock.** `MidiClockSync` estimates BPM over 24-pulse windows
+  (window ends on a block boundary, so roughly +/-1 pulse, ~4%) and the Engine free-runs at that estimate.
+  Expect LSDj to drift in phase against an external master over a long take. Not yet measured: add a
+  drift render (like `reaper:lsdj-*` / `--drift`) before deciding how much to invest.
+- [ ] **Initial window size ignores the project.** Always opens 640x480; the plugin asks
+  `__rp_initialWindowSize`. Minor (the fit-to-grid effect resizes after mount).
+
+## 3. Release packaging
+
+- [ ] **Windows: console subsystem.** No `WIN32_EXECUTABLE` on the target, so a console window opens with
+  the app. Use the GUI subsystem (keep a `--console` / log-file path for diagnostics).
+- [ ] **Windows: Auto driver resolves to MME.** `autoOutputHostApiIndex` falls back to the platform
+  default host API, which is MME (first in `deps/portaudio/src/os/win/pa_win_hostapis.c`). Prefer WASAPI
+  on Windows (CoreAudio on macOS is fine).
+- [ ] **macOS: bare executable.** No `.app` bundle, no embedded `SDL2.framework` / `@executable_path`
+  rpath, no Info.plist / icon, no signing / notarization.
+- [ ] **CLI / launch UX.** Fullscreen only via `RETROPLUG_SDL_FULLSCREEN` (no flag, no toggle key); no
+  positional file argument (open-with / file association); no `--help` / `--version`; unknown args
+  silently ignored; `--width` / `--height` unvalidated (0 is accepted).
+- [ ] **Device hotplug.** PortAudio's device list is fixed at `Pa_Initialize`, so a USB interface plugged
+  in later never appears in Settings > Audio until restart. MIDI ports are likewise scanned at open (and
+  on a pick).
+- [ ] **Release workflow.** Add `retroplug-sdl` to the four `release.yml` packaging allowlists (and drop
+  the "deliberately NOT packaged" comments) once the rest of this file is done; decide whether
+  `retroplug-jack` keeps shipping.
+
+## 4. Config / persistence
+
+- [ ] **`audio.json` / `midi.json` are unversioned.** Native-owned reflect-cpp JSON with no version stamp,
+  against the AGENTS.md config-migration rule. `midi.json` already changed meaning silently (`""` was All
+  Devices, now None). Stamp them (or move them into the TS-owned versioned config) and write atomically
+  (temp file + rename; `writeTextFile` truncates in place).
+
+## 5. Code quality / duplication
+
+- [ ] **Shared host hook binder.** Duplicated with `PluginUI` (*audit*): window-geometry latch
+  (`wmControlled` / `sizeHonored` / `requestedW/H`), file-browser hook + delivery, quit / openPath / title
+  hooks, PNG screenshot (x3 with `test/ui/RenderCore.cpp`), control-plane boot (x4 with CLI + Node). One
+  binder taking a small host interface would also bring Render (section 2) to SDL for free.
+- [ ] **Test scaffolding in the shipping `main()`** (*audit*). 23 `getenv("RETROPLUG_...")` call sites (18 distinct variables),
+  including a complete `MidiClockSync` unit test. Move `MidiClockSync` to `src/host` with a Catch2 test;
+  gate the rest behind one self-test entry point.
+- [ ] **Split `sdl/main.cpp`** (~1900 lines) into audio / input / window / hooks units.
+- [ ] **Stale comments, here and in `sdl-standalone.md`:** "SDL2 audio callback" (it's PortAudio), "SDL
+  drives Mali GLES2 internally" (`SDL_RENDERER_SOFTWARE` forces the software renderer), header says the
+  gamepad feeds the keypad indev (`pumpGamepad`'s comment says it must not), `see audioCb` (gone),

diff --git a/packages/native/test/midi/MidiIoRing.test.cpp b/packages/native/test/midi/MidiIoRing.test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..bde57a850
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/native/test/midi/MidiIoRing.test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+// Guards MidiIo's input ring against its real threading: MANY producers, one consumer. Every open RtMidiIn
+// (the always-open virtual "RetroPlug In" plus one per selected hardware input) delivers on its own
+// callback thread, so picking a hardware device - or All Devices - puts two or more threads in pushRing at
+// once, while the audio thread drains with poll(). The ring was written for a single producer, which let
+// those threads race the tail index, the sequence counter and a slot's vector.
+//
+// injectForTest() is the same pushRing an RtMidi callback calls, and neither it nor poll() touches RtMidi,
+// so this needs no MIDI system. A plain build only catches the race when it happens to tear a slot; under
+// ThreadSanitizer (build this target in build-tsan/) an unserialized producer side is reported every run.
+
+#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
+
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <set>
+#include <thread>
+#include <utility>
+#include <vector>
+
+#include "host/input/MidiIo.hpp"
+
+namespace {
+
+constexpr int kProducers = 4;
+constexpr int kPerProducer = 5000;
+// Producers yield this often. Without it a few unpaced producers fill the 256-slot ring and nearly
+// everything takes the drop path, which writes no slot - so on a 1-2 core runner the racy write path ran
+// only ~255 times out of 20000. Paced, most messages land and the slot writes actually contend.
+constexpr int kYieldEvery = 16;
+// More than one ring's worth has to arrive, or the slot writes never wrapped onto a reused slot.
+constexpr std::size_t kRing = retroplug::MidiIo::kCapacity;
+
+// Message i from producer p: a status byte naming the producer, i split over two data bytes, then a tail
+// whose length (0-4 bytes) and contents both depend on i - so a slot assembled from two writers fails the
+// decode rather than passing as some other valid message.
+std::vector<std::uint8_t> encode(int p, int i) {
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> m = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x90 | p), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i & 0x7F),
+                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>((i >> 7) & 0x7F)};
+    for (int k = 0; k < i % 5; ++k) m.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>((i + k) & 0x7F));
+    return m;
+}
+
+// The (producer, i) a message encodes, or {-1, -1} if it isn't a well-formed message from encode().
+std::pair<int, int> decode(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& m) {
+    if (m.size() < 3 || (m[0] & 0xF0) != 0x90) return {-1, -1};
+    const int p = m[0] & 0x0F;
+    const int i = m[1] | (m[2] << 7);
+    if (p >= kProducers || i >= kPerProducer || m != encode(p, i)) return {-1, -1};
+    return {p, i};
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+TEST_CASE("MidiIo ring: concurrent producers deliver every message intact, once, in order") {
+    retroplug::MidiIo midi;
+    std::atomic<int> producersLeft{kProducers};
+    // Start gate: thread creation is slow enough that, ungated, one producer could finish all its pushes
+    // before the next exists, and nothing would ever overlap.
+    std::atomic<int> ready{0};
+
+    std::vector<std::thread> producers;
+    for (int p = 0; p < kProducers; ++p)
+        producers.emplace_back([&midi, &producersLeft, &ready, p] {
+            ready.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
+            while (ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire) < kProducers) std::this_thread::yield();
+            for (int i = 0; i < kPerProducer; ++i) {
+                const std::vector<std::uint8_t> m = encode(p, i);
+                midi.injectForTest(m.data(), m.size());
+                if (i % kYieldEvery == 0) std::this_thread::yield();
+            }
+            producersLeft.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_release);
+        });
+
+    // The consumer drains while the producers run (the audio thread's shape), then once more after.
+    std::vector<retroplug::MidiIo::Message> received;
+    std::thread consumer([&] {
+        std::vector<retroplug::MidiIo::Message> batch;
+        bool last = false;
+        while (!last) {
+            last = producersLeft.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;
+            midi.poll(batch);
+            for (auto& m : batch) received.push_back(std::move(m));
+        }
+    });
+
+    for (auto& t : producers) t.join();
+    consumer.join();
+
+    std::set<std::pair<int, int>> seen;
+    int lastIndex[kProducers];
+    for (int& v : lastIndex) v = -1;
+    std::uint64_t lastSeq = 0;
+    int malformed = 0, duplicates = 0, reordered = 0, seqGaps = 0;
+    for (const auto& m : received) {
+        const auto [p, i] = decode(m.bytes);
+        if (p < 0) { ++malformed; continue; }
+        if (!seen.insert({p, i}).second) ++duplicates;
+        if (i <= lastIndex[p]) ++reordered;
+        lastIndex[p] = i;
+        // A drop takes no sequence number, so arrivals are contiguous: a gap is a lost slot write.
+        if (m.seq != lastSeq + 1) ++seqGaps;
+        lastSeq = m.seq;
+    }
+
+    CHECK(malformed == 0);
+    CHECK(duplicates == 0);
+    CHECK(reordered == 0);
+    CHECK(seqGaps == 0);
+    // Overflow is allowed (a full ring drops and counts), but nothing may vanish uncounted.
+    CHECK(received.size() + midi.droppedCount() == static_cast<std::size_t>(kProducers * kPerProducer));
+    // Nothing landing would make every check above vacuous. Deliberately no tighter threshold: the drop
+    // rate depends on the scheduler, and a rate bound would be a flaky test.
+    CHECK(received.size() > kRing);
+}

### Task 2: the `midi` package, and the Launchpad pack onto it

Design section 4 (4.1 to 4.7) and the design's stage S1. The host's MIDI stops being `MidiIo`'s: `packages/midi` owns
one interface (`MidiBackend` / `MidiPort`), RtMidi as its real backend, an in-process fake for tests, the ONE copy of
the port filters, and `MidiStream` - `MidiIo`'s policy rewritten over the interface, with the receive ring the merge
fixed and an output set published through a `seq_cst` epoch handshake so that a change to the selection costs no audio
stop. The CLI's `MidiRpcService` becomes the package's provider facet (`rp_midi_provider`), mounted by naming `midi` in
a product's `PROVIDERS`, and the Launchpad pack drops its own smaller seam (`MidiPort.hpp`, `RtMidiPort.*`,
`MidiPortFilter.hpp`) and its two copies of the filter for the package's.

`retroplug-midi` is deliberately NOT a manifest `native` item: `cmake/packages.cmake` links every non-provider target of
a listed package into every product that lists it, which would put RtMidi into the host, the render-host test, the Node
addon and every test binary naming the desktop list. It is an unlisted library target, linked BY NAME by
`retroplug-sdl` and by the facet, so a product that lists `midi` without naming it in `PROVIDERS` links no RtMidi. The
fake is test support behind an INTERFACE target, on no product's include path.

Two REDs are the stage's own order: the stream's cases first (a compile failure, the header is the last file), then the
output swap against a `waitForSends()` that does not wait (ThreadSanitizer reports the race, and the fake's
`sendsAfterClose()` counts sends to a freed port). The review's probes that needed the OLD code are quoted from
`/tmp/f5bpro` with the step that produced each, and each is a committed case now.

`midi/MidiBackend.hpp` is the contract: `Receiver` (the backend's own thread), `MidiPort` (one endpoint, one
direction; destroying an input cancels its callback before it returns; an input's `send` is a no-op), `MidiBackend`
(`id`, `usable`, `listInputs` / `listOutputs` with every port the system names, `clientName`, `withClientName`,

surface), and the two doors `systemMidi()` and `rtMidiBackend(name)` declared in `RtMidiBackend.hpp` so this header
names no MIDI library at all. `midi/PortFilter.hpp` is the one copy of `midiPortAllowedBy`, `midiPortAllowed`,
`isHardwareMidiPort`, `hardwarePortIndices`, `matchPortIndex`, `kAllInputs`, `inputPortsToOpen` (over a list and an
`all` flag), `scanSuspendsInputs` and `extractRealtime`, moved out of the deleted `MidiIo.hpp`.

Create `packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiBackend.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The MIDI backend contract (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 4.1): the one interface the host's MIDI
// goes through, so what the ports are called stops being RtMidi's vocabulary and a second implementation (the fake)
// can fill it. Nothing above this header names a MIDI library: RtMidiBackend.cpp is the only file in the package that
// includes RtMidi.h.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace rp::midi {

/** One received message: the bytes, on the backend's OWN callback thread. */
using Receiver = std::function<void(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t)>;

/** One endpoint, one direction, owned by whoever opened it. Destroying an input cancels its callback: when the
 *  destructor returns, no receiver call is running and none will run. An output's send may block (a WinMM bulk SysEx
 *  waits for the bytes to leave the wire), which is why the Launchpad pack writes on a thread of its own. */
class MidiPort {
public:
    virtual ~MidiPort() = default;
    /** An input's send is a no-op. */
    virtual void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) = 0;
};

/** A MIDI system: the ports it names and the ones it opens. Every open throws std::runtime_error when the port is
 *  absent or will not open - one exception type, so a caller catches the refusal and reads its words rather than
 *  knowing a library's error class. */
class MidiBackend {
public:
    virtual ~MidiBackend() = default;
    /** "rtmidi", "fake": what a log line or a test names the backend by. */
    virtual std::string id() const = 0;
    /** False when the system refuses to be used at all (a macOS CoreMIDI client that would not be created), so a
     *  caller answers "no MIDI" instead of opening a port that cannot exist. */
    virtual bool usable() = 0;
    /** Every port the system names, unfiltered: the one copy of the port filters (PortFilter.hpp) decides in the
     *  callers which of them are hardware, which are allowed, and which a control surface holds. */
    virtual std::vector<std::string> listInputs() = 0;
    virtual std::vector<std::string> listOutputs() = 0;
    /** The client name this system opens its ports under: what other tools see, and what the port filters judge a name
     *  by. The backend owns it, once, so the ports it opens and the ports it publishes cannot be named differently. */
    virtual std::string clientName() const = 0;
    /** This system again under `clientName`, for a caller whose virtual ports must be told apart from this instance's.
     *  The CLI's facet publishes one stream per session, each named after the session ("RetroPlug N8", "RetroPlug
     *  Loopback"), which is a name a DAW routes to; the Launchpad pack likewise holds its own instance under its own
     *  name. Null when the system has one fixed name, in which case a caller keeps the instance it was given. */
    virtual std::unique_ptr<MidiBackend> withClientName(std::string /*clientName*/) { return nullptr; }
    virtual std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openInput(const std::string& name, Receiver receiver) = 0;
    virtual std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openOutput(const std::string& name) = 0;
    /** Whether this system can publish a port others connect to. False on Windows, where WinMM's openVirtualPort
     *  prints a warning and returns: said rather than found out by a catch, so the stream logs what is true. */
    virtual bool supportsVirtual() const = 0;
    /** A virtual port a DAW or an aconnect user connects to: "<clientName> In" / "<clientName> Out", on a backend
     *  that supports them. Throws std::runtime_error where it does not, like every other refused open. */
    virtual std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualInput(Receiver receiver) = 0;
    virtual std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualOutput() = 0;
};

}  // namespace rp::midi
````

Create `packages/midi/native/src/midi/PortFilter.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The host's MIDI port rules (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md sections 4.1 and 4.5), the ONE copy: which names
// are hardware at all, which the test-only allow list hides, and which ports a selection opens. The stream and the
// Launchpad pack both read them here, so a port a pack's scan would offer and a port the host would open are the same
// rule, and this package's test holds that rule on whichever platform builds it.
//
// Everything here is pure: a plain vector of names in, indices out. The backend's listing is unfiltered and these
// decide, so the fake can be tested against the same rule the real system is held to.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace rp::midi {

/** Whether a control-surface SCAN's held edge means anything for this stream: true only where a MIDI input is EXCLUSIVE
 *  (Windows), because there the stream has to let one go for the scan to hear it. An ALSA sequencer input and a
 *  CoreMIDI endpoint are shared - the scan opens its own connection and hears everything the stream does - so closing
 *  the stream's inputs would cost the user their MIDI for the scan's seconds and buy nothing. The pack asks every
 *  product the same question (rp_device_host::suspend_hardware_inputs) and the SDL answers it by this; a function
 *  rather than a constant, so the rule is held on whichever platform builds it. */
inline bool scanSuspendsInputs() {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    return true;
#else
    return false;
#endif
}

/** Whether `name` passes the allow list `spec` (RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW's text): a comma-separated list of SUBSTRINGS a
 *  port's name must contain. An empty spec (or one of separators alone) allows every port, so an ordinary run is
 *  unchanged.
 *
 *  The list is TEST-ONLY, and it is what keeps a check off real hardware: tools/run-sdl-controller.sh drives a real
 *  standalone against a fake Launchpad on the ALSA sequencer, and a stream on "All Devices" would otherwise open every
 *  MIDI input the machine has, a mixer's and a USB cable's included. The harness names its fakes by their WHOLE port
 *  names, client number included, so an entry it wrote cannot match a real device. A product never sets it. */
inline bool midiPortAllowedBy(const std::string& name, const std::string& spec) {
    std::string entry;
    std::string::size_type at = 0;
    bool any = false;
    while (at <= spec.size()) {
        const std::string::size_type comma = spec.find(',', at);
        entry = spec.substr(at, comma == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : comma - at);
        const std::string::size_type first = entry.find_first_not_of(" \t");
        const std::string::size_type last  = entry.find_last_not_of(" \t");
        entry = first == std::string::npos ? std::string() : entry.substr(first, last - first + 1);
        if (!entry.empty()) {
            any = true;
            if (name.find(entry) != std::string::npos) return true;
        }
        if (comma == std::string::npos) break;
        at = comma + 1;
    }
    return !any;
}

/** `midiPortAllowedBy(name, RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW)`. Read on every call: the callers list or open a port, never the audio
 *  thread, so a test can set the filter up and take it down around a case. */
inline bool midiPortAllowed(const std::string& name) {
    const char* spec = std::getenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
    return midiPortAllowedBy(name, spec ? spec : "");
}

/** Whether `name` is a hardware port at all: false for RetroPlug's own virtual ports (a name containing `clientName`,
 *  which "RetroPlug" also matches in the Launchpad pack's "RetroPlug Launchpad:<device>" link ports, so a second
 *  instance's claimed pair is never taken for a device) and for ALSA's "Midi Through", a loopback with no device behind
 *  it. One predicate, so every list and every open set agrees on which names exist. */
inline bool isHardwareMidiPort(const std::string& name, const std::string& clientName) {
    if (name.find(clientName) != std::string::npos) return false;  // our own virtual port
    if (name.find("Through") != std::string::npos) return false;    // ALSA MIDI-through (no hardware)
    return true;
}

/** Indices of every hardware port in `names` (skipping our own virtual port, ALSA "Through", `reserved`, and any port
 *  the test-only allow list hides - so a filtered process neither lists nor opens it, whichever selection asks). */
inline std::vector<std::size_t> hardwarePortIndices(const std::vector<std::string>& names,
                                                   const std::string& clientName, const std::string& reserved = {}) {
    std::vector<std::size_t> out;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < names.size(); ++i) {
        if (!isHardwareMidiPort(names[i], clientName)) continue;  // our own virtual port, or ALSA's Through
        if (!reserved.empty() && names[i] == reserved) continue;   // claimed by a control surface
        if (!midiPortAllowed(names[i])) continue;                  // hidden by RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW
        out.push_back(i);
    }
    return out;
}

/** Index of the hardware port named exactly `selection`, or none (empty selection / no match / a skipped port). Exact
 *  because the caller picked the name out of the very list this searched - the name matching that survives a move to
 *  another machine lives in TypeScript, which hands this an exact name. */
inline std::optional<std::size_t> matchPortIndex(const std::vector<std::string>& names, const std::string& clientName,
                                                 const std::string& selection, const std::string& reserved = {}) {
    if (selection.empty()) return std::nullopt;
    for (std::size_t i : hardwarePortIndices(names, clientName, reserved))
        if (names[i] == selection) return i;
    return std::nullopt;
}

/** The input selection meaning "every hardware port at once". An explicit CHOICE, not the default: opening every device
 *  turns out to be a surprising thing to do by default, because a device plugged in for one purpose is then also a MIDI
 * source - a control surface's free-running clock ends up driving the host tempo, a controller's mixer ports send notes
 * at the cart. The stream's own selection is a list plus an `all` flag; this is the spelling a saved or persisted
 * single selection uses for it (the CLI facet's "*", the SDL app's midi.json shim's "*"). */
inline constexpr const char* kAllInputs = "*";

/** Indices of the input ports to open for a selection of `names`: none when the selection is empty and `all` is false
 *  (the default), every hardware port for `all`, else each port whose name is one of `selected`, exactly. A port
 *  `reserved` by a control surface is skipped in every case, and a stream whose inputs are `suspended` (a
 *  control-surface scan holds them, on the one platform where a scan needs it) opens nothing at all.
 *
 *  Pure so the policy itself is testable (retroplug-midi-test) rather than only observable by watching which ports a
 *  running standalone happens to open. */
inline std::vector<std::size_t> inputPortsToOpen(const std::vector<std::string>& names, const std::string& clientName,
                                                 const std::vector<std::string>& selected, bool all,
                                                 const std::string& reserved = {}, bool suspended = false) {
    if (suspended) return {};
    const std::vector<std::size_t> hardware = hardwarePortIndices(names, clientName, reserved);
    if (all) return hardware;
    std::vector<std::size_t> open;
    for (std::size_t i : hardware) {
        for (const std::string& name : selected) {
            if (!name.empty() && names[i] == name) {
                open.push_back(i);
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    return open;
}

/** Pull the System Real-Time bytes (0xF8..0xFF: clock, start/continue/stop, reset) out of one incoming message, handing
 *  each to `onRealtime` in order, and leave `bytes` holding whatever else was there.
 *
 *  Real-time bytes are a stream WITHIN the stream: the spec lets them appear at any byte boundary, including between
 *  the data bytes of another message, and a transport is free to hand several events over as one buffer. Matching only
 *  a one-byte message therefore both MISSES clock (a batched pair reads as no clock at all - a tempo estimate built on
 *  those pulses comes out a whole ratio slow) and corrupts what is left (a clock byte staged into the middle of a
 *  NoteOn goes down a cart's link port as noise).
 *
 *  Shrinks in place: this runs per message on the audio thread, so it must not allocate. */
template <typename F>
inline void extractRealtime(std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes, F&& onRealtime) {
    std::size_t write = 0;
    for (std::size_t read = 0; read < bytes.size(); ++read) {
        const std::uint8_t b = bytes[read];
        if (b >= 0xF8) onRealtime(b);
        else bytes[write++] = b;
    }
    bytes.resize(write);
}

}  // namespace rp::midi
````

````cpp
#include "midi/RtMidiBackend.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <memory>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "RtMidi.h"
#include "midi/PortFilter.hpp"

#if defined(__APPLE__)
#include <CoreMIDI/CoreMIDI.h>

#include <chrono>
#include <thread>
#endif

namespace rp::midi {
namespace {

/** True when an RtMidiIn/RtMidiOut can safely be CONSTRUCTED. On macOS this creates (and then keeps) the process's one
 *  CoreMIDI client first.
 *
 *  RtMidi makes that client inside MidiInCore::getCoreMidiClientSingleton(), which is declared throw() -- while its
 *  failure path calls error(DRIVER_ERROR), and that THROWS. A throw crossing a noexcept boundary is an immediate
 *  std::terminate (__cxa_call_unexpected), so when MIDIClientCreate fails the host ABORTS outright and not one catch
 *  block can see it - they never get to unwind. Upstream thestk/rtmidi, so it is not ours to fix in place.
 *
 *  Observed as an Abort trap out of the port listing at startup, when several short-lived hosts run back to back:
 *  MIDIClientCreate intermittently returns -304 or -2 while MIDIServer - an on-demand daemon that stops once its last
 *  client goes - is still coming back up. So make the client ourselves first and let a failure mean "no MIDI" rather
 *  than a dead host. It is kept for the process lifetime deliberately: RtMidi's own singleton then rides on an
 *  already-warm connection, and holding it keeps MIDIServer up for the rest of the run. Every RtMidi object this file
 *  builds asks this first; everything above it is the interface's. */
bool midiSystemUsable() {
#if defined(__APPLE__)
    static const bool ok = [] {
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; ++attempt) {
            MIDIClientRef client = 0;
            if (MIDIClientCreate(CFSTR("RetroPlug"), nullptr, nullptr, &client) == noErr)
                return true;  // never disposed: it is the keepalive
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
        }
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] MIDI unavailable: CoreMIDI would not create a client "
                             "(continuing without MIDI)\n");
        return false;
    }();
    return ok;
#else
    return true;
#endif
}

/** The names of every port an endpoint of one direction names, as the system reports them (nothing filtered here: the
 *  callers hold the one rule). The probe object is created per call, so a port plugged in since the last listing is
 *  there the next time - there is no hotplug watch, a list is read when it is asked for. */
std::vector<std::string> probePortNames(bool input, const std::string& clientName) {
    std::vector<std::string> names;
    if (!midiSystemUsable()) return names;
    try {
        if (input) {
            RtMidiIn probe(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const unsigned count = probe.getPortCount();
            for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) names.push_back(probe.getPortName(i));
        } else {
            RtMidiOut probe(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const unsigned count = probe.getPortCount();
            for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) names.push_back(probe.getPortName(i));
        }
    } catch (RtMidiError&) {
        names.clear();  // no MIDI system
    }
    return names;
}

/** Index of the port named exactly `name` on an open RtMidi endpoint, or none. Exact, because the caller picked this
 *  name out of the very list this enumerated, and by NAME on the object that opens it: a port hot-plugged between the
 *  two shifts every index after it, so opening by number could take a port no filter judged. */
template <class T>
std::optional<unsigned> findPort(T& endpoint, const std::string& name) {
    const unsigned count = endpoint.getPortCount();
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        if (endpoint.getPortName(i) == name) return i;
    return std::nullopt;
}

// One port, one direction. An input keeps its RtMidiIn LAST, so it is destroyed first and its callback is cancelled
// before the receiver it calls goes away.
class RtMidiPort final : public MidiPort {
public:
    RtMidiPort(const std::string& clientName, bool input, const std::string& name, Receiver receiver)
        : receiver_(std::move(receiver)) {
        if (input) {
            in_            = std::make_unique<RtMidiIn>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const auto idx = findPort(*in_, name);
            if (!idx) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI input port not found: " + name);
            // (sysex, time, sense) - false means DELIVER. SysEx is a control surface's language and a cart bridge's;
            // clock is kept because what to do with it is the reader's call; active sensing (a keepalive nothing here
            // wants) is dropped.
            in_->ignoreTypes(false, false, true);
            in_->setCallback(&RtMidiPort::onMidiIn, this);
            in_->openPort(*idx, name);
        } else {
            out_           = std::make_unique<RtMidiOut>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const auto idx = findPort(*out_, name);
            if (!idx) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI output port not found: " + name);
            out_->openPort(*idx, name);
        }
    }

    ~RtMidiPort() override {
        in_.reset();  // cancels the callback before receiver_ dies
        out_.reset();
    }

    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override {
        if (!out_ || !data || n == 0) return;  // an input's send is a no-op
        try {
            out_->sendMessage(data, n);
        } catch (RtMidiError&) {
            // A transient send failure (the device was unplugged) must not take down the caller's block.
        }
    }

private:
    static void onMidiIn(double, std::vector<unsigned char>* message, void* userData) {
        if (!message || message->empty()) return;
        auto* self = static_cast<RtMidiPort*>(userData);
        if (self->receiver_) self->receiver_(message->data(), message->size());
    }

    Receiver                   receiver_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiOut> out_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiIn>  in_;  // LAST: destroyed first, cancelling the callback
};

// A virtual port: one the system publishes for others to connect to, so a DAW or an aconnect user reaches the stream
// the way it reaches the plugin in a host.
class RtMidiVirtualPort final : public MidiPort {
public:
    RtMidiVirtualPort(const std::string& clientName, bool input, const std::string& portName, Receiver receiver)
        : receiver_(std::move(receiver)) {
        if (input) {
            in_ = std::make_unique<RtMidiIn>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            in_->ignoreTypes(false, false, true);  // as an opened port: sysex delivered
            in_->setCallback(&RtMidiVirtualPort::onMidiIn, this);
            in_->openVirtualPort(portName);
        } else {
            out_ = std::make_unique<RtMidiOut>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            out_->openVirtualPort(portName);
        }
    }

    ~RtMidiVirtualPort() override {
        in_.reset();
        out_.reset();
    }

    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override {
        if (!out_ || !data || n == 0) return;
        try {
            out_->sendMessage(data, n);
        } catch (RtMidiError&) {
            // As a hardware output's send: a transient failure is not the audio thread's to die of.
        }
    }

private:
    static void onMidiIn(double, std::vector<unsigned char>* message, void* userData) {
        if (!message || message->empty()) return;
        auto* self = static_cast<RtMidiVirtualPort*>(userData);
        if (self->receiver_) self->receiver_(message->data(), message->size());
    }

    Receiver                   receiver_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiOut> out_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiIn>  in_;  // LAST: destroyed first, cancelling the callback
};

/** RtMidi behind the interface, under one client name: the process's "RetroPlug" (systemMidi) and the Launchpad pack's
 *  "RetroPlug Launchpad", whose link ports a product's stream must not take for a device. The client name is what other
 *  tools see and what the port filters judge a name by, so two instances of this are two named systems. */
class RtMidiBackend final : public MidiBackend {
public:
    explicit RtMidiBackend(std::string clientName) : clientName_(std::move(clientName)) {}

    std::string id() const override { return "rtmidi"; }
    std::string clientName() const override { return clientName_; }
    // Another RtMidi system under the requested name: a separate client, so its virtual ports are published beside this
    // one's rather than replacing them (that is how a CLI session's "RetroPlug N8 In" sits next to the app's
    // "RetroPlug In").
    std::unique_ptr<MidiBackend> withClientName(std::string clientName) override {
        return std::make_unique<RtMidiBackend>(std::move(clientName));
    }
    bool usable() override { return midiSystemUsable(); }
    std::vector<std::string> listInputs() override { return probePortNames(true, clientName_); }
    std::vector<std::string> listOutputs() override { return probePortNames(false, clientName_); }
    bool supportsVirtual() const override {
#if defined(_WIN32)
        // WinMM's openVirtualPort does not throw: it raises a WARNING (RtMidi.cpp's openVirtualPort on Windows) that
        // prints and returns, so a port announced as open would not exist. Said here, once, rather than found out by a
        // catch that never fires.
        return false;
#else
        return true;
#endif
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openInput(const std::string& name, Receiver receiver) override {
        // The test-only allow list, refused here as well as by the callers: a filtered process may not open a port it
        // may not list either, whatever path reaches this.
        if (!midiPortAllowed(name)) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI port not allowed: " + name);
        if (!midiSystemUsable()) throw std::runtime_error("no MIDI system");
        try {
            return std::make_unique<RtMidiPort>(clientName_, true, name, std::move(receiver));
        } catch (RtMidiError& e) {
            throw std::runtime_error(e.what());  // one exception type for every caller to catch
        }
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openOutput(const std::string& name) override {
        if (!midiPortAllowed(name)) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI port not allowed: " + name);
        if (!midiSystemUsable()) throw std::runtime_error("no MIDI system");
        try {
            return std::make_unique<RtMidiPort>(clientName_, false, name, nullptr);
        } catch (RtMidiError& e) {
            throw std::runtime_error(e.what());
        }
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualInput(Receiver receiver) override {
        refuseVirtual();
        try {
            return std::make_unique<RtMidiVirtualPort>(clientName_, true, clientName_ + " In", std::move(receiver));
        } catch (RtMidiError& e) {
            throw std::runtime_error(e.what());
        }
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualOutput() override {
        refuseVirtual();
        try {
            return std::make_unique<RtMidiVirtualPort>(clientName_, false, clientName_ + " Out", nullptr);
        } catch (RtMidiError& e) {
            throw std::runtime_error(e.what());
        }
    }

private:
    /** WinMM's openVirtualPort does not throw: it raises a WARNING that prints and returns, leaving a port that does
     *  not exist announced as open. A caller that asked anyway gets the refusal every other failed open gives, rather
     *  than a silent nothing. */
    void refuseVirtual() const {
        if (!supportsVirtual()) throw std::runtime_error("virtual ports are not supported");
        if (!midiSystemUsable()) throw std::runtime_error("no MIDI system");
    }

    std::string clientName_;
};

}  // namespace

MidiBackend& systemMidi() {
    static RtMidiBackend backend{"RetroPlug"};
    return backend;
}

std::unique_ptr<MidiBackend> rtMidiBackend(std::string clientName) {
    return std::make_unique<RtMidiBackend>(std::move(clientName));
}

}  // namespace rp::midi
````
