- [ ] **Step 4: `MidiStream`, and the fake its cases drive**

`MidiStream.cpp` is `MidiIo`'s policy over a `MidiBackend&`: exact-name lists with an `all` flag, the reservation and
the scan's held edge, a 256-slot receive ring whose producers serialise on a mutex (the merge's fix) and whose `poll`
takes none, a drop count, and the outputs as an immutable set published through one atomic pointer - a change
publishes the new set, waits out the send in flight and only then frees the old one. `send` is the audio thread's
alone: the virtual output travels IN the published set (so a change never re-opens it and a DAW's connection
survives), `close()` is the same publish-and-wait, and the four operations on the counter and the pointer are
`seq_cst` because the shape is store-buffering (the comment says why, and that no TSan run can see it).
`FakeMidiBackend.hpp` is test support: the listed ports (independent of what opens), a `refuse` set, an event log,
everything every output received (kept outside the port, so it survives the port's destruction), `deliver(name,
bytes)`, an `onSend` hook a scripted device answers an inquiry through, a per-send delay with the started/finished
counters the writer-thread case waits on, inline or threaded delivery, an `exclusivePorts` set (a second open of an
open name refuses, as WinMM does), and `withClientName` returning a copy of the same scripted machine without the
hooks.

Create `packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "midi/MidiStream.hpp"

#include <cassert>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>

#include "midi/PortFilter.hpp"

namespace rp::midi {
namespace {

/** Whether `names` holds `name` (the selection's own small list, so a duplicate selection opens one port). */
bool contains(const std::vector<std::string>& names, const std::string& name) {
    for (const std::string& n : names)
        if (n == name) return true;
    return false;
}

}  // namespace

MidiStream::MidiStream(MidiBackend& backend) : backend_(&backend) {}

MidiStream::~MidiStream() { close(); }

bool MidiStream::open() {
    close();  // idempotent: a second open replaces the first, ports and ring alike
    clientName_ = backend_->clientName();
    log_.store(std::getenv("RETROPLUG_MIDI_LOG") != nullptr);  // set before a callback thread can start
    if (!backend_->usable()) return false;
    if (backend_->supportsVirtual()) {
        // A backend with no virtual ports says so (MidiBackend::supportsVirtual) rather than attempting one that cannot
        // exist: WinMM's openVirtualPort raises a warning and returns, so the old code announced two ports that were
        // not there. Linux and macOS are unchanged: the line is the one the harnesses read.
        try {
            virtualIn_ =
                backend_->openVirtualInput([this](const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { pushRing(data, n); });
            virtualOut_ = backend_->openVirtualOutput();
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            emit(std::string("MIDI unavailable: ") + e.what() + " (running without MIDI)");
            virtualIn_.reset();
            virtualOut_.reset();
            return false;
        }
        emit("MIDI: virtual ports '" + clientName_ + " In' / '" + clientName_ + " Out' open");
    }
    open_ = true;
    applyInputs(Apply::Reopen);    // nothing was open: this is the change, and the lines say what it opened
    applyOutputs(Apply::Reopen);
    return true;
}

void MidiStream::close() {
    // Nothing is published any more (not even an empty set: the virtual output is freed below, and a set naming it
    // would let a send that starts after the publish reach a freed port), and the send in flight is waited out here.
    OutputSet* old = outputs_.exchange(nullptr, std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    retire(old);
    openOutputs_.clear();
    hwOut_.clear();      // closed only now: no published set named them, so no send can be inside one
    virtualIn_.reset();  // cancels its callback: no receiver runs after this returns
    hwIn_.clear();       // each port cancels its own callback as it goes
    openInputs_.clear();
    virtualOut_.reset();
    open_ = false;
    // The ring's indices are NOT reset: poll() runs on the audio thread and may be between its load of head_ and its
    // store of it, so a reset here would have it store a stale index over the empty ring and replay moved-from slots.
    // They are consistent as they stand - a message that arrived before the close is still one that arrived.
}

std::vector<std::string> MidiStream::listInputs() const {
    const std::vector<std::string> raw = backend_->listInputs();
    std::vector<std::string>       out;
    for (std::size_t i : hardwarePortIndices(raw, clientName_)) out.push_back(raw[i]);
    return out;
}

std::vector<std::string> MidiStream::listOutputs() const {
    const std::vector<std::string> raw = backend_->listOutputs();
    std::vector<std::string>       out;
    for (std::size_t i : hardwarePortIndices(raw, clientName_)) out.push_back(raw[i]);
    return out;
}

void MidiStream::setInputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names, bool all, Apply mode) {
    selectedIn_ = names;
    allInputs_  = all;
    if (open_) applyInputs(mode);
}

void MidiStream::setOutputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names, Apply mode) {
    selectedOut_ = names;
    if (open_) applyOutputs(mode);
}

void MidiStream::setReserved(const std::string& input, const std::string& output) {
    if (reservedIn_ == input && reservedOut_ == output) return;
    reservedIn_  = input;
    reservedOut_ = output;
    if (!open_) return;
    applyInputs(Apply::Diff);   // diffed: the claim changes what is open, and nothing else moves
    applyOutputs(Apply::Diff);
}

void MidiStream::setHardwareInputsSuspended(bool suspended) {
    if (inputsSuspended_ == suspended) return;
    inputsSuspended_ = suspended;
    if (open_) applyInputs(Apply::Diff);
    emit(std::string("MIDI in: hardware inputs ") +
         (suspended ? "suspended for a control-surface scan" : "resumed"));
}

void MidiStream::applyInputs(Apply mode) {
    const std::vector<std::string> names = backend_->listInputs();
    std::vector<std::string>       want;
    for (std::size_t i : inputPortsToOpen(names, clientName_, selectedIn_, allInputs_, reservedIn_, inputsSuspended_))
        want.push_back(names[i]);
    if (mode == Apply::Diff && want == openInputs_) return;
    // Said once per real change: it describes the state the stream is now in, not a call it answered.
    if (want.empty() && selectedIn_.empty() && !allInputs_ && !inputsSuspended_)
        emit("MIDI in: no hardware device selected (Settings > MIDI)");
    // A port the change keeps stays open, so a project load costs no connection (and a clock arriving on it loses no
    // message). A REOPEN lets every port go first and only then opens it again: a MIDI input is exclusive on the one
    // platform where a re-pick is the remedy for an unplugged device (Windows), so opening before closing is refused.
    if (mode == Apply::Reopen) {
        hwIn_.clear();  // each port cancels its own callback in its destructor, so no receiver runs after this
        openInputs_.clear();
    } else {
        std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::unique_ptr<MidiPort>>> kept;
        for (const std::string& name : want)
            for (auto& entry : hwIn_)
                if (entry.first == name) {
                    kept.push_back(std::move(entry));
                    break;
                }
        hwIn_ = std::move(kept);  // the rest are closed here, once the selection no longer names them
        openInputs_.clear();
    }
    for (const std::string& name : want) {
        bool held = false;
        for (const auto& entry : hwIn_)
            if (entry.first == name) {
                held = true;
                break;
            }
        if (held) continue;
        try {
            hwIn_.emplace_back(name, backend_->openInput(name, [this](const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
                                   pushRing(data, n);
                               }));
            emit("MIDI in: connected hardware port '" + name + "'");
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            emit("MIDI: input open failed for '" + name + "': " + e.what());
        }
    }
    for (const std::string& name : want)  // what OPENED, in the selection's order (a name that refused is missing)
        for (const auto& entry : hwIn_)
            if (entry.first == name) {
                openInputs_.push_back(name);
                break;
            }
}

void MidiStream::applyOutputs(Apply mode) {
    const std::vector<std::string> names = backend_->listOutputs();
    std::vector<std::string>       want;
    for (const std::string& sel : selectedOut_) {
        if (sel.empty()) continue;
        if (!reservedOut_.empty() && sel == reservedOut_) {
            emit("MIDI out: '" + sel + "' is held by the control surface");
            continue;
        }
        if (matchPortIndex(names, clientName_, sel)) {
            if (!contains(want, sel)) want.push_back(sel);
        } else {
            emit("MIDI out: selected port '" + sel + "' not present");
        }
    }
    std::vector<std::string> keep;  // what stays open: a diff's unchanged names, and none at all under a reopen
    if (mode == Apply::Diff)
        for (const std::string& name : openOutputs_)
            if (contains(want, name)) keep.push_back(name);
    if (mode == Apply::Diff && keep == openOutputs_ && keep.size() == want.size()) return;

    if (mode == Apply::Reopen) {
        // A port being asked for again has to be LET GO first: opening a name the stream still holds is refused where a
        // port is exclusive (a WinMM output), which is how the second open used to lose the device the re-pick meant to
        // heal. Nothing is published while that happens, so a send in the gap reaches no hardware output - the price of
        // the re-pick, and the reason a project load diffs instead.
        publishOutputs({});  // waits out the send in flight, so no send is inside a port when it is closed
        hwOut_.clear();
        openOutputs_.clear();
    }
    // A port the selection ADDS opens while the set it is joining is still published, so a send in that gap reaches the
    // ports the change keeps and nothing goes nowhere.
    std::vector<std::string> next = keep;
    for (const std::string& name : want) {
        if (contains(next, name)) continue;
        try {
            hwOut_.emplace_back(name, backend_->openOutput(name));
            next.push_back(name);
            emit("MIDI out: connected hardware port '" + name + "'");
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            emit("MIDI: output open failed for '" + name + "': " + e.what());
        }
    }
    openOutputs_ = next;
    publishOutputs(openOutputs_);
    // Only now are the ports the selection dropped closed: the set just published no longer names them, and the send
    // that could still have been inside one has been waited out.
    for (auto it = hwOut_.begin(); it != hwOut_.end();) {
        if (contains(openOutputs_, it->first)) {
            ++it;
            continue;
        }
        it = hwOut_.erase(it);  // closes it
    }
}

void MidiStream::publishOutputs(const std::vector<std::string>& open) {
    auto next         = std::make_unique<OutputSet>();
    next->virtualPort = virtualOut_.get();  // carried, never reopened: see the class comment
    for (const std::string& name : open)
        for (const auto& entry : hwOut_)
            if (entry.first == name) {
                next->ports.push_back(entry.second.get());
                break;
            }
    OutputSet* old = outputs_.exchange(next.release(), std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    retire(old);  // waits out the send in flight, which is the only thing that could still be inside the old set
}

void MidiStream::waitForSends() {
    // The wait is for the ONE send in flight, so it is bounded by a send and never by a run of them: the counter is
    // read once, and an odd value is waited out until it CHANGES (the in-flight send has exited). A send that starts
    // afterwards has read the newly published set, so it is no reason to wait; waiting "while odd" would instead chase
    // every send that follows, which under back-to-back sends is unbounded.
    const std::uint32_t seen = epoch_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    if ((seen & 1u) == 0) return;
    // A few yields first - a send is usually short - then short sleeps: a WinMM bulk SysEx blocks about 170 ms inside
    // send(), and 170 ms of a spinning UI thread is a visible stall, where a sleeping one is not.
    for (int spin = 0; epoch_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst) == seen; ++spin) {
        if (spin < 64) std::this_thread::yield();
        else std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(100));
    }
}

void MidiStream::retire(OutputSet* old) {
    if (!old) return;
    // The new set is published before this, so a send either sees it or is still inside the old one; waiting out that
    // send is all this needs. The orders are seq_cst because this is the store-buffering (Dekker) shape: send() writes
    // the counter and then reads the set, while this writes the set and then reads the counter. Under acquire/release
    // the two reordered store-load pairs let send() read the OLD set while this reads an even counter, and the old
    // ports are then freed under a send still using them. x86 hides that (its `lock xadd` is a full fence) and
    // ThreadSanitizer cannot see it either (it checks happens-before, not weak-memory reordering); AArch64, which the
    // handheld targets are, does not hide it. The four operations on the two locations are therefore seq_cst, which is
    // free on x86.
    waitForSends();
    delete old;
}

void MidiStream::pushRing(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) {
    if (!data || len == 0) return;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(pushMutex_);  // one producer at a time (see the class comment)
        const std::size_t t = tail_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        const std::size_t n = (t + 1) % kCapacity;
        if (n == head_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {  // full → drop
            dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);  // counted, so a lost clock isn't invisible
            return;
        }
        ring_[t].seq = ++seq_;
        ring_[t].bytes.assign(data, data + len);
        tail_.store(n, std::memory_order_release);
    }

    if (log_.load()) {
        std::string line = "MIDI in: ";
        char        hex[4];
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < len; ++i) {
            std::snprintf(hex, sizeof(hex), "%02X ", data[i]);
            line += hex;
        }
        emit(line);
    }
}

void MidiStream::poll(std::vector<Message>& out) {
    out.clear();
    std::size_t       h = head_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const std::size_t t = tail_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    while (h != t) {
        out.push_back(std::move(ring_[h]));
        h = (h + 1) % kCapacity;
    }
    head_.store(h, std::memory_order_release);
}

void MidiStream::send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (!data || n == 0) return;
    if (log_.load()) {
        std::string line = "MIDI out: ";
        char        hex[4];
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            std::snprintf(hex, sizeof(hex), "%02X ", data[i]);
            line += hex;
        }
        emit(line);
    }
    // The bracket covers the virtual output and the published set alike, so close() waits both out. ONE caller: the
    // audio thread. A second one would be a bug of the same class as freeing a port under a send - its entry would read
    // an odd counter and make it even again while the first caller is still inside a port, and a swap landing between
    // them would free that port. The counter is the invariant's only witness, so the entry checks it where a build
    // keeps its assertions.
    const std::uint32_t was = epoch_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_seq_cst);  // odd: a send is in flight
    (void)was;
    assert((was & 1u) == 0 && "MidiStream::send has one caller (the audio thread)");
    OutputSet* set = outputs_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    if (set) {
        if (set->virtualPort) set->virtualPort->send(data, n);
        for (auto& port : set->ports) port->send(data, n);
    }
    epoch_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_seq_cst);  // even: done, and everything above happens-before a retire
}

void MidiStream::emit(const std::string& text) {
    // The prefix the app has always written: the CLI prints it too, and three harness patterns grep past it.
    const std::string line = "[retroplug-sdl] " + text;
    if (sink_) {
        sink_(line);
        return;
    }
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", line.c_str());
}

}  // namespace rp::midi
````

````cpp
#include <string>
#include <thread>

namespace rp::midi {

class FakeMidiBackend;

/** What one port did, kept OUTSIDE the port object: the close bytes are written moments before an output is dropped,
 *  and a test reads them afterwards. A send that reaches a record whose port the stream has closed is a send the stream
 *  let go of too early - the output-set swap's failure, counted rather than only crashing. */
struct FakePortRecord {
    std::string        name;
    bool               input  = false;
    bool               closed = false;
    std::vector<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> received;  // what an output was sent, in order
    std::size_t        sendsAfterClose = 0;
};

/** One port of the fake. `send` copies its record FIRST, so a write that began before a swap counts itself against a
 *  record the fake still owns even if the port object is gone - which is what a swap that freed the port under a send
 *  does, and what the case that must fail without the epoch handshake measures. */
class FakePort final : public MidiPort {
public:
    FakePort(FakeMidiBackend& backend, std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord> rec, Receiver receiver);
    ~FakePort() override;
    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override;
    /** Play one message into this input: on the caller's thread, or queued to this port's own when the backend asked
     *  for threaded delivery. */
    void deliver(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n);

private:
    void drain();

    FakeMidiBackend&                      backend_;
    std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord>       record_;
    Receiver                              receiver_;
    std::mutex                            queueMutex_;
    std::condition_variable               queueWake_;
    std::deque<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> queue_;
    bool                                  stop_ = false;
    // LAST: joined by ~FakePort() before any member it reads is destroyed.
    std::thread                           worker_;
};

class FakeMidiBackend : public MidiBackend {
public:
    using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

    // --- what the machine has, and what it did ------------------------------------------------------------------

    // The ports the machine LISTS. Independent of what opens: opening a port no list names still works, so a claim of a
    // vanished port is the lister's refusal, as on a real machine.
    std::vector<std::string> inputs;
    std::vector<std::string> outputs;
    std::set<std::string>    refuse;   // ports whose open throws
    std::vector<std::string> events;   // "open in:X", "close out:Y", "virtual in:C" / "virtual out:C", in order
    std::map<std::string, std::vector<Bytes>> written;    // output name -> what went out, in order
    std::map<std::string, Receiver>           listening;  // currently-open inputs
    std::vector<std::string>                  listed;     // "in" / "out" per listing call
    // Whether an output is EXCLUSIVE, as a WinMM one is: opening a name the stream still holds throws. It is the
    // failure a re-pick has to avoid by letting the port go first, and it is off for every ordinary case. Inputs are
    // exclusive on Windows too, so the flag covers both directions.
    bool exclusivePorts = false;
    // A send hook, called by every output port once the bytes are recorded: a scripted device answers an inquiry
    // through it (the Launchpad pack's Pro MK3), and a case can watch a write arrive.
    std::function<void(FakeMidiBackend&, const std::string&, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t)> onSend;
    // How long a write to an OUTPUT blocks in the port, in milliseconds: a WinMM bulk SysEx waits for the bytes to
    // leave the wire (~170 ms), which is why the Launchpad's output leaves on a writer thread. 0 for every ordinary
    // case.
    int sendDelayMs = 0;
    // Writes in flight, so a case can wait until the writer is INSIDE the port before it times a send() against it.
    std::atomic<int> sendsStarted{0};
    std::atomic<int> sendsFinished{0};

    // --- the fake's own answers ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // The name this system opens its ports under, as a real backend's own client name is (the stream filters by it).
    std::string clientNameValue = "RetroPlug";
    bool usableFlag    = true;   // false: the system refuses to be used at all
    bool virtualPorts  = true;   // false: the Windows shape, no virtual ports
    bool threadedDelivery = false;  // true: an input's receiver runs on the port's own thread, as RtMidi's does

    std::string              id() const override { return "fake"; }
    std::string              clientName() const override { return clientNameValue; }
    /** A second fake listing the same machine under another client name. Its records, ports and hooks are its own (a
     *  renamed stream opens its own ports), so a case that drives a device model keeps driving the instance it made. */
    std::unique_ptr<MidiBackend> withClientName(std::string clientName) override {
        auto next           = std::make_unique<FakeMidiBackend>();
        next->inputs        = inputs;
        next->outputs       = outputs;
        next->refuse        = refuse;
        next->clientNameValue = std::move(clientName);
        next->usableFlag      = usableFlag;
        next->virtualPorts    = virtualPorts;
        next->exclusivePorts  = exclusivePorts;
        return next;
    }
    bool                     usable() override { return usableFlag; }
    std::vector<std::string> listInputs() override {
        listed.push_back("in");
        return inputs;
    }
    std::vector<std::string> listOutputs() override {
        listed.push_back("out");
        return outputs;
    }
    bool supportsVirtual() const override { return virtualPorts; }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openInput(const std::string& name, Receiver receiver) override {
        return open(true, name, std::move(receiver));
    }
    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openOutput(const std::string& name) override { return open(false, name, nullptr); }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualInput(Receiver receiver) override {
        return openVirtual(true, clientNameValue, std::move(receiver));
    }
    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtualOutput() override { return openVirtual(false, clientNameValue, nullptr); }

    /** Play the device: deliver `msg` on input `name`, as that port's callback thread would. Called under the fake's
     *  own lock, so an input the control thread closes at that moment cannot be destroyed between the lookup and the
     *  call (the port is alive until its own destructor takes the same lock, which waits for this delivery). */
    void deliver(const std::string& name, const Bytes& msg) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        const auto                  it = deliverers_.find(name);
        if (it != deliverers_.end()) it->second->deliver(msg.data(), msg.size());
    }

    /** Outputs sent to `name` so far (the record survives the port, so a close's goodbye is readable afterwards). */
    std::vector<Bytes> sentTo(const std::string& name) const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        std::vector<Bytes>          out;
        for (const auto& r : records_)
            if (!r->input && r->name == name) out.insert(out.end(), r->received.begin(), r->received.end());
        return out;
    }
    /** Every send any output recorded, across every port that ever opened, so a lost send shows as a short count. */
    std::size_t totalReceived() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        std::size_t                 n = 0;
        for (const auto& r : records_)
            if (!r->input) n += r->received.size();
        return n;
    }
    /** Sends that reached a port after the stream closed it: zero, whichever thread swapped the selection. */
    std::size_t sendsAfterClose() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        std::size_t                 n = 0;
        for (const auto& r : records_) n += r->sendsAfterClose;
        return n;
    }
    /** Records made so far (one per open port, virtual included): how a case waits for a scan or a swap to land. */
    std::size_t records() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        return records_.size();
    }

    // --- the ports' own calls (public so the header-only ports can make them) -------------------------------------

    void pushEvent(const std::string& event) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        events.push_back(event);
    }

    /** One output's send: recorded against its record, then handed to the hook. */
    void sendThrough(const std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord>& rec, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
        if (!data || n == 0) return;
        sendsStarted.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (sendDelayMs > 0) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(sendDelayMs));
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
            if (rec->input) {
                // an input's send is a no-op
            } else if (rec->closed) {
                rec->sendsAfterClose++;  // the port this write belongs to was let go while the write was in flight
            } else {
                rec->received.emplace_back(data, data + n);
                written[rec->name].emplace_back(data, data + n);
            }
        }
        if (onSend) onSend(*this, rec->name, data, n);
        sendsFinished.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }

    /** A port went away: say so once, and stop routing deliveries to it. The machine's open-input map is written under
     *  the same lock registerInput writes it under, so a test reading it while a port closes sees either state, not
     *  half of one. */
    void closePort(const std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord>& rec) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
        rec->closed = true;
        deliverers_.erase(rec->name);
        if (rec->input) listening.erase(rec->name);
        events.push_back(std::string("close ") + (rec->input ? "in:" : "out:") + rec->name);
    }

private:
    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> open(bool input, const std::string& name, Receiver receiver) {
        if (refuse.count(name) || !usableFlag) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI port not found: " + name);
        if (exclusivePorts) {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
            for (const auto& r : records_)
                if (r->name == name && r->input == input && !r->closed)
                    throw std::runtime_error("MIDI port is already in use: " + name);
        }
        auto rec = std::make_shared<FakePortRecord>();
        rec->name  = name;
        rec->input = input;
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
            records_.push_back(rec);
        }
        pushEvent(std::string("open ") + (input ? "in:" : "out:") + name);
        auto port = std::make_unique<FakePort>(*this, rec, std::move(receiver));
        if (input) registerInput(name, *port, /*machinePort=*/true);
        return port;
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> openVirtual(bool input, const std::string& client, Receiver receiver) {
        if (!virtualPorts || !usableFlag) throw std::runtime_error("virtual ports are not supported");
        // A virtual port is a port with no machine name behind it: "<client> In" / "<client> Out", as RtMidi publishes
        // it, recorded like any other so a case sees what the stream opened and logged.
        const std::string name = client + (input ? " In" : " Out");
        pushEvent(std::string("virtual ") + (input ? "in:" : "out:") + client);
        auto rec = std::make_shared<FakePortRecord>();
        rec->name  = name;
        rec->input = input;
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
            records_.push_back(rec);
        }
        auto port = std::make_unique<FakePort>(*this, rec, std::move(receiver));
        if (input) registerInput(name, *port, /*machinePort=*/false);
        return port;
    }

    /** An input that opened: where a delivery goes. The receiver is the port's own delivery path, so a threaded port
     *  queues and an inline one calls on the caller's thread. `listening` is the MACHINE's open inputs (what a case
     * reads as "is it open"): a virtual port the stream publishes is not one the machine lists, so it is left out of
     * it. */
    void registerInput(const std::string& name, FakePort& port, bool machinePort);

    friend class FakePort;

    mutable std::mutex                       mutex_;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord>> records_;
    std::map<std::string, FakePort*>         deliverers_;  // open inputs, for threaded delivery
};

// --- the port's definitions, after the backend it calls ---------------------------------------------------------

inline void FakeMidiBackend::registerInput(const std::string& name, FakePort& port, bool machinePort) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mutex_);
    if (machinePort) listening[name] = [&port](const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { port.deliver(data, n); };
    deliverers_[name] = &port;
}

inline FakePort::FakePort(FakeMidiBackend& backend, std::shared_ptr<FakePortRecord> rec, Receiver receiver)
    : backend_(backend), record_(std::move(rec)), receiver_(std::move(receiver)) {
    if (backend_.threadedDelivery) worker_ = std::thread([this] { drain(); });
}

inline FakePort::~FakePort() {
    if (worker_.joinable()) {
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(queueMutex_);
            stop_ = true;
        }
        queueWake_.notify_one();
        worker_.join();  // no receiver call is running when this returns
    }
    // Unrouted under the fake's lock, so a delivery already in flight finishes before this returns and no later one can
    // look the port up; only then does the receiver a delivery would call go away (the MidiPort contract: no receiver
    // call runs once the destructor has returned).
    backend_.closePort(record_);
    receiver_ = nullptr;
}

inline void FakePort::send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    auto rec = record_;  // a copy: alive whatever happens to this object (see the class comment)
    backend_.sendThrough(rec, data, n);
}

inline void FakePort::deliver(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (!record_->input || !data || n == 0) return;
    if (!worker_.joinable()) {
        if (receiver_) receiver_(data, n);
        return;
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(queueMutex_);
        queue_.emplace_back(data, data + n);
    }
    queueWake_.notify_one();
}

inline void FakePort::drain() {
    for (;;) {
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
        {
            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk(queueMutex_);
            queueWake_.wait(lk, [this] { return stop_ || !queue_.empty(); });
            if (queue_.empty()) return;  // stop_ and nothing left
            bytes = std::move(queue_.front());
            queue_.pop_front();
        }
        if (receiver_) receiver_(bytes.data(), bytes.size());
    }
}

}  // namespace rp::midi
````

````cpp
// Unit-tests MidiStream, the host's one MIDI stream, over FakeMidiBackend: which ports a selection opens (the lists and
// "all"), a re-pick reopening what it names, the reservation and the scan's suspended edge, the receive ring under
// concurrent producers and under a delivery thread, an output swap and a close under a send in flight, the log lines
// the harnesses grep, a backend with no virtual ports, a refused open, and the test-only allow list reaching the
// stream's own list and opens. No MIDI system and no hardware: the backend is the fake in midi/FakeMidiBackend.hpp.
//
// The output-swap and close cases are the ones that must be run in build-tsan/ as well (section 4.7 of
// docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md): the ports a send() may be using are freed only once the send in flight has
// been waited out.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <atomic>
#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "midi/FakeMidiBackend.hpp"
#include "midi/MidiStream.hpp"

using rp::midi::FakeMidiBackend;
using rp::midi::MidiStream;

namespace {

/** RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW is a developer's environment variable (tools/run-sdl-controller.sh exports it for the
 *  standalone's harness), and a hand run of that harness leaves it in the shell. The cases here open the fake's own
 *  ports, so the file clears it on load and puts back whatever it found at exit; the one case that wants a list sets it
 *  for its own scope. */
struct UnfilteredFileScope {
    UnfilteredFileScope() {
        const char* was = std::getenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
        had_            = was != nullptr;
        if (had_) was_ = was;
#if defined(_WIN32)
        _putenv_s("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", "");
#else
        unsetenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
#endif
    }
    ~UnfilteredFileScope() {
#if defined(_WIN32)
        _putenv_s("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", had_ ? was_.c_str() : "");
#else
        if (had_) setenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", was_.c_str(), 1);
        else unsetenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
#endif
    }
    bool        had_ = false;
    std::string was_;
};
const UnfilteredFileScope kUnfiltered;

/** RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW for one case, put back as it was when it goes (the filter reads it on every call). */
struct PortAllowList {
    explicit PortAllowList(const char* spec) {
        const char* was = std::getenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
        had_            = was != nullptr;
        if (had_) was_ = was;
#if defined(_WIN32)
        _putenv_s("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", spec);
#else
        setenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", spec, 1);
#endif
    }
    ~PortAllowList() {
#if defined(_WIN32)
        _putenv_s("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", had_ ? was_.c_str() : "");
#else
        if (had_) setenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW", was_.c_str(), 1);
        else unsetenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
#endif
    }
    PortAllowList(const PortAllowList&)            = delete;
    PortAllowList& operator=(const PortAllowList&) = delete;

    bool        had_ = false;
    std::string was_;
};

/** A machine with two controllers and a synth's output, and nothing open: what the stream's cases start from. The fake
 *  holds a mutex, so it is neither copyable nor movable and the rig holds it by value rather than returning one. */
struct Machine {
    FakeMidiBackend backend;
    Machine() {
        backend.inputs  = {"Keys in", "Pads in", "Midi Through:Midi Through Port-0 14:0",
                           "RetroPlug:RetroPlug In 128:0"};
        backend.outputs = {"Synth out", "Interface out", "RetroPlug:RetroPlug Out 128:1"};
    }
};

/** The "open ..." events a rig recorded, so a case can hold WHICH ports the stream opened and in what order. */
std::vector<std::string> opensOf(const FakeMidiBackend& backend) {
    std::vector<std::string> out;
    for (const std::string& e : backend.events)
        if (e.rfind("open ", 0) == 0 || e.rfind("virtual ", 0) == 0) out.push_back(e);
    return out;
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes(int a, int b, int c = -1) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> out{static_cast<std::uint8_t>(a), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(b)};
    if (c >= 0) out.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c));
    return out;
}

}  // namespace

// ---- what a selection opens ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("an empty selection opens no hardware port: the virtual pair and nothing else") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    // The stream opened the virtual pair ("RetroPlug In" / "RetroPlug Out") and no hardware port.
    CHECK(opensOf(backend) == std::vector<std::string>{"virtual in:RetroPlug", "virtual out:RetroPlug"});
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 0);
    CHECK(stream.listInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Keys in", "Pads in"});
    CHECK(stream.listOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out", "Interface out"});
}

TEST_CASE("a list of exact names opens exactly those ports") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Pads in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Interface out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 0);
    // The output: a send lands on the selected port and the virtual one, nowhere else.
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Interface out").size() == 1);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").empty());
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("RetroPlug Out").size() == 1);  // the virtual output mirrors, as it always did
}

TEST_CASE("all devices opens every hardware input, once each, and no virtual one twice") {
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({}, true);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 1);
    // The rig's own virtual port and ALSA's Through are not hardware: neither is opened, and the virtual pair the
    // stream published is still exactly one port each.
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("RetroPlug:RetroPlug In 128:0") == 0);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Midi Through:Midi Through Port-0 14:0") == 0);
    CHECK(opensOf(backend) == std::vector<std::string>{"virtual in:RetroPlug", "virtual out:RetroPlug",
                                                       "open in:Keys in", "open in:Pads in"});
    // Every open input feeds the one ring: a message on either is drained with its bytes intact.
    backend.deliver("Keys in", bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
    backend.deliver("Pads in", bytes(0xB0, 0x07, 0x64));
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> got;
    stream.poll(got);
    REQUIRE(got.size() == 2);
    CHECK(got[0].bytes == bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
    CHECK(got[1].bytes == bytes(0xB0, 0x07, 0x64));
    CHECK(got[0].seq < got[1].seq);
}

TEST_CASE("a name that is not present opens nothing, and a later apply picks it up when it appears") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Unplugged keys"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Unplugged synth"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(backend.listening.empty());
    CHECK(backend.totalReceived() == 0);
    // The name stayed in the selection: the device appears (a machine's list is read when it is asked), and the next
    // apply opens it. Nothing was dropped from the selection by the failed attempt.
    backend.inputs.push_back("Unplugged keys");
    backend.outputs.push_back("Unplugged synth");
    stream.setInputs({"Unplugged keys"}, false);  // the next apply
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Unplugged keys") == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a re-pick of the same device closes and reopens it: how an unplugged port heals") {
    // There is no hotplug watch, so picking the device again in Settings > MIDI is the user's one remedy after an
    // unplug and a replug - and it has to reopen, not diff to the name it already held. That is what Apply::Reopen
    // asks for: a diff (a project load) would leave the dead port open.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    const std::size_t afterFirstPick = backend.records();
    // The same selection again: the ports it names are let go and opened afresh (one record each, and the fake's event
    // log shows the closes in between).
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"}, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
    CHECK(backend.records() == afterFirstPick + 2);
    // Two opens of that output in the log: the first pick's and the re-pick's.
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "open out:Synth out") == 2);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "close out:Synth out") == 1);
    // And what is open is what was asked for, which is what the rows read.
    CHECK(stream.openedInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Keys in"});
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").size() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a diff re-applies only what moved: a port the selection keeps is never reopened") {
    // A project load applies the selection a project's section names, and almost every port in it may already be open
    // (the same project reloaded, a second section that agrees). Reopening those would cost the connection: a clock
    // arriving on a hardware input loses what arrives in the gap, and on Windows an exclusive port can be lost
    // outright. Only the names the change moved are touched.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    const std::size_t afterFirstPick = backend.records();
    // Adding an input and an output opens exactly the two that were added, and leaves the two that were kept alone.
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out", "Interface out"});
    CHECK(backend.records() == afterFirstPick + 2);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "open in:Keys in") == 1);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "close in:Keys in") == 0);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "open out:Synth out") == 1);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "close out:Synth out") == 0);
    CHECK(stream.openedInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Keys in", "Pads in"});
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out", "Interface out"});
    // Dropping one closes it and nothing else: the kept input's receiver still delivers.
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "close in:Pads in") == 1);
    CHECK(std::count(backend.events.begin(), backend.events.end(), "close in:Keys in") == 0);
    backend.deliver("Keys in", bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> got;
    stream.poll(got);
    REQUIRE(got.size() == 1);
    CHECK(got[0].bytes == bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
    // Restating the unchanged selection costs nothing at all.
    const std::size_t before = backend.records();
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out", "Interface out"});
    CHECK(backend.records() == before);
}

TEST_CASE("an exclusive port: a re-pick must let the port go before it is opened again, or it is lost") {
    // The review's probe, over the fake's model of a WinMM port: a second open of a name this stream still holds is
    // refused. A re-pick that opened before it closed therefore lost the device it meant to heal - the output went
    // silent for good, and the event log says so (a refused open, then a close, then nothing).
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.exclusivePorts   = true;
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    REQUIRE(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out"});
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"}, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
    // The port is still the stream's: the close came first, so the second open was accepted.
    CHECK(stream.openedInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Keys in"});
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out"});
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").size() == 1);
    // A diff keeps the port and never asks for it again, so it is not refused either.
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out", "Interface out"});
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out", "Interface out"});
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Interface out").size() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("what opened is not what was selected: a missing name and a held port are not in the opened sets") {
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Not here"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out", "Not here either"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(stream.openedInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Keys in"});
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out"});
    // A claimed port is selected and not opened, which is what the checklist's held mark says.
    stream.setReserved("Keys in", "Synth out");
    CHECK(stream.openedInputs().empty());
    CHECK(stream.openedOutputs().empty());
}

TEST_CASE("closing the stream gives every port back, and re-opening re-applies the selection") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    REQUIRE(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    stream.close();
    CHECK(backend.listening.empty());
    CHECK_FALSE(stream.isOpen());
    // A send after the close goes nowhere (not to a port the close freed).
    const std::size_t before = backend.totalReceived();
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.totalReceived() == before);
    // Re-opened, the selection is applied again.
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a close under a send in flight frees no port the send is using, nor the virtual output") {
    // A device loss is one reason a product closes the stream while audio still renders; the close publishes the end of
    // the set and waits the send out, so the ports (and the virtual output, whose sends the same bracket covers) are
    // never freed under a caller still inside one.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.sendDelayMs      = 1;
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    constexpr int     kSends = 200;
    std::atomic<bool> started{false};
    std::thread       audio([&] {
        const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
        started.store(true);
        for (int i = 0; i < kSends; ++i) stream.send(note, 3);
    });
    while (!started.load()) std::this_thread::yield();
    // A few sends in, so one is in flight when the close lands.
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(5));
    stream.close();
    audio.join();
    CHECK(backend.sendsAfterClose() == 0);
    // Whatever had not been sent by the close went nowhere at all: no port was left published to receive it.
    CHECK(backend.sendsStarted.load() < kSends);
}

// ---- the reservation and the scan's held edge ------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a reserved port is skipped under all devices and under a list naming it, and the claim itself is a no-op "
          "when nothing moved") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    REQUIRE(backend.listening.size() == 2);
    const std::size_t recordsBefore = backend.records();
    // Claiming an open port makes the stream let go of it, and of nothing else.
    stream.setReserved("Keys in", "Synth out");
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 0);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 1);
    // The output did not move? It did: the claim named it, so it is held and closed.
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").empty());
    // The claim and the scan's edge apply what is open after a diff, so restating one costs no port churn (the claimed
    // port stays out, and the one output is still held). A SELECTION setter is diffed too: a re-pick is what asks for a
    // reopen, and that is the case above.
    const std::size_t recordsAfterClaim = backend.records();
    stream.setReserved("Keys in", "Synth out");
    stream.setHardwareInputsSuspended(false);  // already resumed: no apply at all
    CHECK(backend.records() == recordsAfterClaim);
    // A claim only ever CLOSES: the ports it takes away are let go and nothing is opened in their place.
    CHECK(recordsAfterClaim == recordsBefore);
    // Releasing gives both back.
    stream.setReserved("", "");
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").size() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a reserved input under all devices still leaves every OTHER input open") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({}, true);
    stream.setReserved("Pads in", "");
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a scan's held edge closes every input and resuming re-applies the selection") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    REQUIRE(backend.listening.size() == 2);
    stream.setHardwareInputsSuspended(true);
    CHECK(stream.hardwareInputsSuspended());
    CHECK(backend.listening.empty());
    // The selection was not disturbed: resuming opens exactly what it held.
    stream.setHardwareInputsSuspended(false);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 1);
}

// ---- the receive ring ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

namespace {

constexpr int kProducers   = 4;
constexpr int kPerProducer = 5000;
// Producers yield this often. Without it a few unpaced producers fill the ring and nearly everything takes the drop
// path, which writes no slot - so on a 1-2 core runner the racy write path runs only a couple of hundred times out of
// twenty thousand. Paced, most messages land and the slot writes actually contend.
constexpr int kYieldEvery = 16;
constexpr std::size_t kRing = MidiStream::kCapacity;

// Message i from producer p: a status byte naming the producer, i split over two data bytes, then a tail whose length
// (0-4 bytes) and contents both depend on i - so a slot assembled from two writers fails the decode rather than passing
// as some other valid message.
std::vector<std::uint8_t> encode(int p, int i) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> m = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x90 | p), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i & 0x7F),
                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>((i >> 7) & 0x7F)};
    for (int k = 0; k < i % 5; ++k) m.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>((i + k) & 0x7F));
    return m;
}

// The (producer, i) a message encodes, or {-1, -1} if it isn't a well-formed message from encode().
std::pair<int, int> decode(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& m) {
    if (m.size() < 3 || (m[0] & 0xF0) != 0x90) return {-1, -1};
    const int p = m[0] & 0x0F;
    const int i = m[1] | (m[2] << 7);
    if (p >= kProducers || i >= kPerProducer || m != encode(p, i)) return {-1, -1};
    return {p, i};
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("the input ring: concurrent producers deliver every message intact, once, in order") {
    // Every open input delivers on its own callback thread - the virtual one plus one per selected hardware port - so a
    // selection of several puts two or more threads in pushRing at once while the audio thread drains with poll(). The
    // ring has one producer at a time (pushMutex_); without that, these threads race the tail index, the sequence
    // counter and a slot's vector, which build-tsan/ reports every run.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    // The stream's ring has three producers here: the virtual input and the two hardware ones. The case drives the two
    // hardware ports directly, on more threads than there are ports, which is the shape the race was in.
    std::atomic<int> producersLeft{kProducers};
    std::atomic<int> ready{0};

    std::vector<std::thread> producers;
    for (int p = 0; p < kProducers; ++p)
        producers.emplace_back([&backend, &producersLeft, &ready, p] {
            ready.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
            while (ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire) < kProducers) std::this_thread::yield();
            // Half the producers speak on each port: deliver() calls that port's receiver on THIS thread, which is the
            // shape an RtMidi callback has - one thread per open input, all pushing into the one ring.
            const std::string port = p % 2 == 0 ? "Keys in" : "Pads in";
            for (int i = 0; i < kPerProducer; ++i) {
                backend.deliver(port, encode(p, i));
                if (i % kYieldEvery == 0) std::this_thread::yield();
            }
            producersLeft.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_release);
        });

    // The consumer drains while the producers run (the audio thread's shape), then once more after.
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> received;
    std::thread consumer([&] {
        std::vector<MidiStream::Message> batch;
        bool last = false;
        while (!last) {
            last = producersLeft.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;
            stream.poll(batch);
            for (auto& m : batch) received.push_back(std::move(m));
        }
    });

    for (auto& t : producers) t.join();
    consumer.join();

    std::set<std::pair<int, int>> seen;
    int lastIndex[kProducers];
    for (int& v : lastIndex) v = -1;
    std::uint64_t lastSeq = 0;
    int malformed = 0, duplicates = 0, reordered = 0, seqGaps = 0;
    for (const auto& m : received) {
        const auto [p, i] = decode(m.bytes);
        if (p < 0) { ++malformed; continue; }
        if (!seen.insert({p, i}).second) ++duplicates;
        if (i <= lastIndex[p]) ++reordered;
        lastIndex[p] = i;
        // A drop takes no sequence number, so arrivals are contiguous: a gap is a lost slot write.
        if (m.seq != lastSeq + 1) ++seqGaps;
        lastSeq = m.seq;
    }

    CHECK(malformed == 0);
    CHECK(duplicates == 0);
    CHECK(reordered == 0);
    CHECK(seqGaps == 0);
    // Overflow is allowed (a full ring drops and counts), but nothing may vanish uncounted.
    CHECK(received.size() + stream.droppedCount() == static_cast<std::size_t>(kProducers * kPerProducer));
    // Nothing landing would make every check above vacuous. Deliberately no tighter threshold: the drop rate depends on
    // the scheduler, and a rate bound would be a flaky test.
    CHECK(received.size() > kRing);
}

TEST_CASE("a full ring drops the incoming message and counts it, and what did land is intact") {
    Machine             machine;
    FakeMidiBackend&    backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream          stream(machine.backend);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    const std::size_t overflow = 40;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kRing + overflow; ++i) {
        const std::vector<std::uint8_t> m = bytes(0x90, static_cast<int>(i & 0x7F), 0x40);
        stream.injectForTest(m.data(), m.size());
    }
    // The ring keeps one slot free for its full/empty distinction, so kRing - 1 land and the rest are dropped and
    // counted.
    CHECK(stream.droppedCount() == kRing + overflow - (kRing - 1));
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> got;
    stream.poll(got);
    CHECK(got.size() == kRing - 1);
    CHECK(got.front().bytes == bytes(0x90, 0x00, 0x40));
    CHECK(got.back().bytes == bytes(0x90, static_cast<int>((kRing - 2) & 0x7F), 0x40));
    // And it keeps working afterwards.
    stream.injectForTest(bytes(0x90, 0x40, 0x7F).data(), 3);
    stream.poll(got);
    REQUIRE(got.size() == 1);
    CHECK(got[0].bytes == bytes(0x90, 0x40, 0x7F));
    CHECK(got[0].seq == kRing);  // a drop takes no sequence number: arrivals are contiguous
}

// ---- the output set's swap ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("an output swap under a send in flight: every send lands on one live port, and none reaches a freed one") {
    // The hazard the epoch handshake exists for (design 4.3): send() runs on the audio thread and calls a port the
    // control thread is replacing. The ports are freed only once the send in flight has been waited out, so no send
    // reaches a port the stream has let go, and none is lost. The fake counts both, so the failure is a number rather
    // than only a crash - and this case runs in build-tsan/ as well.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.sendDelayMs   = 1;      // a write that takes a moment, as a WinMM bulk SysEx does
    backend.virtualPorts  = false;  // the swap is the hardware set's: no virtual output to count as well
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});  // an output is selected before the audio thread starts, as it is in a run
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    constexpr int kSends = 300;
    std::atomic<bool> done{false};
    std::thread audio([&] {
        const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
        for (int i = 0; i < kSends; ++i) stream.send(note, 3);
        done.store(true);
    });
    int swaps = 0;
    while (!done.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
        stream.setOutputs(swaps % 2 == 0 ? std::vector<std::string>{"Synth out"}
                                         : std::vector<std::string>{"Interface out"});
        ++swaps;
    }
    audio.join();
    CHECK(swaps > 2);
    CHECK(backend.sendsStarted.load() == kSends);   // every send reached a port: none went to no output at all
    CHECK(backend.sendsFinished.load() == kSends);
    CHECK(backend.records() >= 2);                  // the swap really opened new ports under the sender
    CHECK(backend.sendsAfterClose() == 0);
    CHECK(backend.totalReceived() == static_cast<std::size_t>(kSends));
}

TEST_CASE("a swap behind back-to-back long sends waits out one send, never the run of them") {
    // A WinMM bulk SysEx blocks about 170 ms inside send(), and a block may send several. The wait must be bounded by
    // the ONE send in flight - the set the swap published is what the next send reads - so a reconfigure waits one
    // send, not the stream of them. Waiting "while the epoch is odd" instead chases every send that follows: this case
    // measured hundreds of milliseconds on a 32-thread box and never returned under `taskset -c 0` (the swap spins out
    // the whole run). The bound is three sends, loose enough for a loaded runner and tight enough to fail that wait.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.sendDelayMs      = 20;
    backend.virtualPorts     = false;  // the swap is the hardware set's
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    constexpr int kSends = 40;  // 800 ms of unbroken sends
    std::thread   audio([&] {
        const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
        for (int i = 0; i < kSends; ++i) stream.send(note, 3);
    });
    while (backend.sendsStarted.load() == 0) std::this_thread::yield();  // a send is in flight as the swap lands
    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    stream.setOutputs({"Interface out"});
    const auto waited =
        std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
    audio.join();
    // One in-flight send plus slack: four sends' time, because a ThreadSanitizer run inside the parallel kit stretches
    // a 20 ms send and the scheduling around it.
    CHECK(waited < 4 * backend.sendDelayMs);
    CHECK(backend.sendsAfterClose() == 0);
    CHECK(backend.totalReceived() == static_cast<std::size_t>(kSends));
}

TEST_CASE("every message a delivery thread queued is delivered before its port's destructor returns") {
    // The MidiPort contract (midi/MidiBackend.hpp) is "no receiver call after the destructor returns", and it is what
    // lets a selection change close inputs under a running stream: the fake delivers on a thread of its own here, as
    // RtMidi does, and a swap must lose none of what was queued for a port it lets go. Run in build-tsan/ too.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.threadedDelivery = true;
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    constexpr int kEach = 50;
    for (int i = 0; i < kEach; ++i) {
        backend.deliver("Keys in", bytes(0x90, i & 0x7F, 0x40));
        backend.deliver("Pads in", bytes(0xB0, i & 0x7F, 0x10));
    }
    // The swap closes "Pads in", joining its delivery thread before it is gone; "Keys in" STAYS (a diff), so its own
    // thread is still delivering. Poll until the kept port's queue has caught up: the port that was let go owes every
    // message its destructor's join drained, and the one that stayed simply delivers asynchronously, as RtMidi does.
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> got;
    std::vector<MidiStream::Message> batch;
    for (int tries = 0; tries < 1000 && got.size() < 2 * kEach; ++tries) {
        if (tries > 0) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
        batch.clear();
        stream.poll(batch);
        got.insert(got.end(), batch.begin(), batch.end());
    }
    CHECK(got.size() == 2 * kEach);
    CHECK(stream.droppedCount() == 0);
    // Same-thread delivery, the other mode, on the port that stayed: unchanged.
    backend.deliver("Keys in", bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
    got.clear();
    for (int tries = 0; tries < 1000 && got.empty(); ++tries) {  // the port that stayed delivers on its own thread too
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
        stream.poll(got);
    }
    REQUIRE(got.size() == 1);
    CHECK(got[0].bytes == bytes(0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F));
}

TEST_CASE("the log lines the standalone's harnesses grep, byte for byte") {
    // tools/run-sdl-controller.sh greps the reservation line and the virtual-ports line; the smoke greps the rest of
    // the shape. The stream writes them through one sink, so a case can hold the very bytes (and the "[retroplug-sdl] "
    // prefix the app has always used, which the CLI prints too).
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    std::vector<std::string> lines;
    stream.setLogSink([&](const std::string& line) { lines.push_back(line); });
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out", "Nope"});  // "Nope" is not on this machine: the picker's stale name
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    stream.setReserved("Keys in", "Synth out");
    stream.setHardwareInputsSuspended(true);
    stream.setHardwareInputsSuspended(false);
    const std::vector<std::string> expected = {
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI: virtual ports 'RetroPlug In' / 'RetroPlug Out' open",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI in: no hardware device selected (Settings > MIDI)",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI out: selected port 'Nope' not present",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI out: connected hardware port 'Synth out'",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI in: connected hardware port 'Keys in'",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI out: 'Synth out' is held by the control surface",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI out: selected port 'Nope' not present",
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI in: hardware inputs suspended for a control-surface scan",
        // Resumed with its one port still claimed by the surface: the selection is re-applied, and nothing opens.
        "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI in: hardware inputs resumed",
    };
    CHECK(lines == expected);
}

TEST_CASE("send() has ONE caller, and what two would break") {
    // send() marks a send in flight by making the epoch odd on entry and even on exit, and a swap waits that one send
    // out. A SECOND caller breaks the mark: A's entry makes it odd, B's entry makes it EVEN again while A is still
    // inside a port, and a swap that lands between them publishes and retires at once - the port A is writing is freed
    // under it. The review's probe measured exactly that (two senders, 200 swaps, 2 sends reaching a closed port in 20
    // runs), which is why send() asserts the entry found the counter even (an assert, so a Debug build fails loudly;
    // the release build carries none). A block sends sequentially, which is the caller this stream is written for.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    stream.setOutputs({"Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) stream.send(note, 3);  // one thread, one send at a time: the odd/even parity holds
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").size() == 3);
    CHECK(backend.sendsAfterClose() == 0);
}

// ---- the backend's own answers, and the filter ---------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a backend with no virtual ports opens none, and announces none") {
    // WinMM's openVirtualPort prints a warning and returns, so the old stream announced two ports that did not exist
    // and left the user without the "RetroPlug In/Out" a DAW connects to, silently. supportsVirtual() says so instead.
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.virtualPorts     = false;
    MidiStream       stream(backend);
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK_FALSE(stream.supportsVirtual());
    CHECK(opensOf(backend).empty());  // no virtual pair, no hardware input, no output
    // The stream still opens the hardware the selection names.
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in"}, false);
    CHECK(opensOf(backend) == std::vector<std::string>{"open in:Keys in"});
}

TEST_CASE("a refused open is one exception, skipped, and the rest of the list opens") {
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.refuse.insert("Interface out");
    backend.refuse.insert("Pads in");
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({"Keys in", "Pads in"}, false);
    stream.setOutputs({"Interface out", "Synth out"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());  // a refused PORT is not a refused stream
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Keys in") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Pads in") == 0);
    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, 0x3C, 0x7F};
    stream.send(note, 3);
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Synth out").size() == 1);   // the port that did open still gets the stream
    CHECK(backend.sentTo("Interface out").empty());
}

TEST_CASE("a backend that cannot be used at all answers false and opens nothing") {
    Machine          machine;
    FakeMidiBackend& backend = machine.backend;
    backend.usableFlag       = false;
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({}, true);
    CHECK_FALSE(stream.open());
    CHECK_FALSE(stream.isOpen());
    CHECK(backend.records() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the allow list hides a port from the stream's list and from its opens") {
    PortAllowList allow("RPFake");
    FakeMidiBackend backend;
    backend.inputs  = {"RPFake keys", "Zoom L6:1 20:0"};
    backend.outputs = {"RPFake synth", "Zoom L6:1 20:1"};
    MidiStream stream(backend);
    stream.setInputs({}, true);  // all devices, which is the case that would otherwise open everything the machine has
    stream.setOutputs({"Zoom L6:1 20:1"});
    REQUIRE(stream.open());
    CHECK(stream.listInputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"RPFake keys"});
    CHECK(stream.listOutputs() == std::vector<std::string>{"RPFake synth"});
    CHECK(backend.listening.size() == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("RPFake keys") == 1);
    CHECK(backend.listening.count("Zoom L6:1 20:0") == 0);
    CHECK(backend.totalReceived() == 0);  // the filtered output never even opened
}
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The facet: `MidiRpcService` moved, and its provider**

`MidiRpcService.{hpp,cpp}` move into the package as its provider facet with `git mv`; the change is the shape the fix
pass settled on: the RPC method names, parameters and results do not change (`midiListInputs`, `midiListOutputs`,
`midiOpen`, `midiSelectOutput`, `midiPoll`, `midiSend`, `midiClose`), so `realBackend.ts`, the TS sessions and the SDK
do not, while `midiOpen`'s `""` now means every hardware input (E11) and a session's own `clientName` is honoured by
building its stream over `base_.withClientName(clientName)` (one stream, one name). `MidiProvider.{hpp,cpp}` is
`rp_midi_provider`: `create` builds the service over a `MidiStream` on `systemMidi()` opening nothing until
`midiOpen`, `restore` is a no-op, `rpc_service` returns it, `destroy` deletes it, `wake` is null.

The moves, as one script (each `git mv` stages its move, and `set -e` stops at the first that fails):

````bash
mkdir -p packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet
set -e
git mv packages/native/src/host/input/MidiRpcService.cpp packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp
git mv packages/native/src/host/input/MidiRpcService.hpp packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.hpp
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The midi package's provider (graph/rp_provider.h, docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 4.5): what a product
// starts so that the CLI's live-MIDI facet exists without the product naming a class of this package. It owns the
// facet's service (a MidiStream over a backend, opening nothing until midiOpen), and mounts nothing in the engine's
// registry: a stream is not a graph device.
//
// The manifest's `provider` is rp_midi_provider; a product names `midi` in its PROVIDERS (the CLI does) and gets it
// started in that order. A product that uses the stream itself (the SDL app) holds a MidiStream of its own and starts
// no provider.

#include "graph/rp_provider.h"
#include "midi/MidiBackend.hpp"
#include "midi/facet/MidiRpcService.hpp"

namespace rp::midi {

/** rp_midi_provider's create with the backend given: systemMidi() in production, a scripted one in the headless host,
 *  so test-native drives the same facet over a fake's ports. Null when `host` is null or of another ABI version, or
 *  when building the provider threw (said on stderr): nothing it throws leaves here, as nothing may cross the C
 *  table. */
void* createProvider(const rp_device_host* host, MidiBackend& backend);

/** The service a started provider owns (a test reads its stream's state; a product never does). */
MidiRpcService& providerService(void* self);

}  // namespace rp::midi

extern "C" const rp_provider* rp_midi_provider(void);
````

Create `packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiProvider.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "midi/facet/MidiProvider.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <exception>

#include "midi/RtMidiBackend.hpp"

namespace rp::midi {
namespace {

// Everything the provider owns: the backend it was handed (a reference: the product's, or the test's, outlives this)
// and the facet's service over it. Nothing is persisted here - the selection is the project's TypeScript, and a session
// opens a stream through the facet - so there is no state to restore.
struct Provider {
    Provider(MidiBackend& backend, const rp_device_host&) : rpc(backend) {}
    Provider(const Provider&)            = delete;
    Provider& operator=(const Provider&) = delete;

    MidiRpcService rpc;
};

Provider& providerOf(void* self) {
    return *static_cast<Provider*>(self);
}

// The table's entries throw nothing (graph/rp_provider.h): a create that throws (an allocation) answers null and says
// why.
void* createWithSystemMidi(const rp_device_host* host) noexcept {
    if (!host) return nullptr;
    try {
        return createProvider(host, systemMidi());
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the MIDI provider did not start\n");
        return nullptr;
    }
}

// Nothing is persisted here: the selection is the project's (TypeScript), and the SDL app's own stream is its own.
void restore(void* self) noexcept {
    (void)self;
}

void* rpcService(void* self) noexcept {
    return &providerOf(self).rpc;
}

void destroy(void* self) noexcept {
    delete static_cast<Provider*>(self);
}

}  // namespace

void* createProvider(const rp_device_host* host, MidiBackend& backend) {
    if (!host || host->abi_version != RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION) return nullptr;
    try {
        return new Provider(backend, *host);
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the MIDI provider did not start: %s\n", e.what());
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the MIDI provider did not start\n");
    }
    return nullptr;
}

MidiRpcService& providerService(void* self) {
    return providerOf(self).rpc;
}

}  // namespace rp::midi

extern "C" const rp_provider* rp_midi_provider(void) {
    // No `wake`: a stream has no writer thread to pump. The product's frame loop wakes what has one.
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, "midi", &rp::midi::createWithSystemMidi,
                                       &rp::midi::restore, &rp::midi::rpcService, &rp::midi::destroy, nullptr};
    return &kProvider;
}
````

Create `packages/midi/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The midi package (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md sections 4.1, 4.2 and 4.5): the backend interface and the
# one copy of the port rules, RtMidi as the real backend (RtMidiBackend.cpp, the file that includes RtMidi.h), the
# host's MIDI stream over the interface, the in-process fake a test injects, and the facet as a provider with an rpc.
# Added by retroplug_package(midi) (cmake/packages.cmake).
#
# `retroplug-midi` is NOT a manifest `native` item: cmake/packages.cmake links every non-provider target of a listed
# package into every product that lists it, which would put RtMidi into the host, the render-host test, the Node addon,
# retroplug-ui-test and every test binary that names the desktop list. It is an unlisted library target, as
# retroplug-launchpad-harness is, linked BY NAME by the products that use it (retroplug-sdl) and by this package's
# facet, so a product that lists midi without naming it in PROVIDERS links no RtMidi. The test binary below links it
# directly.
#
# The fake is test support, not part of the library: it sits under native/test-support, an include root only the test
# binaries and the headless host add (FakeMidiBackend.hpp), so a product cannot compile it.
#
# Every target here is the desktop's (the facet opens ports, runs threads and answers an RPC), so a device build defines
# none of them: the manifest names no `device` item, and the early return keeps a device configure from building RtMidi.
if(RP_DEVICE_BUILD)
    return()
endif()

# Threads: RtMidi's callback threads are its own, but the stream's epoch handshake and the test's swap case are ours.
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

# --- retroplug-midi: the interface, the RtMidi backend, the port rules and the stream
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-midi
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/midi/RtMidiBackend.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-midi PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-midi
    PRIVATE rtmidi              # deps/rtmidi, behind RtMidiBackend.cpp alone (root scope, cmake/rtmidi.cmake)
            Threads::Threads)

# --- retroplug-midi-facet: MidiRpcService as a provider with an rpc (the manifest's `native` entry)
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-midi-facet
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/midi/facet/MidiProvider.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-midi-facet PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-midi-facet
    PUBLIC  retroplug-midi
            retroplug-node-sdk)  # graph/rp_provider.h, and rfl's byte string in the RPC's DTOs

# --- retroplug-midi-test-support: the fake's include root, for the binaries that script a MIDI system.
# An interface target, so the header is reachable by a test binary and by the headless host (both link this) and by no
# product: nothing in the library above puts test-support on a product's include path.
add_library(retroplug-midi-test-support INTERFACE)
target_include_directories(retroplug-midi-test-support INTERFACE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test-support)

# --- the package's tests (cmake/test-binary.cmake), built by name. Every source resolves against this directory.

# The port rules and the stream are pure logic over a backend the test scripts, so neither case opens a MIDI system:
# retroplug-midi-test links the fake's header and nothing of RtMidi's at runtime, though the library carries it. Build
# this target in build-tsan/ too: the output-swap, the close and the delivery-thread cases are what ThreadSanitizer is
# for.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-midi-test
    SOURCES  test/MidiPortSelect.test.cpp
             test/MidiStream.test.cpp
    LIBS     retroplug-midi               # the interface and the stream
             retroplug-midi-test-support)  # midi/FakeMidiBackend.hpp
````
