- [ ] **Step 8: `MidiStream.hpp`, and the package green**

`MidiStream.hpp` is the surface the design's 4.2 sketches: `Message { seq, bytes }`, `kCapacity = 256`,
`open`/`close`/`isOpen`, `setInputs(names, all, Apply mode = Diff)` and `setOutputs(names, mode = Diff)`,
`setReserved` / `reservedInput` / `reservedOutput`, `setHardwareInputsSuspended` / `hardwareInputsSuspended`,
`listInputs` / `listOutputs` / `supportsVirtual`, `openedInputs` / `openedOutputs`, `poll`, `send`, `droppedCount`,
and the `LogSink` the harnesses' lines go through; `enum class Apply { Diff, Reopen }` sits beside the class, and the
header says both what a mode means and that `send` has one caller.

Create `packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The host's one MIDI stream (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 4.2): the port policy over a MidiBackend,
// so the SDL app's audio loop and the CLI's facet open ports through the same code and a test injects a fake. A change
// of selection publishes a new output set and opens or closes inputs, and neither stops audio.
//
// Threading. Inputs deliver on the backend's own callback threads - the virtual input plus one per connected hardware
// port - so the receive ring has MANY producers and one consumer (the audio thread, which drains it via poll() at block
// start, never allocating). The producers serialize on pushMutex_, which makes the ring single-producer from the
// consumer's side; poll() never takes the lock, so the audio thread stays lock-free.
//
// Outputs are the hazard, because send() calls a port the control thread may be replacing: the open outputs are an
// immutable set reached through one atomic pointer, a change publishes a new one, waits out the send in flight, and
// only then frees the old one (section 4.3). The wait is an epoch handshake: send() bumps a counter to an odd value on
// entry and an even one on exit, and the swapping thread reads it after publishing and, when it read an odd value,
// waits until the counter has CHANGED - so it waits out the one send in flight, never the stream of sends that follows.
// send() is the AUDIO THREAD's alone: that is what makes the parity a valid "a send is in flight" mark, and a second
// concurrent caller would break it (its entry would make the counter even while the first is still inside a port), so
// the entry is asserted. A block runs at most one send per pending message, so the wait is at most about one block -
// none when audio is not running, since the counter is even then.
//
// Every operation that frees a port first publishes what replaces it and then waits, so close() is safe beside a send
// too: send() reaches the virtual output through the same published set (its pointer travels in it), and close() frees
// it only after that wait, so no send is inside it. The virtual port's LIFETIME is the stream's open(), not the set's:
// a selection change publishes a new set naming the same virtual port without reopening it, so a DAW or an aconnect
// user connected to "RetroPlug Out" keeps that connection across a Settings > MIDI change. The hardware ports are the
// CONTROL thread's (hwOut_), and a published set only names them: a port leaving the selection is unpublished, waited
// out, and only then closed, which is also what lets a name be reopened at all where a port is exclusive (Windows).
//
// Logging: every line the harnesses grep goes through one sink, by default the "[retroplug-sdl] " voice to stderr that
// the app has always written (the CLI prints it too), so a test asserts the very bytes that reach the console.

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "midi/MidiBackend.hpp"

namespace rp::midi {

/** How a selection change treats the ports it names. Diff re-opens only what the change moved, which is what a project
 *  load does: a port that stays selected keeps its connection (a clock arriving on it loses nothing, and on Windows,
 *  where a MIDI port is exclusive, it is not lost to a second open). Reopen closes and opens every port the selection
 *  names, which is the user's one remedy for an unplugged device (there is no hotplug watch): Settings > MIDI's picker
 *  asks for it, and so does the Rescan row beside it. */
enum class Apply { Diff, Reopen };

class MidiStream {
public:
    struct Message {
        std::uint64_t             seq = 0;  // monotonic arrival order; a frame offset is derived later
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
    };

    /** The receive ring's size: the most messages one poll() returns. Public so the consumer's scratch can be reserved
     *  to it, and poll() then never grows a vector on the audio thread. */
    static constexpr std::size_t kCapacity = 256;

    explicit MidiStream(MidiBackend& backend);
    ~MidiStream();
    MidiStream(const MidiStream&)            = delete;
    MidiStream& operator=(const MidiStream&) = delete;

    /** The line sink: what would be written to stderr, one line at a time, prefix included. A test installs one to hold
     *  the bytes a harness greps; the default writes them to stderr. */
    using LogSink = std::function<void(const std::string&)>;
    void setLogSink(LogSink sink) { sink_ = std::move(sink); }

    /** Open the virtual "<clientName> In" / "<clientName> Out" ports where the backend supports them, then apply the
     * current selection. The client name is the backend's (MidiBackend::clientName): one owner, so the ports opened and
     * the ports published cannot be named differently. False when the backend refuses (no MIDI system): the host then
     * runs without MIDI. */
    bool open();
    /** Free every port and empty the ring. Safe beside a send: the set is unpublished and waited out, then the virtual
     *  output, whose sends the same handshake covers. */
    void close();
    bool isOpen() const { return open_; }

    /** The input selection: EXACT names (TypeScript matched them, design 6.3). `all` opens every hardware input and
     * `names` is then ignored; an empty list with `all` false is None, the default. Applied at once, by `mode`: a name
     * that is not present is skipped and re-applied by the next call. */
    void setInputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names, bool all, Apply mode = Apply::Diff);
    /** The outputs to mirror send() to; empty is the virtual port only, the default. Applied by `mode`, as setInputs
     *  is. */
    void setOutputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names, Apply mode = Apply::Diff);

    /** Keep a port pair OUT of this stream because another owner holds it (the control surface's link). Empty releases.
     *  The input matters everywhere - a pad NoteOn here is a second, unquantised row launch - and so does the output:
     *  notes meant for a synth would land on the surface and light its pads at random. On Windows both are also
     *  exclusive, so a port this stream holds could not be claimed at all. Neither call stops audio. */
    void               setReserved(const std::string& input, const std::string& output);
    const std::string& reservedInput() const { return reservedIn_; }
    const std::string& reservedOutput() const { return reservedOut_; }

    /** Close every hardware INPUT for the duration of a control-surface SCAN, without disturbing the user's selection
     *  (resuming re-applies it). Not the same lever as setReserved, which names ONE pair a surface holds for as long as
     *  it is connected: a scan needs every input, briefly. A product reaches this only where scanSuspendsInputs() says
     *  the edge is real, which is Windows alone. Neither call stops audio. */
    void setHardwareInputsSuspended(bool suspended);
    bool hardwareInputsSuspended() const { return inputsSuspended_; }

    /** The pickers' lists: the hardware ports only (our own virtual ports, ALSA's "Through" and anything the test-only
     *  allow list hides are not ports a user may pick). A port a control surface holds IS listed: the reservation only
     *  governs what this stream opens, and hiding it would make the list move whenever a Launchpad connects. */
    std::vector<std::string> listInputs() const;
    std::vector<std::string> listOutputs() const;
    bool                     supportsVirtual() const { return backend_->supportsVirtual(); }

    /** What actually OPENED, which is not the same as what was selected: a name the machine does not list, a port a
     *  control surface holds and one that refused to open are all missing here. The UI's "(missing)" entries and its
     *  Rescan row read this rather than inferring it from a listing taken at another moment. */
    const std::vector<std::string>& openedInputs() const { return openInputs_; }
    const std::vector<std::string>& openedOutputs() const { return openOutputs_; }

    /** Drain queued input into `out` (the audio thread, each block; clears `out` first). Lock-free with respect to the
     *  backend's callback threads. Reserved to kCapacity up front, this never allocates. */
    void poll(std::vector<Message>& out);
    /** Send one short message out (the audio thread each block - MI.OUT etc.): the virtual output and every selected
     *  hardware output. No-op when there is no output. */
    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n);
    /** Messages dropped because the ring was full since startup - always 0 in a healthy run. Non-zero means the audio
     *  thread stopped draining, and any transport clock in what was lost is simply gone, which downstream reads as a
     *  tempo that is too slow. */
    std::uint64_t droppedCount() const { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

    /** Test-only: push a message into the input ring as if a port had received it, for a headless self-test that has no
     *  MIDI hardware. Not used in normal operation. */
    void injectForTest(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) { pushRing(data, len); }

private:
    /** What send() reaches, immutable once published: the hardware outputs this set NAMES, and the virtual output
     *  (owned by open(), carried here only so a send reads ONE pointer and close() can wait sends out before freeing
     *  it). It owns no port: hwOut_ is the hardware ports' owner, so a port can be unpublished, waited out and closed
     *  before the same name is opened again. One control-thread allocation per change, nothing on the audio path. */
    struct OutputSet {
        std::vector<MidiPort*> ports;
        MidiPort*              virtualPort = nullptr;
    };

    void applyInputs(Apply mode);
    void applyOutputs(Apply mode);
    void publishOutputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names);  // builds the set from hwOut_ and retires the last
    void waitForSends();          // spins out the send in flight, and only that one
    void retire(OutputSet* old);  // waits out a send in flight, then frees the set (never a port: hwOut_'s)
    void pushRing(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t len);
    void emit(const std::string& line);  // one log line, prefix included, through sink_ or stderr

    MidiBackend* backend_;  // non-const on purpose: a listing probes the system, and listInputs() is const
    std::string  clientName_ = "RetroPlug";  // copied from the backend at open(): what the filters judge a port by
    LogSink      sink_;                      // empty: stderr
    bool         open_       = false;
    // RETROPLUG_MIDI_LOG: dump in + out bytes to stderr. Set by open() on the control thread and read by the ports'
    // callback threads, so it is atomic rather than a plain bool a thread may read torn or hoisted.
    std::atomic<bool> log_{false};

    std::vector<std::string> selectedIn_;   // exact names; ignored when allInputs_
    bool                     allInputs_ = false;
    std::vector<std::string> selectedOut_;
    std::string              reservedIn_;   // "" = nothing claimed by a control surface
    std::string              reservedOut_;  // ditto, the pair's output
    bool                     inputsSuspended_ = false;  // a scan is holding the inputs

    // What the open ports hold (the control thread's record): the getters publish it, and an apply the control surface
    // or a scan triggers (which is diffed) reads it. A selection setter reapplies regardless.
    std::vector<std::string> openInputs_;
    std::vector<std::string> openOutputs_;

    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> virtualIn_;
    std::unique_ptr<MidiPort> virtualOut_;
    // The hardware ports, name and owner together, the CONTROL thread's alone: it opens them, and it closes one only
    // after the published set has stopped naming it and the send in flight has been waited out.
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::unique_ptr<MidiPort>>> hwIn_;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::unique_ptr<MidiPort>>> hwOut_;
    std::atomic<OutputSet*>                                       outputs_{nullptr};  // published for send()
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t>              epoch_{0};          // odd while a send is in flight

    // Fixed-capacity ring, many producers (serialized by pushMutex_) and one consumer. A producer (a callback thread)
    // allocs into a slot's vector; the consumer (audio thread) moves it out. Overflow drops the incoming message (a
    // drained-every-block consumer never realistically fills 256; MIDI loss under an extreme flood is acceptable).
    std::array<Message, kCapacity> ring_;
    std::atomic<std::size_t>       head_{0};  // consumer index (audio thread)
    std::atomic<std::size_t>       tail_{0};  // producer index (written under pushMutex_)
    std::uint64_t                  seq_ = 0;  // monotonic arrival counter (guarded by pushMutex_)
    // Serializes the producers. Without it two ports delivering at once raced tail_, seq_ and the slot vector - heap
    // corruption, not just a lost message. Producer-side only: never taken by poll().
    std::mutex                     pushMutex_;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>     dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace rp::midi
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The RED: the output swap against a stream that does not wait**

The hazard the epoch handshake exists for is a `send` reading an output set the control thread is freeing. The RED is
the shipped code with the wait neutered - `waitForSends()` returning at once, which is what a `setOutputs` that frees
the old port immediately does - and the fake's own counters say what it costs: `sendsAfterClose()` counts the sends
that reached a port after its close, and a use-after-free shows as a SIGSEGV or as a ThreadSanitizer report. The patch
below is that mutation; it is reversed in the next step.

````patch
diff --git a/packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp b/packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp
--- a/packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp
+++ b/packages/midi/native/src/midi/MidiStream.cpp
@@ -237,7 +237,8 @@
     // afterwards has read the newly published set, so it is no reason to wait; waiting "while odd" would instead chase
     // every send that follows, which under back-to-back sends is unbounded.
     const std::uint32_t seen = epoch_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
-    if ((seen & 1u) == 0) return;
+    (void)seen;
+    return;  // RED: the wait is neutered (the old code freed the set at once)
     // A few yields first - a send is usually short - then short sleeps: a WinMM bulk SysEx blocks about 170 ms inside
     // send(), and 170 ms of a spinning UI thread is a visible stall, where a sleeping one is not.
     for (int spin = 0; epoch_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst) == seen; ++spin) {
````

- [ ] **Step 11: The Launchpad pack onto the backend**

The pack's own seam goes: `MidiPort.hpp` (its `IMidiPort` / `MidiPortOpener`), `RtMidiPort.{hpp,cpp}` (the pack's only
RtMidi translation unit, with its own `midiSystemUsable` and `rtMidiPortOpener`) and `MidiPortFilter.hpp` (the second
copy of the allow list and of `isHardwareMidiPort`) are deleted, and `ControllerLink` and `MidiPortPool` take a
`MidiBackend&` instead of an opener. The provider builds its own RtMidi instance under the client name `RetroPlug
Launchpad` (so the on-the-wire names and "a second instance's link ports are not devices" are unchanged) and its
lister goes through the package's filter; `LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPorts` filters the lister's answer again for a host
whose lister is its own. `FakePorts.hpp` shrinks to the device model over `FakeMidiBackend`, and the two test files
are re-pointed at it.

- [ ] **Step 14: The boundary check learns a dependency's own library targets, and its two fixtures**

`check-boundaries.mjs` attributes a native use to a dependency's targets read from the manifest; `retroplug-midi` is
deliberately not a manifest item, so the check gains `libraryTargets(dir)` - every `retroplug_package_library(name`
and `add_library(name` under a package, comments stripped - and those names join the manifest's targets when a native
use is attributed. It is generic: no package is named. Before the change the standing warning was `launchpad: declares
@retroplug/midi, which no file of its imports and no native target of it names` (`1 warning(s)`); after it, the tree
is back to 0. Two fixtures hold both halves: `native-library-use` (beta's unlisted `beta-lib` is linked and credited,
gamma's `gamma-lib` is linked by nothing and still warns) and `native-target-prefix` (a name with `-` in it is one
name, so `gamma-lib-alpha` does not "name" `gamma-lib`).

````diff
diff --git a/packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs b/packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs
index d86964732..ca422016a 100644
--- a/packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs
+++ b/packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs
@@ -220,6 +220,37 @@ function packageOf(specifier) {
   return name.startsWith("@retroplug/") ? name.slice("@retroplug/".length) : null;
 }
 
+/** The library targets a package's own CMakeLists.txt defines - `retroplug_package_library(name ...)` (packages in this
+ *  repository) and `add_library(name ...)` - as names. A package's manifest names the targets a PRODUCT links, and two
+ *  libraries are deliberately not manifest items (`retroplug-midi`, `retroplug-audio`: listing one would link RtMidi or
+ *  PortAudio into every product), so a package that links one by name is a use only this reading of its CMakeLists can
+ *  see. Textual, comments stripped, like the search this feeds; whether the link itself is legal is the configure
+ *  check's, which reads the real target properties. */
+function libraryTargets(dir) {
+  const out = new Set();
+  for (const file of walk(dir, (name) => name === "CMakeLists.txt")) {
+    const text = readFileSync(file, "utf8").replace(/#[^\n]*/g, "");
+    for (const match of text.matchAll(/(?:retroplug_package_library|add_library)\(\s*([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/g)) {
+      out.add(match[1]);
+    }
+  }
+  return [...out];
+}
+
+/** The characters a CMake target name is made of: a `-` is PART of a name, not a separator, so `retroplug-audio-sdl`
+ *  does not name `retroplug-audio` and a backend's own declaration cannot credit the dependency it is named after. */
+const TARGET_NAME_CHAR = "A-Za-z0-9_.+-";
+
+/** Whether `text` (one package's CMakeLists, comments stripped and its own declarations removed) names `target` as a
+ *  WHOLE token. The declarations are removed first: `add_library(retroplug-audio-sdl ...)` is the package naming its
+ *  own target, and reading that as a use of the `retroplug-audio` it starts with is the hole this closes. */
+function namesTarget(text, target) {
+  const declarations = /(?:retroplug_package_library|add_library)\(\s*[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+/g;
+  const withoutOwn = text.replace(declarations, "add_library(");
+  const escaped = target.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
+  return new RegExp(`(^|[^${TARGET_NAME_CHAR}])${escaped}([^${TARGET_NAME_CHAR}]|$)`, "m").test(withoutOwn);
+}
+
 /** The workspace's packages, by name, in name order: the ones with a manifest under packages/. */
 function workspace(root) {
   const base = join(root, PACKAGES);
@@ -248,8 +279,12 @@ function workspace(root) {
         ...Object.entries(manifest.dependencies ?? {}).map(([key, spec]) => ({ key, spec, dev: false })),
         ...Object.entries(manifest.devDependencies ?? {}).map(([key, spec]) => ({ key, spec, dev: true })),
       ],
-      // The CMake targets its manifest names: one way a dependency counts as used.
-      targets: entries.map((entry) => entry.target).filter((target) => typeof target === "string"),
+      // The CMake targets its manifest names, and the libraries its own CMakeLists defines: the ways a dependency counts
+      // as used by another package's native tree.
+      targets: [
+        ...entries.map((entry) => entry.target).filter((target) => typeof target === "string"),
+        ...libraryTargets(join(base, entry.name)),
+      ],
     });
   }
   return new Map([...packages.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)));
@@ -859,7 +894,7 @@ export function checkBoundaries({ root = REPO } = {}) {
     for (const name of [...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies]) {
       const short = packageOf(name);
       const targets = short === null ? [] : (packages.get(short)?.targets ?? []);
-      if (targets.some((target) => new RegExp(`(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${target}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)`, "m").test(text))) {
+      if (targets.some((target) => namesTarget(text, target))) {
         markUsed(pkg, name);
         continue;
       }
diff --git a/packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts b/packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts
index 4901fd5dd..7d0e466da 100644
--- a/packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts
+++ b/packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts
@@ -294,6 +294,34 @@ test("a native target's path is a use and a CMake comment is not, which the warn
   expect(report.warnings).toEqual(["alpha: declares @retroplug/gamma, which no file of its imports and no native target of it names"]);

+test("a dependency's unlisted library target counts as a use, and one nothing links still warns", async () => {
+  // retroplug-midi and retroplug-audio are libraries a package links by name rather than manifest items (listing one
+  // would link RtMidi or PortAudio into every product), so the use has to be read from the dependency's own CMakeLists:
+  // the library it defines, not the targets its manifest lists. Beta is linked that way and gamma is not, and the warning
+  // is the one unused declaration that remains - a base of zero is the sentinel the real tree is held to.
+  const report = await drive("native-library-use");
+  console.log(`# ${(report.warnings as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
+  expect(report.status).toBe(0);
+  expect(report.refused).toEqual([]);
+  expect(report.warnings).toEqual([
+    "alpha: declares @retroplug/gamma, which no file of its imports and no native target of it names",
+  ]);
+});
+
+test("a target whose name merely STARTS with a dependency's is not a use of it", async () => {
+  // A `-` is part of a CMake target name, not a separator: alpha's own `gamma-lib-alpha` names no gamma target, and the
+  // declaration of it is alpha naming itself. Read with `-` as a boundary, the declaration credited alpha's dependency
+  // on gamma and the real tree's audio backends (each `retroplug-audio-<id>`) were never judged - the rule was vacuous
+  // exactly where the packages that need it are. Beta is linked for real, so its use still counts.
+  const report = await drive("native-target-prefix");
+  console.log(`# ${(report.warnings as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
+  expect(report.status).toBe(0);
+  expect(report.refused).toEqual([]);
+  expect(report.warnings).toEqual([
+    "alpha: declares @retroplug/gamma, which no file of its imports and no native target of it names",
+  ]);
+});
+
 test("a shell source importing a cart's module is refused, naming the file and the specifier (rule 9)", async () => {
   const report = await drive("shell-source-forbidden");
````

````cmake
# package's own library, and no "-" makes it a use of gamma's "gamma-lib". beta-lib, on the other hand, is a real link.
# The checking script must tell them apart - reading "gamma-lib-alpha" as gamma would be a use that is not there, and
# the warning for gamma would never fire.
add_library(gamma-lib-alpha STATIC native.cpp)
add_library(gamma-lib-alpha-interface INTERFACE)
target_link_libraries(gamma-lib-alpha PRIVATE beta-lib)
````

already sits in: the scanner gains `--node-exempt`, fed `SHELL_NODE_TYPES`, so the shell's OWN types are exempt from a
package's family guard while every other `rp.midi.*` type is still the package's (and the split is stated: core owns
`rp.midi.route` alone). `test/menu/launchpad.test.ts` and `ui/screens/menu/midiDevices.ts` follow the renamed seam,
and the four harness scripts change only where the stage moved a line: `tools/run-sdl-controller.sh`'s `midi.json`
writes still work through the shim (Task 5 turns them into an autoloaded project), `run-sdl-smoke.sh` and
`run-sdl-pipewire.sh` follow the harness seam, and `run-sanitizer.sh` gains the midi leg (the standing `tsanmidi`
leg).

- [ ] **Step 16: E11 through the real host: `midiOpen("")` opens every hardware input**

`test-native/midi-facet.test.ts` is the live-MIDI contract at its one edge, run through the headless host's facet over
the package's fake (no hardware, no RtMidi): `open("")` opens EVERY hardware input, as the contract says and as
`n8-bridge` with no `--midi-in` expects, and a named input opens that port alone. It writes
`tjs.env.RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` (the filter's test-only list) with the rig's two names, so nothing else can open.

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/midi-facet.test.ts`:

````ts
// The midi package's facet through the real native host: its provider and its RPC facet over a SCRIPTED MIDI system
// (packages/native/src/main.cpp starts it with packages/midi/native/src/midi/FakeMidiBackend.hpp, a machine listing a
// Pro MK3 and an interface's port, and answering every write on each open input). No hardware, no rtmidi, and the same
// facet code the CLI mounts - this is the one door a live-MIDI client has.
//
// What only this file can hold: the live-MIDI contract at its one edge (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md E11).
// `open("")` opens EVERY hardware input, as the contract says and as `n8-bridge` with no `--midi-in` expects; it read
// None for a while. A named input opens that port alone, and the count of replies is how many inputs a stream opened.
//
// Run: pnpm test:native midi-facet
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { createMidiClient, type MidiClient } from "../src/realBackend";

declare const tjs: {
  exePath: string;
  env: Record<string, string>;
  exit(code: number): void;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    options?: {
      env?: Record<string, string>;
      stdout?: "inherit" | "pipe" | "ignore";
      stderr?: "inherit" | "pipe" | "ignore";
    },
  ): {
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
    stdout: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null;
    stderr: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null;
  };
};
declare const __SELF_BUNDLE__: string;
/** This host's opt-in to keep pumping past its bounded spin: the case below awaits a child PROCESS. */
declare const __rp_keepAlive: () => void;

// The test-only port filter, naming the rig's fakes only (RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW,
// packages/midi/native/src/midi/PortFilter.hpp). A case here must not open a real device even if the host process were
// ever given a real backend, and the rig's names are what the filter lets through; every other name the scripted
// machine lists (ALSA's Through, RetroPlug's own virtual ports, a second instance's link) is not hardware and would not
// be opened anyway.
const FAKES = "LPProMK3 MIDI,MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A";
tjs.env.RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW = FAKES;

const PRO = "LPProMK3 MIDI";
const IFACE = "MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A";

/** Drain a child's two pipes concurrently with the wait: reading one then the other deadlocks a noisy child. */
async function drain(
  stream: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null,
): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  const text = new TextDecoder();
  return chunks.map((c) => text.decode(c)).join("");
}

/** A fresh client per case: the facet owns one stream, so a case closes what it opened. */
function client(): MidiClient {
  return createMidiClient();
}

/** What one write hears back: the scripted machine replies once on every input the stream has open, so this is the
 *  number of hardware inputs the selection opened (the virtual port is not one). */
function repliesToAWrite(c: MidiClient): number {
  c.send(Uint8Array.from([0x90, 0x3c, 0x7f]));
  return c.poll().length;
}

test("the facet lists the scripted machine's hardware ports only", () => {
  // The machine also lists RetroPlug's own virtual ports, a second instance's `RetroPlug Launchpad` link ports and
  // ALSA's Midi Through; the one filter drops all three, in the lister and in every open.
  const c = client();
  expect(c.listInputs()).toEqual([PRO, IFACE]);
  expect(c.listOutputs()).toEqual([PRO, IFACE]);
});

test("open('') opens EVERY hardware input: the contract's meaning, and what a bridge with no --midi-in expects", () => {
  const c = client();
  expect(c.open("RetroPlug", "")).toBe(true);
  // One reply per open input: both ports, so both opened. Read as None, this is zero and nothing ever reaches a cart.
  expect(repliesToAWrite(c)).toBe(2);
  c.close();
});

test("a named input opens that port alone", () => {
  const c = client();
  expect(c.open("RetroPlug", PRO)).toBe(true);
  expect(repliesToAWrite(c)).toBe(1);
  c.close();
});

test("a name that is not present opens no input, and the next open picks it up", () => {
  // The Launchpad probe's "(no hardware input)" is exactly this, and it must not fall back to every device.
  const c = client();
  expect(c.open("RetroPlug", "(no hardware input)")).toBe(true);
  expect(repliesToAWrite(c)).toBe(0);
  // ...and the same facet opens what a later call names.
  expect(c.open("RetroPlug", IFACE)).toBe(true);
  expect(repliesToAWrite(c)).toBe(1);
  c.close();
});

// The client name a session ASKS for is the name its virtual ports are published under, which is the contract at
// core/ts/host.ts: a DAW routes to "RetroPlug N8 In", and two sessions (a bridge beside the standalone, two bridges)
// must not share one pair. The stream announces the pair it opened, so this reads the very name the backend recorded -
// from a CHILD process, because that line goes to the child's stderr and a case inside the host cannot read its own.
// Nothing real opens: the child's backend is the same scripted machine, under the allowed fakes.
const NAME_CHILD = "RP_MIDI_NAME_CHILD";
if (tjs.env[NAME_CHILD] === "1") {
  const c = createMidiClient();
  c.open("RetroPlug N8", "");
  c.close();
  tjs.exit(0);
}

test("a session's own client name is the name its virtual ports are published under", async () => {
  __rp_keepAlive(); // the child outlasts the host's bounded spin
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.exePath, __SELF_BUNDLE__], {
    env: { ...tjs.env, [NAME_CHILD]: "1" },
    stdout: "pipe",
    stderr: "pipe",
  });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([drain(child.stdout), drain(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  expect(status.exit_status, `the child process failed:\n${out}\n${err}`).toBe(0);
  // The name the fake recorded: it builds "<clientName> In" / "<clientName> Out", so this is that name, byte for byte.
  expect(err.includes("MIDI: virtual ports 'RetroPlug N8 In' / 'RetroPlug N8 Out' open")).toBe(true);
  // The session's name is its own: it did not publish under the host's default name.
  expect(err.includes("MIDI: virtual ports 'RetroPlug In' / 'RetroPlug Out' open")).toBe(false);
});
````

The RED is the OLD meaning of `""` (None) in the facet, one line of this task's own file: the mutation below is the
prototype's, run before the fix.

````patch
diff --git a/packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp b/packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp
--- a/packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp
+++ b/packages/midi/native/src/midi/facet/MidiRpcService.cpp
@@ -32,7 +32,8 @@
     // hardware input (the contract's meaning; "*" is what an older CLI sent), any other string is the one port it
     // names. midiOpen itself lets every port go first (open() replaces the stream's ports), so a session that calls it
     // again is how it heals a port that was replugged.
-    if (input.empty() || input == kAllInputs) stream_->setInputs({}, true);
+    if (input == kAllInputs) stream_->setInputs({}, true);
+    else if (input.empty()) stream_->setInputs({}, false);  // RED: the old None for ""
     else stream_->setInputs({std::move(input)}, false);
     return stream_->open();
 }
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), a fixed-length string.
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` replaces that string (`Mmm dd yyyy`) with `Nov  4 2026` before hashing, and this
plan's command does the same with `sed` and additionally COUNTS the string first (it must be exactly one, or the
normalisation would be guessing); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
feat(midi): the midi package (MidiBackend, MidiStream, RtMidi and fake backends, the CLI facet as a provider) and the Launchpad onto it

The standalone's MIDI as a package (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 4), lifted out of the shell's
MidiIo / MidiRpcService and out of the Launchpad pack's own copy of an RtMidi port.

The interface (packages/midi/native/src/midi): MidiBackend and MidiPort, one exception type, a backend that owns its
client name (so the ports it opens and publishes cannot differ), supportsVirtual() so a platform with no virtual ports
announces none, and MidiStream over it - the ring the audio thread drains, Apply::Diff on the setters (a pick keeps the
ports an unchanged selection already holds), Apply::Reopen (close, then open: the remedy for a port that was
unplugged), openedInputs() / openedOutputs() reporting what really opened, the virtual output carried in the published
set rather than reopened, and a one-caller assert in send(). RtMidiBackend is the real one, keeping the test-only port
filter a harness pins (RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW, honoured by the lister, the opener and the stream alike), and
FakeMidiBackend is the scripted one the tests drive.

The setters' epoch handshake is the store-buffering shape, so its four operations are seq_cst: under acquire/release
the two store-load pairs may be reordered on AArch64 and the old ports freed under a send, while x86's locked
increment hides it. The wait after a publish is for the ONE send in flight - an odd counter is waited out until it
CHANGES - never "while odd", which chases every send that follows: back-to-back 20 ms sends made a swap wait hundreds
of milliseconds. The five log lines the harnesses grep go through one sink, defaulting to the "[retroplug-sdl] "
voice on stderr, and a case holds them byte for byte.

The facet is MidiRpcService over the stream: the provider rp_midi_provider, which is how a product reaches the Edio of
the host's MIDI without naming a class of it. The CLI and the headless host name it in PROVIDERS (a CLI session opens
one stream under the session's name; "" opens every hardware input again, as the documented contract says), the SDL app
uses MidiStream itself, and the plugin names it not at all. The Launchpad pack drops its RtMidiPort, MidiPortFilter and
MidiPortPool's own port type for ControllerLink and MidiPortPool over MidiStream, with its cases green over the fake.

The shell keeps a shim until the project's own `midi` section lands (section 6): midi.json's single `input` / `output`
maps onto setInputs / setOutputs ("" is None, "*" is every device), so this stage moves no startup order and no harness
line.

Build: retroplug-midi, -facet and -test join the /W4 /WX list, the facet links the node SDK it uses, and
check-boundaries learns the native library targets a dependency's own CMakeLists defines, so an unlisted
retroplug-midi counts as used and the warning base is zero again (with a fixture for both directions).
EOF
````

---

### Task 3: the `audio` packages, `AudioHost` and `AUDIO_BACKENDS`

Design section 5 (5.1 to 5.7) and the design's stage S2. The audio device stops being `main.cpp`'s: `packages/audio`
holds the contract (`AudioBackend` / `AudioStream`, a saved choice by NAME and never a library's numeric id), the `null`
backend, and `AudioHost` - the open/start/stop/reconfigure sequence once, the `null` fallback carrying a status TS shows
as "Muted: <reason>", a lost device and a no-pull watchdog as the same fallback, render-ahead from
`feature/handheld-perf`'s code, per-thread real-time tuning, the stats line, and the log line in today's form (so
PortAudio's is byte-identical and `sdl:pipewire`'s greps hold). `packages/audio-portaudio` and `packages/audio-sdl` are
one backend each, compiled in and chosen at RUNTIME.

The build grows a manifest item kind and a product list: `{ "target", "audioBackend", "id", "device": false }`, and
`AUDIO_BACKENDS portaudio sdl` on a product, with the generated `rp_product_audio_backends.hpp` declaring the factories
in the product's order and a product that lists the package without naming a backend dropping the target (so the CLI,
the headless host, the render-host test, `retroplug-ui-test` and the Node addon link neither PortAudio nor SDL audio).
PortAudio moves to root scope (`cmake/portaudio.cmake`) because a package's target must find it at configure time.

The stage's proof is the `AudioHost` cases over a fake backend (the call order with the OBTAINED rate, the fallback,
a lost device, the watchdog, render-ahead bit-identical across ragged pulls, the single renderer, `describe()`
enumerating only the backend in force) and one engine-graph case the user asked for: a GB core and a NES core built at
48 kHz and re-rated to 44.1 kHz render sample for sample what the same document built at 44.1 kHz renders.

- [ ] **Step 2: The contract, the null device and `AudioHost`**

`audio/AudioBackend.hpp` is the contract: `Driver { id, label }`, `Devices { names, defaultName }`, `Request { driver,
device, sampleRate, blockFrames, channels }` (with `""` = auto / default and `blockFrames 0` = the backend's quantum),
`StreamInfo`, `Pull`, `AudioStream` (`start(error)`, `stop`, `info`, `lost`), `AudioBackend` (`id`, `label`,
`drivers`, `autoDriver`, `devices`, `open` returning a stream that is NOT started, `driverLabel`), the `BackendList`,
`nullAudioBackend()`, and `devicesListableFor(active, requested)` - SDL's one-driver rule as a pure predicate, so a
case can hold it without SDL. The header states the three rules a backend keeps: the factory runs at startup for every
backend a product names, so a constructor must not touch its library; `drivers` and `devices` never disturb a running
stream; `open` returns a stream that is not started. `NullBackend.cpp` is today's sleep-paced pump as a stream on its
own thread, so a machine with no audio still runs the emulator; it always opens and never reports itself lost.
`AudioHost` owns the sequence (stop, release, open, `prepare(info())`, start - the open BEFORE the re-rate, so the
engine is shaped for the rate the device obtained), the fallback, the watchdog (the clock starts at `start()`, stamped
at pull EXIT, bound `max(250 ms, 4 x)` the longer of the render block and the device quantum), render-ahead (the ring,
the counters and the renderer BEFORE `start`), the stats (one thread's accumulator under render-ahead), `describe()`
(the backend IN FORCE only) and `backendDrivers(id)` (a sibling, on request: that call is its library's first use).
`AudioChoice.hpp` maps a driver LABEL to a choice for the interim hooks the app keeps until Task 5.

````cmake
# device, and AudioHost - the open / start / stop / reconfigure sequence, the muted fallback with a status, a lost
# device, the no-pull watchdog, render-ahead and the stats. Added by retroplug_package(audio) (cmake/packages.cmake).
#
# `retroplug-audio` is NOT a manifest `native` item, as `retroplug-midi` is not: listing it would link AudioHost into
# every product that lists the package, and its only product is the SDL standalone, which links it by name. A product
# that names no backend links no audio library at all (cmake/packages.cmake's AUDIO_BACKENDS).
#

    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/audio/AudioHost.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/audio/NullBackend.cpp)
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The audio backend contract (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 5.1): the one interface the SDL
// standalone's audio goes through, so what the device, driver and channel count are called stops being PortAudio's
// vocabulary and a saved choice can carry it by name. PortAudio, SDL2 and the null device fill it; nothing above this
// header names an audio library, so the host - and a test - see names and a pull callback.

#include <cstddef>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace rp::audio {

/** One driver of a backend, by name: "pipewire" / "PipeWire". A backend's own vocabulary, never a library's numeric
 *  id: a saved choice carries this name, and a fork's renumbering must not move it. */
struct Driver {
    std::string id;
    std::string label;
};

/** The devices a driver has, and the name of the one it opens by default. An empty `names` list is a driver that cannot
 *  be enumerated right now (SDL: a driver that is not the one initialised), which the UI shows as "Default". */
struct Devices {
    std::vector<std::string> names;
    std::string              defaultName;
};

/** Whether a backend that runs ONE driver at a time may list `requested`'s devices while `active` is the driver
 *  initialised now: only the driver in force (or a request for "whatever is in force"), because listing another would
 *  mean quitting the one in force - and SDL's quit closes every device the process has open. That is SDL's rule (design
 *  5.1, R8): every other driver answers an empty list, which the row shows as "Default", and picking one opens it after
 *  the host has stopped the old stream. Pure, and in the contract header, so the rule is held without SDL. */
inline bool devicesListableFor(const std::string& active, const std::string& requested) {
    return requested.empty() ? !active.empty() : requested == active;
}

/** What to open. `driver` and `device` empty mean the backend's auto driver and that driver's default device. A
 *  `blockFrames` of 0 asks for the backend's own quantum (a fixed-quantum server's, or render-ahead's). */
struct Request {
    std::string driver;
    std::string device;
    int         sampleRate  = 48000;
    int         blockFrames = 512;
    int         channels    = 2;
};

/** What a stream came up as. The rate may differ from the request (a device that adopts its own), and is what the
 *  engine is re-rated to. */
struct StreamInfo {
    std::string driver;
    std::string device;
    int         sampleRate  = 0;
    int         blockFrames = 0;
    int         channels    = 0;
};

/** The device's pull: fill `interleaved` with `frames` frames of `channels` samples (the stream's channel count, which
 *  is what the request asked for). `underflow` is the device's own report that it ran dry before this call - SDL has
 *  no such flag and never sets it. Called on the backend's real-time thread, so it takes no lock and allocates
 *  nothing. */
using Pull = void (*)(void* ctx, float* interleaved, int frames, bool underflow);

/** One open device. `open` returns it not started: start/stop is the host's, so it can shape the engine between the
 *  two. */
class AudioStream {
public:
    virtual ~AudioStream() = default;
    /** True when the device started. A backend that has no start (the null device's thread is already running) says
     *  true. A refusal puts its own words in `error`, which is what the status row shows: a stream that opens and will
     *  not start is an open failure to the host, not a live-but-silent device. */
    virtual bool start(std::string& error) = 0;
    /** Returns once no pull can run. */
    virtual void stop() = 0;
    virtual StreamInfo info() const = 0;
    /** The device went away, or the stream stopped by itself: the host's cue to fall back (a finished PortAudio stream,
     *  an SDL device whose status is no longer PLAYING). */
    virtual bool lost() const = 0;
};

/** An audio system: the drivers and devices it names, and the streams it opens. Every open that fails reports through
 *  `error` and a null stream, never a throw: a failure is a status the Settings row shows, not an exception the host
 *  has to catch around a device.
 *
 *  Three rules a backend keeps, because the host calls it at these moments and no other:
 *
 *  - the FACTORY runs at startup for every backend a product names (a product's backends are built before anything is
 *    open), so a constructor must not touch its library: `drivers`, `devices` and `autoDriver` are the first use, and
 *    the host calls them only for the backend in force (or on an explicit "More drivers..." step);
 *  - `drivers` / `devices` must never disturb a running stream. SDL is the case in point: switching its driver means
 *    SDL_AudioQuit, which closes every open device, so a listing answers for the driver in force only
 *    (devicesListableFor above);
 *  - `open` returns a stream that is NOT started. The host shapes the engine between open and start, so a backend that
 *    started inside `open` would pull into an engine that is not ready for it. */
class AudioBackend {
public:
    virtual ~AudioBackend() = default;
    /** "portaudio", "sdl", "null": what a saved choice and --audio-backend name it by. */
    virtual std::string id() const = 0;
    /** "PortAudio", "SDL", "Null": what the log line and the Driver row call it. */
    virtual std::string label() const = 0;
    virtual std::vector<Driver> drivers() = 0;
    /** The driver an empty Request::driver resolves to, or "" when none can open (no server, no device). A backend that
     *  enumerates lazily initialises its library here; that is the first use a product makes of it. */
    virtual std::string autoDriver() = 0;
    virtual Devices     devices(const std::string& driver) = 0;
    /** Open a stream, not started. Null (with `error` set) when the device will not open. */
    virtual std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx,
                                              std::string& error) = 0;
    /** The driver's LABEL, for the log line and the Driver row ("PipeWire", not "pipewire"); the id itself when the
     *  backend does not know the driver. */
    virtual std::string driverLabel(const std::string& driver) {
        for (const Driver& d : drivers())
            if (d.id == driver) return d.label;
        return driver;
    }
};

/** The null device: always opens, and advances the engine at the requested block's real-time cadence on a thread of
 *  its own, so a machine with no usable audio still runs the emulator (and the smoke's transport and multi-out checks).
 *  What the host falls back to; a stream of this backend never reports itself lost. */
std::unique_ptr<AudioBackend> nullAudioBackend();

/** Every backend a product names, in its AUDIO_BACKENDS order (rp_product_audio_backends, the generated header). The
 *  host appends the null one itself. */
using BackendList = std::vector<std::unique_ptr<AudioBackend>>;

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

Create `packages/audio/native/src/audio/AudioHost.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The host's audio: the whole open / start / stop / reconfigure sequence, the fallback to the null device with a status
// the UI shows, a lost device as the same fallback, render-ahead and the stats (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md
// section 5.2). It never names the Engine: the product's render loop is behind AudioClient, which is where today's
// renderAudioBlock lives.
//
// The order a reconfigure runs in is stop, release, open, [render-ahead's ring and renderer], prepare(info()), start.
// Opening before prepare is what lets prepare see the rate the device actually runs at: a device may adopt another
// one, and an engine re-rated with the REQUESTED rate would render at the wrong pitch. The ring and its counters are
// set up BEFORE start too: a device's callback can run the moment start() returns, and a pull that found the previous
// run's counters would read a ring nothing had sized yet.
//
// One sender, one renderer: pull() is the audio path and runs on a backend's real-time thread; the render-ahead
// renderer is the same client's render on a thread of its own, and never at the same time as pull's (the ring decides
// which of the two renders a block). The stats are the renderer's alone under render-ahead (the pull only counts
// underruns into an atomic), so the accumulator is one thread's. apply/stop/poll are the control thread's.
//
// Real-time treatment is here too, because only the host sees both threads: on Linux the device callback runs
// SCHED_FIFO 85 above the renderer's 80 under render-ahead (80 otherwise), both pinned to the audio core, applied per
// THREAD (a callback thread is new with each stream, so a per-process latch left a re-opened stream untuned). Best
// effort: without RT permission the default scheduling stands, as it always has.

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "audio/AudioBackend.hpp"

namespace rp::audio {

/** The product's side of the host: the engine, behind an interface AudioHost never names. */
class AudioClient {
public:
    virtual ~AudioClient() = default;
    /** Re-rate, reshape and size the render for the obtained stream. Called between release and start, so the engine is
     *  quiescent, and it HANDS THE ENGINE BACK to the audio thread before it returns: the host's next call is start(),
     *  and the first pull must find an engine it may render. */
    virtual void prepare(double sampleRate, int maxBlockFrames, int channels) = 0;
    /** Render one interleaved block: today's renderAudioBlock, with the buffer sized by the caller. */
    virtual void render(float* interleaved, int frames) = 0;
    /** Take the engine back from the audio thread (the invoker drain), so prepare can re-rate it. */
    virtual void release() = 0;
};

/** One run's audio choice: the `audio` config section's fields plus render-ahead, which the section does not carry (it
 *  is a flag). */
struct AudioConfig {
    std::string backend         = "auto";  // "auto" takes the first backend whose auto driver opens
    std::string driver          = "";
    std::string device          = "";
    int         sampleRate      = 48000;
    int         blockSize       = 512;
    int         channels        = 2;
    int         renderAheadFrames = 0;  // 0 = render inside the pull (the default)
};

/** One run's request with its flags applied. `--audio-backend` / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND replaces only the
 *  BACKEND: the saved driver and device are that backend's own vocabulary, so they survive when the saved section names
 *  the backend the flag pins, and are cleared only when it names another one (whose names would mean nothing to it). A
 *  block-size override wins over the saved block, because a launcher's quantum has to reach the device (E12). */
AudioConfig applyRunOverrides(AudioConfig config, const std::string& backendOverride, int blockSizeOverride);

/** What is running, for the Settings row: empty `error` is a real device; otherwise it is the bare reason the null
 *  fallback is playing, and the row renders it as "Muted: <reason>". */
struct AudioStatus {
    std::string backend;
    std::string driver;
    std::string device;
    int         sampleRate  = 0;
    int         blockFrames = 0;
    int         channels    = 0;
    std::string error;
};

/** One driver of one backend, as the Settings > Audio rows read them. */
struct AudioDriverDescription {
    std::string id;
    std::string label;
    Devices     devices;
};

/** One backend, its drivers and the driver "auto" resolves to right now ("" when none can open). */
struct AudioBackendDescription {
    std::string                    id;
    std::string                    label;
    std::string                    autoDriver;
    std::vector<AudioDriverDescription> drivers;
};

/** What a RUN's flags pin, regardless of what the section saved (--audio-backend, --block-size): the rows name it so a
 *  user can see why the saved choice is not the one running. Empty/0 when no flag is set. */
struct RunOverrides {
    std::string backend;
    int         blockSize = 0;
};

/** Everything the Settings > Audio rows show: each backend with its drivers and devices, the status, and the run's
 *  overrides. */
struct AudioDescription {
    std::vector<AudioBackendDescription> backends;
    AudioStatus                          status;
    RunOverrides                         overrides;
};

class AudioHost {
public:
    /** `preference` is the product's AUDIO_BACKENDS order (rp_product_audio_backends()); the null device is appended
     *  here, last, so a product that names no backend still runs. */
    AudioHost(BackendList preference, AudioClient& client);
    ~AudioHost();
    AudioHost(const AudioHost&)            = delete;
    AudioHost& operator=(const AudioHost&) = delete;

    /** The whole sequence, once: stop, release, open, prepare(info()), start. `backend` empty or "auto" takes the first
     *  backend whose auto driver opens. A failed open falls back to the null device with the reason in the status
     *  (`muted`); true when a real device is running. */
    bool apply(const AudioConfig& config);

    /** The teardown path: stop the device and take the engine back. */
    void stop();

    /** The UI frame: a lost stream (or one the watchdog has not seen a pull from) falls back to the null device, and
     *  the status moves. True when the status changed. */
    bool poll();

    AudioStatus      status() const;
    /** Each backend's id and label, and what the backend IN FORCE has: its drivers with their devices. Enumerating a
     *  backend initialises its library, so no other one is touched here (the Zoom L6 rule, and why a null run's startup
     *  opens nothing). */
    AudioDescription describe() const;
    /** One backend's drivers and devices, on demand: the Driver row that offers another backend asks for it here, and
     *  that call is a real use of its library. */
    std::vector<AudioDriverDescription> backendDrivers(const std::string& backendId) const;
    /** True when a real device (not the null fallback) is open and started. */
    bool live() const;

    /** The audio path: one device callback's worth. Public for the null device and the fake's own thread, which call it
     *  through the Pull it was handed; a product never calls it. */
    void pull(float* interleaved, int frames, bool underflow);
    static void pullTrampoline(void* ctx, float* interleaved, int frames, bool underflow);

    /** The watchdog's bound: a started device that has run no pull for this long is treated as lost. `apply` sets it
     *  to max(250 ms, 4 x the duration of the LONGER of the block the run renders in and the device's own quantum: under
     *  render-ahead the stream is opened with a block of 0 and pulls in its own quantum, which can outlast the render
     *  block. A test may shorten it. */
    void setWatchdogBound(std::chrono::milliseconds bound) { watchdogBound_ = bound; }
    std::chrono::milliseconds watchdogBound() const { return watchdogBound_; }

    /** Render-ahead's underrun count since the stream started: the pull pads a short ring with silence and counts it
     *  once the ring has primed. A render-ahead run that never underruns is what "the ring is deep enough" means. */
    std::uint64_t underruns() const { return underruns_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

    /** The log sink: what would be written to stderr, one line at a time, prefix included. A test installs one to hold
     *  the bytes the harnesses grep and the stats line; the default writes them to stderr. */
    using LogSink = std::function<void(const std::string&)>;
    void setLogSink(LogSink sink) { sink_ = std::move(sink); }

    /** The stats' reporting interval (RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_STATS), and its switch. For a test. */
    void setStatsForTest(bool enabled, std::chrono::milliseconds interval);

private:
    struct Resolved {
        AudioBackend* backend = nullptr;
        std::string   driver;   // the resolved driver's id
        std::string   device;   // the resolved device's name
    };

    /** Resolve the config's backend and driver, then open. Sets `error` and leaves `stream` null on failure. */
    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> openFor(const AudioConfig& config, Resolved& resolved, StreamInfo& info,
                                         std::string& error);
    /** Open AND start: the ring and the renderer before the device can pull, `prepare` with what the device obtained,
     *  `start`, and the watchdog's clock. False on either failure, with nothing left open or started and `error` set:
     *  a stream that opens and will not start is an open failure, not a live-but-silent host. */
    bool openAndStart(const AudioConfig& config, Resolved& resolved, StreamInfo& info, std::string& error);
    /** The null device's open-and-start, with `reason` as the status: every failure lands here, because a machine with
     *  no usable device still runs the emulator (the sleep-paced pump). False when even that failed. */
    bool fallbackToNull(const std::string& reason);
    void setWatchdogFor(int blockFrames);  // the bound a block's duration allows
    void closeCurrent();                   // stops and frees the stream, and ends the renderer if one runs
    void startRenderer(int blockFrames, int channels);
    void stopRenderer();
    void renderLoop(int blockFrames, int channels);
    void reportStats(double renderSec, double renderCpuSec, double blockSec, int blockFrames);
    void logLine(const std::string& text) const;

    BackendList                                       preference_;  // the product's, null last
    AudioClient*                                      client_;
    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream>                      stream_;
    AudioBackend*                                     backend_ = nullptr;  // the open stream's
    AudioConfig                                       config_;
    StreamInfo                                        info_;
    std::string                                       error_;
    bool                                              started_ = false;
    // The thread that built the host (the control thread): a pull on it is a test's hand-cranked one, not a device's.
    std::thread::id                                   controlThread_;

    // Render-ahead: a render thread keeps interleaved frames in a ring and the pull only copies.
    bool                       renderAhead_ = false;
    std::vector<float>         ring_;
    std::size_t                ringFrames_ = 0;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> ringWritten_{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> ringRead_{0};
    std::atomic<bool>          ringPrimed_{false};
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> underruns_{0};
    std::vector<float>         renderScratch_;
    std::thread                renderThread_;
    std::atomic<bool>          renderRun_{false};
    int                        blockFrames_ = 0;  // the block the engine was shaped for (the watchdog's, the stats')

    // The watchdog's witness: when a pull last finished, when the stream started, and the bound. A stream that starts
    // and never pulls is caught by the start stamp; the bound scales with the block, so one long block (a 186 ms
    // quantum, a WinMM SysEx inside it) is not a stall.
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>    pulls_{0};
    std::atomic<std::int64_t>     lastPullMs_{0};
    std::chrono::milliseconds     watchdogBound_{250};

    // The stats (RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_STATS): load, worst block, real frames/s and underruns, every few seconds. One
    // thread's accumulator: under render-ahead the renderer alone reports, and the pull only counts its underruns.
    bool                                                     statsEnabled_ = false;
    std::chrono::milliseconds                                statsInterval_{5000};
    double                                                   statsBusySec_ = 0, statsCpuSec_ = 0, statsWallSec_ = 0;
    double                                                   statsWorst_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t                                            statsBlocks_ = 0, statsUnderflows_ = 0, statsFrames_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t                                            statsTotalUnderflows_ = 0;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>                               pendingUnderflows_{0};
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point                    statsSince_ = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    LogSink                                            sink_;  // empty: stderr
};

}  // namespace rp::audio
````
