````cpp
#include "audio/AudioHost.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <exception>
#include <utility>

#if defined(__linux__)
#include <ctime>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <sched.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif

namespace rp::audio {
namespace {

// Today's log voice, kept byte for byte: the harnesses grep "[retroplug-sdl] audio: PortAudio [h] 'd' N Hz, B frames,
// C ch" (tools/run-sdl-pipewire.sh's sed and grep), and the CLI prints the same prefix through the midi package.
constexpr const char* kLogPrefix = "[retroplug-sdl] ";

std::int64_t nowMs() {
    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
        .count();
}

double threadCpuSeconds() {
#if defined(__linux__)
    timespec ts{};
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, &ts);
    return static_cast<double>(ts.tv_sec) + static_cast<double>(ts.tv_nsec) * 1e-9;
#else
    return 0.0;
#endif
}

std::string normalizedBackend(const AudioConfig& c) { return c.backend.empty() ? std::string("auto") : c.backend; }

/** Whether two requests ask for the same run. The BACKEND is part of the choice: PortAudio and SDL both name a driver
 *  "pipewire", so a switch between them with the same driver, device and rate would otherwise be a no-op that left the
 *  old backend driving the device. */
bool sameChoice(const AudioConfig& a, const AudioConfig& b) {
    return normalizedBackend(a) == normalizedBackend(b) && a.driver == b.driver && a.device == b.device &&
           a.sampleRate == b.sampleRate && a.blockSize == b.blockSize && a.channels == b.channels &&
           a.renderAheadFrames == b.renderAheadFrames;
}

// The real-time priorities the two threads ask for: the device callback above the renderer under render-ahead, so a
// block that the renderer is still filling loses to the pull that copies it.
constexpr int kCallbackPriority        = 80;
constexpr int kCallbackPriorityAhead   = 85;
constexpr int kRendererPriority        = 80;

/** Best effort, ONCE PER THREAD: real-time scheduling and the audio core for the calling thread. Per thread, not per
 *  process: a re-opened stream's callback is a new thread, and each one asks once for itself. Without RT permission,
 *  the default scheduling stands, and the UI's own pin away from the audio core is this product's (main.cpp). */
void tuneAudioThread(int priority) {
#if defined(__linux__)
    static thread_local bool tuned = false;
    if (tuned) return;
    tuned = true;
    const long ncpu = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);
    if (ncpu > 1) {
        cpu_set_t set;
        CPU_ZERO(&set);
        CPU_SET(ncpu - 1, &set);  // the last core, which the UI is pinned away from
        pthread_setaffinity_np(pthread_self(), sizeof(set), &set);
    }
    sched_param sp{};
    sp.sched_priority = priority;
    pthread_setschedparam(pthread_self(), SCHED_FIFO, &sp);
#else
    (void)priority;
#endif
}

/** The hint an open failure carries: the backend's own diagnostics are silent unless asked for, so a muted run says how
 *  to ask. */
const char* debugHint() {
    static const bool debug = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO") != nullptr;
    // The em dash is the one today's line carried (U+2014), spelled as bytes so no execution character set decides it.
    return debug ? "" : " \xE2\x80\x94 re-run with RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO=1 for the backend's diagnostics";
}

}  // namespace

AudioHost::AudioHost(BackendList preference, AudioClient& client)
    : preference_(std::move(preference)), client_(&client), controlThread_(std::this_thread::get_id()) {
    preference_.push_back(nullAudioBackend());  // last, always: a product that names no backend still runs
    statsEnabled_ = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_STATS") != nullptr;
}

AudioHost::~AudioHost() {
    closeCurrent();
}

void AudioHost::logLine(const std::string& text) const {
    const std::string line = std::string(kLogPrefix) + text;
    if (sink_) {
        sink_(line);
        return;
    }
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", line.c_str());
}

bool AudioHost::live() const {
    return started_ && stream_ != nullptr && backend_ != nullptr && backend_->id() != "null";
}

AudioStatus AudioHost::status() const {
    AudioStatus out;
    if (backend_) {
        out.backend = backend_->id();
        out.driver  = info_.driver;
        out.device  = info_.device;
    }
    out.sampleRate  = info_.sampleRate;
    out.blockFrames = info_.blockFrames;
    out.channels    = info_.channels;
    out.error       = error_;
    return out;
}

AudioDescription AudioHost::describe() const {
    // ONLY the backend in force is enumerated, and only while a real one is: a backend initialises its library at its
    // first use, so asking a PortAudio or SDL backend to list its drivers is exactly that use. A `null` run - and the
    // startup of any run before its device is open - therefore touches no other audio library, which is what lets a
    // machine whose default ALSA device is somebody else's card run this app without opening it. A row that needs
    // another backend's drivers asks for it, once, through backendDrivers().
    AudioDescription out;
    const std::string inForce = backend_ ? backend_->id() : std::string();
    for (const auto& backend : preference_) {
        AudioBackendDescription described;
        described.id    = backend->id();
        described.label = backend->label();
        if (described.id != inForce) {
            out.backends.push_back(std::move(described));
            continue;
        }
        described.autoDriver = backend->autoDriver();
        for (const Driver& driver : backend->drivers()) {
            AudioDriverDescription d;
            d.id      = driver.id;
            d.label   = driver.label;
            d.devices = backend->devices(driver.id);
            described.drivers.push_back(std::move(d));
        }
        out.backends.push_back(std::move(described));
    }
    out.status = status();
    return out;
}

AudioConfig applyRunOverrides(AudioConfig config, const std::string& backendOverride, int blockSizeOverride) {
    if (blockSizeOverride > 0) config.blockSize = blockSizeOverride;
    if (backendOverride.empty()) return config;
    if (config.backend != backendOverride) {
        config.driver.clear();
        config.device.clear();
    }
    config.backend = backendOverride;
    return config;
}

std::vector<AudioDriverDescription> AudioHost::backendDrivers(const std::string& backendId) const {
    std::vector<AudioDriverDescription> out;
    for (const auto& backend : preference_) {
        if (backend->id() != backendId) continue;
        for (const Driver& driver : backend->drivers()) {
            AudioDriverDescription d;
            d.id      = driver.id;
            d.label   = driver.label;
            d.devices = backend->devices(driver.id);
            out.push_back(std::move(d));
        }
    }
    return out;
}

std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> AudioHost::openFor(const AudioConfig& config, Resolved& resolved, StreamInfo& info,
                                                std::string& error) {
    Request request;
    request.device      = config.device;
    request.sampleRate  = config.sampleRate;
    request.channels    = config.channels;
    request.blockFrames = config.renderAheadFrames > 0 ? 0 : config.blockSize;

    const bool explicitBackend = !config.backend.empty() && config.backend != "auto";
    for (const auto& backend : preference_) {
        if (explicitBackend && backend->id() != config.backend) continue;
        if (!explicitBackend && backend->id() == "null") continue;  // auto never picks the fallback
        request.driver = config.driver.empty() ? backend->autoDriver() : config.driver;
        if (request.driver.empty()) {
            if (!explicitBackend) continue;  // this backend cannot open anything right now: the next one may
            error = backend->label() + ": no audio driver is usable";
            return nullptr;
        }
        std::string attempt;
        std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> stream = backend->open(request, &AudioHost::pullTrampoline, this, attempt);
        if (stream) {
            resolved.backend = backend.get();
            resolved.driver  = request.driver;
            resolved.device  = stream->info().device;
            info             = stream->info();
            return stream;
        }
        if (!config.driver.empty() || explicitBackend) {
            error = attempt;  // an explicitly named backend or driver: its failure is the answer
            return nullptr;
        }
        error = attempt;  // remembered for the fallback's status; the next backend is tried
    }
    if (error.empty()) error = explicitBackend ? "no audio backend '" + config.backend + "'" : "no audio device";
    return nullptr;
}

bool AudioHost::openAndStart(const AudioConfig& config, Resolved& resolved, StreamInfo& info, std::string& error) {
    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> stream = openFor(config, resolved, info, error);
    if (!stream) return false;
    // Render-ahead is decided BEFORE the request is made (a backend asked for its own quantum is asked because the
    // renderer fills whole blocks); the null device never renders ahead, so a fallback asks for its block and renders
    // in the pull.
    renderAhead_ = config.renderAheadFrames > 0 && resolved.backend->id() != "null";
    const int blockFrames = renderAhead_ ? std::max(1, config.blockSize) : std::max(1, info.blockFrames);
    // The run's state goes in FIRST: the renderer (below) and the pull (after start) read it, so it must be complete
    // before either thread exists.
    stream_      = std::move(stream);
    backend_     = resolved.backend;
    info_        = info;
    blockFrames_ = blockFrames;
    if (renderAhead_) {
        // The ring and the scratch exist before the device can pull, and the renderer runs before start(): a real
        // device's callback can run the moment start() returns, and a pull that found the previous run's counters would
        // read a ring the control thread was reallocating.
        ringFrames_ = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(config.renderAheadFrames, 2 * blockFrames));
        ring_.assign(ringFrames_ * static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(1, info.channels)), 0.0f);
        renderScratch_.assign(
            static_cast<std::size_t>(blockFrames) * static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(1, info.channels)), 0.0f);
    }
    // The engine is shaped by what the DEVICE came up as and by the block the RUN renders in, never by what was asked
    // for: a null fallback pulls in the block the section names, so the engine is sized for that. Before the renderer
    // starts, which is why the ring is sized above and the renderer below.
    client_->prepare(static_cast<double>(std::max(1, info_.sampleRate)), blockFrames, std::max(1, info_.channels));
    if (renderAhead_) startRenderer(blockFrames, info_.channels);  // and before the DEVICE can pull, ring sized
    std::string startError;
    if (!stream_->start(startError)) {
        // A stream that opens and never starts is an OPEN failure: nothing pulls, so the emulator would sit frozen and
        // the status would claim a device. The backend's own words go into the status, and the caller falls to null.
        error = startError.empty() ? resolved.backend->label() + ": the audio device would not start" : startError;
        closeCurrent();
        return false;
    }
    started_ = true;
    pulls_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    lastPullMs_.store(nowMs(), std::memory_order_relaxed);  // a stream that starts and never pulls trips the watchdog
    setWatchdogFor(blockFrames);
    return true;
}

bool AudioHost::apply(const AudioConfig& config) {
    // No change and a REAL device running: none of the sequence runs (a Settings Apply with nothing edited is free).
    // A muted host never takes this path: the same request is how a user retries the device that refused.
    if (started_ && stream_ && sameChoice(config, config_) && backend_ && backend_->id() != "null") return live();

    closeCurrent();
    client_->release();
    config_ = config;

    Resolved    resolved;
    StreamInfo  info;
    std::string error;
    if (!openAndStart(config, resolved, info, error)) {
        // The null device, with the reason in the status: the emulator still advances, and Settings says why it is
        // silent. Today's muted line, with a reason the UI can show as well as the log.
        const std::string reason = error.empty() ? "no audio device" : error;
        logLine("audio: " + reason + " (muted)" + debugHint());
        if (!fallbackToNull(reason)) {
            error_   = reason;
            info_    = StreamInfo{};
            backend_ = nullptr;
            started_ = false;
            return false;
        }
        error_ = reason;
    } else {
        error_.clear();
    }

    // The line openAudio printed, backend neutral: the backend's label and the driver's LABEL, so PortAudio's is
    // byte-identical to today's.
    std::string line = "audio: " + backend_->label() + " [" + backend_->driverLabel(info_.driver) + "] '" +
                       info_.device + "' " + std::to_string(info_.sampleRate) + " Hz, " +
                       std::to_string(blockFrames_) + " frames, " + std::to_string(info_.channels) + " ch";
    if (renderAhead_) line += ", render-ahead ring " + std::to_string(ringFrames_) + " frames";
    logLine(line);
    return live();
}

void AudioHost::stop() {
    closeCurrent();
    client_->release();
}

bool AudioHost::poll() {
    if (!started_ || !stream_ || !backend_) return false;
    if (backend_->id() == "null") return false;  // the fallback is already the answer
    std::string reason;
    if (stream_->lost()) {
        reason = "the audio device went away";
    } else {
        // A backend that never reports still falls back: a pull that has not finished for a few block durations while
        // the stream is started is a stall, and today's app freezes on one (the emulator advances only inside a pull).
        // The clock starts at start(), so a stream that starts and NEVER pulls is caught too.
        const std::int64_t last = lastPullMs_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (last != 0 && nowMs() - last > watchdogBound_.count()) reason = "the audio device stopped pulling";
    }
    if (reason.empty()) return false;

    const AudioStatus before = status();
    closeCurrent();
    client_->release();
    if (!fallbackToNull(reason)) {
        // Nothing to run on: the engine went back to the control plane, and the status says what happened. Recovery is
        // the user's apply (a device that is back shows up as one).
        error_   = reason;
        started_ = false;
    } else {
        logLine("audio: " + reason + " (muted)");
    }
    const AudioStatus after = status();
    return before.backend != after.backend || before.device != after.device || before.error != after.error;
}

bool AudioHost::fallbackToNull(const std::string& reason) {
    // The last resort every failure lands on: the sleep-paced null pump, which always opens and always starts. Its
    // request is the block the section asks for and NOT render-ahead: it renders inside the pull, so the engine is
    // shaped for exactly what it runs - rendering ahead of a pump that pulls in whole blocks would only make the engine
    // refuse blocks over its maximum.
    AudioConfig fallback   = config_;
    fallback.backend       = "null";
    fallback.driver.clear();
    fallback.device.clear();
    fallback.renderAheadFrames = 0;
    Resolved    resolved;
    StreamInfo  info;
    std::string error;
    if (!openAndStart(fallback, resolved, info, error)) {
        if (!error.empty()) error_ = error;
        return false;
    }
    // What the status row shows, and what a later apply clears by opening a real device. The muted line itself is the
    // caller's (it knows whether the failure was an open or a poll), so a muted run logs it once.
    if (!reason.empty()) error_ = reason;
    return true;
}

void AudioHost::closeCurrent() {
    stopRenderer();
    if (stream_) {
        stream_->stop();
        stream_.reset();
    }
    started_     = false;
    ringFrames_  = 0;  // the next run sizes its own, so a pull can never read this one's
    blockFrames_ = 0;
    pulls_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    lastPullMs_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

void AudioHost::setWatchdogFor(int blockFrames) {
    // A few block durations, never under 250 ms: an 8192-frame quantum at 44.1 kHz is 186 ms between pulls, so a fixed
    // quarter of a second would trip on one block's own duration (and a WinMM SysEx inside the block adds its 170 ms).
    // The bound follows the LONGER of the block the run renders in and the DEVICE's own quantum: under render-ahead the
    // stream is opened with blockFrames 0, so the device pulls in its quantum, which can outlast the render block.
    const int pullFrames = std::max(blockFrames, info_.blockFrames);
    const double blockMs =
        info_.sampleRate > 0 ? 1000.0 * static_cast<double>(pullFrames) / info_.sampleRate : 0.0;
    watchdogBound_ = std::chrono::milliseconds(std::max<std::int64_t>(250, static_cast<std::int64_t>(4.0 * blockMs)));
}

void AudioHost::pull(float* interleaved, int frames, bool underflow) {
    // The audio path's first call on this thread: real-time priority and the audio core, once (per thread) - but only
    // on a REAL device's thread. The null device's pump is a sleep-paced emulator loop with nothing to keep ahead of,
    // and a test that pulls by hand would leave the control process's own thread (and every thread it later creates)
    // at SCHED_FIFO on the audio core.
    if (backend_ && backend_->id() != "null" && std::this_thread::get_id() != controlThread_)
        tuneAudioThread(renderAhead_ ? kCallbackPriorityAhead : kCallbackPriority);
    pulls_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (frames <= 0) {
        lastPullMs_.store(nowMs(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return;
    }
    if (renderAhead_) {
        // Copy what the renderer has queued and pad a short ring with silence. The underrun is counted only once the
        // ring has primed: the first pulls of a fresh stream are meant to find it empty.
        const std::uint64_t read  = ringRead_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        const std::uint64_t write = ringWritten_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        const std::uint64_t avail = write - read;
        const std::uint64_t n     = std::min<std::uint64_t>(avail, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(frames));
        const std::size_t   channels = static_cast<std::size_t>(info_.channels);
        for (std::uint64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            const std::size_t at = static_cast<std::size_t>((read + i) % ringFrames_) * channels;
            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < channels; ++c) interleaved[i * channels + c] = ring_[at + c];
        }
        if (n < static_cast<std::uint64_t>(frames)) {
            std::fill(interleaved + n * channels, interleaved + static_cast<std::size_t>(frames) * channels, 0.0f);
            if (ringPrimed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
                underruns_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                pendingUnderflows_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);  // the renderer's count to report
            }
        }
        ringRead_.store(read + n, std::memory_order_release);
        lastPullMs_.store(nowMs(), std::memory_order_relaxed);  // at EXIT: the copy is the whole call
        return;
    }
    const auto   start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const double cpu0  = statsEnabled_ ? threadCpuSeconds() : 0.0;
    client_->render(interleaved, frames);
    // At EXIT: a render longer than the bound is one block's work, not a stall, so the stamp is what the pull FINISHED
    // at. The stats are this thread's alone here - under render-ahead only the renderer reports.
    lastPullMs_.store(nowMs(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (statsEnabled_) {
        const double    renderSec = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
        const double    blockSec  = info_.sampleRate > 0 ? static_cast<double>(frames) / info_.sampleRate : 0.0;
        if (underflow) pendingUnderflows_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        reportStats(renderSec, threadCpuSeconds() - cpu0, blockSec, frames);
    }
}

void AudioHost::pullTrampoline(void* ctx, float* interleaved, int frames, bool underflow) {
    static_cast<AudioHost*>(ctx)->pull(interleaved, frames, underflow);
}

void AudioHost::startRenderer(int blockFrames, int channels) {
    ringWritten_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    ringRead_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    ringPrimed_.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    underruns_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    pendingUnderflows_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    renderRun_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    renderThread_ = std::thread([this, blockFrames, channels] { renderLoop(blockFrames, channels); });
}

void AudioHost::stopRenderer() {
    if (!renderThread_.joinable()) return;
    renderRun_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    renderThread_.join();
}

void AudioHost::renderLoop(int blockFrames, int channels) {
    // The render-ahead producer (ported from feature/handheld-perf's 4b9e39ea8): keep the ring topped up a block at a
    // time, below the device callback's own priority on the same core, so a block that overruns the server's quantum
    // is survivable. This thread alone reports the stats while it runs.
    tuneAudioThread(kRendererPriority);
    const std::size_t   frameSamples = static_cast<std::size_t>(channels);
    const std::uint64_t roomFor      = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockFrames);
    while (renderRun_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
        const std::uint64_t written = ringWritten_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        const std::uint64_t read    = ringRead_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (ringFrames_ - (written - read) < roomFor) {
            if (written - read >= ringFrames_ / 2) ringPrimed_.store(true, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
            continue;
        }
        const auto   start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        const double cpu0  = statsEnabled_ ? threadCpuSeconds() : 0.0;
        client_->render(renderScratch_.data(), blockFrames);
        for (int i = 0; i < blockFrames; ++i) {
            const std::size_t at = static_cast<std::size_t>((written + i) % ringFrames_) * frameSamples;
            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < frameSamples; ++c)
                ring_[at + c] = renderScratch_[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * frameSamples + c];
        }
        ringWritten_.store(written + blockFrames, std::memory_order_release);
        if (statsEnabled_) {
            const double renderSec = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
            const double blockSec  = info_.sampleRate > 0 ? static_cast<double>(blockFrames) / info_.sampleRate : 0.0;
            reportStats(renderSec, threadCpuSeconds() - cpu0, blockSec, blockFrames);
        }
    }
}

void AudioHost::setStatsForTest(bool enabled, std::chrono::milliseconds interval) {
    statsEnabled_  = enabled;
    statsInterval_ = interval;
    statsSince_    = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    statsBusySec_ = statsCpuSec_ = statsWallSec_ = statsWorst_ = 0;
    statsBlocks_ = statsUnderflows_ = statsFrames_ = 0;
}

void AudioHost::reportStats(double renderSec, double renderCpuSec, double blockSec, int blockFrames) {
    statsFrames_ += static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockFrames);
    statsBusySec_ += renderSec;
    statsCpuSec_ += renderCpuSec;
    statsWallSec_ += blockSec;
    if (blockSec > 0) statsWorst_ = std::max(statsWorst_, renderSec / blockSec);
    ++statsBlocks_;
    // The pull's underruns arrive through an atomic, because under render-ahead the two threads must not share a plain
    // field: the renderer alone prints, and the callback only counts.
    statsUnderflows_ += pendingUnderflows_.exchange(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (statsWallSec_ < static_cast<double>(statsInterval_.count()) / 1000.0) return;
    const auto   now     = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const double realSec = std::chrono::duration<double>(now - statsSince_).count();
    statsSince_          = now;
    statsTotalUnderflows_ += statsUnderflows_;
    char line[512];
    std::snprintf(line, sizeof(line),
                  "audio stats: load avg %.0f%% (cpu %.0f%%) max %.0f%% over %llu blocks of %llu, %.0f frames/s real, "
                  "underflows %llu (total %llu)",
                  statsWallSec_ > 0 ? 100.0 * statsBusySec_ / statsWallSec_ : 0.0,
                  statsWallSec_ > 0 ? 100.0 * statsCpuSec_ / statsWallSec_ : 0.0, 100.0 * statsWorst_,
                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(statsBlocks_),
                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(statsBlocks_ ? statsFrames_ / statsBlocks_ : 0),
                  realSec > 0 ? static_cast<double>(statsFrames_) / realSec : 0.0,
                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(statsUnderflows_),
                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(statsTotalUnderflows_));
    logLine(line);
    statsBusySec_ = statsCpuSec_ = statsWallSec_ = statsWorst_ = 0;
    statsBlocks_ = statsUnderflows_ = statsFrames_ = 0;
}

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

````cpp
#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "audio/AudioBackend.hpp"

namespace rp::audio {
namespace {

/** The null device's stream: nothing is opened, and a thread of its own advances the engine at the requested block's
 *  real-time cadence, so a machine with no usable audio still runs (the emulator, the transport, the multi-out
 *  self-test and sdl:smoke's checks all live inside a pull). It is the sleep-paced fallback pump, as a backend. */
class NullStream final : public AudioStream {
public:
    NullStream(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx)
        : pull_(pull), ctx_(ctx), info_{request.driver, "the null device", request.sampleRate,
                                       request.blockFrames > 0 ? request.blockFrames : 512, request.channels} {}

    ~NullStream() override { stop(); }

    bool start(std::string& /*error*/) override {
        if (running_.exchange(true)) return true;
        thread_ = std::thread([this] { loop(); });
        return true;
    }

    void stop() override {
        if (!running_.exchange(false)) return;
        if (thread_.joinable()) thread_.join();
    }

    StreamInfo info() const override { return info_; }
    bool       lost() const override { return false; }

private:
    void loop() {
        std::vector<float> block(static_cast<std::size_t>(info_.blockFrames) * static_cast<std::size_t>(info_.channels),
                                 0.0f);
        while (running_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            pull_(ctx_, block.data(), info_.blockFrames, false);
            const double secs = info_.sampleRate > 0 ? static_cast<double>(info_.blockFrames) / info_.sampleRate
                                                    : static_cast<double>(info_.blockFrames) / 48000.0;
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::duration<double>(secs));  // approximate realtime
        }
    }

    Pull                   pull_;
    void*                  ctx_;
    StreamInfo             info_;
    std::atomic<bool>      running_{false};
    std::thread            thread_;
};

class NullBackend final : public AudioBackend {
public:
    std::string id() const override { return "null"; }
    std::string label() const override { return "Null"; }
    std::vector<Driver> drivers() override { return {{"null", "Null"}}; }
    std::string autoDriver() override { return "null"; }
    Devices     devices(const std::string&) override { return {{"the null device"}, "the null device"}; }

    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx, std::string& error) override {
        if (request.channels <= 0 || request.sampleRate <= 0) {
            error = "the null device needs a positive rate and channel count";
            return nullptr;
        }
        return std::make_unique<NullStream>(request, pull, ctx);
    }
};

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<AudioBackend> nullAudioBackend() { return std::make_unique<NullBackend>(); }

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The Driver row's vocabulary (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md sections 5.1 and 6.4): the Settings > Audio row
// lists one LABEL per driver, "<Backend>: <driver>", and an Apply hands that label back. This is the pure mapping
// between the two, so the row's contract is held by its own cases rather than by a device: "Auto", a label from the
// list, or a stale one (a driver that went away between the list being drawn and Apply being pressed).

#include <string>

#include "audio/AudioHost.hpp"

namespace rp::audio {

/** The label of the row that means "whatever the backend's own automatic choice is": the list's first entry. */
inline constexpr const char* kAutoDriverLabel = "Auto";

/** The Driver row's label for one driver of one backend. The backend is named because two backends may call a driver
 *  the same thing (PortAudio's host API "PipeWire", SDL's driver "pipewire"): the driver id alone does not say which
 *  device an Apply would open, and the labels are what the row shows anyway. */
inline std::string driverChoiceLabel(const std::string& backendLabel, const std::string& driverLabel) {
    return backendLabel + ": " + driverLabel;
}

/** What a Driver row's label names, in the vocabulary apply() takes: "auto" is the automatic choice. */
struct AudioChoice {
    std::string backend = "auto";
    std::string driver;
};

/** Map a row's label to the choice it names: "Auto" (or an empty label, which an older UI bundle sent) is the automatic
 *  choice, and a "<Backend label>: <driver label>" entry of `description` is that pair. A label the description does not
 *  carry is a STALE row and answers `current`, so an Apply that changed only the rate keeps the device the run already
 *  had - the same rule the pre-package hook had ("an unknown name keeps the current driver"). Pure: no device, no
 *  library, no allocation beyond the strings. */
inline AudioChoice choiceForDriverLabel(const std::string& label, const AudioDescription& description,
                                        const AudioChoice& current) {
    if (label.empty() || label == kAutoDriverLabel) return AudioChoice{};
    for (const AudioBackendDescription& backend : description.backends) {
        if (backend.id == "null") continue;
        for (const AudioDriverDescription& driver : backend.drivers)
            if (driverChoiceLabel(backend.label, driver.label) == label) return AudioChoice{backend.id, driver.id};
    }
    return current;
}

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// An audio system a test scripts, filling the same interface PortAudio and SDL do (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-
// design.md section 5.7). Header-only test support under native/test-support, an include root the tests add and no
// product does: what a case needs is a stream it opens by hand, a rate it may adopt, an open it may refuse, a start it
// may refuse, a device it may lose, a pull it drives itself at whatever ragged sizes it likes, and - for the re-apply
// cases - a stream that pulls on a thread of its own the moment start() returns, as a real device does.

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "audio/AudioBackend.hpp"

namespace rp::audio {

class FakeAudioBackend final : public AudioBackend {
public:
    /** One stream the fake opened. `pull` copies the callback's buffer so a case can read the sample stream a host
     *  produced, whatever the pull sizes were. */
    struct Stream final : AudioStream {
        StreamInfo description;
        Pull       pull = nullptr;
        void*      ctx  = nullptr;
        bool       started = false;
        bool       stopped = false;
        bool        startFails = false;
        std::string startError = "the device would not start";
        bool        lostFlag   = false;
        // A real device's callback can run the moment start() returns. With this set, the stream pulls `pullFrames`
        // (or its own block) on a thread of its own until stop(), which is how a re-apply is exercised under a pull.
        bool        pullOnStart = false;
        int         pullFrames  = 0;
        std::thread worker;
        std::atomic<bool> running{false};
        std::vector<std::string>* log = nullptr;  // the backend's event log, so a case reads start/stop with the rest
        std::vector<float> captured;              // what the last pull wrote

        bool start(std::string& error) override {
            started = !startFails;
            if (!started && error.empty()) error = startError;
            if (log) log->push_back(started ? "start" : "start-failed");
            if (started && pullOnStart) {
                running.store(true);
                worker = std::thread([this] {
                    const int frames = pullFrames > 0 ? pullFrames : description.blockFrames;
                    while (running.load()) {
                        drive(frames);
                        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
                    }
                });
            }
            return started;
        }
        void stop() override {
            running.store(false);
            if (worker.joinable()) worker.join();  // no pull is running when this returns, as the contract says
            stopped = true;
            started = false;
            if (log) log->push_back("stop");
        }
        StreamInfo info() const override { return description; }
        bool       lost() const override { return lostFlag; }

        /** One device callback of `frames`: what the backend's real-time thread would do. */
        void drive(int frames) {
            captured.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(frames) * static_cast<std::size_t>(description.channels), 0.0f);
            if (pull && frames > 0) pull(ctx, captured.data(), frames, false);
        }
    };

    // --- what a case scripts -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    std::string              idValue     = "fake";
    std::string              labelValue  = "Fake";
    std::string              autoDriverValue = "fake-driver";
    bool                     openFails   = false;
    std::string              openError   = "the fake refused the device";
    std::string              startError  = "the device would not start";  // what a stream it opens reports
    bool                     startFails  = false;                         // every stream this backend opens refuses
    bool                     pullOnStart = false;  // ...and every stream pulls on its own thread from start(), as a
                                                   // real device does (the re-apply cases and the TSan leg)
    int                      adoptRate   = 0;      // 0: the requested rate; else the rate the device reports
    int                      actualBlock = 0;      // 0: the requested block; else the device's own quantum
    std::vector<std::string>* events = nullptr;     // "open <driver>/<device>", "start", "stop": shared with a client
    // How often the backend was asked to enumerate: a description must not be a use of a library a run never chose.
    int autoDriverCalls = 0;
    int driverCalls     = 0;
    int deviceCalls     = 0;
    Stream*                  lastStream  = nullptr;  // the last stream opened (the HOST owns it; read before stop)

    std::string id() const override { return idValue; }
    std::string label() const override { return labelValue; }
    std::vector<Driver> drivers() override {
        ++driverCalls;
        return {{"fake-driver", "Fake Driver"}, {"other", "Other Driver"}};
    }
    std::string autoDriver() override {
        ++autoDriverCalls;
        return autoDriverValue;
    }
    Devices devices(const std::string& driver) override {
        ++deviceCalls;
        if (driver != "fake-driver") return {};
        return {{"Fake Out", "Fake Out 2"}, "Fake Out"};
    }

    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx, std::string& error) override {
        if (openFails) {
            error = openError;
            return nullptr;
        }
        auto stream         = std::make_unique<Stream>();
        stream->description = StreamInfo{request.driver, request.device.empty() ? "Fake Out" : request.device,
                                        adoptRate > 0 ? adoptRate : request.sampleRate,
                                        actualBlock > 0 ? actualBlock
                                                        : (request.blockFrames > 0 ? request.blockFrames : 512),
                                        request.channels};
        stream->pull = pull;
        stream->ctx  = ctx;
        stream->log  = events;
        if (events) events->push_back("open " + request.driver + "/" + stream->description.device);
        stream->startFails  = startFails;
        stream->startError  = startError;
        stream->pullOnStart = pullOnStart;
        lastStream         = stream.get();
        return stream;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

Create `packages/audio/native/test/AudioHost.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// Unit-tests AudioHost over the fake backend (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 5.7): the reconfigure's
// call order with the rate the device OBTAINED, the no-change apply that runs none of it (and the BACKEND part of the
// choice), a failed open AND a failed start falling back to the null device with a status, a lost device and the
// no-pull watchdog doing the same (a stream that never pulls included, and the bound the block allows), render-ahead
// producing the in-callback stream sample for sample across ragged pulls that wrap its ring and never underrun, the
// single renderer the client may see, the stats through a sink, the log lines byte for byte, and the Settings row's
// label-to-choice mapping.
//
// No device, no PortAudio, no SDL: the backend is test support (audio/FakeAudioBackend.hpp). The two real backends are
// compiled by the ordinary build and proved against a real server by tools/run-sdl-pipewire.sh.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "audio/AudioChoice.hpp"
#include "audio/AudioHost.hpp"
#include "audio/FakeAudioBackend.hpp"

using namespace rp::audio;

namespace {

/** The product's side, as a deterministic signal: frame i writes a value that depends on i AND on what the renderer
 *  wrote before it, so a ring that reorders, repeats or drops a block cannot produce the same stream. Every call is
 *  recorded in one log shared with the fake, which is how a case reads the order the host ran in. */
struct TestClient final : AudioClient {
    std::vector<std::string>*          log = nullptr;
    std::vector<float>                 stream;      // every sample rendered, in order
    // Frames rendered so far, atomic because a render-ahead renderer increments it while the case waits on it.
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>         position{0};
    double                             rate     = 0;
    int                                block    = 0;
    int                                channels = 0;
    double                             last = 0.0;
    std::atomic<int>                   renders{0};
    std::atomic<int>                   inFlight{0};
    std::atomic<int>                   maxInFlight{0};
    bool                               renderSleeps = false;

    void prepare(double sampleRate, int maxBlockFrames, int ch) override {
        if (log) log->push_back("prepare " + std::to_string(static_cast<int>(sampleRate)) + " " +
                                std::to_string(maxBlockFrames) + " " + std::to_string(ch));
        rate     = sampleRate;
        block    = maxBlockFrames;
        channels = ch;
        stream.clear();
        position.store(0);
        last = 0.0;
    }

    void render(float* interleaved, int frames) override {
        const int now = inFlight.fetch_add(1) + 1;
        int       was = maxInFlight.load();
        while (now > was && !maxInFlight.compare_exchange_weak(was, now)) {
        }
        if (renderSleeps) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
        for (int i = 0; i < frames; ++i) {
            for (int c = 0; c < channels; ++c) {
                const double v =
                    static_cast<double>(position.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(i)) +
                    0.001 * c + last;
                interleaved[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * channels + c] = static_cast<float>(v);
            }
            last = 1e-6 * static_cast<double>(interleaved[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * channels]);
        }
        // NOT an entry in `log`: that vector is the control thread's (and the fake's), and a renderer writing to it
        // would be a race in the harness rather than in the host. A count says the same thing.
        renders.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        position.fetch_add(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(frames));
        for (int i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
            for (int c = 0; c < channels; ++c)
                stream.push_back(interleaved[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * channels + c]);
        inFlight.fetch_sub(1);
    }

    void release() override {
        if (log) log->push_back("release");
    }
};

/** The host's preference list holds backends by unique_ptr; the case holds the fake by value so it can script it, so
 *  this forwards every call to that one. */
struct Forward final : AudioBackend {
    FakeAudioBackend* target = nullptr;

    std::string id() const override { return target->id(); }
    std::string label() const override { return target->label(); }
    std::vector<Driver> drivers() override { return target->drivers(); }
    std::string autoDriver() override { return target->autoDriver(); }
    Devices     devices(const std::string& driver) override { return target->devices(driver); }
    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx, std::string& error) override {
        return target->open(request, pull, ctx, error);
    }
};

/** The host's log sink, as a case reads it: the control thread and the render-ahead renderer BOTH write lines (the
 *  open line is the control thread's, the stats line the renderer's), so the vector is behind a mutex rather than being
 *  a race in the harness. */
struct Lines {
    std::mutex               mutex;
    std::vector<std::string> items;

    void add(const std::string& line) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        items.push_back(line);
    }
    std::vector<std::string> snapshot() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        return items;
    }
};

/** A host over one fake backend, the fake and the client sharing one event log. */
struct Rig {
    FakeAudioBackend           backend;
    std::vector<std::string>   log;
    TestClient                 client;
    std::unique_ptr<AudioHost> host;

    Rig() {
        backend.events = &log;
        client.log       = &log;
        auto fwd         = std::make_unique<Forward>();
        fwd->target      = &backend;
        BackendList preference;
        preference.push_back(std::move(fwd));
        host = std::make_unique<AudioHost>(std::move(preference), client);
    }

    AudioConfig config(int rate = 48000, int block = 512, int channels = 2) const {
        AudioConfig c;
        c.sampleRate = rate;
        c.blockSize  = block;
        c.channels   = channels;
        return c;
    }

    FakeAudioBackend&       fwd() { return backend; }
};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a reconfigure runs stop, release, open, prepare(what the DEVICE obtained), start") {
    // The order report item 2 settled: the engine is re-rated to the rate the device came up at, not to the rate that
    // was asked for. A device that adopts 44100 while 48000 was requested must reach prepare as 44100.
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().adoptRate = 44100;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(48000, 256, 2)));
    const std::vector<std::string> expected = {
        "release",
        "open fake-driver/Fake Out",
        "prepare 44100 256 2",  // what the device says, not 48000
        "start",
    };
    CHECK(rig.log == expected);
    CHECK(rig.host->status().sampleRate == 44100);
    CHECK(rig.host->status().driver == "fake-driver");
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error.empty());
    CHECK(rig.host->live());
}

TEST_CASE("a second apply of the same choice runs none of the sequence") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    const std::size_t after = rig.log.size();
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    CHECK(rig.log.size() == after);  // no stop, no release, no open, no prepare, no start
    // A different choice runs all of it: stop of the old device first.
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(48000, 1024, 2)));
    CHECK(rig.log[after] == "stop");
    CHECK(rig.log[after + 1] == "release");
}

TEST_CASE("the client renders only between start and the next stop") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    // The fake drives one callback, as its own thread would.
    rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(64);
    CHECK(rig.client.stream.size() == 64 * 2);
    CHECK(rig.client.renders.load() == 1);
    // Reconciling runs stop and release before anything else; nothing renders until start again.
    rig.log.clear();
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(44100)));
    CHECK(rig.log.front() == "stop");
    CHECK(rig.log[1] == "release");
    const auto startAt = std::find(rig.log.begin(), rig.log.end(), "start");
    REQUIRE(startAt != rig.log.end());
    CHECK(rig.client.renders.load() == 1);  // nothing between release and start
    // After the start, the next callback does render again.
    rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(16);
    CHECK(rig.client.renders.load() == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("an open failure falls to the null device with the reason, and a later apply recovers") {
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().openFails = true;
    REQUIRE_FALSE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    // Muted, with the backend's words as the status: Settings shows "Muted: <reason>" instead of silence.
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error == rig.fwd().openError);
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->live());
    // The null device still renders (its own thread), so the emulator advances on a muted run.
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (rig.client.position.load() == 0 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
    CHECK(rig.client.position.load() > 0);
    // The device comes back: a later apply opens it and the status clears.
    rig.fwd().openFails = false;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    CHECK(rig.host->live());
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("a lost device is the same fallback, reported by poll()") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    rig.fwd().lastStream->lostFlag = true;
    CHECK(rig.host->poll());
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->status().error.empty());
    // Once muted, poll() is quiet: there is nothing left to lose.
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->poll());
}

TEST_CASE("the watchdog: a started device that pulls nothing falls back, and a steady one never does") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    // apply sets the bound a block allows; a case may shorten it.
    rig.host->setWatchdogBound(std::chrono::milliseconds(20));
    // Pulling steadily: the watchdog never fires.
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(32);
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(5));
        CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->poll());
    }
    // Then the device stops: after the bound, the host treats it as lost and mutes.
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(40));
    CHECK(rig.host->poll());
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    // And it never fires while stopped.
    rig.host->stop();
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(40));
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->poll());
}

TEST_CASE("render-ahead produces the in-callback stream sample for sample, across ragged pulls") {
    // The ring must be invisible in the OUTPUT: a render-ahead host playing into ragged device callbacks produces the
    // byte-for-byte stream a host rendering inside the callback does.
    auto pullAll = [](AudioHost& host, FakeAudioBackend::Stream& stream, const std::vector<int>& sizes,
                      std::vector<float>* out) {
        for (int frames : sizes) {
            stream.drive(frames);
            out->insert(out->end(), stream.captured.begin(), stream.captured.end());
        }
    };
    const std::vector<int> ragged = {64, 1, 7, 255, 512, 1000, 64, 33, 17, 512};

    Rig plain;
    REQUIRE(plain.host->apply(plain.config(48000, 512, 2)));
    std::vector<float> plainOut;
    pullAll(*plain.host, *plain.fwd().lastStream, ragged, &plainOut);
    plain.host->stop();

    Rig ahead;
    AudioConfig cfg = ahead.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames = 4096;
    REQUIRE(ahead.host->apply(cfg));
    // Let the renderer prime the ring: it fills until the device drains it.
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (ahead.client.position.load() < 4096 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    std::vector<float> aheadOut;
    pullAll(*ahead.host, *ahead.fwd().lastStream, ragged, &aheadOut);
    ahead.host->stop();

    REQUIRE(plainOut.size() == aheadOut.size());
    CHECK(plainOut == aheadOut);
}

TEST_CASE("a render-ahead host never renders on two threads at once") {
    // The single-renderer rule the stream's send() relies on in the app: with render-ahead the pull only copies, so a
    // device callback running while the renderer renders never enters the client.
    Rig rig;
    rig.client.renderSleeps = true;
    AudioConfig cfg         = rig.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames   = 1024;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(cfg));
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::milliseconds(300);
    while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
        rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(16);
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    }
    rig.host->stop();
    CHECK(rig.client.maxInFlight.load() == 1);
    CHECK(rig.client.position.load() > 0);
}

TEST_CASE("describe() enumerates only the backend in force: a null run touches no other library") {
    // A backend's library comes up at its first use, and listing its drivers IS that use. So a description reports
    // the backend in force, and the others by id and label alone - which is what makes a null-pinned run, and the
    // startup of any run, safe on a machine whose default audio device is a card it must not open.
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().openFails = true;  // auto tries the fake, fails, and the host runs on the null device
    REQUIRE_FALSE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    REQUIRE(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    const int autoCalls   = rig.fwd().autoDriverCalls;  // the attempt itself
    const int driverCalls = rig.fwd().driverCalls;
    const int deviceCalls = rig.fwd().deviceCalls;
    const AudioDescription described = rig.host->describe();
    CHECK(rig.fwd().driverCalls == driverCalls);   // untouched
    CHECK(rig.fwd().deviceCalls == deviceCalls);
    CHECK(rig.fwd().autoDriverCalls >= autoCalls);
    // The fake is in the list by name, with no drivers: nothing was asked of it.
    REQUIRE(described.backends.size() == 2);
    CHECK(described.backends[0].id == "fake");
    CHECK(described.backends[0].drivers.empty());
    CHECK(described.backends[0].label == "Fake");
    // The null device, in force, is described in full.
    CHECK(described.backends[1].id == "null");
    CHECK(described.backends[1].drivers.size() == 1);
    // And a row that offers another backend asks for it explicitly, which is that backend's first use.
    const auto fakeDrivers = rig.host->backendDrivers("fake");
    CHECK(fakeDrivers.size() == 2);
    CHECK(fakeDrivers[0].devices.names.size() == 2);
    CHECK(rig.fwd().deviceCalls > deviceCalls);
}

TEST_CASE("the stats line reports load, the real frame rate and underruns") {
    // The line 4b9e39ea8 added, backend neutral: a case reads it from the client's host with a short interval.
    Rig rig;
    rig.host->setStatsForTest(true, std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(48000, 480, 2)));
    for (int i = 0; i < 12; ++i) rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(480);
    rig.host->stop();
    CHECK(rig.client.position.load() == 12 * 480);
    CHECK(rig.host->status().blockFrames == 480);
}

TEST_CASE("a device that starts and never pulls is caught by the watchdog, and the bound scales with the block") {
    // The probe: a stream that opens and starts but never calls back (a PipeWire stream that never links, a stuck host)
    // was invisible while the watchdog waited for a FIRST pull it never saw. The clock starts at start() instead, so
    // the stall is the stall - and the bound is the block's (a 8192-frame quantum at 44.1 kHz is 186 ms between pulls,
    // so a fixed 250 ms would trip on one block's own duration).
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(44100, 8192, 2)));
    // max(250 ms, 4 x 186 ms): the block the stream runs at sets it, not a constant.
    CHECK(rig.host->watchdogBound().count() >= 740);
    CHECK(rig.host->watchdogBound().count() <= 760);
    // Shortened for the case: with no pull at all, the host mutes after the bound.
    rig.host->setWatchdogBound(std::chrono::milliseconds(20));
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->poll());  // inside the bound, nothing yet
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(40));
    CHECK(rig.host->poll());
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error.find("stopped pulling") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("a stream that opens and will not start is an open failure: null, with the reason, and the engine back") {
    // The probe: apply() returned false with an EMPTY status, nothing pulled, and prepare had already handed the engine
    // to an audio thread that never existed - the control plane's edits queued undrained and the emulator froze, which
    // is exactly what the muted status exists to end.
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().startFails = true;
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");          // the null device, which does run
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error == "the device would not start");  // the backend's own words, not an empty string
    // The engine is fed: the null pump pulls on its thread, so the emulator advances on a run whose device refused.
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (rig.client.position.load() == 0 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
    CHECK(rig.client.position.load() > 0);
    // The refused stream was stopped and freed, not kept half-open: the last thing the log says about the fake is its
    // stop, and a later apply with a working device recovers.
    rig.fwd().startFails = false;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    CHECK(rig.host->live());
    CHECK(rig.host->status().error.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("a switch of BACKEND with the same driver, device and rate is a real change") {
    // The probe: PortAudio and SDL both name a driver "pipewire", so comparing everything but the backend made
    // "PortAudio: PipeWire" -> "SDL: pipewire" a silent no-op that left the old backend on the device.
    FakeAudioBackend a, b;
    TestClient       client;
    auto             fa = std::make_unique<Forward>();
    fa->target          = &a;
    auto fb             = std::make_unique<Forward>();
    fb->target          = &b;
    BackendList preference;
    preference.push_back(std::move(fa));
    preference.push_back(std::move(fb));
    AudioHost host(std::move(preference), client);
    AudioConfig cfg;
    cfg.sampleRate = 48000;
    cfg.blockSize  = 512;
    cfg.driver     = "fake-driver";  // the same driver id in both backends
    cfg.backend    = "fake";
    REQUIRE(host.apply(cfg));
    CHECK(host.status().backend == "fake");
    // The second backend renames itself so the switch is observable through the status.
    b.idValue = "other";
    cfg.backend = "other";
    REQUIRE(host.apply(cfg));
    CHECK(host.status().backend == "other");  // it reopened, rather than returning "nothing changed"
}

TEST_CASE("a render-ahead run that falls to null shapes the engine for what the NULL device pulls") {
    // The probe: --block-size 256 --render-ahead 2048 against a refused device prepared the engine for 256 while the
    // null pump pulled 512, and Engine::processBlock refuses a block over its maximum: silence, staged MIDI dropped.
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().openFails = true;
    AudioConfig cfg     = rig.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames = 2048;
    REQUIRE_FALSE(rig.host->apply(cfg));
    CHECK(rig.host->status().backend == "null");
    // The null device renders in the block the SECTION asks for, and prepare was told exactly that.
    CHECK(rig.client.block == 256);
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (rig.client.position.load() == 0 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
    REQUIRE(rig.client.position.load() > 0);
    rig.host->stop();
    CHECK(rig.client.position.load() % 256 == 0);  // every block the null pump pulled is one the engine was sized for
}

TEST_CASE("render-ahead wraps its ring many times over and counts no underrun once primed") {
    // The shipped identity case pulled less than one ring, so the ring never wrapped and the renderer never refilled a
    // slot the pull was about to read - the two things a broken ring gets wrong. This pulls several rings' worth while
    // the renderer runs, then holds the underrun count at zero.
    Rig plain;
    REQUIRE(plain.host->apply(plain.config(48000, 256, 2)));
    std::vector<float> plainOut;
    for (int i = 0; i < 200; ++i) {
        plain.fwd().lastStream->drive(97);
        plainOut.insert(plainOut.end(), plain.fwd().lastStream->captured.begin(),
                        plain.fwd().lastStream->captured.end());
    }
    plain.host->stop();

    Rig ahead;
    AudioConfig cfg       = ahead.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames = 2048;  // 2096 framing: the ring wraps more than nine times over the pulls below
    REQUIRE(ahead.host->apply(cfg));
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(5);
    while (ahead.client.position.load() < 4096 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    std::vector<float> aheadOut;
    for (int i = 0; i < 200; ++i) {
        // Slow enough that the renderer keeps up: the identity is what is held, not an underrun-free real time.
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(500));
        ahead.fwd().lastStream->drive(97);
        aheadOut.insert(aheadOut.end(), ahead.fwd().lastStream->captured.begin(),
                        ahead.fwd().lastStream->captured.end());
    }
    const std::uint64_t underruns = ahead.host->underruns();
    ahead.host->stop();
    REQUIRE(plainOut.size() == aheadOut.size());
    CHECK(plainOut == aheadOut);
    CHECK(underruns == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the log lines the harnesses grep: the open line and the muted line, byte for byte") {
    // run-sdl-pipewire.sh reads "audio: PortAudio [h] 'd' N Hz, B frames, C ch" through its own sed, and the muted line
    // is what a user sees when a persisted device is gone. Both go through the host's sink, so a case holds the bytes.
    Rig   rig;
    Lines lines;
    rig.host->setLogSink([&](const std::string& line) { lines.add(line); });
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(rig.config(44100, 256, 2)));
    REQUIRE(lines.snapshot().size() == 1);
    CHECK(lines.snapshot()[0] == "[retroplug-sdl] audio: Fake [Fake Driver] 'Fake Out' 44100 Hz, 256 frames, 2 ch");
    // A refused device: the backend's words, "(muted)", and how to ask for its diagnostics.
    rig.host->stop();
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(lines.mutex);
        lines.items.clear();
    }
    rig.fwd().openFails = true;
    REQUIRE_FALSE(rig.host->apply(rig.config()));
    const std::vector<std::string> written = lines.snapshot();
    REQUIRE(written.size() == 2);
    CHECK(written[0] == "[retroplug-sdl] audio: the fake refused the device (muted) \xE2\x80\x94 re-run with "
                        "RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO=1 for the backend's diagnostics");
    // ...and the device that IS running, so the log says both why the run is muted and what is advancing the engine.
    CHECK(written[1] == "[retroplug-sdl] audio: Null [Null] 'the null device' 48000 Hz, 512 frames, 2 ch");
}

TEST_CASE("the stats are one thread's accumulator, and say so: the renderer's block, and the underrun total") {
    // The probe: under render-ahead the pull and the renderer both accumulated into the same plain fields, which is a
    // data race AND a nonsense line (blocks of 128 alternating with blocks of 256, and the wall time counted twice).
    // Now the renderer alone reports and the pull only counts its underruns: every line names the renderer's block, and
    // the cumulative total is printed.
    Rig   rig;
    Lines lines;
    rig.host->setLogSink([&](const std::string& line) { lines.add(line); });
    rig.host->setStatsForTest(true, std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    AudioConfig cfg       = rig.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames = 1024;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(cfg));
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
        rig.fwd().lastStream->drive(1000);  // a pull of 1000 frames: a line that counted it would say so
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
    }
    rig.host->stop();
    std::size_t stats = 0;
    for (const std::string& line : lines.snapshot()) {
        if (line.find("audio stats:") == std::string::npos) continue;
        ++stats;
        CHECK(line.find("blocks of 256") != std::string::npos);
        CHECK(line.find("(total ") != std::string::npos);
    }
    CHECK(stats > 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the Driver row's label maps to the choice an apply takes, and an unknown label keeps the current one") {
    // rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel is what the Settings > Audio hook leans on: "Auto" is the automatic choice, a
    // "<Backend>: <driver>" label is that pair (the backend named because two backends may call a driver alike), and a
    // label the description does not carry is a stale row that must not move the choice.
    AudioDescription described;
    AudioBackendDescription backend;
    backend.id   = "portaudio";
    backend.label = "PortAudio";
    AudioDriverDescription pipe;
    pipe.id    = "pipewire";
    pipe.label = "PipeWire";
    backend.drivers.push_back(pipe);
    described.backends.push_back(backend);
    AudioBackendDescription other;
    other.id    = "sdl";
    other.label = "SDL";
    AudioDriverDescription sdlPipe;
    sdlPipe.id    = "pipewire";  // the same driver id, a different backend
    sdlPipe.label = "pipewire";
    other.drivers.push_back(sdlPipe);
    described.backends.push_back(other);

    const AudioChoice current{"sdl", "pipewire"};
    CHECK(choiceForDriverLabel("Auto", described, current).backend == "auto");
    CHECK(choiceForDriverLabel("Auto", described, current).driver.empty());
    CHECK(choiceForDriverLabel("", described, current).backend == "auto");  // an older bundle's spelling
    const AudioChoice pa = choiceForDriverLabel("PortAudio: PipeWire", described, current);
    CHECK(pa.backend == "portaudio");
    CHECK(pa.driver == "pipewire");
    const AudioChoice sd = choiceForDriverLabel("SDL: pipewire", described, current);
    CHECK(sd.backend == "sdl");
    CHECK(sd.driver == "pipewire");
    const AudioChoice stale = choiceForDriverLabel("PortAudio: Gone", described, current);
    CHECK(stale.backend == "sdl");
    CHECK(stale.driver == "pipewire");
    CHECK(driverChoiceLabel("PortAudio", "PipeWire") == "PortAudio: PipeWire");
}

TEST_CASE("a backend that runs one driver at a time lists only the driver in force") {
    // SDL's rule, held without SDL (devicesListableFor): enumerating another driver would mean quitting the one in
    // force, and SDL's quit closes every open device - the listing used to mute a running stream. A test never
    // initialises SDL audio, so the rule lives in the contract header and is held here.
    CHECK(devicesListableFor("pipewire", "pipewire"));
    CHECK(devicesListableFor("pipewire", ""));       // "whatever is in force"
    CHECK_FALSE(devicesListableFor("pipewire", "alsa"));
    CHECK_FALSE(devicesListableFor("", "pipewire"));  // nothing initialised: nothing to list
    CHECK_FALSE(devicesListableFor("", ""));
}

TEST_CASE("a re-apply under a pull that runs as soon as the device starts is safe") {
    // The probe: the ring and its counters were rebuilt AFTER start(), so a real device's first pulls (the fake's own
    // thread here) read the previous run's indices while the control thread reallocated the ring - under
    // ThreadSanitizer a data race, and on a real device permanent silence (written - read wrapped, no room).
    // Run in build-tsan/ too.
    Rig rig;
    rig.fwd().pullOnStart = true;
    AudioConfig cfg       = rig.config(48000, 256, 2);
    cfg.renderAheadFrames = 1024;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(cfg));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
        cfg.renderAheadFrames = (i % 2 == 0) ? 4096 : 1024;  // a re-apply with a different ring
        REQUIRE(rig.host->apply(cfg));
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
    }
    CHECK(rig.host->live());
    rig.host->stop();
    CHECK(rig.client.inFlight.load() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a run's flags replace its backend but keep a saved driver and device the same backend names") {
    // E12's override rule (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md 5.2): --audio-backend / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND
    // replaces only the BACKEND. A saved driver and device belong to that backend's own vocabulary, so a harness that
    // pins the backend its section already names still opens the file's device; naming another backend clears them,
    // because its names would mean nothing there.
    AudioConfig saved;
    saved.backend  = "portaudio";
    saved.driver   = "pipewire";
    saved.device   = "RetroPlug Low Priority";
    saved.blockSize = 512;

    const AudioConfig pinned = applyRunOverrides(saved, "portaudio", 0);
    CHECK(pinned.backend == "portaudio");
    CHECK(pinned.driver == "pipewire");
    CHECK(pinned.device == "RetroPlug Low Priority");
    CHECK(pinned.blockSize == 512);

    const AudioConfig another = applyRunOverrides(saved, "sdl", 0);
    CHECK(another.backend == "sdl");
    CHECK(another.driver.empty());
    CHECK(another.device.empty());

    // A block-size flag wins over the saved block whatever the backend does.
    const AudioConfig block = applyRunOverrides(saved, "", 256);
    CHECK(block.blockSize == 256);
    CHECK(block.driver == "pipewire");
    CHECK(block.device == "RetroPlug Low Priority");

    // No flag at all is the saved choice untouched.
    CHECK(applyRunOverrides(saved, "", 0).backend == "portaudio");
}
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The PortAudio backend, at root scope**

`PortAudioBackend.cpp` is today's `main.cpp` code moved: the host-API and device lookup, `autoDriver()` (PipeWire when
its host API has an output device, then WASAPI on Windows - edge E14 - then the platform default's host), the
low-latency request, the obtained rate, the wide-output warning, the driver ids from a fixed table keyed by
`PaHostApiTypeId` (so a fork renaming a host API cannot move a saved choice), the ALSA/JACK/PaUtil log quieting run
BEFORE `Pa_Initialize` at the backend's first use, `Pa_Terminate` in the destructor behind a file-scope state, and
`lost()` counting a negative `Pa_IsStreamActive` too. The target links `portaudio`, ALSA by name on Linux
(`find_package(ALSA REQUIRED)`, because the quieting calls `snd_lib_error_set_handler` and rtmidi no longer brings it)
and `${CMAKE_DL_LIBS}` for the libjack `dlopen`.

````cmake
# The PortAudio backend (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 5.3): today's PortAudio code out of the SDL
# app's main.cpp - the host-API and device lookup, the low-latency request, the obtained rate and the wide-output
# warning, the ALSA/PipeWire/JACK log quietening run before Pa_Initialize at the backend's first use - behind the audio
# package's interface. Added by retroplug_package(audio-portaudio); its manifest item is what a product names in
# AUDIO_BACKENDS, so the CLI, the headless host and the plugin link neither PortAudio nor this.
#
# `portaudio` itself is added at ROOT scope (cmake/portaudio.cmake), before the packages: this target must find it.
if(RP_DEVICE_BUILD)
    return()
endif()

retroplug_package_library(retroplug-audio-portaudio ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/PortAudioBackend.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-audio-portaudio
    PUBLIC  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src
    PRIVATE ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/portaudio/include)  # a subdirectory build does not export it
target_link_libraries(retroplug-audio-portaudio PUBLIC retroplug-audio PRIVATE portaudio)

if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)
    # The quietening calls snd_lib_error_set_handler directly, which libasound must therefore be linked for by name:
    # until now it arrived through rtmidi's static link, which is another package's business (report item 22).
    find_package(ALSA REQUIRED)
    target_link_libraries(retroplug-audio-portaudio PRIVATE ALSA::ALSA)
    target_link_libraries(retroplug-audio-portaudio PRIVATE ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS})  # the libjack dlopen
endif()
````

````cpp
#include "PortAudioBackend.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdarg>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
````
