````cpp
#include <alsa/asoundlib.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#endif

#include <portaudio.h>

namespace rp::audio {
namespace {

// RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO: the backends' own chatter and the host API / device enumeration. Read once (it cannot change
// under us), and by the log handlers below as well as open().
bool debugEnabled() {
    static const bool on = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO") != nullptr;
    return on;
}

// The driver ids this backend's host APIs are named by. A FIXED table keyed by the host API TYPE, not the display
// name: a saved choice carries this id (config.json's `audio.driver`), and a fork that renames a host API's display
// string ("Core Audio" -> "CoreAudio") must not move every saved choice. A library's numeric PaHostApiTypeId is exactly
// what a saved file may not carry; this table is the stable NAME for it. A type no table names (a fork's own host API)
// falls back to its display name, lower-cased, so it still has an id rather than none.
std::string driverIdFor(PaHostApiTypeId type, const std::string& hostApiName) {
    switch (type) {
        case paALSA:            return "alsa";
        case paJACK:            return "jack";
        case paOSS:             return "oss";
        case paSndio:           return "sndio";
        case paPipeWire:        return "pipewire";
        case paCoreAudio:       return "coreaudio";
        case paSoundManager:    return "soundmanager";
        case paWASAPI:          return "wasapi";
        case paWDMKS:           return "wdmks";
        case paMME:             return "mme";
        case paDirectSound:     return "directsound";
        case paASIO:            return "asio";
        case paAudioScienceHPI: return "audioscience";
        case paInDevelopment:   break;
    }
    std::string id;
    for (char c : hostApiName) {
        if (c == ' ') id.push_back('-');
        else id.push_back(static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c))));
    }
    return id;
}

std::string driverId(const PaHostApiInfo& h) { return driverIdFor(h.type, h.name); }

PaHostApiIndex hostApiForDriver(const std::string& driver) {
    for (PaHostApiIndex i = 0; i < Pa_GetHostApiCount(); ++i) {
        const PaHostApiInfo* h = Pa_GetHostApiInfo(i);
        if (h && driverId(*h) == driver) return i;
    }
    return paHostApiNotFound;
}

// The output-capable device names in a host API (Settings > Audio > Output Device). Empty for an invalid index.
std::vector<std::string> outputDevicesForHostApi(PaHostApiIndex idx) {
    std::vector<std::string> out;
    const PaHostApiInfo*     h = (idx >= 0) ? Pa_GetHostApiInfo(idx) : nullptr;
    if (!h) return out;
    for (int i = 0; i < h->deviceCount; ++i) {
        const PaDeviceIndex dev = Pa_HostApiDeviceIndexToDeviceIndex(idx, i);
        if (dev < 0) continue;
        const PaDeviceInfo* di = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(dev);
        if (di && di->maxOutputChannels > 0) out.push_back(di->name);
    }
    return out;
}

std::string defaultOutputName(PaHostApiIndex idx) {
    const PaHostApiInfo* h = (idx >= 0) ? Pa_GetHostApiInfo(idx) : nullptr;
    if (!h || h->defaultOutputDevice == paNoDevice) return {};
    const PaDeviceInfo* di = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(h->defaultOutputDevice);
    return (di && di->name) ? std::string(di->name) : std::string();
}

PaDeviceIndex findOutputDeviceByName(PaHostApiIndex idx, const std::string& name) {
    const PaHostApiInfo* h = (idx >= 0 && !name.empty()) ? Pa_GetHostApiInfo(idx) : nullptr;
    if (!h) return paNoDevice;
    for (int i = 0; i < h->deviceCount; ++i) {
        const PaDeviceIndex dev = Pa_HostApiDeviceIndexToDeviceIndex(idx, i);
        if (dev < 0) continue;
        const PaDeviceInfo* di = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(dev);
        if (di && di->maxOutputChannels > 0 && name == di->name) return dev;
    }
    return paNoDevice;
}

// The Auto output host API: PipeWire when its host API has an output device (today's rule, which the harness greps),
// then WASAPI on Windows (report item 10: MME is the first host there, and the release-readiness list names it), else
// the host of the platform default output.
//
// WINDOWS, for the agent that runs it (E14, R2): a shared-mode WASAPI device refuses a rate other than its mix format
// unless PaWasapiStreamInfo::flags has paWinWasapiAutoConvert set, and this open passes no host API specific flags. So
// a saved rate WASAPI will not take fails the OPEN, and the host moves to the next BACKEND (SDL), not to MME: if the
// Windows run shows that, the fix is the flag or a fallback to the platform default's host inside this backend.
PaHostApiIndex autoHostApiIndex() {
    auto hasOutput = [](PaHostApiTypeId type) {
        const PaHostApiIndex idx = Pa_HostApiTypeIdToHostApiIndex(type);
        const PaHostApiInfo* h   = (idx >= 0) ? Pa_GetHostApiInfo(idx) : nullptr;
        return (h && h->defaultOutputDevice != paNoDevice) ? idx : static_cast<PaHostApiIndex>(paHostApiNotFound);
    };
    for (PaHostApiTypeId preferred : {paPipeWire, paWASAPI}) {
        const PaHostApiIndex idx = hasOutput(preferred);
        if (idx >= 0) return idx;
    }
    const PaDeviceIndex def = Pa_GetDefaultOutputDevice();
    if (def != paNoDevice) {
        const PaDeviceInfo* di = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(def);
        if (di) return di->hostApi;
    }
    return paHostApiNotFound;
}

// ---- the log quietening ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Pa_Initialize brings up EVERY compiled-in host API, and enumerating them is loud on a normal desktop: PortAudio's
// ALSA backend builds its device list by opening every PCM named in the system alsa.conf (rear, center_lfe, side,
// hdmi, modem, phoneline, dsp, a52, usb_stream, dsnoop...), and libasound's default error handler prints each
// failure to stderr - roughly forty lines of "error" about devices we are never going to open. The probe then adds
// its own "GropeDevice: ... set_rate_near failed!" lines through PaUtil_DebugPrint, and libjack prints "jack server
// is not running or cannot be started" wherever no JACK server happens to be up. None of it indicates a problem,
// but it buries the one line that says which device opened. So route all three here: silent by default, verbatim under
// RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO. Nothing is lost; it takes an env var to see it.
#if defined(__linux__)
void alsaLogHandler(const char* file, int line, const char* function, int err, const char* fmt, ...) {
    if (!debugEnabled()) return;
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] ALSA %s:%d:(%s) ", file ? file : "?", line, function ? function : "?");
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, fmt);
    std::vfprintf(stderr, fmt, args);
    va_end(args);
    if (err) std::fprintf(stderr, ": %s", snd_strerror(err));
    std::fputc('\n', stderr);
}

void jackLogHandler(const char* msg) {
    if (debugEnabled() && msg) std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] JACK: %s\n", msg);
}
#endif

void paLogHandler(const char* log) {
    if (debugEnabled() && log) std::fputs(log, stderr);
}

// PortAudio's own diagnostics. Its callback hands us a preformatted line, newline included; the symbol is declared here
// rather than by including pa_debugprint.h, a PRIVATE PortAudio header, for two symbols.
extern "C" {
typedef void (*PaUtilLogCallback)(const char* log);
void PaUtil_SetDebugPrintFunction(PaUtilLogCallback cb);
}

// Install the handlers. Must run BEFORE Pa_Initialize: that is where the enumeration (and the noise) happens.
void quietenLogs() {
    PaUtil_SetDebugPrintFunction(paLogHandler);
#if defined(__linux__)
    snd_lib_error_set_handler(alsaLogHandler);
    // libjack is NOT linked: PortAudio dlopen's it (PA_JACK_DYNAMIC), and only once Pa_Initialize runs, which is
    // already too late to catch its first complaint. So load it ourselves first and keep the handle: PortAudio's dlopen
    // then reuses the same library with our handlers in place. Absent libjack simply means no JACK host API.
    if (void* jack = dlopen("libjack.so.0", RTLD_LAZY)) {
        using JackLogSetter = void (*)(void (*)(const char*));
        if (auto setError = reinterpret_cast<JackLogSetter>(dlsym(jack, "jack_set_error_function")))
            setError(jackLogHandler);
        if (auto setInfo = reinterpret_cast<JackLogSetter>(dlsym(jack, "jack_set_info_function")))
            setInfo(jackLogHandler);
        // deliberately not dlclose'd: unloading would drop the handlers we just installed
    }
#endif
}

// The library is initialised on the backend's FIRST USE (finding the auto driver, listing, or opening), never by a
// product that merely links it: the Zoom L6 rule, and what makes a `null` run prove no other backend loaded. Guarded so
// a second call is free.
std::atomic<int> g_paState{0};  // 0 = never, 1 = initialising/ok, 2 = failed (file scope: the destructor reads it)

bool ensureInitialised() {
    std::atomic<int>& state = g_paState;
    int               was   = 0;
    if (!state.compare_exchange_strong(was, 1)) return state.load() == 1;
    quietenLogs();
    const PaError err = Pa_Initialize();
    if (err != paNoError) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] PortAudio: Pa_Initialize failed: %s\n", Pa_GetErrorText(err));
        state.store(2);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

/** What a callback reads: the host's pull and context. It is allocated before the stream opens (PortAudio needs the
 *  pointer at Pa_OpenStream time) and owned by the stream, so it outlives every callback the stream runs. */
struct Call {
    Pull  pull = nullptr;
    void* ctx  = nullptr;
};

class PortAudioStream final : public AudioStream {
public:
    PortAudioStream(PaStream* stream, StreamInfo info, std::unique_ptr<Call> call)
        : stream_(stream), info_(info), call_(std::move(call)) {}
    ~PortAudioStream() override {
        stop();
        if (stream_) {
            Pa_CloseStream(stream_);
            stream_ = nullptr;
        }
    }

    bool start(std::string& error) override {
        if (!stream_) {
            error = "PortAudio: the stream is not open";
            return false;
        }
        const PaError err = Pa_StartStream(stream_);
        if (err != paNoError) {
            // Into the status as well as the log: a device that opens and will not start is why a run is muted.
            error = std::string("Pa_StartStream failed: ") + Pa_GetErrorText(err);
            return false;
        }
        started_ = true;
        return true;
    }

    void stop() override {
        if (!stream_ || !started_) return;
        Pa_StopStream(stream_);  // blocks until the callback returns (joins it)
        started_ = false;
    }

    StreamInfo info() const override { return info_; }

    bool lost() const override {
        if (!stream_ || !started_) return false;
        // 1 = active, 0 = stopped, negative = the query itself failed: both of the last two mean nothing is pulling.
        return Pa_IsStreamActive(stream_) <= 0;
    }

    static int callback(const void*, void* output, unsigned long frameCount, const PaStreamCallbackTimeInfo*,
                        PaStreamCallbackFlags statusFlags, void* userData) {
        auto* call = static_cast<Call*>(userData);
        if (call && call->pull)
            call->pull(call->ctx, static_cast<float*>(output), static_cast<int>(frameCount),
                       (statusFlags & paOutputUnderflow) != 0);
        return paContinue;
    }

private:
    PaStream*                stream_ = nullptr;
    StreamInfo               info_;
    std::unique_ptr<Call>    call_;
    bool                     started_ = false;
};

class PortAudioBackend final : public AudioBackend {
public:
    ~PortAudioBackend() override {
        // Terminate exactly what ensureInitialised started, so a host that opens nothing never initialises the library
        // and a host that did gives it back. The latch goes back to NEVER, because a backend built after this one must
        // initialise the library again rather than believe the state a destroyed instance left behind.
        if (g_paState.load() == 1) Pa_Terminate();
        g_paState.store(0);
    }

    std::string id() const override { return "portaudio"; }
    std::string label() const override { return "PortAudio"; }

    std::vector<Driver> drivers() override {
        std::vector<Driver> out;
        if (!ensureInitialised()) return out;
        for (PaHostApiIndex i = 0; i < Pa_GetHostApiCount(); ++i) {
            const PaHostApiInfo* h = Pa_GetHostApiInfo(i);
            // A host API with no output device is no driver a user can pick: it would fail at the open.
            if (h && h->defaultOutputDevice != paNoDevice) out.push_back({driverId(*h), h->name});
        }
        return out;
    }

    std::string autoDriver() override {
        if (!ensureInitialised()) return {};
        const PaHostApiIndex idx = autoHostApiIndex();
        const PaHostApiInfo* h   = (idx >= 0) ? Pa_GetHostApiInfo(idx) : nullptr;
        if (!h || h->defaultOutputDevice == paNoDevice) return {};
        return driverId(*h);
    }

    Devices devices(const std::string& driver) override {
        Devices out;
        if (!ensureInitialised()) return out;
        const PaHostApiIndex idx = driver.empty() ? autoHostApiIndex() : hostApiForDriver(driver);
        out.names                = outputDevicesForHostApi(idx);
        out.defaultName          = defaultOutputName(idx);
        return out;
    }

    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx, std::string& error) override {
        if (!ensureInitialised()) {
            error = "PortAudio would not initialise";
            return nullptr;
        }
        if (debugEnabled()) {
            for (PaHostApiIndex i = 0; i < Pa_GetHostApiCount(); ++i) {
                const PaHostApiInfo* h = Pa_GetHostApiInfo(i);
                if (h)
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] host API %d: %s (type=%d, devices=%d, defaultOut=%d)\n", i,
                                 h->name, static_cast<int>(h->type), h->deviceCount, h->defaultOutputDevice);
            }
            for (PaDeviceIndex d = 0; d < Pa_GetDeviceCount(); ++d) {
                const PaDeviceInfo* di = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(d);
                if (di && di->maxOutputChannels > 0)
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] output device %d: [%s] '%s' (maxOut=%d)\n", d,
                                 Pa_GetHostApiInfo(di->hostApi)->name, di->name, di->maxOutputChannels);
            }
        }

        const PaHostApiIndex hostIdx = request.driver.empty() ? autoHostApiIndex() : hostApiForDriver(request.driver);
        if (hostIdx < 0) {
            error = "PortAudio: no driver '" + request.driver + "' with an output device";
            return nullptr;
        }
        PaDeviceIndex dev = paNoDevice;
        if (!request.device.empty()) {
            dev = findOutputDeviceByName(hostIdx, request.device);
            if (dev == paNoDevice)
                std::fprintf(stderr,
                             "[retroplug-sdl] audio: output device '%s' not found in the chosen driver, using its "
                             "default\n",
                             request.device.c_str());
        }
        if (dev == paNoDevice) {
            const PaHostApiInfo* hi = Pa_GetHostApiInfo(hostIdx);
            if (hi && hi->defaultOutputDevice != paNoDevice) dev = hi->defaultOutputDevice;
        }
        if (dev == paNoDevice) dev = Pa_GetDefaultOutputDevice();  // last resort
        if (dev == paNoDevice) {
            error = "PortAudio: no default output device";
            return nullptr;
        }

        PaStreamParameters out{};
        out.device                    = dev;
        out.channelCount              = request.channels;
        out.sampleFormat              = paFloat32;  // interleaved float, frame-major (what the pull writes)
        out.suggestedLatency          = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(dev)->defaultLowOutputLatency;
        out.hostApiSpecificStreamInfo = nullptr;
        // A block of 0 asks for the server's own quantum: what render-ahead wants, so a fixed-quantum server schedules
        // the callback at its cycle rather than at ours.
        const unsigned long callbackFrames =
            request.blockFrames > 0 ? static_cast<unsigned long>(request.blockFrames) : paFramesPerBufferUnspecified;
        auto      call    = std::make_unique<Call>();
        call->pull        = pull;
        call->ctx         = ctx;
        PaStream* stream  = nullptr;
        const PaError err = Pa_OpenStream(&stream, nullptr, &out, request.sampleRate, callbackFrames, paNoFlag,
                                          &PortAudioStream::callback, call.get());
        if (err != paNoError) {
            error = std::string("Pa_OpenStream(") + std::to_string(request.sampleRate) + " Hz, " +
                    std::to_string(request.blockFrames) + " frames, " + std::to_string(request.channels) +
                    " ch) failed: " + Pa_GetErrorText(err);
            return nullptr;
        }

        const PaDeviceInfo* deviceInfo = Pa_GetDeviceInfo(dev);
        StreamInfo          info;
        info.driver       = driverId(*Pa_GetHostApiInfo(hostIdx));
        info.device       = deviceInfo->name;
        info.channels     = request.channels;
        info.blockFrames  = request.blockFrames;
        info.sampleRate   = request.sampleRate;
        if (const PaStreamInfo* si = Pa_GetStreamInfo(stream)) info.sampleRate = static_cast<int>(si->sampleRate);
        // Wider than the device takes: legal on PipeWire (the stream carries its own layout), but only the pairs the
        // device has ports for are connected, and the rest wait for a patchbay. Say so, or "Out Channels: 8 and I only
        // hear the first pair" looks like a bug rather than a routing step.
        if (request.channels > deviceInfo->maxOutputChannels)
            std::fprintf(stderr,
                         // The em dash is the bytes today's line carries (U+2014), spelled as bytes so no compiler's
                         // execution character set decides what the output says.
                         "[retroplug-sdl] audio: '%s' takes %d ch \xE2\x80\x94 pairs beyond the first %d channel(s) "
                         "are "
                         "unconnected until you patch them (qpwgraph / your DAW)\n",
                         deviceInfo->name, deviceInfo->maxOutputChannels, deviceInfo->maxOutputChannels);

        return std::make_unique<PortAudioStream>(stream, info, std::move(call));
    }
};

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<AudioBackend> rp_portaudio_backend() { return std::make_unique<PortAudioBackend>(); }

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

for float32 output at an exact channel count with the frequency allowed to change (and adopted), maps `blockFrames 0`

````cpp
/** What a callback reads: the host's pull and its context. SDL hands the pointer back unchanged, and the device is
 *  closed before the stream goes, so it outlives every call. */
struct SdlCall {
    Pull  pull     = nullptr;
    void* ctx      = nullptr;
    int   channels = 2;
};

bool audioSubsystemReady() {
    // Once, and the failure is said once: a run whose audio subsystem will not come up would otherwise print the same
    // line on every listing and every open.
    static std::once_flag once;
    static bool           ok = false;
    std::call_once(once, [] {
        ok = SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_AUDIO) == 0;
        if (!ok) std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] SDL: audio subsystem init failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
    });
    return ok;
}

/** The drivers a user may pick: SDL's own list, less the `dummy` and `disk` test drivers, which exist for CI and for
 *  writing a file rather than for playing anything. */
std::vector<std::string> usableDrivers() {
    std::vector<std::string> out;
    if (!audioSubsystemReady()) return out;
    const int count = SDL_GetNumAudioDrivers();
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        const char* name = SDL_GetAudioDriver(i);
        if (!name) continue;
        if (std::strcmp(name, "dummy") == 0 || std::strcmp(name, "disk") == 0) continue;
        out.push_back(name);
    }
    return out;
}

/** The driver initialised right now, or "" when none is. SDL runs ONE audio driver at a time (SDL_AudioInit /
 *  SDL_AudioQuit), which is why a device list is real only for the active one. */
std::string activeDriver() {
    const char* name = SDL_GetCurrentAudioDriver();
    return name ? std::string(name) : std::string();
}

/** How many of this backend's devices are open right now. SDL runs ONE audio driver at a time and SDL_AudioQuit closes
 *  every device the process has open, so a driver may only be switched while this is 0: the host stops and closes the
 *  stream before it opens another. */
std::atomic<int>& openDevices() {
    static std::atomic<int> count{0};
    return count;
}

/** Initialise `driver` ("" asks for SDL's choice, which it makes once). Switching drivers means quitting the current
 *  one first, which is only legal with nothing of ours open (see openDevices): a listing never switches. */
bool ensureDriver(const std::string& driver, std::string& error) {
    if (!audioSubsystemReady()) {
        error = "SDL: audio subsystem initialisation failed";
        return false;
    }
    const std::string current = activeDriver();
    if (driver.empty()) {
        if (!current.empty()) return true;
        if (SDL_AudioInit(nullptr) != 0) {
            error = std::string("SDL_AudioInit failed: ") + SDL_GetError();
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    }
    if (current == driver) return true;
    if (openDevices().load() > 0) {
        error = "SDL: cannot switch audio driver to '" + driver + "' while a device is open";
        return false;
    }
    if (!current.empty()) SDL_AudioQuit();
    if (SDL_AudioInit(driver.c_str()) != 0) {
        error = std::string("SDL_AudioInit('") + driver + "') failed: " + SDL_GetError();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

class SdlStream final : public AudioStream {
public:
    SdlStream(SDL_AudioDeviceID device, StreamInfo info, std::unique_ptr<SdlCall> call)
        : device_(device), info_(info), call_(std::move(call)) {
        openDevices().fetch_add(1);
    }
    ~SdlStream() override {
        stop();
        if (device_ != 0) {
            SDL_CloseAudioDevice(device_);
            openDevices().fetch_sub(1);
        }
    }

    bool start(std::string& error) override {
        if (device_ == 0) {
            error = "SDL: the audio device is not open";
            return false;
        }
        SDL_PauseAudioDevice(device_, 0);
        started_ = true;
        return true;
    }

    void stop() override {
        if (device_ == 0 || !started_) return;
        SDL_PauseAudioDevice(device_, 1);  // returns once the callback is paused
        started_ = false;
    }

    StreamInfo info() const override { return info_; }

    bool lost() const override {
        if (device_ == 0 || !started_) return false;
        // SDL 2.0.4 and later report a removed device as no longer PLAYING.
        return SDL_GetAudioDeviceStatus(device_) != SDL_AUDIO_PLAYING;
    }

    static void SDLCALL callback(void* userData, Uint8* stream, int len) {
        auto* call = static_cast<SdlCall*>(userData);
        if (!call || !call->pull || len <= 0) return;
        const int frames =
            len / static_cast<int>(sizeof(float) * static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(1, call->channels)));
        // SDL has no "the device ran dry" flag: it hands a buffer to fill and never says whether it underran.
        call->pull(call->ctx, reinterpret_cast<float*>(stream), frames, false);
    }

private:
    SDL_AudioDeviceID     device_ = 0;
    StreamInfo            info_;
    std::unique_ptr<SdlCall> call_;
    bool                  started_ = false;
};

/** SDL's audio backend: one driver at a time, a float32 pull callback, the frequency allowed to change and adopted,
 *  the channel count exact (the engine renders for that width). */
class SdlBackend final : public AudioBackend {
public:
    std::string id() const override { return "sdl"; }
    std::string label() const override { return "SDL"; }

    std::vector<Driver> drivers() override {
        std::vector<Driver> out;
        for (const std::string& id : usableDrivers()) {
            // SDL's driver names are lowercase ids with no separate label ("pipewire", "pulseaudio", "wasapi"), so the
            // label is the id: the Driver row reads "SDL: pipewire", as the design's example does.
            out.push_back({id, id});
        }
        return out;
    }

    std::string autoDriver() override {
        if (usableDrivers().empty()) return {};
        std::string error;
        if (!ensureDriver("", error)) return {};
        return activeDriver();  // what SDL chose
    }

    Devices devices(const std::string& driver) override {
        // The list is real ONLY for the driver initialised now: SDL runs one at a time, and enumerating another would
        // mean SDL_AudioQuit + SDL_AudioInit, which closes every open device - the one thing a listing must never do
        // (the UI calls this several times per menu render). Every other driver answers empty, which the row shows as
        // "Default"; picking that driver opens it, and the host has stopped the old stream by then (design 5.1, R8).
        Devices out;
        if (!audioSubsystemReady()) return out;
        if (!devicesListableFor(activeDriver(), driver)) return out;
        const int count = SDL_GetNumAudioDevices(0);
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            const char* name = SDL_GetAudioDeviceName(i, 0);
            if (name) out.names.push_back(name);
        }
        // SDL 2.24 and later name the default device; the same shape as PortAudio's defaultOutputName, which is what an
        // empty device selection resolves to.
        char*         defaultName = nullptr;
        SDL_AudioSpec spec{};
        if (SDL_GetDefaultAudioInfo(&defaultName, &spec, 0) == 0 && defaultName) {
            out.defaultName = defaultName;
            SDL_free(defaultName);
        }
        return out;
    }

    std::unique_ptr<AudioStream> open(const Request& request, Pull pull, void* ctx, std::string& error) override {
        // The one call that may switch drivers: the host has stopped and closed the previous stream (a switch with
        // anything open is refused by ensureDriver), so nothing runs under the quit.
        if (!ensureDriver(request.driver, error)) return nullptr;

        SDL_AudioSpec want{};
        want.freq     = request.sampleRate;
        want.format   = AUDIO_F32SYS;
        want.channels = static_cast<Uint8>(request.channels > 0 ? request.channels : 2);
        // SDL has no "unspecified" block size: 0 means a value of SDL's. A request of 0 (render-ahead's) gets a small
        // power of two, and the obtained size is reported in StreamInfo either way.
        want.samples  = static_cast<Uint16>(request.blockFrames > 0 ? request.blockFrames : 512);
        auto call     = std::make_unique<SdlCall>();
        call->pull    = pull;
        call->ctx     = ctx;
        call->channels = want.channels;
        want.callback = &SdlStream::callback;
        want.userdata = call.get();

        SDL_AudioSpec     have{};
        bool              usedDefault = request.device.empty();
        const char*       deviceName  = request.device.empty() ? nullptr : request.device.c_str();
        SDL_AudioDeviceID id = SDL_OpenAudioDevice(deviceName, 0, &want, &have, SDL_AUDIO_ALLOW_FREQUENCY_CHANGE);
        if (id == 0 && deviceName) {
            // A saved name the driver no longer lists (a device unplugged, or a pick from another machine): say so and
            // use the driver's default, the same fallback PortAudio's backend makes. Muting for it would leave a user
            // with no sound and no obvious cause.
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] audio: output device '%s' not found in the chosen driver, using its "
                                 "default\n",
                         request.device.c_str());
            deviceName  = nullptr;
            usedDefault = true;
            id = SDL_OpenAudioDevice(nullptr, 0, &want, &have, SDL_AUDIO_ALLOW_FREQUENCY_CHANGE);
        }
        if (id == 0) {
            error = std::string("SDL_OpenAudioDevice('") + (request.device.empty() ? "default" : request.device) +
                    "') failed: " + SDL_GetError();
            return nullptr;
        }
        StreamInfo info;
        info.driver = activeDriver();
        // The name a choice can be saved as and reopened by: SDL's default device name where it has one, "" (the
        // driver's default) where it does not. "Default" was neither - open() cannot reopen it.
        info.device = usedDefault ? "" : request.device;
        if (info.device.empty()) {
            char*         defaultName = nullptr;
            SDL_AudioSpec spec{};
            if (SDL_GetDefaultAudioInfo(&defaultName, &spec, 0) == 0 && defaultName) {
                info.device = defaultName;
                SDL_free(defaultName);
            }
        }
        info.sampleRate  = have.freq;
        info.blockFrames = have.samples;
        // The channel count is exact, never allowed to change: the engine renders for this width.
        info.channels = have.channels;
        // A wide request against SDL's PipeWire driver is accepted at the API (the host renders this width, and it is
        // what StreamInfo reports) but the node SDL registers has 2 output ports, so only the first pair reaches the
        // sink - whether SDL mixes it or the server's stream adapter does is not established (design R11). PortAudio's
        // declared layout is the opposite: one port per channel, with the pairs beyond the device's own left
        // unconnected until they are patched, which is a routing step a user can see. This one is silent, so it says so.
        if (info.channels > 2 && info.driver == "pipewire")
            std::fprintf(stderr,
                         "[retroplug-sdl] audio: this %d-channel stream's PipeWire node has 2 output ports, so only the "
                         "first pair reaches the sink (Settings > Audio > Driver, PortAudio, is one port per channel)\n",
                         info.channels);
        return std::make_unique<SdlStream>(id, info, std::move(call));
    }
};

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<AudioBackend> rp_sdl_backend() { return std::make_unique<SdlBackend>(); }

}  // namespace rp::audio
````

Create `cmake/portaudio.cmake`:

````cmake
# PortAudio (deps/portaudio submodule, `pipewire` branch): the standalone's audio backend, behind the audio package's
# interface (packages/audio-portaudio, whose target links it; the plugin uses its DAW host's audio, and the CLI and the
# headless host name no audio backend at all). Static. Included at ROOT scope, BESIDE cmake/rtmidi.cmake and before
# cmake/packages.cmake, because a package's native/CMakeLists.txt is added while that list configures the packages and
# retroplug-audio-portaudio must find this target then. Its own cache options and probes (ALSA, PipeWire, JACK) run for
# every build, plugin-only included.
#
# The `portaudio` CMake auto-selects ALSA (dev present), the native PipeWire host API where libpipewire-0.3 is found,
# and JACK where jack dev is found. The Settings > Audio > Driver picker lists whatever host APIs end up compiled in here.
# libasound is still a DT_NEEDED of retroplug-sdl, but not through RtMidi any more: retroplug-audio-portaudio names
# ALSA itself (its quietening calls snd_lib_error_set_handler) and retroplug-midi brings its own through RtMidi.
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, so `portaudio` builds only because a product's audio backend links it.
set(PA_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_BUILD_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_BUILD_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
# We want PipeWire (native) + ALSA (fallback) + JACK. PortAudio auto-enables every host API whose dev libs it
# finds, and libsdl2-dev drags in libpulse-dev + libsndio-dev - so without these the binary ends up NEEDing
# libpulse / libsndio.so.7, which the muOS device doesn't ship (it failed to load there). Force them off.
set(PA_USE_SNDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_USE_PULSEAUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_USE_OSS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
# Load the three Linux backends with dlopen rather than linking them, so none of libasound.so.2 /
# libpipewire-0.3.so.0 / libjack.so.0 is a DT_NEEDED entry on retroplug-sdl. Compiling a backend in no longer
# means the binary refuses to START where that lib is absent (a PipeWire-less desktop, a JACK-less box, the
# muOS handheld); a missing lib now just omits that one host API from the Settings > Audio > Driver picker and
# leaves the rest working (the backends' *_Initialize soft-fail: *hostApi=NULL + paNoError, which Pa_Initialize
# skips). This is the runtime half of the same problem the PA_USE_* force-offs above solve at compile time, and
# it's why those are still needed: dlopen only helps for backends we actually want. libSDL2 stays linked: it is the
# window/input shell.
set(PA_ALSA_DYNAMIC ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_PIPEWIRE_DYNAMIC ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(PA_JACK_DYNAMIC ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
# With no launch penalty left, JACK needs no opt-in flag: `unset` clears any stale cached PA_USE_JACK so the
# fork's cmake_dependent_option(PA_USE_JACK ... ON JACK_FOUND OFF) re-decides on JACK_FOUND: compiled in
# wherever jack dev headers are present, and absent by construction where they aren't (the arm sysroot has
# none, so the handheld build is simply JACK-less, and it launches fine regardless).
unset(PA_USE_JACK CACHE)
add_subdirectory(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/portaudio ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/portaudio EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(portaudio)
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The app's audio: `AudioHost`'s calls, the client, and the hooks**

`main.cpp` loses the PortAudio enumeration, the callback, the pump, the quietening, `openAudio`, `reconfigureAudio`'s
body and the `audio.json` writer's shape; it gains the product's `AudioClient`: `prepare` re-rates, shapes and sizes
the engine and hands it back, `render` is today's `renderAudioBlock` unchanged, `release` drains the invoker.
`setupSdl` opens nothing; `main` reads the shim then applies; the frame loop calls `poll()`; the teardown calls
`stop()`. The two audio JS hooks are rebuilt over `AudioHost` with the LABEL shape TS's rows read
(`__rp_getAudioConfig` returns the drivers' labels and the devices keyed by them, `__rp_setAudioConfig` maps the label
through `choiceForDriverLabel`), so Settings keeps working until Task 5 replaces both sides; a run's `--audio-backend`
/ `RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND` beats any UI or saved choice (`AppState::backendOverride`), and `--block-size` /
`--render-ahead` override the saved choice for the run (E12).

````diff
+// __rp_getAudioConfig(): the shape the Settings > Audio rows read while this is the shim (audioDraft.ts,
+// nativeHooks.ts): { sampleRate, blockSize, outChannels, driver, drivers, devicesByDriver, defaultByDriver, autoDriver,
+// device, muted, error }.
+//
+//  - `drivers` is "Auto" plus one LABEL per driver of the backend IN FORCE ("PortAudio: PipeWire", "SDL: pipewire"):
+//    the backend names itself because two backends may call a driver alike, and only the backend in force is enumerated
+//    (asking another is its library's first use - the Zoom L6 rule).
+//  - `driver` is the SELECTED label: "Auto" when the choice is automatic, else the label of the chosen pair.
+//  - `devicesByDriver` / `defaultByDriver` are keyed by those labels (plus "Auto" for the automatic driver), and
+//    `defaultByDriver` is what an empty device selection resolves to, which the row shows beside "Default".
+//  - `autoDriver` is the driver label "Auto" currently resolves to, so the row can read "Auto (PipeWire)".
+//  - `device` is the CHOSEN name, "" for the driver's default: the RESOLVED device is the status's, and feeding it back
+//    as the choice would pin the concrete sink the session default happens to be today.
+JSValue jsGetAudioConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
+    JSValue o = JS_NewObject(ctx);
+    if (g_app) {
+        auto toArray = [&](const std::vector<std::string>& names) {
+            JSValue a = JS_NewArray(ctx);
+            for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < names.size(); ++i)
+                JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, a, i, JS_NewString(ctx, names[i].c_str()));
+            return a;
+        };
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "sampleRate",  JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqSampleRate));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "blockSize",   JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqBlockSize));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "outChannels", JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqOutChannels));
+        const rp::audio::AudioDescription described =
+            g_app->audio ? g_app->audio->describe() : rp::audio::AudioDescription{};
+
+        JSValue     drivers   = JS_NewArray(ctx);
+        JSValue     byDriver  = JS_NewObject(ctx);
+        JSValue     defaults  = JS_NewObject(ctx);
+        std::string selected  = rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel;
+        std::string autoLabel;
+        std::uint32_t at = 0;
+        JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, drivers, at++, JS_NewString(ctx, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel));
+        for (const auto& backend : described.backends) {
+            if (backend.id == "null") continue;
+            const std::string autoKey =
+                backend.autoDriver.empty()
+                    ? std::string()
+                    : rp::audio::driverChoiceLabel(backend.label,
+                                                   [&] {
+                                                       for (const auto& d : backend.drivers)
+                                                           if (d.id == backend.autoDriver) return d.label;
+                                                       return backend.autoDriver;
+                                                   }());
+            for (const auto& driver : backend.drivers) {
+                const std::string label = rp::audio::driverChoiceLabel(backend.label, driver.label);
+                JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, drivers, at++, JS_NewString(ctx, label.c_str()));
+                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, label.c_str(), toArray(driver.devices.names));
+                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, label.c_str(), JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
+                if (g_app->reqBackend == backend.id && g_app->reqDriver == driver.id) selected = label;
+                if (driver.id == backend.autoDriver) {
+                    // "Auto" resolves to this driver: the same devices and default, under the row the user picks.
+                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel, toArray(driver.devices.names));
+                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel,
+                                      JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
+                    autoLabel = driver.label;
+                }
+            }
+            if (!autoKey.empty()) autoLabel = autoLabel.empty() ? autoKey : autoLabel;
+        }
+        if (g_app->reqBackend == "auto") selected = rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel;
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "drivers", drivers);
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "driver", JS_NewString(ctx, selected.c_str()));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "devicesByDriver", byDriver);
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "defaultByDriver", defaults);
+        // The DRIVER's label, as the row shows it beside "Auto" ("Auto (PipeWire)"): what the row's bracket reads.
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "autoDriver", JS_NewString(ctx, autoLabel.c_str()));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "device",  JS_NewString(ctx, g_app->reqOutputDevice.c_str()));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "muted",   JS_NewBool(ctx, !described.status.error.empty()));
+        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "error",   JS_NewString(ctx, described.status.error.c_str()));
+    }
+    return o;
+}
+
+// __rp_setAudioConfig(sampleRate, blockSize[, outChannels[, driverLabel[, device]]]): apply a live device change through
+// AudioHost, which stops the stream, takes the engine back, opens the new request, re-rates to what the DEVICE obtained
+// and starts it - one pass, never a partial reconfigure. The chosen values are persisted (audio.json is the shim until
+// the TypeScript half owns the section).
+//
+// `driverLabel` is a label from `drivers` above: "Auto"/"" is the automatic choice, and "<Backend>: <driver>" is that
+// pair (rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel). An unknown label keeps the choice in force, so an Apply that changed only the
+// rate cannot mute the run by naming a backend that does not exist. outChannels is optional (an older bundle omits
+// it), and 2/4/6/8 - anything else keeps the current count.
+JSValue jsSetAudioConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
+    if (g_app && argc >= 2) {
+        int sr = 0, bs = 0, ch = g_app->reqOutChannels;
+        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &sr, argv[0]);
+        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &bs, argv[1]);
+        if (argc >= 3) {
+            int c = 0;
+            JS_ToInt32(ctx, &c, argv[2]);
+            if (c >= 2 && c <= 8 && (c % 2) == 0) ch = c;
+        }
+        std::string device = g_app->reqOutputDevice;
+        if (argc >= 5) {
+            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[4]);
+            device        = s ? s : "";
+            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
+        }
+        if (argc >= 4) {
+            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[3]);
+            const std::string label = s ? s : "";
+            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
+            // The row's label, mapped to the (backend, driver) an apply takes. A backend's library comes up here, which
+            // is a real use: the row offered it because the user asked for it.
+            const rp::audio::AudioDescription described =
+                g_app->audio ? g_app->audio->describe() : rp::audio::AudioDescription{};
+            const rp::audio::AudioChoice current{g_app->reqBackend, g_app->reqDriver};
+            const rp::audio::AudioChoice choice = rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel(label, described, current);
+            g_app->reqBackend                   = choice.backend;
+            g_app->reqDriver                    = choice.driver;
+            // The row's choice is the SAVED one; a run's --audio-backend still decides what this run opens.
+        }
+        if (sr > 0 && bs > 0) reconfigureAudio(*g_app, sr, bs, ch, device);
+    }
+    return JS_UNDEFINED;
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The engine-graph re-rate equality case**

The user's item 1 keeps the startup order (cores built at the default rate, re-rated once at `prepare`) and asks for
the case that holds it: a GB core and a NES core built at the default 48 kHz and re-rated to 44.1 kHz before their
first block render sample for sample what the same document built at 44.1 kHz renders over 40 blocks of 1024 frames,
EACH lane non-silent (the first version checked the mix, so a silent NES would have passed). If it failed, the
rendezvous would move before the autoload; it passes on the real engine, so the order stays.

````diff
diff --git a/packages/native/test/engine-graph/EngineGraph.test.cpp b/packages/native/test/engine-graph/EngineGraph.test.cpp
index ee7dabf96..1e8e3c5b5 100644
--- a/packages/native/test/engine-graph/EngineGraph.test.cpp
+++ b/packages/native/test/engine-graph/EngineGraph.test.cpp
@@ -229,6 +229,47 @@ TEST_CASE("a sample-rate change re-rates the running plan's cores", "[engine-gra
     CHECK(raw->sampleRate_ == 44100.0);
 }
 
+TEST_CASE("a core re-rated to 44.1 kHz renders what one built at 44.1 kHz renders", "[engine-graph][c4]") {
+    // The startup order the audio design keeps (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 6.6, report item 1): the
+    // engine is constructed and its cores are built at the DEFAULT rate, and AudioHost's prepare re-rates them once the
+    // device has opened at whatever rate it obtained. That is only sound if a re-rated core is the core it would have
+    // been built as, so this holds a GB and a NES to it: the same document, the same seeds, one run built at 44.1 kHz and
+    // one built at 48 kHz and re-rated before its first block, and the two streams must be identical sample for sample.
+    constexpr std::size_t kLane = 1024;  // one system's samples per block
+    auto renderAt = [](bool fromDefault) {
+        Engine e(fromDefault ? kRate : 44100.0);
+        rp::host::test::Roms roms;
+        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(request(e, roms, {{1, kGb}, {2, kNes}})).ok);
+        if (fromDefault) e.setSampleRate(44100.0);  // AudioHost's prepare, after the device obtained 44100
+        std::vector<float> lanes(2 * kLane);
+        float*             outs[2] = {&lanes[0], &lanes[kLane]};
+        std::vector<float> stream;
+        for (int block = 0; block < 40; ++block) {
+            std::fill(lanes.begin(), lanes.end(), 0.0f);
+            e.processBlock(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kLane), outs, 2);
+            REQUIRE(e.faultCount() == 0);
+            stream.insert(stream.end(), lanes.begin(), lanes.end());
+        }
+        return stream;
+    };
+    const std::vector<float> fresh  = renderAt(false);
+    const std::vector<float> rerated = renderAt(true);
+    REQUIRE(fresh.size() == rerated.size());
+    CHECK(fresh == rerated);
+    // Not silence, and EACH core's lane is not silence: the mix's non-silence alone would let a silent NES pass, and a
+    // core that goes silent after a re-rate is exactly what a rate the core never took looks like.
+    const auto sounds = [](const float* from, const float* to) {
+        return std::any_of(from, to, [](float v) { return v != 0.0f; });
+    };
+    bool gbLane = false, nesLane = false;
+    for (std::size_t at = 0; at + 2 * kLane <= fresh.size(); at += 2 * kLane) {
+        gbLane  = gbLane || sounds(fresh.data() + at, fresh.data() + at + kLane);
+        nesLane = nesLane || sounds(fresh.data() + at + kLane, fresh.data() + at + 2 * kLane);
+    }
+    CHECK(gbLane);
+    CHECK(nesLane);
+}
+
 TEST_CASE("bad tap requests are refused", "[engine-graph][b2]") {
     Engine e(kRate);
     rp::host::test::Roms roms;
````

The L6 rule, proved by reading and by a run: with `backend == "null"`, `AudioHost::openFor` skips every other backend
and `describe()` enumerates only the backend in force, so neither PortAudio's `ensureInitialised()` nor SDL's
`audioSubsystemReady()` is reached. The first run of the app with `null` pinned, under the `/dev/snd` guard and
`strace` (with the guard in front of `LD_PRELOAD`), shows the one `/dev/snd` path attempted is the sequencer. The
kit's copy of the shim is checked (and built from its own source if absent) first, because an `LD_PRELOAD` path that
does not exist is only a warning to ld.so and the run would then be unguarded.

Run: `bash -c 'test -s .superpowers/verify/nosnd.so || cc -shared -fPIC -O2 -o .superpowers/verify/nosnd.so .superpowers/verify/nosnd.c -ldl; test -s .superpowers/verify/nosnd.so && echo "the kit's guard is built"'`
Expected: `the kit's guard is built`: `.superpowers/verify/nosnd.so` is the kit's own copy of the shim, built from its `nosnd.c` (the kit builds it at the start of a run; this step builds it from that same source if it is absent), and every guarded command below preloads that exact path. From Task 6 the tracked `tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh` replaces it.

Run: `bash -c 'T=$(mktemp -d); RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND=null RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR=$T RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=20 LD_PRELOAD=$PWD/.superpowers/verify/nosnd.so NOSND_LOG=$T/nosnd.log strace -f -e trace=openat,open -o $T/strace.log build/bin/retroplug-sdl >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "non-seq: $(grep dev/snd $T/strace.log | grep -vc dev/snd/seq)"; echo "seq opens: $(grep -c dev/snd/seq $T/strace.log)"; echo "guard: $(wc -c < $T/nosnd.log) bytes"; rm -rf $T'`

No `/dev/snd/pcm*` path at all: the app on the null backend reaches no card. `grep 'dev/snd' f2-strace.log | grep -vc 'dev/snd/seq'   -> 0` is the prototype's own line.


An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), a fixed-length string.
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` replaces that string (`Mmm dd yyyy`) with `Nov  4 2026` before hashing, and this
plan's command does the same with `sed` and additionally COUNTS the string first (it must be exactly one, or the
normalisation would be guessing); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Expected: `1` then `38665e2c0199a5972a9accdb6851f30422a6d208246ce857435fd893214ee997  -`: the check image is the baseline's, byte for byte, so nothing portable moved.

````bash
feat(audio): the audio packages, AudioHost and AUDIO_BACKENDS

The SDL standalone's device stops being the product's: packages/audio holds the backend interface
(AudioBackend / AudioStream, a saved choice a plain file can carry by name and never a library's
numeric id), the null device (today's sleep-paced pump, as a backend) and AudioHost, which owns the
whole sequence once - stop, release, open, prepare with what the DEVICE obtained, start - so a
device that adopts another rate no longer plays an engine rendering at the rate that was asked for.
A failed open falls to the null device with a status (muted, and why), a lost device is the same
fallback from the UI frame, and a backend that never reports is caught by a no-pull watchdog
(a started device that runs no pull for a few block durations is lost). Render-ahead is ported from
feature/handheld-perf's 4b9e39ea8, backend neutral: a render thread fills a ring in the configured
block size, the pull only copies, and the stream opens with the server's own quantum. The five-second
stats line moves with it, and the log line keeps today's form and is byte-identical for PortAudio.

packages/audio-portaudio and packages/audio-sdl fill the interface: PortAudio's host APIs as drivers,
its devices by name, the ALSA/PipeWire/JACK log quietening and the wide-output warning, with the
static PortAudio added at root scope (cmake/portaudio.cmake) and ALSA linked by name on Linux; SDL's
audio drivers as drivers, one initialised at a time with the dummy and disk test drivers hidden, and
2, 4, 6 or 8 channels. Each initialises its library only on first use, and AudioHost::describe()
enumerates only the backend in force - so a run that pins the null device opens no audio library at
all (proved by a case and by an strace of the app under the /dev/snd guard: nothing but seq touched).

AUDIO_BACKENDS joins retroplug_product: a product names its backends by id, a manifest item carries
the factory and the id, the generated rp_product_audio_backends.hpp returns them in that order, and a
product that lists the package without naming it links neither PortAudio nor SDL audio. Four
configure refusals (an id no manifest declares, one named twice, one whose package the product does
not list, an item that is an audioBackend and an entry or a provider at once, and one on a device)
each have a fixture, and the generator has a positive control in the product-lists fixture.
retroplug-audio is an unlisted library target, linked by name, as retroplug-midi is; the desktop list
gains the three audio packages after core.

retroplug-sdl's audio region becomes the product's AudioClient (render is today's renderAudioBlock)
and AudioHost's calls; --audio-backend / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND picks the backend for a run,
--render-ahead starts the ring, and --block-size overrides a saved audio.json for that run.
sdl:smoke and sdl:controller pin the null backend and drop the stale SDL_AUDIODRIVER export, so
neither can open a real device. retroplug-audio-host-test holds the reconfigure order, the fallback,
the lost device, the watchdog, render-ahead against the in-callback stream across ragged pulls, the
single renderer and the description rule; the engine-graph suite gains the re-rate equality case a GB
and a NES core held to (built at the default rate and re-rated to 44.1 kHz against a fresh build).

The review's findings, amended in:

The Settings > Audio hook keeps the shape the TypeScript still reads (audioDraft.ts): the getter
publishes drivers as LABELS ("Auto", "PortAudio: PipeWire"), the selected label, devicesByDriver,
defaultByDriver, autoDriver and the CHOSEN device, and the setter's 4th argument is one of those
labels, mapped to (backend, driver) by rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel (packages/audio's AudioChoice
header, with its own cases). Before, the label went in as a backend id, so every Apply resolved to
"no audio backend 'Auto'" and fell to the null device: a rate change muted the standalone.

The SDL backend never switches the active driver while a device of ours is open: devices() answers the
real list only for the driver in force (devicesListableFor, held without SDL) and empty for the rest,
which is what the row shows as "Default"; only open() switches, and only with nothing open.

Render-ahead sizes its ring, resets its counters and starts the renderer BEFORE the stream starts
(4b9e39ea8's order), because a real device pulls the moment start() returns. The stream's state and
prepare come before the renderer exists.

AudioHost tunes the threads again, as 4b9e39ea8 did on Linux: the device callback at SCHED_FIFO 85
above the renderer's 80 under render-ahead (80 otherwise), both on the audio core, per THREAD rather
than once per process, best effort.

The watchdog starts its clock at start(), so a stream that starts and never pulls is caught, and its
bound scales with the block (max(250 ms, 4 x the block)). A stream that opens and will not start is
an open failure: the null fallback with the backend's own words in the status, the engine back with
the control plane. sameChoice compares the backend (PortAudio and SDL both name a driver "pipewire").
Whatever stream ends up running shapes the engine - the null fallback included, which renders in the
pull and is asked for the section's block. The stats are one thread's accumulator under render-ahead
(the renderer reports, the pull counts underruns into an atomic), and restore the average block and
the cumulative total. AudioHost has a log sink, and its lines are held byte for byte.

The minors: PortAudio driver ids from a fixed host-API type table (not display names), Pa_Terminate in
the backend's destructor, an inactive-or-failed stream counts as lost, the WASAPI note for the Windows
agent, the wide-output em dash kept as bytes; SDL's device name for a default request, an init failure
logged once; the em dashes gone from cmake/portaudio.cmake, its libasound note corrected; the no-op
REPLACE pair, the dead product-lists "holds" branch and the "backend-named" case that never existed
fixed, the product-level DEVICE + AUDIO_BACKENDS refusal and the missing-device and duplicate-id
manifest refusals given fixtures; stale comments and the over-long lines rewritten.

RED, the review's probes against the S2 code as it shipped (/tmp/f5bpro/red-s2, one program, the fake
backend only):

  probeC: apply=0 backend=fake error='' renders=0              (opens, will not start: neither live nor muted)
  probeD: prepare max=256, biggest render=512, backend=null    (render-ahead shaped the engine 256, null pulls 512)
  probeF (TSan): 3/3 runs report a data race in pull / reportStats   (two threads' accumulator)

With the fixes the same probes print: A `backend=null polls-fired=1 error='the audio device stopped
pulling'`; B `backend=other`; C `apply=0 backend=null error='the device would not start' renders=19`;
D `prepare max=256, biggest render=256`; F no ThreadSanitizer report in 10 consecutive runs. C3's own
probe (a fake stream that pulls from start()) reports `data race ... renderLoop` 3/3 against the old
order and passes against the new one. C1's is the smoke leg below.
````
