### Task 4: `main.cpp` split into the window, input, hooks and audio loop

Design section 5.5 and the design's stage S2b. `main.cpp` is a pure move into six files: `app.hpp` holds the process's
one state (`AppState`, `MidiClockSync`, `g_app`) and a declaration of every function one unit defines and another
calls; `window.cpp` takes the LVGL glue, `setupSdl`'s video and game controller, `setupUi`, `present`, the size latches
and the screenshot; `input.cpp` the key translation, the gamepad pump and `handleEvents`; `hooks.cpp` `callGlobal`, the
window hooks, the file dialog, the transport and clock hooks and the audio and MIDI row hooks; `audioLoop.cpp` the
product's `AudioClient`, the control-surface calls and the shims; `main.cpp` keeps the man page, the boot, `main`, the
`RETROPLUG_` hooks and the frame loop (the largest piece, so the file's history stays with it and no rename is needed).

Nothing was rewritten: of the old file's 1683 non-blank lines, 1680 appear verbatim in exactly one of the six, and the
three that do not are the anonymous-namespace braces no unit has any more. What was ADDED is only what the split needs:
`app.hpp`'s `#pragma once` and include block, one `#include "app.hpp"` per unit, the unit banners, the cross-unit
declarations, `extern AppState* g_app;` beside its definition, and `readReady`'s wrapper. Every cross-unit function has
external linkage: MSVC's C4505 (an unused static under `/W4 /WX`) would fail a helper used only in its own unit, so the
private helpers stay in an anonymous namespace per unit and the shared ones are declared in `app.hpp`. The namespace is
`retroplug::sdl` (the generic names - `present`, `setupUi`, `handleEvents`, `callGlobal` - must not sit at global
scope), and it is this task's: `app.hpp` includes neither generated product header (`main.cpp` alone does) and
`~AppState` is out of line.

This is the task the S2 report left undone ("NOT DONE, and the one real gap"), made its own commit so that the move
reviews as one diff.

**Files:**

- Create (5): `packages/native/sdl/app.hpp`, `packages/native/sdl/audioLoop.cpp`, `packages/native/sdl/hooks.cpp`, `packages/native/sdl/input.cpp`, `packages/native/sdl/window.cpp`
- Modify (2 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 1 under `packages/native/`; 1 under `packages/native/sdl/`)

- [ ] **Step 1: `app.hpp`: the shared state and the declarations**

`app.hpp` is the whole of the old `main.cpp`'s file-scope state, minus the audio members that are `AudioHost`'s now:
`AppState` with its engine, stores, providers, the midi stream, the clock sync, the flags and the request fields the
audio and MIDI hooks record, `extern AppState* g_app;`, and a declaration for every function another unit calls -
`present`, `setupSdl`, `setupUi`, `handleEvents`, `pumpGamepad`, `feedback`, the hook installers,
`ProductAudioClient`'s class and the boot's helpers. Its include block is the old file's own, with the platform guards
around `pthread.h` / `sched.h` / `unistd.h` and `SDL_MAIN_HANDLED` before `SDL.h`; nothing generated is included here.

Create `packages/native/sdl/app.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The SDL shell's shared declarations (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 5.5): the process's one state, its
// one instance, and the functions one unit defines and another calls. The split is a MOVE and nothing else: every
// definition still lives in the unit whose region of main.cpp it came from, and the includes below are the file's own.

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <deque>
#include <memory>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#if defined(__linux__)
#include <pthread.h>
#include <sched.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif

// We own main() (a plain console entry). On Windows/macOS SDL's <SDL.h> otherwise #defines main → SDL_main
// and pulls in the SDL2main entry shim (which we don't link — only SDL2::SDL2). Defining SDL_MAIN_HANDLED
// before the include keeps our main() intact on every platform; setupSdl() calls SDL_SetMainReady() to match.
// (Harmless on Linux, where SDL never redefines main.)
#define SDL_MAIN_HANDLED
#include <SDL.h>

#include "audio/AudioChoice.hpp"             // the Settings > Audio row's label, mapped to the choice it names
#include "audio/AudioHost.hpp"              // the host's audio: open/start/stop/reconfigure, the muted fallback

#include <rfl/json.hpp>  // audio.json / midi.json (device settings), tolerant JSON like the role-config crossing

extern "C" {
#include "lvgl.h"
}

#include "dpfjs/LvglJsEngine.hpp"            // LVGL display layer over the shared txiki host
#include "dpfjs/host/TjsHostRuntime.hpp"     // shared txiki/QuickJS host (+ tjs.h/quickjs.h)

#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "host/engine/EngineInvoker.hpp"
#include "host/input/GamepadManager.hpp"     // SDL controller poll (shared UI-thread input)
#include "host/input/GamepadPump.hpp"        // the event->bus switch, shared with the plugin editor
#include "midi/RtMidiBackend.hpp"           // systemMidi(): the process's one RtMidi system
#include "midi/MidiStream.hpp"               // the host's MIDI stream: virtual + hardware ports, the receive ring
#include "midi/PortFilter.hpp"               // kAllInputs, extractRealtime, scanSuspendsInputs
#include "host/devices/ProviderHost.hpp"     // the rp_device_host this product starts its providers with
#include "graph/desktop/Providers.hpp"       // rp::Providers, the product's started providers (one member of AppState)
#include "host/rpc/BackendRpcRegistration.hpp"
#include "host/ui/LvglWheelScroll.hpp"       // shared wheel -> hit-tested scroll (also used by the plugin/test UI)
#include "host/ui/SoftwareLvglDisplay.hpp"   // shared LvInputState + display/indev scaffold (also used by test/ui)
#include "TypedRpcServer.h"
#include "codecs/QuickJSCodec.h"
#include "transports/QuickJSTransport.h"

#include "native/components/component.hpp"   // GetWindowInstance() — the lv_binding_js React-tree root
#include "native/core/img/png/lodepng.h"     // lodepng_encode24_file (headless screenshot proof)

#include "host/ui/NativeFileDialog.hpp"      // OS-native file picker (pfd) backing __rp_openFileBrowser
#include "host/ui/OpenPath.hpp"
#include "host/QuickJsGlobals.hpp"
#include "host/HostServices.hpp"
#include "host/IdleReclaimProbe.hpp"     // the idle tick's smoke hook (RETROPLUG_IDLE_RECLAIM_TEST)

// The product's own names in one namespace: every symbol this shell exports is `retroplug::sdl::...`, so it cannot
// collide with a core, a package or a test binary's symbol of the same short name. main() is the one exception (the
// entry point), and it says so.
namespace retroplug::sdl {

// The embedded bytecode bundles (tjsc, rp_ prefix), generated by CMake — the SAME artifacts the plugin
// links: cp-bundle_data.c (control plane, composes the stores + __rp_* globals) and
// ui-bundle_data.c (the React UI, registers __rp_mountUI).
extern "C" {
extern const std::uint8_t  rp_cp_bundle[];
extern const std::uint32_t rp_cp_bundle_size;
extern const std::uint8_t  rp_ui_bundle[];
extern const std::uint32_t rp_ui_bundle_size;
}

// LVGL is built LV_GLOBAL_CUSTOM: the application must supply lv_global_default(). In the plugin DPF's
// LVGLWidget provides a per-instance one; standalone (single window, single runtime) we provide one

using BackendRpcServer = rpcpp::TypedRpcServer<rpcpp::Empty, rpcpp::QuickJSCodec>;

// Derives the host transport (BPM + playing) from incoming MIDI real-time bytes, so an external clock
// master drives LSDj sync-to-external (the rp.lsdj.sync node regenerates 0xF8 from Engine tempo/transport
// with its own tick clock - it doesn't read the raw wire clock, so feeding setBpm/setTransport is all it takes).
// Audio-thread-only: fed from audioCb, never touched elsewhere → plain members, no locking.
//
// Clock timing: RtMidi timestamps are discarded and messages arrive block-quantized, so we measure the
// pulse rate in audio frames accumulated across blocks (24 PPQN): BPM = 60·sr·pulses / (frames·24). Playing
// follows 0xFA/0xFB (start/continue) and 0xFC (stop), plus a ~0.5 s clock-presence timeout so a bare-clock
// master with no start/stop still plays. With NO clock at all we fall back to a free-running 120/playing
// (the standalone's prior always-on behaviour), so non-sync use (mGB, un-synced LSDj) is unchanged.
struct MidiClockSync {
    double sampleRate = 48000.0;
    long long frameClock = 0;      // monotonic frames processed
    long long lastClockFrame = 0;  // frameClock at the most recent 0xF8
    long long windowFrames = 0;    // frames accumulated in the current tempo window
    int  windowPulses = 0;         // 0xF8 count in the current window
    double bpm = 120.0;            // last good estimate
    bool active = false;           // clock seen within the timeout
    bool stopped = false;          // explicit 0xFC latch (overrides clock presence)
    bool debug = false;            // RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO: report each tempo estimate's inputs
    std::uint64_t droppedMessages = 0;  // the stream's ring drops, folded in so the report names the culprit
    bool manualPlaying = false;    // the local transport (Instance menu > MIDI Clock); used when no clock master
    double manualBpm = 120.0;      // the local tempo, likewise — what the sync roles clock at when we're the master

    static constexpr int    kWindowPulses = 24; // one quarter-note → a stable estimate ~2×/s
    static constexpr double kTimeoutSec   = 0.5;
    // The tempo range an estimate is trusted in — also what the local tempo is clamped to, so a hand-set
    // tempo and a measured one can't disagree about what counts as legal.
    static constexpr double kMinBpm = 20.0;
    static constexpr double kMaxBpm = 999.0;

    // One drained real-time byte. Returns true if it was a transport byte (so the caller skips staging it).
    bool onByte(std::uint8_t status) {
        switch (status) {
            case 0xF8: active = true; lastClockFrame = frameClock; ++windowPulses; return true; // clock
            case 0xFA: case 0xFB: active = true; stopped = false; lastClockFrame = frameClock; return true; // start/continue
            case 0xFC: stopped = true; return true; // stop
            default: return false;
        }
    }

    // Call once per audio block, after that block's bytes, with the block's frame count.
    void advance(long long frames) {
        if (active) {
            windowFrames += frames;
            if (windowPulses >= kWindowPulses && windowFrames > 0) {
                const double est = 60.0 * sampleRate * windowPulses / (static_cast<double>(windowFrames) * 24.0);
                if (debug)
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] clock: %d pulses / %lld frames @ %.0f Hz -> %.1f BPM"
                                 " (%.1f pulses/s, %llu message(s) dropped)\n",
                                 windowPulses, windowFrames, sampleRate, est,
                                 sampleRate * windowPulses / static_cast<double>(windowFrames),
                                 static_cast<unsigned long long>(droppedMessages));
                if (est >= kMinBpm && est <= kMaxBpm) bpm = est;
                windowPulses = 0;
                windowFrames = 0;
            }
            if (frameClock - lastClockFrame > static_cast<long long>(sampleRate * kTimeoutSec)) {
                active = false; stopped = false; windowPulses = 0; windowFrames = 0; // master gone → free-run
            }
        }
        frameClock += frames;
    }

    double outBpm() const { return active ? bpm : manualBpm; }
    // An external master wins while it is there; otherwise the local transport decides. That local transport
    // starts STOPPED, which is a change from the standalone's original always-playing behaviour: a running
    // transport is not idle state, it is a clock — the LSDj/risa sync roles turn it into link-port bytes, so
    // a SYNC=MIDI cart used to start running at 120 BPM the moment it booted, with nothing plugged in and no
    // way to stop it. Non-sync use (mGB, an un-synced cart) never looked at the transport and is unaffected.
    bool   outPlaying() const { return active ? !stopped : manualPlaying; }

};

// Whole-process state, reached by the LVGL indev read callbacks (via driver_data), the SDL audio
// callback (via userdata), and the __rp_* window hooks (single instance → a file-scope pointer is fine,
// unlike the plugin's per-context routing for multi-instance DAWs).
struct AppState {
    // --- the shared runtime + backend graph (PluginDSP's control plane) ---
    TjsHostRuntime host;
    // Three facets only, same as the plugin's channel — no debug, no audio-driver. See
    // host/HostServices.hpp for why those two are not members rather than merely unmounted.
    HostServices   svc;
    std::unique_ptr<rpcpp::QuickJSTransport> transport;
    std::unique_ptr<BackendRpcServer>        server;

    // --- the UI display layer (PluginUI), on the SAME host ---
    LvglJsEngine  ui{host};   // external-host ctor: adds only the LVGL layer, never shuts host down
    lv_display_t* display = nullptr;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> drawBuf;
    lv_group_t*   group = nullptr;
    lv_indev_t*   keypad = nullptr;
    lv_indev_t*   pointer = nullptr;

    // synthetic input state the shared keypad/pointer indev read callbacks pull from (driver_data == &input)
    retroplug::ui::LvInputState input;

    // A desktop file drag-and-drop in progress: SDL delivers one SDL_DROPFILE per file between
    // SDL_DROPBEGIN and SDL_DROPCOMPLETE, so we accumulate the paths here and emit one newline-joined
    // "file-drop" on complete (matching PluginUI::uiFileDropped — resolveDropAction needs ROM+.sav together).
    std::vector<std::string> dropBatch;

    // The in-flight OS-native file dialog (opened by __rp_openFileBrowser). Async: opened here, polled each
    // frame in the main loop (pollFileDialog), the pick delivered to JS on ready. Shared with the plugin host.
    retroplug::ui::NativeFileDialog nativeDialog;

    // --- SDL shell ---
    SDL_Window*   window = nullptr;
    SDL_Renderer* renderer = nullptr;
    SDL_Texture*  texture = nullptr;
    rp::audio::AudioHost* audio = nullptr;     // the device, its reconfigure and its muted fallback (main owns it)
    retroplug::GamepadManager gamepad;
    rp::midi::MidiStream midi{rp::midi::systemMidi()};  // in/out; drained into the Engine on the audio thread each block
    std::vector<rp::midi::MidiStream::Message> midiScratch;  // reused per block; reserved to the ring size in main()
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> midiStaged{0};             // count staged into the Engine (headless self-test)
    // midi.json's single `input` / `output` as the file spells them ("" = None, "*" = every device), because the shim
    // that reads and writes that file has to answer the Settings > MIDI pickers with one name until the selection is the
    // project's. The stream itself holds lists.
    std::string midiInputJson, midiOutputJson;
    MidiClockSync clockSync;                              // MIDI-clock → BPM/transport (audio thread only)

    // The local transport (Instance menu > Transport), across the UI/audio thread boundary. clockSync itself
    // is audio-thread-only, so the menu can't poke it: the UI writes the REQUEST, the callback folds it into
    // clockSync each block and publishes back what the transport actually is (an external clock master
    // overrides the local flag, and the menu shows that rather than lying about who is in charge).
    std::atomic<bool>  transportRequest{false};   // UI -> audio: the local play/stop the user picked
    std::atomic<float> clockBpmRequest{120.0f};   // UI -> audio: the local tempo (persisted in audio.json)
    std::atomic<bool>  transportPlaying{false};   // audio -> UI: what the Engine is actually being told
    std::atomic<bool>  transportExternal{false};  // audio -> UI: a MIDI clock master is driving it
    std::atomic<float> transportBpm{120.0f};      // audio -> UI: the tempo in force (theirs when external)

    // The device links the graph's hardware nodes bind (rp.host.devices/2), and the facets beside them: the ones the
    // providers of this product's packages install and mount (the N8 pack's streaming link, n8.cfg and the cart link;
    // the Launchpad pack's control-surface link and its port facet). svc (the engine) is declared above them (the
    // providers read its config dir), so it is destroyed after all of them. The destructor below reclaims the plans
    // first, while every member is still alive: a node may use its handle in destroy, and it must reach a live link.
    // The engine has no plan left to destroy by then.
    //
    // The three control-surface calls a provider makes are this product's (rp_provider.h): the claimed pair leaves the
    // shared MIDI stream before it is opened, a scan steps the stream's hardware inputs aside, and MIDI and audio wait
    // for the control plane's restore (see the definitions beside startAudio/stopAudio).
    rp::host::ProviderHost deviceHost{svc.engine, svc.host.configDir(),
                                      rp::host::ProviderHost::Calls{this, &AppState::onReserveMidi,
                                                                    &AppState::onSuspendInputs, &AppState::onRestored}};
    rp::Providers          providers;  // started in main, before the control plane can publish a graph
    // RETROPLUG_IDLE_RECLAIM_TEST: inert unless the smoke arms it. Holds this loop to the idle tick it owes the
    // engine (HostServices::reclaimOnIdle), which no in-process test can reach.
    retroplug::IdleReclaimProbe idleProbe;
    // Whether the control plane has reported its restored selection yet. main() holds MIDI and audio until it is true
    // (restoreControlSurface), so a restored surface's claim lands before the shared stream ever opens its ports; a
    // claim that arrives later is reserved through the stream's own handshake, which costs no audio stop either.
    bool controlSurfaceRestored = false;

    // Out of line in main.cpp, the one unit that includes the generated provider table: a unit that only uses AppState
    // reads no generated declaration.
    ~AppState();

    static bool onReserveMidi(void* ctx, const std::string& input, const std::string& output);
    static void onSuspendInputs(void* ctx, bool suspended);
    static void onRestored(void* ctx);

    std::uint32_t width = 640;
    std::uint32_t height = 480;
    bool running = true;
    // Fullscreen (the handheld): the WM owns a fixed panel, so the UI fits its grid via zoom and
    // __rp_setWindowSize is inert. Windowed (desktop): the window is ours to size, so it grows/shrinks to
    // the grid like the DPF standalone. Set from the SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN flag in setupSdl.
    bool fullscreen = false;

    // Window-geometry ownership — mirrors PluginUI's wmControlled_ / sizeHonored_ / requestedW/H latch, so the
    // resizable SDL window behaves like the DPF standalone under a tiling WM (Wayland/Hyprland). wmControlled
    // starts true for fullscreen and for the Wayland backend (see setupSdl - a Wayland compositor never tells
    // us whether it honored a resize); it also latches true when the compositor hands us a size we never asked
    // for (a tile) before any requested size was ever honored - then we stop driving SDL_SetWindowSize and the
    // UI fits its grid via zoom instead. sizeHonored proves the window is floating (a request took), which
    // vetoes the clamp latch so a spurious compositor resize isn't mistaken for a tiling takeover.
    bool          wmControlled = false;
    bool          sizeHonored = false;
    std::uint32_t requestedW = 0;   // last size asked of the WM (the clamp-detection baseline)
    std::uint32_t requestedH = 0;
    bool          debugResize = false;  // RETROPLUG_DEBUG_RESIZE: log every request / WM resize (WM debugging)
    bool          logWheel = false;     // RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_WHEEL: report each wheel event + whether it scrolled

    int    numOutputs = 2;         // what the device came up at (AudioHost prepared the engine for it)
    double sampleRate = 48000.0;   // obtained device rate (drives the Engine)
    int    reqSampleRate = 48000;  // requested (UI-configurable) rate + block + channels, persisted to audio.json
    int    reqBlockSize  = 512;    // low-latency default; low-power devices (the handheld) pass a bigger buffer
                                   // via --block-size (e.g. 4096) so the audio callback keeps its deadline
    int    reqOutChannels = 2;     // 2 = stereo mix (default); 4/6/8 = wide stems for a multichannel device
    std::string backendOverride;   // --audio-backend / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND: this RUN's backend, which no saved or
                                   // UI choice may move (the Settings row's Apply sets reqBackend, not this)
    std::string reqBackend;        // the backend the saved choice names ("" = auto): --audio-backend's
    std::string reqDriver;         // the driver's ID in that backend's vocabulary ("" = its auto driver)
    std::string reqOutputDevice;   // the device's NAME ("" = the driver's default device). Persisted to audio.json.
    int    renderAhead = 0;        // frames the render thread keeps queued (--render-ahead / RETROPLUG_SDL_RENDER_AHEAD)
    // audio scratch: `numOutputs` planar channel buffers (sized by prepare, so a block never allocates). The Engine
    // renders planar and routes each system to its pair per audioRouting; render() interleaves into the device's
    // buffer. numOutputs is what the device came up at, which the engine was shaped for.
    std::vector<std::vector<float>> audioPlanar;
    std::vector<float*>             audioPtrs;

    // Present only when LVGL actually redrew: the flush cb unions the changed area here; the loop skips
    // the SDL texture upload + blit entirely on idle frames (a static menu → ~0% CPU instead of a full
    // 640×480 upload every frame). dirty starts true so the first frame always shows.
    bool dirty = true;
    lv_area_t dirtyRect{0, 0, 0, 0};
};

/** The shell's one instance (single window, single runtime): the LVGL indev callbacks, the audio callback and the
 *  __rp_* window hooks all reach it, unlike the plugin's per-context routing for multi-instance DAWs. */
extern AppState* g_app;

// The audio device's configuration, and MIDI's: declared here so a hook (hooks.cpp) and the frame loop (main.cpp) can
// drive them, and defined beside the audio client (audioLoop.cpp).
// Audio device (re)configuration - declared here so the __rp_setAudioConfig hook (bound earlier) can drive a live
// sample-rate / block-size / backend change. AudioHost runs the sequence; these build its Config from the shim or the
// hook's arguments.
bool audioDebugEnabled();   // RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO
rp::audio::AudioConfig audioConfigOf(const AppState& a);
void applyAudioConfig(AppState& a);
void reconfigureAudio(AppState& a, int sampleRate, int blockSize, int channels, const std::string& device);
void loadAudioConfig(AppState& a);
void saveAudioConfig(AppState& a);
// MIDI device (re)selection - declared here so the __rp_setMidiInput/Output hooks (bound earlier) can apply a live
// change; defined next to the audio configuration. Neither stops audio: a selection change publishes a new output set
// and waits out one block (the stream's epoch handshake), and an input port cancels its own callback as it closes.
void selectMidi(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name, rp::midi::Apply mode);
void applyMidiSelection(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name);
void loadMidiConfig(AppState& a);

// Resize the window + everything that tracks its dimensions (the __rp_setWindowSize seam). Defined after the
// LVGL glue; declared here so the window hook can call it. Runs on the UI thread (same as present), so the
// texture/buffer/width swap is race-free.
void requestWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h);

// The smallest window we ask for / allow (mirrors the plugin's setGeometryConstraints). SDL clamps every
// SDL_SetWindowSize to this floor, so requestWindowSize has to clamp identically - see the comment there.
constexpr std::uint32_t kMinWindowW = 480;
constexpr std::uint32_t kMinWindowH = 432;

// What each unit holds: window.cpp (the LVGL glue, setupSdl's video and game controller, setupUi, present, the
// window-size latches, the screenshot), input.cpp (key translation, the gamepad pump, handleEvents), hooks.cpp
// (callGlobal, the __rp_* window hooks, the file dialog, the audio and MIDI hooks, installWindowHooks), audioLoop.cpp
// (the audio client, the control-surface calls, the audio and MIDI configuration), main.cpp (the boot, main, the
// arguments, the test hooks, the frame loop).
// The product's audio client: the engine behind AudioHost's interface (defined here because main() constructs it before
// the host, and its three methods live in audioLoop.cpp).
struct ProductAudioClient final : rp::audio::AudioClient {
    AppState* app = nullptr;

    void prepare(double sampleRateIn, int maxBlockFrames, int channels) override;
    void render(float* out, int frames) override;
    void release() override;
};


void        restoreControlSurface(AppState& a);
void        pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore();
bool        audioDebugEnabled();
bool        bootControlPlane(AppState& a);
bool        setupSdl(AppState& a);
bool        setupUi(AppState& a);
void        present(AppState& a);
void        applyWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h, bool fromWm);
void        onWindowSizeChanged(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h);
void        requestWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h);
void        handleEvents(AppState& a);
void        pumpGamepad(AppState& a);
bool        frameIsBlank(const AppState& a);
bool        writeScreenshot(AppState& a, const std::string& path);
void        installWindowHooks(JSContext* ctx);
void        pollFileDialog(AppState& a);
std::string callGlobal(TjsHostRuntime& host, const char* name, const char* arg);
bool        hasGlobalFunction(JSContext* ctx, const char* name);
void        setHostOutputs(AppState& a);

}  // namespace retroplug::sdl
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The window and the input**

`window.cpp` takes the LVGL glue LVGL calls back into, `setupSdl`'s video and game-controller half (the audio device
is Task 3's `AudioHost` and `setupSdl` opens nothing), `setupUi`, `present`, the window-size latches,
`pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore`'s UI half and the screenshot. `input.cpp` takes the key translation, `feedKey`,
`mapSdlKey`, the gamepad pump and `handleEvents`. Each keeps its own private helpers in an anonymous namespace.

Create `packages/native/sdl/window.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "app.hpp"

namespace retroplug::sdl {


// The SDL window: the LVGL glue LVGL calls back into, setupSdl's video and game controller, the UI mount, the frame's
// present, and the window-size latches a tiling WM makes necessary (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md 5.5).

// LVGL is built LV_GLOBAL_CUSTOM: the application must supply lv_global_default(). In the plugin DPF's
// LVGLWidget provides a per-instance one; standalone (single window, single runtime) we provide one
// process-wide instance, zero-initialized like DPF's calloc — lv_init() populates it. (Same pattern as
// RenderCore.cpp.)
extern "C" lv_global_t* lv_global_default(void) {
    static lv_global_t* g = static_cast<lv_global_t*>(std::calloc(1, sizeof(lv_global_t)));
    return g;
}

// ---- LVGL glue (mirrors RenderCore's non-GL subset) -----------------------------------------------

// Flush: in LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT the draw buffer already holds the full rendered frame; we just
// record which region changed (union across the refresh's flush calls) so the loop uploads + presents
// only that rect, and skips presenting entirely when nothing changed.
namespace {
// This unit's own glue: LVGL's display flush callback and its tick. Nothing outside window.cpp names them.
void flushCb(lv_display_t* disp, const lv_area_t* area, uint8_t*) {
    if (g_app && area) {
        if (!g_app->dirty) { g_app->dirtyRect = *area; g_app->dirty = true; }
        else {
            g_app->dirtyRect.x1 = std::min(g_app->dirtyRect.x1, area->x1);
            g_app->dirtyRect.y1 = std::min(g_app->dirtyRect.y1, area->y1);
            g_app->dirtyRect.x2 = std::max(g_app->dirtyRect.x2, area->x2);
            g_app->dirtyRect.y2 = std::max(g_app->dirtyRect.y2, area->y2);
        }
    }
    lv_display_flush_ready(disp);
}

// Keypad + pointer indev read callbacks live in host/ui/SoftwareLvglDisplay.hpp (shared with the test
// harness). AppState embeds retroplug::ui::LvInputState and hands &input to both indevs as driver_data.

// LVGL's tick source: real wall-clock ms so timers/animations run in real time.
std::uint32_t sdlTicksCb(void) { return SDL_GetTicks(); }
}  // namespace

bool setupUi(AppState& a) {
    lv_init();
    lv_tick_set_cb(sdlTicksCb);

    // Display + indevs: the shared software-LVGL scaffold (host/ui/SoftwareLvglDisplay.hpp), also used by the
    // headless test harness. SDL supplies its own dirty-tracking flush (present() uploads only the changed rect).
    auto sd = retroplug::ui::createSoftwareDisplay(a.width, a.height, a.drawBuf, flushCb, &a.input);
    if (!sd.display) return false;
    a.display = sd.display;
    a.group   = sd.group;
    a.keypad  = sd.keypad;
    a.pointer = sd.pointer;

    if (!a.ui.init()) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] LvglJsEngine init failed\n"); return false; }

    JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext();
    if (ctx && !hasGlobalFunction(ctx, "__rp_mountUI")) {
        if (a.ui.evalModuleBytecode(rp_ui_bundle, rp_ui_bundle_size) != 0) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] failed to eval UI bundle\n");
            return false;
        }
    }
    a.ui.attachDisplay(); // → __rp_mountUI

    // Black screen, stripped chrome, root pinned to 100% — same as PluginUI (shared with the test harness).
    retroplug::ui::applyChromelessScreen();
    if (ctx) installWindowHooks(ctx);

    // Headless proof of the OS-dialog seam. Reports whether __rp_openFileBrowser is bound + whether a desktop
    // helper is available; if one is (a real or a fake zenity/kdialog in PATH), it drives a real pfd request
    // whose pick pollFileDialog then delivers + logs — exercising the whole request→helper→parse→deliver path.
    if (std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_DIALOG_SELFTEST")) {
        const bool bound = ctx && hasGlobalFunction(ctx, "__rp_openFileBrowser");
        const bool avail = retroplug::ui::NativeFileDialog::available();
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] dialog self-test: __rp_openFileBrowser %s, helper %s\n",
                     bound ? "BOUND" : "MISSING", avail ? "available" : "absent");
        if (avail) a.nativeDialog.request("Self-test", "*.gb", false, "", "/tmp", false);
    }
    return true;
}

bool setupSdl(AppState& a) {
    SDL_SetMainReady(); // required when SDL_MAIN_HANDLED is set (see the <SDL.h> include note)
    // A stable application name → the Wayland app_id / X11 WM_CLASS, so a tiling WM's window rules can target
    // RetroPlug (e.g. Hyprland `windowrulev2 = tile, class:(RetroPlug)`). Set before SDL_Init.
    SDL_SetHint(SDL_HINT_APP_NAME, "RetroPlug");
    // Audio is PortAudio now (not SDL) — init only video + gamepad here.
    if (SDL_Init(SDL_INIT_VIDEO | SDL_INIT_GAMECONTROLLER) != 0) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] SDL_Init failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
        return false;
    }
    a.fullscreen = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_FULLSCREEN") != nullptr;
    // Resizable (not a fixed-size toplevel) so a tiling WM tiles the window instead of auto-floating it, and a
    // floating window can be dragged to any size — the DPF standalone is resizable for exactly this reason. A
    // fullscreen handheld ignores the flag. The min-size floor mirrors the plugin's setGeometryConstraints.
    Uint32 winFlags = a.fullscreen ? SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN : SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE;
    a.window = SDL_CreateWindow("RetroPlug", SDL_WINDOWPOS_CENTERED, SDL_WINDOWPOS_CENTERED,
                                a.width, a.height, winFlags);
    if (!a.window) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] SDL_CreateWindow failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError()); return false; }
    SDL_SetWindowMinimumSize(a.window, static_cast<int>(kMinWindowW), static_cast<int>(kMinWindowH));
    a.debugResize = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_DEBUG_RESIZE") != nullptr;

    // Seed the geometry-ownership state: fullscreen is WM-controlled from the start; arm the clamp baseline with
    // the initial size so the FIRST compositor resize that differs (a tile) is recognised as a WM takeover.
    //
    // Wayland is WM-controlled too, always. On X11 a resize request is VERIFIABLE: SDL_SetWindowSize round-trips
    // it and reports back the geometry the WM actually granted (X11_SetWindowSize waits on the server, then
    // sends RESIZED with the real size), so a WM that refuses is detected and adopted by onWindowSizeChanged.
    // Wayland has no such feedback - xdg-shell has no client resize request at all: we simply commit the size
    // we want, and the compositor either goes along with it (mutter/kwin) or keeps its own box and SCALES our
    // now-mismatched surface into it, sending nothing either way. Under a compositor that owns geometry
    // (Hyprland, sway, every tiling compositor) that scaling is what stretched a freshly loaded tile across the
    // whole window until the next real configure - a user resize - put surface and window back in step. Since
    // "honored" and "ignored" are indistinguishable from here, we don't guess: the compositor owns the window
    // and the UI fits its grid via zoom. RETROPLUG_SDL_FIT_WINDOW=1 opts back into driving the window size on a
    // compositor known to honor it.
    const char* videoDriver = SDL_GetCurrentVideoDriver();
    const bool  wayland     = videoDriver && SDL_strcmp(videoDriver, "wayland") == 0;
    const bool  forceFit    = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_FIT_WINDOW") != nullptr;
    a.wmControlled = a.fullscreen || (wayland && !forceFit);
    a.requestedW = a.width;
    a.requestedH = a.height;
    if (a.debugResize)
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] video driver '%s' - window geometry %s\n",
                     videoDriver ? videoDriver : "?", a.wmControlled ? "owned by the WM" : "ours to size");
    a.renderer = SDL_CreateRenderer(a.window, -1, SDL_RENDERER_SOFTWARE);
    if (!a.renderer) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] SDL_CreateRenderer failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError()); return false; }
    a.texture = SDL_CreateTexture(a.renderer, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888, SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_STREAMING,
                                  a.width, a.height);
    if (!a.texture) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] SDL_CreateTexture failed: %s\n", SDL_GetError()); return false; }

    // No audio device is opened here: setupSdl initialises video and the game controller, and AudioHost opens the
    // device after the persisted settings are read (main's audio step), so a run that names the null backend touches no
    // audio library at all. The backends initialise their own library at first use.
    return true;
}

void present(AppState& a) {
    if (!a.dirty) return; // nothing redrew this frame — leave the screen as-is (huge idle CPU saving)
    const int stride = static_cast<int>(lv_draw_buf_width_to_stride(a.width, lv_display_get_color_format(a.display)));
    // Upload only the changed region (clamped) from the draw buffer; the streaming texture keeps the rest.
    int x1 = std::max(0, (int)a.dirtyRect.x1), y1 = std::max(0, (int)a.dirtyRect.y1);
    int x2 = std::min((int)a.width - 1, (int)a.dirtyRect.x2), y2 = std::min((int)a.height - 1, (int)a.dirtyRect.y2);
    if (x2 >= x1 && y2 >= y1) {
        SDL_Rect rect{x1, y1, x2 - x1 + 1, y2 - y1 + 1};
        const std::uint8_t* src = a.drawBuf.data() + static_cast<std::size_t>(y1) * stride + static_cast<std::size_t>(x1) * 4;
        SDL_UpdateTexture(a.texture, &rect, src, stride);
    }
    SDL_RenderCopy(a.renderer, a.texture, nullptr, nullptr);
    SDL_RenderPresent(a.renderer);
    a.dirty = false;
}

// Adopt an actual window size — resize every dimension-tracking resource in lockstep: the SDL window (only
// when WE initiated it; a WM-driven change already sized the window), the LVGL display resolution + its
// DIRECT-mode draw buffer, and the streaming SDL texture (a STREAMING texture can't resize in place —
// recreate it). Then force a full-window redraw and tell the UI so it re-lays-out. This inlines what DPF's
// platform resize callback does for the plugin (LVGL::recreateTextureData + emit "resize").
void applyWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h, bool fromWm) {
    if (!a.window || !a.display || !a.renderer) return;
    if (w == a.width && h == a.height && a.texture) return; // already at this size — nothing to realloc

    if (!fromWm) SDL_SetWindowSize(a.window, static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(h)); // ask the WM

    // LVGL display: set the new resolution, then re-point it at a freshly sized DIRECT buffer.
    const lv_color_format_t cf = lv_display_get_color_format(a.display);
    const std::uint32_t stride = lv_draw_buf_width_to_stride(w, cf);
    a.drawBuf.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(stride) * h, 0);
    lv_display_set_resolution(a.display, w, h);
    lv_display_set_buffers(a.display, a.drawBuf.data(), nullptr, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(a.drawBuf.size()), LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT);

    // SDL streaming texture: recreate at the new size (can't be resized in place).
    if (a.texture) SDL_DestroyTexture(a.texture);
    a.texture = SDL_CreateTexture(a.renderer, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888, SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_STREAMING,
                                  static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(h));

    a.width = w;
    a.height = h;
    a.dirty = true; // present the whole new surface next frame (lv_timer_handler redraws into the new buffer)
    a.dirtyRect = {0, 0, static_cast<std::int32_t>(w) - 1, static_cast<std::int32_t>(h) - 1};

    if (JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext()) { // mirror PluginUI::onResize → the UI re-reads Dimensions.window
        JSValue args[2] = {JS_NewUint32(ctx, w), JS_NewUint32(ctx, h)};
        a.ui.emit("resize", 2, args);
        JS_FreeValue(ctx, args[0]);
        JS_FreeValue(ctx, args[1]);
    }
}

// The __rp_setWindowSize seam: the UI asks the WM for a w×h window (grow/shrink to the grid). Mirrors
// PluginUI::requestWindowSize — record the request as the clamp baseline, but don't fight a WM that owns
// geometry (a tiling compositor or a fullscreen handheld); there the UI fits its grid via zoom instead.
void requestWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h) {
    // Clamp to the window minimum FIRST, because SDL_SetWindowSize does: a 1x/2x grid (160x144 / 320x288) is
    // below the floor, so the window can only ever become 480x432. Applying the raw request would size the
    // LVGL surface to something the window never takes - and a surface that doesn't match the window is
    // exactly what a compositor scales to fit, which is how a freshly loaded tile ended up stretched across
    // the whole window. The clamped size also has to be what we RECORD, or it comes back through
    // onWindowSizeChanged as "a size we never asked for", i.e. a tiling takeover, wrongly latching
    // wmControlled and killing fit-to-grid for the rest of the session.
    w = std::max(w, kMinWindowW);
    h = std::max(h, kMinWindowH);
    a.requestedW = w; // recorded even when WM-controlled, so onWindowSizeChanged can still latch sizeHonored
    a.requestedH = h;
    if (a.wmControlled) {
        if (a.debugResize)
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] resize request %ux%u ignored (WM owns geometry)\n", w, h);
        return;
    }
    applyWindowSize(a, w, h, /*fromWm=*/false);
}

// SDL_WINDOWEVENT_SIZE_CHANGED: the actual window size changed (our SDL_SetWindowSize, a user drag, or a
// tiling-WM tile). Mirrors PluginUI::onResize — latch sizeHonored when the WM grants a size we asked for
// (proof the window is floating, ours to size), and detect a tiling takeover: a size we never requested,
// before any request was ever honored, means the compositor owns geometry, so latch wmControlled and stop
// driving SDL_SetWindowSize (fullscreen is already wmControlled). Then adopt the new size.
void onWindowSizeChanged(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h) {
    if (a.requestedW != 0 && a.requestedH != 0 && w == a.requestedW && h == a.requestedH) a.sizeHonored = true;
    if (!a.wmControlled && !a.sizeHonored && a.requestedW != 0 && a.requestedH != 0 &&
        (w != a.requestedW || h != a.requestedH)) {
        a.wmControlled = true;
        if (a.debugResize)
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] WM owns geometry (tiled): got %ux%u, never asked for it\n", w, h);
    }
    if (a.debugResize)
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] onResize %ux%u (req %ux%u wmC=%d honored=%d)\n", w, h, a.requestedW,
                     a.requestedH, (int)a.wmControlled, (int)a.sizeHonored);
    applyWindowSize(a, w, h, /*fromWm=*/true);
}

bool writeScreenshot(AppState& a, const std::string& path) {
    if (!a.display || a.drawBuf.empty()) return false;
    const std::uint32_t w = a.width, h = a.height;
    const std::uint32_t stride = lv_draw_buf_width_to_stride(w, lv_display_get_color_format(a.display));
    std::vector<unsigned char> rgb(static_cast<std::size_t>(w) * h * 3);
    for (std::uint32_t y = 0; y < h; ++y)
        for (std::uint32_t x = 0; x < w; ++x) {
            const std::uint8_t* px = a.drawBuf.data() + static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * stride + x * 4;
            unsigned char* out = rgb.data() + (static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + x) * 3;
            out[0] = px[2]; out[1] = px[1]; out[2] = px[0]; // ARGB8888 (B,G,R,A) -> R,G,B
        }
    const unsigned err = lodepng_encode24_file(path.c_str(), rgb.data(), w, h);
    if (err) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] screenshot error %u\n", err); return false; }
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] screenshot -> %s (%ux%u)\n", path.c_str(), w, h);
    return true;
}

// ---- screenshot (headless proof) ------------------------------------------------------------------
// Dump the display's composited draw buffer (the exact frame presented, including top-layer overlays
// like the file browser) so a headless run (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen) can screenshot for a test.
bool writeScreenshot(AppState& a, const std::string& path);

// True if the rendered frame is a single flat colour (nothing drew) — the CI smoke's "the UI actually
// rendered, not just booted" gate. Compares the draw buffer as 32-bit pixels against the first.
bool frameIsBlank(const AppState& a) {
    if (a.drawBuf.size() < 8) return true;
    const auto* px = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint32_t*>(a.drawBuf.data());
    const std::size_t n = a.drawBuf.size() / 4;
    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) if (px[i] != px[0]) return false;
    return true;
}

}  // namespace retroplug::sdl
````

````cpp
#include "app.hpp"

namespace retroplug::sdl {


// Input: SDL keyboard and gamepad to the LVGL keypad indev and the JS buses, and the SDL event loop (docs/modular-
// graph-phase-f5b-design.md 5.5).

// ---- input translation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Push an LVGL key onto the keypad queue AND emit the "key" JS bus (press+release), mirroring
// RenderCore::tapKey / PluginUI::onKeyboard. dpf is the DPF keycode the TS input layer expects.
// SDL's modifier state -> DPF's Modifier mask (dgl/Base.hpp), which is what the "key" bus carries.
// The bus is shared with the plugin host, so the mask has to mean the same thing on both sides.
namespace {
// Key translation: this unit's alone, and the only place an SDL keycode becomes an LVGL one.
std::uint32_t dpfModsFromSdl(std::uint16_t sdlMod) {
    std::uint32_t mods = 0;
    if (sdlMod & KMOD_SHIFT) mods |= 1U << 0U; // kModifierShift
    if (sdlMod & KMOD_CTRL)  mods |= 1U << 1U; // kModifierControl
    if (sdlMod & KMOD_ALT)   mods |= 1U << 2U; // kModifierAlt
    if (sdlMod & KMOD_GUI)   mods |= 1U << 3U; // kModifierSuper
    return mods;
}

void feedKey(AppState& a, std::uint32_t lvKey, std::uint32_t dpf, bool press, std::uint32_t mods) {
    JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext();
    if (press && lvKey != 0) a.input.keyQueue.push_back(lvKey);  // only real LVGL nav keys reach the keypad indev
    if (ctx) {
        // THREE args, matching PluginUI. DPF gives the unshifted code point ('a' for the A key whether or
        // not Shift is down), so the modifier mask is the only way the prompt text-input can apply
        // Shift -> uppercase - Menu.tsx's key handler takes it as `mod = 0` (NativeEvents in
        // useNativeEvent.ts types the channel). This emitted two args for a long time, so that default
        // silently made Shift a no-op in the standalone while it worked in the DAW.
        JSValue args[3] = {JS_NewUint32(ctx, dpf), JS_NewBool(ctx, press), JS_NewUint32(ctx, mods)};
        a.ui.emit("key", 3, args);
        for (JSValue& v : args) JS_FreeValue(ctx, v);
    }
}

// Map an SDL keysym to (LVGL key, DPF keycode). The DPF code is what the TS input layer (keyCodes.ts)
// expects on the "key" bus: arrows in the 0xE03x band, ShiftL/R at 0xE051/2, and — crucially — printable
// keys carry their ASCII code verbatim (dpfCodeToKeyName does String.fromCharCode). Only the navigation
// keys get a real LVGL keypad code (`lv`); everything else is bus-only (lv = 0) — game buttons, capture,
// and app actions all live on the "key" bus, not the keypad. Returns false for keys we don't translate.
//
// This must cover every key the default bindings use (bindingMap.ts): dpad = arrows, A = Z, B = X,
// Start = Enter, Select = ShiftL/ShiftR/Backspace — plus anything the user might rebind to. Previously only
// arrows/Enter/Esc were mapped, so A/B/Select (and any letter/modifier binding) never reached the emulator
// OR the key-capture editor.
bool mapSdlKey(SDL_Keycode k, std::uint32_t& lv, std::uint32_t& dpf) {
    lv = 0;
    switch (k) {
        case SDLK_UP:       lv = LV_KEY_UP;    dpf = 0xE036; return true;
        case SDLK_DOWN:     lv = LV_KEY_DOWN;  dpf = 0xE038; return true;
        case SDLK_RIGHT:    lv = LV_KEY_RIGHT; dpf = 0xE037; return true;
        case SDLK_LEFT:     lv = LV_KEY_LEFT;  dpf = 0xE035; return true;
        case SDLK_RETURN:   lv = LV_KEY_ENTER; dpf = 0x0D;   return true;
        case SDLK_KP_ENTER: lv = LV_KEY_ENTER; dpf = 0x0D;   return true;
        case SDLK_ESCAPE:   lv = LV_KEY_ESC;   dpf = 0x1B;   return true;
        // Bus-only keys (no keypad nav): the GB Select defaults + editor keys.
        case SDLK_LSHIFT:   dpf = 0xE051; return true;   // ShiftL
        case SDLK_RSHIFT:   dpf = 0xE052; return true;   // ShiftR
        case SDLK_BACKSPACE:dpf = 0x08;   return true;   // Backspace (Select default; clears a capture row)
        case SDLK_TAB:      dpf = 0x09;   return true;   // Tab (default Cycle-Instances app action)
        case SDLK_PAGEUP:   dpf = 0xE031; return true;   // menu coarse-step
        case SDLK_PAGEDOWN: dpf = 0xE032; return true;
        default:
            // Printable ASCII (letters/digits/punctuation/space): SDL's keycode IS the ASCII code, which is
            // exactly the DPF/DGL "key" bus convention. Covers A=Z, B=X and anything the user rebinds to.
            if (k >= 0x20 && k <= 0x7e) { dpf = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(k); return true; }
            return false;
    }
}

// Poll controllers once per frame → re-emit each transition onto the gamepad-* JS bus (exactly as
// PluginUI::pumpGamepad). The gamepad drives BOTH menu navigation and in-game input purely through this
// bus: the React Menu has its own gamepad handler, and the design contract is that the gamepad bus never
// reaches the LVGL keypad indev (Menu.tsx). So we must NOT also translate gamepad → keypad here — doing
// so double-drives the menu (every move counted twice) while leaving in-game input single (the keypad
// keys hit the idle focus sink). Keyboard still feeds the keypad (mapSdlKey/feedKey) for desktop use.
}  // namespace

void pumpGamepad(AppState& a) { pumpGamepadInto(a.gamepad, a.ui, a.ui.getContext()); }

void handleEvents(AppState& a) {
    SDL_Event ev;
    while (SDL_PollEvent(&ev)) {
        switch (ev.type) {
            // OS window-close (window button / WM / Ctrl-C) → route through the unsaved-changes guard, exactly
            // as the DPF standalone's PluginUI::onClose does (and the Exit menu row already does via JS). The
            // JS guard returns true to veto (it raises the save prompt and later calls __rp_quitWindow itself
            // once the user confirms Save/Discard); false = clean project, quit now. Without this, closing a
            // dirty project by the window button would skip the prompt and lose work.
            case SDL_QUIT: {
                // No allowClose_ latch here: jsQuitWindow just clears `running`, so this never re-enters.
                if (!jsCloseVetoed(a.ui.getContext())) a.running = false;
                break;
            }
            // Desktop drag-and-drop → the "file-drop" JS bus (mirrors PluginUI::uiFileDropped). SDL2's
            // SDL_DropEvent carries no coordinates (the x/y fields are SDL3-only) and one path per event, so
            // we batch across begin→complete and read the cursor ourselves for the tile hit-test.
            case SDL_DROPBEGIN: a.dropBatch.clear(); break;
            case SDL_DROPFILE:
                if (ev.drop.file) { a.dropBatch.emplace_back(ev.drop.file); SDL_free(ev.drop.file); }
                break;
            case SDL_DROPCOMPLETE:
                if (JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext(); ctx && !a.dropBatch.empty()) {
                    std::string joined;
                    for (const std::string& p : a.dropBatch) { if (!joined.empty()) joined += '\n'; joined += p; }
                    int mx = 0, my = 0;
                    SDL_GetMouseState(&mx, &my); // window-pixel space — the coords hitTestTile expects (best-effort)
                    JSValue args[3] = {JS_NewString(ctx, joined.c_str()),
                                       JS_NewFloat64(ctx, mx), JS_NewFloat64(ctx, my)};
                    a.ui.emit("file-drop", 3, args);
                    for (JSValue& v : args) JS_FreeValue(ctx, v);
                }
                a.dropBatch.clear();
                break;
            case SDL_KEYDOWN:
            case SDL_KEYUP: {
                std::uint32_t lv, dpf;
                if (mapSdlKey(ev.key.keysym.sym, lv, dpf))
                    feedKey(a, lv, dpf, ev.type == SDL_KEYDOWN, dpfModsFromSdl(ev.key.keysym.mod));
                break;
            }
            // The WM/user resized the window (a drag-grip resize, or a tiling compositor tiling us) → adopt the
            // new size + run the tiling-clamp detection. SIZE_CHANGED fires for both API- and WM-driven changes.
            case SDL_WINDOWEVENT:
                if (ev.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_SIZE_CHANGED)
                    onWindowSizeChanged(a, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ev.window.data1),
                                        static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ev.window.data2));
                break;
            case SDL_MOUSEMOTION: a.input.mousePos = {ev.motion.x, ev.motion.y}; break;
            case SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN:
            case SDL_MOUSEBUTTONUP:
                a.input.mousePos = {ev.button.x, ev.button.y};
                a.input.mouseDown = ev.type == SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN;
                break;
            // Wheel -> scroll the scrollable ancestor under the cursor (the overflowing menu), the same
            // shared hit-test scroll PluginUI::onScroll runs for the DPF editor. Without this the wheel was
            // simply dead in the standalone: LVGL has no wheel handling of its own. We're on the UI thread
            // here, which is also the one running lv_timer_handler, so scrolling from here is safe.
            case SDL_MOUSEWHEEL: {
                float wx = static_cast<float>(ev.wheel.x), wy = static_cast<float>(ev.wheel.y);
#if SDL_VERSION_ATLEAST(2, 0, 18)
                // Trackpads / high-resolution wheels report sub-notch deltas here (the integer x/y are the
                // accumulated whole notches, and stay 0 until a full one builds up).
                if (ev.wheel.preciseX != 0.0f || ev.wheel.preciseY != 0.0f) {
                    wx = ev.wheel.preciseX;
                    wy = ev.wheel.preciseY;
                }
#endif
                if (ev.wheel.direction == SDL_MOUSEWHEEL_FLIPPED) { wx = -wx; wy = -wy; }
                // SDL2's wheel event carries no position (mouseX/mouseY are SDL3-only). Use the
                // motion-tracked cursor rather than SDL_GetMouseState: it's the same point the pointer indev
                // hovers with, so the wheel scrolls exactly what's highlighted under it (and a synthetic
                // motion event can drive it headlessly). Window-pixel space == LVGL display space.
                const lv_point_t& p = a.input.mousePos;
                const bool scrolled = retroplug::ui::scrollAtPoint(p.x, p.y, wx, wy);
                if (a.logWheel)
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] wheel: notches=(%.2f,%.2f) at (%d,%d) scrolled=%d\n",
                                 wx, wy, p.x, p.y, static_cast<int>(scrolled));
                break;
            }
            default: break;
        }
    }
}

}  // namespace retroplug::sdl
````

````cpp
#include "app.hpp"

namespace retroplug::sdl {


// The __rp_* window hooks: the seam the UI optional-chains for the window, the file dialog, the transport, the audio and
// MIDI device rows, and the install that binds them (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md 5.5).

// ---- backend boot (PluginDSP::bootControlPlane, DPF-free) ------------------------------------------

// Call globalThis[name](arg?) on the control-plane context (main thread). Returns the string result, or
// "" for non-string / missing / exception. Shared with PluginDSP::callGlobal.
//
// `ready` is true unconditionally here, and that is not laziness: bootControlPlane returns false if the
// host fails to initialise OR the bundle never signals ready, and main exits 1 on either. An unready SDL
// host is a dead process, so by the time anything calls this there is nothing to guard against. The
// plugin cannot take that route - a DAW scan must degrade rather than exit - which is why the shared
// body carries the guard and this caller opts out of it explicitly.
std::string callGlobal(TjsHostRuntime& host, const char* name, const char* arg) {
    JsGlobals g{ host.context(), /*ready=*/true,
                 [](const char* n, const char* detail) {
                     std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] %s threw: %s\n", n, detail);
                 } };
    return jsCallGlobal(g, name, arg);
}

bool hasGlobalFunction(JSContext* ctx, const char* name) { return jsHasGlobalFunction(ctx, name); }

// Tell the control plane how many output channels the device has: it builds the graph's output wiring for
// that many. Before the audio thread takes the Engine, so the plan it publishes applies at once.
void setHostOutputs(AppState& a) {
    if (callGlobal(a.host, "__rp_setHostOutputs", std::to_string(a.numOutputs).c_str()) != "true")
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] the %d-output host shape did not plan; the outputs keep the shape before it\n",
                     a.numOutputs);
}

// ---- __rp_* window hooks (PluginUI's window-op seam, single-instance) ------------------------------
// The UI optional-chains these, so anything we omit is simply inert. We provide the handful a handheld
// standalone needs; renders need no hook here, they are engine jobs through the shared backend's RPCs.

namespace {
// The hook bodies themselves: installWindowHooks binds them, and nothing outside this unit names one.
JSValue jsQuitWindow(JSContext*, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
    if (g_app) g_app->running = false;
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}
// A WM-controlled window (a fullscreen handheld, or a window a tiling compositor tiled) → the UI fits its grid
// via zoom rather than resizing. A floating desktop window is ours to size, so the App's fit-to-grid effect
// drives resizes. Mirrors PluginUI::isWindowSizeControlled — the latch that keeps us from fighting the WM.
JSValue jsIsWindowSizeControlled(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
    return JS_NewBool(ctx, g_app ? g_app->wmControlled : 1);
}
// __rp_setWindowSize(w, h): grow/shrink the window to the grid. Mirrors the DPF standalone, where setSize() →
// the platform resize callback reallocs the LVGL buffer + emits "resize"; SDL gives us no such callback, so
// requestWindowSize asks the WM and the SDL_WINDOWEVENT_SIZE_CHANGED handler does the realloc. Inert once the
// WM owns geometry (a fullscreen handheld, or a tiling compositor) — requestWindowSize handles that.
JSValue jsSetWindowSize(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (!g_app || argc < 2) return JS_UNDEFINED;
    std::uint32_t w = 0, h = 0;
    JS_ToUint32(ctx, &w, argv[0]);
    JS_ToUint32(ctx, &h, argv[1]);
    if (w != 0 && h != 0) requestWindowSize(*g_app, w, h);
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}
JSValue jsSetWindowTitle(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (g_app && g_app->window && argc >= 1) {
        const char* t = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[0]);
        if (t && *t) SDL_SetWindowTitle(g_app->window, t);
        if (t) JS_FreeCString(ctx, t);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}
JSValue jsOpenPath(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (argc >= 1) {
        const char* p = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[0]);
        if (p && *p) openPathInFileManager(p);
        if (p) JS_FreeCString(ctx, p);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

// Deliver a native file dialog's pick into JS by calling the __rp_onFileBrowserResult resolver the real
// Backend registered (empty path = cancel → null). Same shared context / UI thread that pumps the JS loop,
// so a direct call is safe — the awaiting Promise settles on the next tick. Copy of PluginUI::uiFileBrowserSelected.
void deliverFileBrowserResult(JSContext* ctx, const std::string& path) {
    jsDeliverFileBrowserResult(ctx, path.c_str());
}

// __rp_openFileBrowser(title, patterns, saving, defaultName, startDir, directory): open the OS-native file
// dialog (bound only where NativeFileDialog::available()). Async — the pick is delivered later by
// pollFileDialog. `patterns` is a whitespace-separated glob list; `directory` picks a FOLDER (the render
// "Output Dir"); `saving` seeds the save name with defaultName.
JSValue jsOpenFileBrowser(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (!g_app || argc < 6) return JS_UNDEFINED;
    auto arg = [&](int i) -> std::string {
        const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[i]);
        std::string out = (s && *s) ? s : "";
        if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
        return out;
    };
    g_app->nativeDialog.request(arg(0), arg(1), JS_ToBool(ctx, argv[2]) == 1, arg(3), arg(4),
                                JS_ToBool(ctx, argv[5]) == 1);
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

// Poll the in-flight OS file dialog once per frame; when the helper finishes, deliver the pick (cancel = empty)
// into JS. Cheap no-op when nothing is open.
}  // namespace

void pollFileDialog(AppState& a) {
    JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext();
    if (!ctx) return;
    a.nativeDialog.poll([ctx](const std::string& pick) {
        if (std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_DIALOG_SELFTEST")) // headless E2E: prove the full pfd round-trip delivered
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] dialog self-test: picked '%s'\n", pick.c_str());
        deliverFileBrowserResult(ctx, pick);
    });
}

// __rp_getTransport(): { playing, external, bpm, localBpm } — the state behind the Instance menu's MIDI Clock
// submenu. `bpm` is the tempo in force (an external master's when `external`); `localBpm` is our own setting,
// which is what comes back when the master goes away. Standalone-only: a DAW / the DPF standalone take the
// transport from their host, so those builds never bind this and the submenu is absent.
namespace {
JSValue jsGetTransport(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
    JSValue o = JS_NewObject(ctx);
    if (g_app) {
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "playing",  JS_NewBool(ctx, g_app->transportPlaying.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "external", JS_NewBool(ctx, g_app->transportExternal.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "bpm",      JS_NewFloat64(ctx, g_app->transportBpm.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "localBpm", JS_NewFloat64(ctx, g_app->clockBpmRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)));
    }
    return o;
}

// __rp_setTransport(playing): start/stop the local transport. Takes effect on the next audio block; with an
// external clock master present it is recorded but overridden (see jsGetTransport).
JSValue jsSetTransport(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (g_app && argc >= 1)
        g_app->transportRequest.store(JS_ToBool(ctx, argv[0]) != 0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

// __rp_setClockBpm(bpm): the local tempo, clamped to the same range the clock estimator will accept from an
// external master (so the two sources can't disagree about what a legal tempo is). Persisted to audio.json.
JSValue jsSetClockBpm(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    double bpm = 0.0;
    if (g_app && argc >= 1 && JS_ToFloat64(ctx, &bpm, argv[0]) == 0) {
        bpm = std::clamp(bpm, MidiClockSync::kMinBpm, MidiClockSync::kMaxBpm);
        g_app->clockBpmRequest.store(static_cast<float>(bpm), std::memory_order_relaxed);
        saveAudioConfig(*g_app);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

// __rp_getMidiConfig(): { inputs: string[], outputs: string[], selectedInput, selectedOutput } - the live hardware MIDI
// ports + the current device selection, for the Settings > MIDI pickers. One name each, as midi.json still spells the
// selection until the project carries it ("" = None, "*" = every device). Standalone-only; absent in the plugin (DAW
// routes MIDI).
JSValue jsGetMidiConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
    JSValue o = JS_NewObject(ctx);
    if (g_app) {
        auto toArray = [&](const std::vector<std::string>& names) {
            JSValue a = JS_NewArray(ctx);
            for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < names.size(); ++i)
                JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, a, i, JS_NewString(ctx, names[i].c_str()));
            return a;
        };
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "inputs",  toArray(g_app->midi.listInputs()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "outputs", toArray(g_app->midi.listOutputs()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "selectedInput",  JS_NewString(ctx, g_app->midiInputJson.c_str()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "selectedOutput", JS_NewString(ctx, g_app->midiOutputJson.c_str()));
    }
    return o;
}

// __rp_setMidiInput(name) / __rp_setMidiOutput(name): choose a hardware device by port name ("" = None, "*" = every
// device on the input side). Applies immediately, without stopping audio, and persists to midi.json.
JSValue jsSetMidiInput(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (g_app && argc >= 1) {
        const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[0]);
        applyMidiSelection(*g_app, true, s ? s : "");
        if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}
JSValue jsSetMidiOutput(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (g_app && argc >= 1) {
        const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[0]);
        applyMidiSelection(*g_app, false, s ? s : "");
        if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

// __rp_getAudioConfig(): the shape the Settings > Audio rows read while this is the shim (audioDraft.ts,
// nativeHooks.ts): { sampleRate, blockSize, outChannels, driver, drivers, devicesByDriver, defaultByDriver, autoDriver,
// device, muted, error }.
//
//  - `drivers` is "Auto" plus one LABEL per driver of the backend IN FORCE ("PortAudio: PipeWire", "SDL: pipewire"):
//    the backend names itself because two backends may call a driver alike, and only the backend in force is enumerated
//    (asking another is its library's first use - the Zoom L6 rule).
//  - `driver` is the SELECTED label: "Auto" when the choice is automatic, else the label of the chosen pair.
//  - `devicesByDriver` / `defaultByDriver` are keyed by those labels (plus "Auto" for the automatic driver), and
//    `defaultByDriver` is what an empty device selection resolves to, which the row shows beside "Default".
//  - `autoDriver` is the driver label "Auto" currently resolves to, so the row can read "Auto (PipeWire)".
//  - `device` is the CHOSEN name, "" for the driver's default: the RESOLVED device is the status's, and feeding it back
//    as the choice would pin the concrete sink the session default happens to be today.
JSValue jsGetAudioConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*) {
    JSValue o = JS_NewObject(ctx);
    if (g_app) {
        auto toArray = [&](const std::vector<std::string>& names) {
            JSValue a = JS_NewArray(ctx);
            for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < names.size(); ++i)
                JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, a, i, JS_NewString(ctx, names[i].c_str()));
            return a;
        };
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "sampleRate",  JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqSampleRate));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "blockSize",   JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqBlockSize));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "outChannels", JS_NewInt32(ctx, g_app->reqOutChannels));
        const rp::audio::AudioDescription described =
            g_app->audio ? g_app->audio->describe() : rp::audio::AudioDescription{};

        JSValue     drivers   = JS_NewArray(ctx);
        JSValue     byDriver  = JS_NewObject(ctx);
        JSValue     defaults  = JS_NewObject(ctx);
        std::string selected  = rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel;
        std::string autoLabel;
        std::uint32_t at = 0;
        JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, drivers, at++, JS_NewString(ctx, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel));
        for (const auto& backend : described.backends) {
            if (backend.id == "null") continue;
            const std::string autoKey =
                backend.autoDriver.empty()
                    ? std::string()
                    : rp::audio::driverChoiceLabel(backend.label,
                                                   [&] {
                                                       for (const auto& d : backend.drivers)
                                                           if (d.id == backend.autoDriver) return d.label;
                                                       return backend.autoDriver;
                                                   }());
            for (const auto& driver : backend.drivers) {
                const std::string label = rp::audio::driverChoiceLabel(backend.label, driver.label);
                JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, drivers, at++, JS_NewString(ctx, label.c_str()));
                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, label.c_str(), toArray(driver.devices.names));
                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, label.c_str(), JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
                if (g_app->reqBackend == backend.id && g_app->reqDriver == driver.id) selected = label;
                if (driver.id == backend.autoDriver) {
                    // "Auto" resolves to this driver: the same devices and default, under the row the user picks.
                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel, toArray(driver.devices.names));
                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel,
                                      JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
                    autoLabel = driver.label;
                }
            }
            if (!autoKey.empty()) autoLabel = autoLabel.empty() ? autoKey : autoLabel;
        }
        if (g_app->reqBackend == "auto") selected = rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel;
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "drivers", drivers);
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "driver", JS_NewString(ctx, selected.c_str()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "devicesByDriver", byDriver);
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "defaultByDriver", defaults);
        // The DRIVER's label, as the row shows it beside "Auto" ("Auto (PipeWire)"): what the row's bracket reads.
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "autoDriver", JS_NewString(ctx, autoLabel.c_str()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "device",  JS_NewString(ctx, g_app->reqOutputDevice.c_str()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "muted",   JS_NewBool(ctx, !described.status.error.empty()));
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "error",   JS_NewString(ctx, described.status.error.c_str()));
    }
    return o;
}

// __rp_setAudioConfig(sampleRate, blockSize[, outChannels[, driverLabel[, device]]]): apply a live device change through
// AudioHost, which stops the stream, takes the engine back, opens the new request, re-rates to what the DEVICE obtained
// and starts it - one pass, never a partial reconfigure. The chosen values are persisted (audio.json is the shim until
// the TypeScript half owns the section).
//
// `driverLabel` is a label from `drivers` above: "Auto"/"" is the automatic choice, and "<Backend>: <driver>" is that
// pair (rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel). An unknown label keeps the choice in force, so an Apply that changed only the
// rate cannot mute the run by naming a backend that does not exist. outChannels is optional (an older bundle omits
// it), and 2/4/6/8 - anything else keeps the current count.
JSValue jsSetAudioConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    if (g_app && argc >= 2) {
        int sr = 0, bs = 0, ch = g_app->reqOutChannels;
        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &sr, argv[0]);
        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &bs, argv[1]);
        if (argc >= 3) {
            int c = 0;
            JS_ToInt32(ctx, &c, argv[2]);
            if (c >= 2 && c <= 8 && (c % 2) == 0) ch = c;
        }
        std::string device = g_app->reqOutputDevice;
        if (argc >= 5) {
            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[4]);
            device        = s ? s : "";
            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
        }
        if (argc >= 4) {
            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[3]);
            const std::string label = s ? s : "";
            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
            // The row's label, mapped to the (backend, driver) an apply takes. A backend's library comes up here, which
            // is a real use: the row offered it because the user asked for it.
            const rp::audio::AudioDescription described =
                g_app->audio ? g_app->audio->describe() : rp::audio::AudioDescription{};
            const rp::audio::AudioChoice current{g_app->reqBackend, g_app->reqDriver};
            const rp::audio::AudioChoice choice = rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel(label, described, current);
            g_app->reqBackend                   = choice.backend;
            g_app->reqDriver                    = choice.driver;
            // The row's choice is the SAVED one; a run's --audio-backend still decides what this run opens.
        }
        if (sr > 0 && bs > 0) reconfigureAudio(*g_app, sr, bs, ch, device);
    }
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

}  // namespace

void installWindowHooks(JSContext* ctx) {
    JSValue g = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx);
    auto bind = [&](const char* name, JSCFunction* fn, int len) {
        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, g, name, JS_NewCFunction(ctx, fn, name, len));
    };
    bind("__rp_quitWindow", jsQuitWindow, 0);
    bind("__rp_isWindowSizeControlled", jsIsWindowSizeControlled, 0);
    bind("__rp_setWindowSize", jsSetWindowSize, 2);
    bind("__rp_setWindowTitle", jsSetWindowTitle, 1);
    bind("__rp_openPath", jsOpenPath, 1);
    bind("__rp_getAudioConfig", jsGetAudioConfig, 0);
    bind("__rp_setAudioConfig", jsSetAudioConfig, 2);
    // Local transport (Instance menu > Transport) — standalone-only, like the audio/MIDI device seams.
    bind("__rp_getTransport", jsGetTransport, 0);
    bind("__rp_setTransport", jsSetTransport, 1);
    bind("__rp_setClockBpm", jsSetClockBpm, 1);
    // MIDI device selection (Settings > MIDI). RtMidi is compiled into retroplug-sdl, so the seam always
    // exists here; the plugin never binds these (hasMidiConfig() is false there → the submenu is hidden).
    bind("__rp_getMidiConfig", jsGetMidiConfig, 0);
    bind("__rp_setMidiInput", jsSetMidiInput, 1);
    bind("__rp_setMidiOutput", jsSetMidiOutput, 1);
    // The OS-native file dialog — only where a desktop helper exists (zenity/kdialog/…). Where none does
    // (the muOS handheld, a bare container) we DON'T bind it: useFileBrowser sees no nativeHook and the
    // "File Dialogs: OS Native" toggle transparently stays in-app. The self-test forces the bind to prove it.
    if (retroplug::ui::NativeFileDialog::available() || std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_DIALOG_SELFTEST"))
        bind("__rp_openFileBrowser", jsOpenFileBrowser, 6);
    // Mark this as a standalone host so the UI shows the "Exit" menu row (a DAW hides it).
    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, g, "__rp_isStandalone", JS_NewBool(ctx, 1));
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, g);
}

}  // namespace retroplug::sdl
````
