````cpp
#include "app.hpp"

namespace retroplug::sdl {


// The audio loop: the product's AudioClient (the engine behind AudioHost's interface), the control-surface calls this
// product answers for, and the audio.json / midi.json shim until TypeScript owns the settings (docs/modular-graph-phase-
// f5b-design.md 5.5).

// ---- the audio-thread scheduling this product still owns -------------------------------------------
#if defined(__linux__)
// Keep the UI/emulator-advancing work off the audio core (the last one), where AudioHost's callback and renderer run:
// a preempted or core-shared audio thread underruns under an A53's load. Best effort: a failure (no RT permission, too
// few cores) is ignored and the default scheduling stands.
void pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore() {
    const long ncpu = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);
    if (ncpu <= 2) return; // too few cores to segregate
    cpu_set_t set; CPU_ZERO(&set);
    for (long c = 0; c + 1 < ncpu; ++c) CPU_SET(c, &set); // all cores except the audio core (the last)
    pthread_setaffinity_np(pthread_self(), sizeof(set), &set);
}
#else
void pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore() {}
#endif

// ---- the audio client: the Engine, behind AudioHost's interface -------------------------------------
// render() is today's renderAudioBlock, unchanged except that the buffer is the pull's: AudioHost sizes it, and the
// engine renders planar into our own channel buffers which render() interleaves. prepare/release are the
// reconfigure's quiescent half, called by AudioHost between stop and start.

// ---- the control surface, as this product answers for it ------------------------------------------
//
// The three calls a provider makes of the product that owns the shared MIDI stream (rp_provider.h, design section 3).
// The Launchpad pack's facet asks for them and knows nothing about the stream's type; what they mean here is the two
// hazards a claimed port has in a stream that is already open: the stream must let go of it BEFORE it is opened (a
// Windows input is exclusive, and everywhere a pad press reaching both would fire every launch twice while notes out of
// the stream would light the surface's pads), and closing an input under a running callback. Neither costs an audio
// stop: an input's port cancels its own callback as it is destroyed, and the output set is replaced through the stream's
// epoch handshake, which waits out at most the send in flight (one block's sends, none when audio is not running).

bool AppState::onReserveMidi(void* ctx, const std::string& input, const std::string& output) {
    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);
    if (a.midi.reservedInput() == input && a.midi.reservedOutput() == output) return true;  // already so
    a.midi.setReserved(input, output);
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] control surface: reserved MIDI input '%s', output '%s'\n",
                 input.empty() ? "(none)" : input.c_str(), output.empty() ? "(none)" : output.c_str());
    return true;
}

void AppState::onSuspendInputs(void* ctx, bool suspended) {
    // The scan's held edge, and the one platform where it is real (midi/PortFilter.hpp's scanSuspendsInputs). Answering
    // before touching the stream is what makes this a no-op off Windows rather than a MIDI outage for the scan's
    // length.
    // Off Windows (ALSA's sequencer, CoreMIDI) an input is SHARED: the scan hears everything the stream does without it
    // closing anything.
    if (!rp::midi::scanSuspendsInputs()) return;
    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);
    a.midi.setHardwareInputsSuspended(suspended);  // logs the suspended / resumed line, and is a no-op if unchanged
}

void AppState::onRestored(void* ctx) { static_cast<AppState*>(ctx)->controlSurfaceRestored = true; }

// Let the control plane apply the control surface it persisted (config.json, launchpadDevices.ts restoreLaunchpad)
// before MIDI opens and audio starts. A claim made from here lands with audio not yet started, so it is reserved
// before the shared stream ever opens the port and costs no restart; a claim that arrives after the bound below is a
// MIDI-SESSION reserve, which onReserveMidi handles the same way a later Connect does.
//
// What it waits on is the facet's restored() reaching this product (rp_device_host::restored), because the selection
// is TS's and the claim is asynchronous with respect to the mount: React runs the restore in an effect, on a later
// pump of the JS loop. So pump the loop until it lands. Bounded in TIME, not pumps: a pump does not block, so a count
// would be over in a millisecond. A UI that never reports (a broken bundle, no facet at all) costs half a second at
// startup and then starts anyway, so a missing or unreadable config.json can never keep the app silent. A product that
// started no control-surface provider has nothing to wait FOR - no facet is mounted, so TS never calls restored() - and
// waits not at all.
void restoreControlSurface(AppState& a) {
    if (!a.providers.startedNamed("launchpad")) return;
    const Uint32 start = SDL_GetTicks();
    while (!a.controlSurfaceRestored && SDL_GetTicks() - start < 500) {
        a.ui.tick();
        if (!a.controlSurfaceRestored) SDL_Delay(1);
    }
    if (!a.controlSurfaceRestored)
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] control surface: the UI did not report its restore; continuing\n");
}

// RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO: the audio backends' own chatter and the host API / device enumeration. Read once (it cannot
// change under us), by the render loop's clock sync and by the PortAudio backend's log handlers, which are its own.
bool audioDebugEnabled() {
    static const bool on = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO") != nullptr;
    return on;
}

// ---- the audio client's body ------------------------------------------------------------------------

void ProductAudioClient::prepare(double sampleRateIn, int maxBlockFrames, int channels) {
    AppState& a = *app;
    // AudioHost runs this between stop and start, so the engine is quiescent: the same three calls today's
    // reconfigureAudio made, in the order its own comment describes (re-rate live cores, shape the host, size the
    // render), except that the rate and width are the DEVICE's rather than the request's.
    a.sampleRate       = sampleRateIn;
    a.numOutputs       = channels > 0 ? channels : 2;
    a.reqBlockSize     = maxBlockFrames > 0 ? maxBlockFrames : a.reqBlockSize;
    a.svc.engine.setSampleRate(sampleRateIn);
    setHostOutputs(a);
    a.svc.engine.setMaxBlockFrames(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(a.reqBlockSize));
    a.audioPlanar.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.numOutputs),
                         std::vector<float>(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.reqBlockSize), 0.0f));
    a.audioPtrs.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.numOutputs), nullptr);
    for (int c = 0; c < a.numOutputs; ++c) a.audioPtrs[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] = a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].data();
    // Hand the engine back: AudioHost's next call is start(), and the first pull renders on the audio thread.
    a.svc.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
}

void ProductAudioClient::release() {
    AppState& a = *app;
    // Take the Engine back from the audio thread: control-plane edits become push-only while it is away, and the
    // invoker's queue is drained into it so nothing is lost across the reconfigure (the plugin's
    // deactivate -> setSampleRate -> activate handoff, DPF-free).
    a.svc.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    a.svc.invoker.drainInto(a.svc.engine);
}

void ProductAudioClient::render(float* out, int frames) {
    AppState& a = *app;
    const int N = a.numOutputs;
    if (frames <= 0 || N <= 0) return;
    if (static_cast<int>(a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(0)].size()) < frames)
        for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c) {
            a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(frames));
            a.audioPtrs[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] = a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].data();
        }

    a.svc.invoker.drainInto(a.svc.engine);
    // Drain MIDI the backend's callback threads staged into the ring, and hand it to the Engine - we own it on this
    // (audio) thread, exactly like PluginDSP::run stages host MIDI. Frame 0 for now: live hardware MIDI carries no
    // sub-block timing worth preserving (a proper offset from the block clock is a later step).
    a.midi.poll(a.midiScratch);
    a.clockSync.sampleRate         = a.sampleRate;
    a.clockSync.debug              = audioDebugEnabled();
    a.clockSync.droppedMessages    = a.midi.droppedCount();
    for (auto& m : a.midiScratch) {
        if (m.bytes.empty()) continue;
        // System Real-Time first, wherever it sits in the message. It drives the host transport and is never staged,
        // never sent to a cart: the sync roles regenerate whatever each core needs from Engine tempo/transport, and
        // risa's generated stream reaches the N8 through the graph's fan-out, so forwarding the wire bytes too would
        // double-clock it. Testing only for a ONE-BYTE message (what this did before) drops any clock a transport
        // batched with another event, and a tempo estimate missing pulses reads a whole ratio slow.
        rp::midi::extractRealtime(m.bytes, [&](std::uint8_t status) { a.clockSync.onByte(status); });
        if (m.bytes.empty()) continue;
        // A physical N8 is fed from the graph, not from here: an rp.n8.nes node, placed by a system's "drive the real
        // cart" setting, takes the same protocol-node MIDI and bytes its emulated NES's core does, at their frames.
        // Sysex is still not staged as musical MIDI: no role consumes it, and the passthrough translators (mGB, LSDj
        // MidiPassthrough) push every byte they are given straight down the cart's link port - so a controller's
        // handshake or bulk-LED message would arrive at the Game Boy as noise. A control surface has its own stream
        // for this (rp.launchpad.surface-in, read by the controller session).
        if (m.bytes[0] == 0xF0) continue;
        // Everything left (notes / CC / ...) is staged as host MIDI in.
        a.svc.engine.stageMidi(0, m.bytes);
        a.midiStaged.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    a.clockSync.advance(frames);

    // Fold in the menu's play/stop + tempo, then publish what the transport ended up being (see AppState).
    a.clockSync.manualPlaying = a.transportRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    a.clockSync.manualBpm     = a.clockBpmRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const double bpm          = a.clockSync.outBpm();
    const bool   playing      = a.clockSync.outPlaying();
    a.transportPlaying.store(playing, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    a.transportExternal.store(a.clockSync.active, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    a.transportBpm.store(static_cast<float>(bpm), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    a.svc.engine.setBpm(bpm);            // 120 free-run until an external clock master appears
    a.svc.engine.setTransport(playing);  // then locks to its tempo + start/stop
    // Multi-out: render into the N planar channel buffers; the Engine zeroes them, and the plan routes each system to
    // its pair per audioRouting (TS builds the graph for the N-channel host shape). N=2 collapses every mode to the
    // stereo mix. N=4/6/8 spreads stems across the device's pairs.
    a.svc.engine.processBlock(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frames), a.audioPtrs.data(), static_cast<std::size_t>(N));

    // Host MIDI out (LSDj MI.OUT / Master Sync, the controller's launches) to the stream, then clear the block's
    // queue. Mirrors PluginDSP::run's writeMidiEvent drain (there it goes to the DAW), each message's frame dropped:
    // the stream's send takes no timestamp, so a message goes when its block is rendered. No length cap: a control
    // surface's LED traffic is sysex.
    for (const auto& mo : a.svc.engine.midiOut())
        if (!mo.data.empty()) a.midi.send(mo.data.data(), mo.data.size());
    a.svc.engine.clearMidiOut();

    for (int i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
        for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c)
            out[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * static_cast<std::size_t>(N) + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] =
                a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)][static_cast<std::size_t>(i)];
}

// ---- the audio configuration: the shim, the flags and the hook ----------------------------------------

rp::audio::AudioConfig audioConfigOf(const AppState& a) {
    rp::audio::AudioConfig c;
    c.driver            = a.reqDriver;
    c.device            = a.reqOutputDevice;
    c.sampleRate        = a.reqSampleRate;
    c.blockSize         = a.reqBlockSize;
    c.channels          = a.reqOutChannels;
    c.renderAheadFrames = a.renderAhead;
    return c;
}

// The whole sequence, once, through AudioHost: stop, release, open, prepare(info()), start (section 5.2). `--backend`
// is the flag's / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND's override, applied where the shim is read so it wins over audio.json
// (design 5.2, report item 8).
void applyAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
    if (!a.audio) return;
    rp::audio::AudioConfig c = audioConfigOf(a);
    c.backend                = a.reqBackend;
    if (!a.backendOverride.empty()) {
        // The run's flag wins over every saved or UI choice for its duration (design 5.2, E12): a harness pins `null`
        // so nothing else can come up, whatever a row or a click says.
        c.backend = a.backendOverride;
        c.driver.clear();
        c.device.clear();
    }
    a.audio->apply(c);
}

// audio.json / midi.json are NATIVE-owned device settings, read here at startup (setupSdl) before
// bootControlPlane brings up the JS runtime that owns config.json — so they can't live in the TS config, and
// they're standalone-only anyway (the plugin gets audio/MIDI from its DAW). They're small reflect-cpp JSON
// blobs, decoded tolerantly (DefaultIfMissing) exactly like the per-system role config that crosses to native
// (a missing/garbage field takes the struct default). Whole file into a string (empty if unreadable).
std::string slurpTextFile(const std::string& path) {
    std::string out;
    if (FILE* f = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "rb")) {
        char buf[4096];
        size_t n;
        while ((n = std::fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0) out.append(buf, n);
        std::fclose(f);
    }
    return out;
}
void writeTextFile(const std::string& path, const std::string& text) {
    if (FILE* f = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "wb")) {
        std::fwrite(text.data(), 1, text.size(), f);
        std::fclose(f);
    }
}

// The standalone audio device settings: a SHIM, until the choice is config.json's `audio` section (the TypeScript
// half). The fields a saved file carries are the ones the device opens with. `hostApi` is neither read nor resolved: a
// PaHostApiTypeId is a library's numeric id, which a saved choice may not be (section 5.1), and the backend and driver
// come from --audio-backend / the backend's auto choice / the Settings row. The field is still WRITTEN (as -1) so a file
// this build writes keeps the shape an older one had, and reading it ignores it. The rate, block and channel count
// apply. Defaults mirror AppState's so a partial file lands on them.
struct AudioCfgJson {
    int sampleRate = 48000;
    int blockSize = 512;
    int outChannels = 2;
    int hostApi = -1; // written for an old file's shape, never read: a numeric library id selects nothing
    std::string outputDevice; // the device's name in the driver's vocabulary; "" = the driver's default
    // The MIDI Clock submenu's tempo. Not an audio-device setting, but it belongs to the same
    // native-owned, standalone-only settings file rather than earning one of its own. The transport's
    // play/stop is deliberately NOT here: a tempo is a preference, a running clock is not — that starts
    // stopped every launch.
    double clockBpm = 120.0;
};

std::string audioCfgPath(AppState& a) { return a.svc.host.configDir() + "/audio.json"; }

void loadAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
    const std::string json = slurpTextFile(audioCfgPath(a));
    if (json.empty()) return; // absent/unreadable → keep the compiled-in / --block-size-seeded defaults
    const auto r = rfl::json::read<AudioCfgJson, rfl::DefaultIfMissing>(json);
    if (!r) return; // unparseable → keep defaults
    const AudioCfgJson c = r.value();
    if (c.sampleRate > 0) a.reqSampleRate = c.sampleRate;
    if (c.blockSize > 0) a.reqBlockSize = c.blockSize;
    if (c.outChannels >= 2 && c.outChannels <= 8 && (c.outChannels % 2) == 0) a.reqOutChannels = c.outChannels;
    a.reqOutputDevice = c.outputDevice; // resolved by name in the backend; falls back to its default if absent
    if (c.clockBpm >= MidiClockSync::kMinBpm && c.clockBpm <= MidiClockSync::kMaxBpm)
        a.clockBpmRequest.store(static_cast<float>(c.clockBpm), std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

void saveAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
    const AudioCfgJson c{ a.reqSampleRate, a.reqBlockSize, a.reqOutChannels, -1, a.reqOutputDevice,
                          a.clockBpmRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) };
    writeTextFile(audioCfgPath(a), rfl::json::write(c) + "\n");
}

// The chosen MIDI input/output device names (Settings > MIDI). "" = None in both directions (the virtual ports only),
// the default; the input also takes rp::midi::kAllInputs ("*") as an explicit "every device".
//
// A SHIM, kept until the selection is the project's (a `midi` project section, its ports by name): this file holds one
// name each, and the mapping onto the stream's lists lives in applyMidiSelection. Then it is ignored outright, like
// audio.json, and the SDL app never shipped.
//
// NOTE for anyone reading an old midi.json: "" used to mean All Devices on the input side, and there is no way to tell
// that apart from "never chose" - both wrote the same empty string. So an existing file simply lands on the current
// default, which is the behaviour a default change should have.
struct MidiCfgJson {
    std::string input;
    std::string output;
};

std::string midiCfgPath(AppState& a) { return a.svc.host.configDir() + "/midi.json"; }

// The one-name mapping onto the stream's lists, shared by the startup load and the picker's hooks. It neither persists
// nor logs: reading the stored file back over itself would rewrite it at every launch, and the log line belongs to the
// user's change, not to a value the file already held.
//
// `mode` is the stream's: the load DIFFS, so reopening a project costs no connection it already had, while the picker's
// change REOPENS, which is the user's one remedy for a port that was unplugged and plugged back in (there is no hotplug
// watch).
void selectMidi(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name, rp::midi::Apply mode) {
    if (input) {
        a.midiInputJson = name;
        if (name.empty()) a.midi.setInputs({}, false, mode);
        else if (name == rp::midi::kAllInputs) a.midi.setInputs({}, true, mode);
        else a.midi.setInputs({name}, false, mode);
    } else {
        a.midiOutputJson = name;
        if (name.empty()) a.midi.setOutputs({}, mode);
        else a.midi.setOutputs({name}, mode);
    }
}

void loadMidiConfig(AppState& a) {
    const std::string json = slurpTextFile(midiCfgPath(a));
    if (json.empty()) return;
    const auto r = rfl::json::read<MidiCfgJson, rfl::DefaultIfMissing>(json);
    if (!r) return;
    const MidiCfgJson c = r.value();
    // Applied when midi.open() publishes the ports: the same one-name mapping the picker's hooks use, in its diffing
    // mode (nothing the file names is reopened here, because nothing is open yet).
    selectMidi(a, true, c.input, rp::midi::Apply::Diff);
    selectMidi(a, false, c.output, rp::midi::Apply::Diff);
}

void saveMidiConfig(AppState& a) {
    const MidiCfgJson c{ a.midiInputJson, a.midiOutputJson };
    writeTextFile(midiCfgPath(a), rfl::json::write(c) + "\n");
}

// Live audio reconfigure (the Audio settings submenu): AudioHost runs the whole sequence once (stop, release, open,
// prepare with what the DEVICE obtained, start), and the chosen values are persisted so the next launch opens the same
// device. Called on the UI thread. A no-change request costs nothing: AudioHost returns at once for a config it is
// already running.
void reconfigureAudio(AppState& a, int sampleRate, int blockSize, int channels, const std::string& device) {
    a.reqSampleRate   = sampleRate;
    a.reqBlockSize    = blockSize;
    a.reqOutChannels  = channels;
    a.reqOutputDevice = device;
    applyAudioConfig(a);
    saveAudioConfig(a);
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] audio reconfigured: %d Hz, %d frames, %d ch (backend '%s', device '%s')\n",
                 a.reqSampleRate, a.reqBlockSize, a.reqOutChannels,
                 a.reqBackend.empty() ? "auto" : a.reqBackend.c_str(),
                 a.reqOutputDevice.empty() ? "default" : a.reqOutputDevice.c_str());
}

// Live MIDI device reselection (Settings > MIDI), while audio may be running. It does not stop audio: the stream closes
// and opens inputs, each port cancelling its own callback as it goes, and replaces its output set through the epoch
// handshake, which waits out at most the send in flight. A brief audio gap on a device change belongs to
// reconfigureAudio alone, where the device itself changes.
//
// The picker offers one name each while midi.json is the selection's home (the shim): "" is None, "*" is every device
// on the input side, and anything else is that port. The stream itself takes lists.
void applyMidiSelection(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name) {
    selectMidi(a, input, name, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
    saveMidiConfig(a);  // the picker's change is the one that persists it (loadMidiConfig does not)
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI %s device -> '%s'\n", input ? "input" : "output",
                 name.empty() ? "None" : (name == rp::midi::kAllInputs ? "All Devices" : name.c_str()));
}

}  // namespace retroplug::sdl
````

````diff
-
-// Flush: in LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT the draw buffer already holds the full rendered frame; we just
-// record which region changed (union across the refresh's flush calls) so the loop uploads + presents
-// only that rect, and skips presenting entirely when nothing changed.
-void flushCb(lv_display_t* disp, const lv_area_t* area, uint8_t*) {
-    if (g_app && area) {
-        if (!g_app->dirty) { g_app->dirtyRect = *area; g_app->dirty = true; }
-        else {
-            g_app->dirtyRect.x1 = std::min(g_app->dirtyRect.x1, area->x1);
-            g_app->dirtyRect.y1 = std::min(g_app->dirtyRect.y1, area->y1);
-            g_app->dirtyRect.x2 = std::max(g_app->dirtyRect.x2, area->x2);
-            g_app->dirtyRect.y2 = std::max(g_app->dirtyRect.y2, area->y2);
-        }
-    }
-    lv_display_flush_ready(disp);
-}

-// Call globalThis[name](arg?) on the control-plane context (main thread). Returns the string result, or
-// "" for non-string / missing / exception. Shared with PluginDSP::callGlobal.
-//
-// `ready` is true unconditionally here, and that is not laziness: bootControlPlane returns false if the
-// host fails to initialise OR the bundle never signals ready, and main exits 1 on either. An unready SDL
-// host is a dead process, so by the time anything calls this there is nothing to guard against. The
-// plugin cannot take that route - a DAW scan must degrade rather than exit - which is why the shared
-// body carries the guard and this caller opts out of it explicitly.
-std::string callGlobal(TjsHostRuntime& host, const char* name, const char* arg) {
-    JsGlobals g{ host.context(), /*ready=*/true,
-                 [](const char* n, const char* detail) {
-                     std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] %s threw: %s\n", n, detail);
-                 } };
-    return jsCallGlobal(g, name, arg);
-}

-bool hasGlobalFunction(JSContext* ctx, const char* name) { return jsHasGlobalFunction(ctx, name); }

-                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, label.c_str(), toArray(driver.devices.names));
-                JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, label.c_str(), JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
-                if (g_app->reqBackend == backend.id && g_app->reqDriver == driver.id) selected = label;
-                if (driver.id == backend.autoDriver) {
-                    // "Auto" resolves to this driver: the same devices and default, under the row the user picks.
-                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, byDriver, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel, toArray(driver.devices.names));
-                    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, defaults, rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel,
-                                      JS_NewString(ctx, driver.devices.defaultName.c_str()));
-                    autoLabel = driver.label;
-                }
-            }
-            if (!autoKey.empty()) autoLabel = autoLabel.empty() ? autoKey : autoLabel;
-        }
-        if (g_app->reqBackend == "auto") selected = rp::audio::kAutoDriverLabel;
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "drivers", drivers);
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "driver", JS_NewString(ctx, selected.c_str()));
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "devicesByDriver", byDriver);
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "defaultByDriver", defaults);
-        // The DRIVER's label, as the row shows it beside "Auto" ("Auto (PipeWire)"): what the row's bracket reads.
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "autoDriver", JS_NewString(ctx, autoLabel.c_str()));
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "device",  JS_NewString(ctx, g_app->reqOutputDevice.c_str()));
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "muted",   JS_NewBool(ctx, !described.status.error.empty()));
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, o, "error",   JS_NewString(ctx, described.status.error.c_str()));
-    }
-    return o;
-}
-
-// __rp_setAudioConfig(sampleRate, blockSize[, outChannels[, driverLabel[, device]]]): apply a live device change through
-// AudioHost, which stops the stream, takes the engine back, opens the new request, re-rates to what the DEVICE obtained
-// and starts it - one pass, never a partial reconfigure. The chosen values are persisted (audio.json is the shim until
-// the TypeScript half owns the section).
-//
-// `driverLabel` is a label from `drivers` above: "Auto"/"" is the automatic choice, and "<Backend>: <driver>" is that
-// pair (rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel). An unknown label keeps the choice in force, so an Apply that changed only the
-// rate cannot mute the run by naming a backend that does not exist. outChannels is optional (an older bundle omits
-// it), and 2/4/6/8 - anything else keeps the current count.
-JSValue jsSetAudioConfig(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
-    if (g_app && argc >= 2) {
-        int sr = 0, bs = 0, ch = g_app->reqOutChannels;
-        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &sr, argv[0]);
-        JS_ToInt32(ctx, &bs, argv[1]);
-        if (argc >= 3) {
-            int c = 0;
-            JS_ToInt32(ctx, &c, argv[2]);
-            if (c >= 2 && c <= 8 && (c % 2) == 0) ch = c;
-        }
-        std::string device = g_app->reqOutputDevice;
-        if (argc >= 5) {
-            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[4]);
-            device        = s ? s : "";
-            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
-        }
-        if (argc >= 4) {
-            const char* s = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[3]);
-            const std::string label = s ? s : "";
-            if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
-            // The row's label, mapped to the (backend, driver) an apply takes. A backend's library comes up here, which
-            // is a real use: the row offered it because the user asked for it.
-            const rp::audio::AudioDescription described =
-                g_app->audio ? g_app->audio->describe() : rp::audio::AudioDescription{};
-            const rp::audio::AudioChoice current{g_app->reqBackend, g_app->reqDriver};
-            const rp::audio::AudioChoice choice = rp::audio::choiceForDriverLabel(label, described, current);
-            g_app->reqBackend                   = choice.backend;
-            g_app->reqDriver                    = choice.driver;
-            // The row's choice is the SAVED one; a run's --audio-backend still decides what this run opens.
-        }
-        if (sr > 0 && bs > 0) reconfigureAudio(*g_app, sr, bs, ch, device);
-    }
-    return JS_UNDEFINED;
-}
-
-void installWindowHooks(JSContext* ctx) {
-    JSValue g = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx);
-    auto bind = [&](const char* name, JSCFunction* fn, int len) {
-        JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, g, name, JS_NewCFunction(ctx, fn, name, len));
-    };
-    bind("__rp_quitWindow", jsQuitWindow, 0);
-    bind("__rp_isWindowSizeControlled", jsIsWindowSizeControlled, 0);
-    bind("__rp_setWindowSize", jsSetWindowSize, 2);
-    bind("__rp_setWindowTitle", jsSetWindowTitle, 1);
-    bind("__rp_openPath", jsOpenPath, 1);
-    bind("__rp_getAudioConfig", jsGetAudioConfig, 0);
-    bind("__rp_setAudioConfig", jsSetAudioConfig, 2);
-    // Local transport (Instance menu > Transport) — standalone-only, like the audio/MIDI device seams.
-    bind("__rp_getTransport", jsGetTransport, 0);
-    bind("__rp_setTransport", jsSetTransport, 1);
-    bind("__rp_setClockBpm", jsSetClockBpm, 1);
-    // MIDI device selection (Settings > MIDI). RtMidi is compiled into retroplug-sdl, so the seam always
-    // exists here; the plugin never binds these (hasMidiConfig() is false there → the submenu is hidden).
-    bind("__rp_getMidiConfig", jsGetMidiConfig, 0);
-    bind("__rp_setMidiInput", jsSetMidiInput, 1);
-    bind("__rp_setMidiOutput", jsSetMidiOutput, 1);
-    // The OS-native file dialog — only where a desktop helper exists (zenity/kdialog/…). Where none does
-    // (the muOS handheld, a bare container) we DON'T bind it: useFileBrowser sees no nativeHook and the
-    // "File Dialogs: OS Native" toggle transparently stays in-app. The self-test forces the bind to prove it.
-    if (retroplug::ui::NativeFileDialog::available() || std::getenv("RETROPLUG_SDL_DIALOG_SELFTEST"))
-        bind("__rp_openFileBrowser", jsOpenFileBrowser, 6);
-    // Mark this as a standalone host so the UI shows the "Exit" menu row (a DAW hides it).
-    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, g, "__rp_isStandalone", JS_NewBool(ctx, 1));
-    JS_FreeValue(ctx, g);
-}
-
-// ---- input translation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-// Push an LVGL key onto the keypad queue AND emit the "key" JS bus (press+release), mirroring
-// RenderCore::tapKey / PluginUI::onKeyboard. dpf is the DPF keycode the TS input layer expects.
-// SDL's modifier state -> DPF's Modifier mask (dgl/Base.hpp), which is what the "key" bus carries.
-// The bus is shared with the plugin host, so the mask has to mean the same thing on both sides.
-std::uint32_t dpfModsFromSdl(std::uint16_t sdlMod) {
-    std::uint32_t mods = 0;
-    if (sdlMod & KMOD_SHIFT) mods |= 1U << 0U; // kModifierShift
-    if (sdlMod & KMOD_CTRL)  mods |= 1U << 1U; // kModifierControl
-    if (sdlMod & KMOD_ALT)   mods |= 1U << 2U; // kModifierAlt
-    if (sdlMod & KMOD_GUI)   mods |= 1U << 3U; // kModifierSuper
-    return mods;
-}
-
-void feedKey(AppState& a, std::uint32_t lvKey, std::uint32_t dpf, bool press, std::uint32_t mods) {
-    JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext();
-    if (press && lvKey != 0) a.input.keyQueue.push_back(lvKey);  // only real LVGL nav keys reach the keypad indev
-    if (ctx) {
-        // THREE args, matching PluginUI. DPF gives the unshifted code point ('a' for the A key whether or
-        // not Shift is down), so the modifier mask is the only way the prompt text-input can apply
-        // Shift -> uppercase - Menu.tsx's key handler takes it as `mod = 0` (NativeEvents in
-        // useNativeEvent.ts types the channel). This emitted two args for a long time, so that default
-        // silently made Shift a no-op in the standalone while it worked in the DAW.
-        JSValue args[3] = {JS_NewUint32(ctx, dpf), JS_NewBool(ctx, press), JS_NewUint32(ctx, mods)};
-        a.ui.emit("key", 3, args);
-        for (JSValue& v : args) JS_FreeValue(ctx, v);
-    }
-}
-
-// Map an SDL keysym to (LVGL key, DPF keycode). The DPF code is what the TS input layer (keyCodes.ts)
-// expects on the "key" bus: arrows in the 0xE03x band, ShiftL/R at 0xE051/2, and — crucially — printable
-// keys carry their ASCII code verbatim (dpfCodeToKeyName does String.fromCharCode). Only the navigation
-// keys get a real LVGL keypad code (`lv`); everything else is bus-only (lv = 0) — game buttons, capture,
-// and app actions all live on the "key" bus, not the keypad. Returns false for keys we don't translate.
-//
-// This must cover every key the default bindings use (bindingMap.ts): dpad = arrows, A = Z, B = X,
-// Start = Enter, Select = ShiftL/ShiftR/Backspace — plus anything the user might rebind to. Previously only
-// arrows/Enter/Esc were mapped, so A/B/Select (and any letter/modifier binding) never reached the emulator
-// OR the key-capture editor.
-bool mapSdlKey(SDL_Keycode k, std::uint32_t& lv, std::uint32_t& dpf) {
-    lv = 0;
-    switch (k) {
-        case SDLK_UP:       lv = LV_KEY_UP;    dpf = 0xE036; return true;
-        case SDLK_DOWN:     lv = LV_KEY_DOWN;  dpf = 0xE038; return true;
-        case SDLK_RIGHT:    lv = LV_KEY_RIGHT; dpf = 0xE037; return true;
-        case SDLK_LEFT:     lv = LV_KEY_LEFT;  dpf = 0xE035; return true;
-        case SDLK_RETURN:   lv = LV_KEY_ENTER; dpf = 0x0D;   return true;
-        case SDLK_KP_ENTER: lv = LV_KEY_ENTER; dpf = 0x0D;   return true;
-        case SDLK_ESCAPE:   lv = LV_KEY_ESC;   dpf = 0x1B;   return true;
-        // Bus-only keys (no keypad nav): the GB Select defaults + editor keys.
-        case SDLK_LSHIFT:   dpf = 0xE051; return true;   // ShiftL
-        case SDLK_RSHIFT:   dpf = 0xE052; return true;   // ShiftR
-        case SDLK_BACKSPACE:dpf = 0x08;   return true;   // Backspace (Select default; clears a capture row)
-        case SDLK_TAB:      dpf = 0x09;   return true;   // Tab (default Cycle-Instances app action)
-        case SDLK_PAGEUP:   dpf = 0xE031; return true;   // menu coarse-step
-        case SDLK_PAGEDOWN: dpf = 0xE032; return true;
-        default:
-            // Printable ASCII (letters/digits/punctuation/space): SDL's keycode IS the ASCII code, which is
-            // exactly the DPF/DGL "key" bus convention. Covers A=Z, B=X and anything the user rebinds to.
-            if (k >= 0x20 && k <= 0x7e) { dpf = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(k); return true; }
-            return false;
-    }
-}
-
-// Poll controllers once per frame → re-emit each transition onto the gamepad-* JS bus (exactly as
-// PluginUI::pumpGamepad). The gamepad drives BOTH menu navigation and in-game input purely through this
-// bus: the React Menu has its own gamepad handler, and the design contract is that the gamepad bus never
-// reaches the LVGL keypad indev (Menu.tsx). So we must NOT also translate gamepad → keypad here — doing
-// so double-drives the menu (every move counted twice) while leaving in-game input single (the keypad
-// keys hit the idle focus sink). Keyboard still feeds the keypad (mapSdlKey/feedKey) for desktop use.
-void pumpGamepad(AppState& a) { pumpGamepadInto(a.gamepad, a.ui, a.ui.getContext()); }
-
-// ---- the audio-thread scheduling this product still owns -------------------------------------------
-#if defined(__linux__)
-// Keep the UI/emulator-advancing work off the audio core (the last one), where AudioHost's callback and renderer run:
-// a preempted or core-shared audio thread underruns under an A53's load. Best effort: a failure (no RT permission, too
-// few cores) is ignored and the default scheduling stands.
-void pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore() {
-    const long ncpu = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);
-    if (ncpu <= 2) return; // too few cores to segregate
-    cpu_set_t set; CPU_ZERO(&set);
-    for (long c = 0; c + 1 < ncpu; ++c) CPU_SET(c, &set); // all cores except the audio core (the last)
-    pthread_setaffinity_np(pthread_self(), sizeof(set), &set);
-}
-#else
-void pinUiThreadAwayFromAudioCore() {}
-#endif
-
-// ---- the audio client: the Engine, behind AudioHost's interface -------------------------------------
-// render() is today's renderAudioBlock, unchanged except that the buffer is the pull's: AudioHost sizes it, and the
-// engine renders planar into our own channel buffers which render() interleaves. prepare/release are the
-// reconfigure's quiescent half, called by AudioHost between stop and start.
-struct ProductAudioClient final : rp::audio::AudioClient {
-    AppState* app = nullptr;
-
-    void prepare(double sampleRateIn, int maxBlockFrames, int channels) override;
-    void render(float* out, int frames) override;
-    void release() override;
-};
-
-// ---- the control surface, as this product answers for it ------------------------------------------
-//
-// The three calls a provider makes of the product that owns the shared MIDI stream (rp_provider.h, design section 3).
-// The Launchpad pack's facet asks for them and knows nothing about the stream's type; what they mean here is the two
-// hazards a claimed port has in a stream that is already open: the stream must let go of it BEFORE it is opened (a
-// Windows input is exclusive, and everywhere a pad press reaching both would fire every launch twice while notes out of
-// the stream would light the surface's pads), and closing an input under a running callback. Neither costs an audio
-// stop: an input's port cancels its own callback as it is destroyed, and the output set is replaced through the stream's
-// epoch handshake, which waits out at most the send in flight (one block's sends, none when audio is not running).
-
-bool AppState::onReserveMidi(void* ctx, const std::string& input, const std::string& output) {
-    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);
-    if (a.midi.reservedInput() == input && a.midi.reservedOutput() == output) return true;  // already so
-    a.midi.setReserved(input, output);
-    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] control surface: reserved MIDI input '%s', output '%s'\n",
-                 input.empty() ? "(none)" : input.c_str(), output.empty() ? "(none)" : output.c_str());
-    return true;
-}
-
-void AppState::onSuspendInputs(void* ctx, bool suspended) {
-    // The scan's held edge, and the one platform where it is real (midi/PortFilter.hpp's scanSuspendsInputs). Answering
-    // before touching the stream is what makes this a no-op off Windows rather than a MIDI outage for the scan's
-    // length.
-    // Off Windows (ALSA's sequencer, CoreMIDI) an input is SHARED: the scan hears everything the stream does without it
-    // closing anything.
-    if (!rp::midi::scanSuspendsInputs()) return;
-    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);
-    a.midi.setHardwareInputsSuspended(suspended);  // logs the suspended / resumed line, and is a no-op if unchanged
-}
-
-void AppState::onRestored(void* ctx) { static_cast<AppState*>(ctx)->controlSurfaceRestored = true; }
-
-// Let the control plane apply the control surface it persisted (config.json, launchpadDevices.ts restoreLaunchpad)
-// before MIDI opens and audio starts. A claim made from here lands with audio not yet started, so it is reserved
-// before the shared stream ever opens the port and costs no restart; a claim that arrives after the bound below is a
-// MIDI-SESSION reserve, which onReserveMidi handles the same way a later Connect does.
-//
-// What it waits on is the facet's restored() reaching this product (rp_device_host::restored), because the selection
-// is TS's and the claim is asynchronous with respect to the mount: React runs the restore in an effect, on a later
-// pump of the JS loop. So pump the loop until it lands. Bounded in TIME, not pumps: a pump does not block, so a count
-// would be over in a millisecond. A UI that never reports (a broken bundle, no facet at all) costs half a second at
-// startup and then starts anyway, so a missing or unreadable config.json can never keep the app silent. A product that
-// started no control-surface provider has nothing to wait FOR - no facet is mounted, so TS never calls restored() - and
-// waits not at all.
-void restoreControlSurface(AppState& a) {
-    if (!a.providers.startedNamed("launchpad")) return;
-    const Uint32 start = SDL_GetTicks();
-    while (!a.controlSurfaceRestored && SDL_GetTicks() - start < 500) {
-        a.ui.tick();
-        if (!a.controlSurfaceRestored) SDL_Delay(1);
-    }
-    if (!a.controlSurfaceRestored)
-        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] control surface: the UI did not report its restore; continuing\n");
-}
-
-// RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO: the audio backends' own chatter and the host API / device enumeration. Read once (it cannot
-// change under us), by the render loop's clock sync and by the PortAudio backend's log handlers, which are its own.
-bool audioDebugEnabled() {
-    static const bool on = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO") != nullptr;
-    return on;
-}
-
-// ---- the audio client's body ------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-void ProductAudioClient::prepare(double sampleRateIn, int maxBlockFrames, int channels) {
-    AppState& a = *app;
-    // AudioHost runs this between stop and start, so the engine is quiescent: the same three calls today's
-    // reconfigureAudio made, in the order its own comment describes (re-rate live cores, shape the host, size the
-    // render), except that the rate and width are the DEVICE's rather than the request's.
-    a.sampleRate       = sampleRateIn;
-    a.numOutputs       = channels > 0 ? channels : 2;
-    a.reqBlockSize     = maxBlockFrames > 0 ? maxBlockFrames : a.reqBlockSize;
-    a.svc.engine.setSampleRate(sampleRateIn);
-    setHostOutputs(a);
-    a.svc.engine.setMaxBlockFrames(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(a.reqBlockSize));
-    a.audioPlanar.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.numOutputs),
-                         std::vector<float>(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.reqBlockSize), 0.0f));
-    a.audioPtrs.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(a.numOutputs), nullptr);
-    for (int c = 0; c < a.numOutputs; ++c) a.audioPtrs[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] = a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].data();
-    // Hand the engine back: AudioHost's next call is start(), and the first pull renders on the audio thread.
-    a.svc.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
-}
-
-void ProductAudioClient::release() {
-    AppState& a = *app;
-    // Take the Engine back from the audio thread: control-plane edits become push-only while it is away, and the
-    // invoker's queue is drained into it so nothing is lost across the reconfigure (the plugin's
-    // deactivate -> setSampleRate -> activate handoff, DPF-free).
-    a.svc.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
-    a.svc.invoker.drainInto(a.svc.engine);
-}
-
-void ProductAudioClient::render(float* out, int frames) {
-    AppState& a = *app;
-    const int N = a.numOutputs;
-    if (frames <= 0 || N <= 0) return;
-    if (static_cast<int>(a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(0)].size()) < frames)
-        for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c) {
-            a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(frames));
-            a.audioPtrs[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] = a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)].data();
-        }
-
-    a.svc.invoker.drainInto(a.svc.engine);
-    // Drain MIDI the backend's callback threads staged into the ring, and hand it to the Engine - we own it on this
-    // (audio) thread, exactly like PluginDSP::run stages host MIDI. Frame 0 for now: live hardware MIDI carries no
-    // sub-block timing worth preserving (a proper offset from the block clock is a later step).
-    a.midi.poll(a.midiScratch);
-    a.clockSync.sampleRate         = a.sampleRate;
-    a.clockSync.debug              = audioDebugEnabled();
-    a.clockSync.droppedMessages    = a.midi.droppedCount();
-    for (auto& m : a.midiScratch) {
-        if (m.bytes.empty()) continue;
-        // System Real-Time first, wherever it sits in the message. It drives the host transport and is never staged,
-        // never sent to a cart: the sync roles regenerate whatever each core needs from Engine tempo/transport, and
-        // risa's generated stream reaches the N8 through the graph's fan-out, so forwarding the wire bytes too would
-        // double-clock it. Testing only for a ONE-BYTE message (what this did before) drops any clock a transport
-        // batched with another event, and a tempo estimate missing pulses reads a whole ratio slow.
-        rp::midi::extractRealtime(m.bytes, [&](std::uint8_t status) { a.clockSync.onByte(status); });
-        if (m.bytes.empty()) continue;
-        // A physical N8 is fed from the graph, not from here: an rp.n8.nes node, placed by a system's "drive the real
-        // cart" setting, takes the same protocol-node MIDI and bytes its emulated NES's core does, at their frames.
-        // Sysex is still not staged as musical MIDI: no role consumes it, and the passthrough translators (mGB, LSDj
-        // MidiPassthrough) push every byte they are given straight down the cart's link port - so a controller's
-        // handshake or bulk-LED message would arrive at the Game Boy as noise. A control surface has its own stream
-        // for this (rp.launchpad.surface-in, read by the controller session).
-        if (m.bytes[0] == 0xF0) continue;
-        // Everything left (notes / CC / ...) is staged as host MIDI in.
-        a.svc.engine.stageMidi(0, m.bytes);
-        a.midiStaged.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    }
-    a.clockSync.advance(frames);
-
-    // Fold in the menu's play/stop + tempo, then publish what the transport ended up being (see AppState).
-    a.clockSync.manualPlaying = a.transportRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    a.clockSync.manualBpm     = a.clockBpmRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    const double bpm          = a.clockSync.outBpm();
-    const bool   playing      = a.clockSync.outPlaying();
-    a.transportPlaying.store(playing, std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    a.transportExternal.store(a.clockSync.active, std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    a.transportBpm.store(static_cast<float>(bpm), std::memory_order_relaxed);
-    a.svc.engine.setBpm(bpm);            // 120 free-run until an external clock master appears
-    a.svc.engine.setTransport(playing);  // then locks to its tempo + start/stop
-    // Multi-out: render into the N planar channel buffers; the Engine zeroes them, and the plan routes each system to
-    // its pair per audioRouting (TS builds the graph for the N-channel host shape). N=2 collapses every mode to the
-    // stereo mix. N=4/6/8 spreads stems across the device's pairs.
-    a.svc.engine.processBlock(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(frames), a.audioPtrs.data(), static_cast<std::size_t>(N));
-
-    // Host MIDI out (LSDj MI.OUT / Master Sync, the controller's launches) to the stream, then clear the block's
-    // queue. Mirrors PluginDSP::run's writeMidiEvent drain (there it goes to the DAW), each message's frame dropped:
-    // the stream's send takes no timestamp, so a message goes when its block is rendered. No length cap: a control
-    // surface's LED traffic is sysex.
-    for (const auto& mo : a.svc.engine.midiOut())
-        if (!mo.data.empty()) a.midi.send(mo.data.data(), mo.data.size());
-    a.svc.engine.clearMidiOut();
-
-    for (int i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
-        for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c)
-            out[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) * static_cast<std::size_t>(N) + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] =
-                a.audioPlanar[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)][static_cast<std::size_t>(i)];
-}
-
-// ---- the audio configuration: the shim, the flags and the hook ----------------------------------------
-
-rp::audio::AudioConfig audioConfigOf(const AppState& a) {
-    rp::audio::AudioConfig c;
-    c.driver            = a.reqDriver;
-    c.device            = a.reqOutputDevice;
-    c.sampleRate        = a.reqSampleRate;
-    c.blockSize         = a.reqBlockSize;
-    c.channels          = a.reqOutChannels;
-    c.renderAheadFrames = a.renderAhead;
-    return c;
-}
-
-// The whole sequence, once, through AudioHost: stop, release, open, prepare(info()), start (section 5.2). `--backend`
-// is the flag's / RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND's override, applied where the shim is read so it wins over audio.json
-// (design 5.2, report item 8).
-void applyAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
-    if (!a.audio) return;
-    rp::audio::AudioConfig c = audioConfigOf(a);
-    c.backend                = a.reqBackend;
-    if (!a.backendOverride.empty()) {
-        // The run's flag wins over every saved or UI choice for its duration (design 5.2, E12): a harness pins `null`
-        // so nothing else can come up, whatever a row or a click says.
-        c.backend = a.backendOverride;
-        c.driver.clear();
-        c.device.clear();
-    }
-    a.audio->apply(c);
-}

-// audio.json / midi.json are NATIVE-owned device settings, read here at startup (setupSdl) before
-// bootControlPlane brings up the JS runtime that owns config.json — so they can't live in the TS config, and
-// they're standalone-only anyway (the plugin gets audio/MIDI from its DAW). They're small reflect-cpp JSON
-// blobs, decoded tolerantly (DefaultIfMissing) exactly like the per-system role config that crosses to native
-// (a missing/garbage field takes the struct default). Whole file into a string (empty if unreadable).
-std::string slurpTextFile(const std::string& path) {
-    std::string out;
-    if (FILE* f = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "rb")) {
-        char buf[4096];
-        size_t n;
-        while ((n = std::fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0) out.append(buf, n);
-        std::fclose(f);
-    }
-    return out;
-}
-void writeTextFile(const std::string& path, const std::string& text) {
-    if (FILE* f = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "wb")) {
-        std::fwrite(text.data(), 1, text.size(), f);
-        std::fclose(f);
-    }
-}
-
-// The standalone audio device settings: a SHIM, until the choice is config.json's `audio` section (the TypeScript
-// half). The fields a saved file carries are the ones the device opens with. `hostApi` is neither read nor resolved: a
-// PaHostApiTypeId is a library's numeric id, which a saved choice may not be (section 5.1), and the backend and driver
-// come from --audio-backend / the backend's auto choice / the Settings row. The field is still WRITTEN (as -1) so a file
-// this build writes keeps the shape an older one had, and reading it ignores it. The rate, block and channel count
-// apply. Defaults mirror AppState's so a partial file lands on them.
-struct AudioCfgJson {
-    int sampleRate = 48000;
-    int blockSize = 512;
-    int outChannels = 2;
-    int hostApi = -1; // written for an old file's shape, never read: a numeric library id selects nothing
-    std::string outputDevice; // the device's name in the driver's vocabulary; "" = the driver's default
-    // The MIDI Clock submenu's tempo. Not an audio-device setting, but it belongs to the same
-    // native-owned, standalone-only settings file rather than earning one of its own. The transport's
-    // play/stop is deliberately NOT here: a tempo is a preference, a running clock is not — that starts
-    // stopped every launch.
-    double clockBpm = 120.0;
-};
-
-std::string audioCfgPath(AppState& a) { return a.svc.host.configDir() + "/audio.json"; }
-
-void loadAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
-    const std::string json = slurpTextFile(audioCfgPath(a));
-    if (json.empty()) return; // absent/unreadable → keep the compiled-in / --block-size-seeded defaults
-    const auto r = rfl::json::read<AudioCfgJson, rfl::DefaultIfMissing>(json);
-    if (!r) return; // unparseable → keep defaults
-    const AudioCfgJson c = r.value();
-    if (c.sampleRate > 0) a.reqSampleRate = c.sampleRate;
-    if (c.blockSize > 0) a.reqBlockSize = c.blockSize;
-    if (c.outChannels >= 2 && c.outChannels <= 8 && (c.outChannels % 2) == 0) a.reqOutChannels = c.outChannels;
-    a.reqOutputDevice = c.outputDevice; // resolved by name in the backend; falls back to its default if absent
-    if (c.clockBpm >= MidiClockSync::kMinBpm && c.clockBpm <= MidiClockSync::kMaxBpm)
-        a.clockBpmRequest.store(static_cast<float>(c.clockBpm), std::memory_order_relaxed);
-}
-
-void saveAudioConfig(AppState& a) {
-    const AudioCfgJson c{ a.reqSampleRate, a.reqBlockSize, a.reqOutChannels, -1, a.reqOutputDevice,
-                          a.clockBpmRequest.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) };
-    writeTextFile(audioCfgPath(a), rfl::json::write(c) + "\n");
-}
-
-// The chosen MIDI input/output device names (Settings > MIDI). "" = None in both directions (the virtual ports only),
-// the default; the input also takes rp::midi::kAllInputs ("*") as an explicit "every device".
-//
-// A SHIM, kept until the selection is the project's (a `midi` project section, its ports by name): this file holds one
-// name each, and the mapping onto the stream's lists lives in applyMidiSelection. Then it is ignored outright, like
-// audio.json, and the SDL app never shipped.
-//
-// NOTE for anyone reading an old midi.json: "" used to mean All Devices on the input side, and there is no way to tell
-// that apart from "never chose" - both wrote the same empty string. So an existing file simply lands on the current
-// default, which is the behaviour a default change should have.
-struct MidiCfgJson {
-    std::string input;
-    std::string output;
-};
-
-std::string midiCfgPath(AppState& a) { return a.svc.host.configDir() + "/midi.json"; }
-
-// The one-name mapping onto the stream's lists, shared by the startup load and the picker's hooks. It neither persists
-// nor logs: reading the stored file back over itself would rewrite it at every launch, and the log line belongs to the
-// user's change, not to a value the file already held.
-//
-// `mode` is the stream's: the load DIFFS, so reopening a project costs no connection it already had, while the picker's
-// change REOPENS, which is the user's one remedy for a port that was unplugged and plugged back in (there is no hotplug
-// watch).
-void selectMidi(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name, rp::midi::Apply mode) {
-    if (input) {
-        a.midiInputJson = name;
-        if (name.empty()) a.midi.setInputs({}, false, mode);
-        else if (name == rp::midi::kAllInputs) a.midi.setInputs({}, true, mode);
-        else a.midi.setInputs({name}, false, mode);
-    } else {
-        a.midiOutputJson = name;
-        if (name.empty()) a.midi.setOutputs({}, mode);
-        else a.midi.setOutputs({name}, mode);
-    }
-}
-
-void loadMidiConfig(AppState& a) {
-    const std::string json = slurpTextFile(midiCfgPath(a));
-    if (json.empty()) return;
-    const auto r = rfl::json::read<MidiCfgJson, rfl::DefaultIfMissing>(json);
-    if (!r) return;
-    const MidiCfgJson c = r.value();
-    // Applied when midi.open() publishes the ports: the same one-name mapping the picker's hooks use, in its diffing
-    // mode (nothing the file names is reopened here, because nothing is open yet).
-    selectMidi(a, true, c.input, rp::midi::Apply::Diff);
-    selectMidi(a, false, c.output, rp::midi::Apply::Diff);
-}
-
-void saveMidiConfig(AppState& a) {
-    const MidiCfgJson c{ a.midiInputJson, a.midiOutputJson };
-    writeTextFile(midiCfgPath(a), rfl::json::write(c) + "\n");
-}

-// Live audio reconfigure (the Audio settings submenu): AudioHost runs the whole sequence once (stop, release, open,
-// prepare with what the DEVICE obtained, start), and the chosen values are persisted so the next launch opens the same
-// device. Called on the UI thread. A no-change request costs nothing: AudioHost returns at once for a config it is
-// already running.
-void reconfigureAudio(AppState& a, int sampleRate, int blockSize, int channels, const std::string& device) {
-    a.reqSampleRate   = sampleRate;
-    a.reqBlockSize    = blockSize;
-    a.reqOutChannels  = channels;
-    a.reqOutputDevice = device;
-    applyAudioConfig(a);
-    saveAudioConfig(a);
-    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] audio reconfigured: %d Hz, %d frames, %d ch (backend '%s', device '%s')\n",
-                 a.reqSampleRate, a.reqBlockSize, a.reqOutChannels,
-                 a.reqBackend.empty() ? "auto" : a.reqBackend.c_str(),
-                 a.reqOutputDevice.empty() ? "default" : a.reqOutputDevice.c_str());
-}
-
-// Live MIDI device reselection (Settings > MIDI), while audio may be running. It does not stop audio: the stream closes
-// and opens inputs, each port cancelling its own callback as it goes, and replaces its output set through the epoch
-// handshake, which waits out at most the send in flight. A brief audio gap on a device change belongs to
-// reconfigureAudio alone, where the device itself changes.
-//
-// The picker offers one name each while midi.json is the selection's home (the shim): "" is None, "*" is every device
-// on the input side, and anything else is that port. The stream itself takes lists.
-void applyMidiSelection(AppState& a, bool input, const std::string& name) {
-    selectMidi(a, input, name, rp::midi::Apply::Reopen);
-    saveMidiConfig(a);  // the picker's change is the one that persists it (loadMidiConfig does not)
-    std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] MIDI %s device -> '%s'\n", input ? "input" : "output",
-                 name.empty() ? "None" : (name == rp::midi::kAllInputs ? "All Devices" : name.c_str()));
-}

-// True if the rendered frame is a single flat colour (nothing drew) — the CI smoke's "the UI actually
-// rendered, not just booted" gate. Compares the draw buffer as 32-bit pixels against the first.
-bool frameIsBlank(const AppState& a) {
-    if (a.drawBuf.size() < 8) return true;
-    const auto* px = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint32_t*>(a.drawBuf.data());
-    const std::size_t n = a.drawBuf.size() / 4;
-    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) if (px[i] != px[0]) return false;
-    return true;
-}

-    //
-    // Wayland is WM-controlled too, always. On X11 a resize request is VERIFIABLE: SDL_SetWindowSize round-trips
-    // it and reports back the geometry the WM actually granted (X11_SetWindowSize waits on the server, then
-    // sends RESIZED with the real size), so a WM that refuses is detected and adopted by onWindowSizeChanged.

-    a.requestedH = a.height;

-    // device after the persisted settings are read (main's audio step), so a run that names the null backend touches no

-void present(AppState& a) {

-// Adopt an actual window size — resize every dimension-tracking resource in lockstep: the SDL window (only
-// when WE initiated it; a WM-driven change already sized the window), the LVGL display resolution + its
-// DIRECT-mode draw buffer, and the streaming SDL texture (a STREAMING texture can't resize in place —
-// recreate it). Then force a full-window redraw and tell the UI so it re-lays-out. This inlines what DPF's
-// platform resize callback does for the plugin (LVGL::recreateTextureData + emit "resize").
-void applyWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h, bool fromWm) {
-    if (!a.window || !a.display || !a.renderer) return;
-    if (w == a.width && h == a.height && a.texture) return; // already at this size — nothing to realloc
-
-    if (!fromWm) SDL_SetWindowSize(a.window, static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(h)); // ask the WM
 
-    // LVGL display: set the new resolution, then re-point it at a freshly sized DIRECT buffer.
-    const lv_color_format_t cf = lv_display_get_color_format(a.display);
-    const std::uint32_t stride = lv_draw_buf_width_to_stride(w, cf);
-    a.drawBuf.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(stride) * h, 0);
-    lv_display_set_resolution(a.display, w, h);
-    lv_display_set_buffers(a.display, a.drawBuf.data(), nullptr, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(a.drawBuf.size()), LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT);

-    // SDL streaming texture: recreate at the new size (can't be resized in place).
-    if (a.texture) SDL_DestroyTexture(a.texture);
-    a.texture = SDL_CreateTexture(a.renderer, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888, SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_STREAMING,
-                                  static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(h));
-
-    a.width = w;
-    a.height = h;
-    a.dirty = true; // present the whole new surface next frame (lv_timer_handler redraws into the new buffer)
-    a.dirtyRect = {0, 0, static_cast<std::int32_t>(w) - 1, static_cast<std::int32_t>(h) - 1};
-
-    if (JSContext* ctx = a.ui.getContext()) { // mirror PluginUI::onResize → the UI re-reads Dimensions.window
-        JSValue args[2] = {JS_NewUint32(ctx, w), JS_NewUint32(ctx, h)};
-        a.ui.emit("resize", 2, args);

-// The __rp_setWindowSize seam: the UI asks the WM for a w×h window (grow/shrink to the grid). Mirrors
-// PluginUI::requestWindowSize — record the request as the clamp baseline, but don't fight a WM that owns
-// geometry (a tiling compositor or a fullscreen handheld); there the UI fits its grid via zoom instead.
-void requestWindowSize(AppState& a, std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h) {
-    // Clamp to the window minimum FIRST, because SDL_SetWindowSize does: a 1x/2x grid (160x144 / 320x288) is
-    // below the floor, so the window can only ever become 480x432. Applying the raw request would size the
-    // LVGL surface to something the window never takes - and a surface that doesn't match the window is
-    // exactly what a compositor scales to fit, which is how a freshly loaded tile ended up stretched across
-    // the whole window. The clamped size also has to be what we RECORD, or it comes back through
-    // onWindowSizeChanged as "a size we never asked for", i.e. a tiling takeover, wrongly latching
-    // wmControlled and killing fit-to-grid for the rest of the session.
-    w = std::max(w, kMinWindowW);
-    h = std::max(h, kMinWindowH);
-    a.requestedW = w; // recorded even when WM-controlled, so onWindowSizeChanged can still latch sizeHonored
-    a.requestedH = h;
-    if (a.wmControlled) {
-        if (a.debugResize)
-            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] resize request %ux%u ignored (WM owns geometry)\n", w, h);
-        return;
-    }
-    applyWindowSize(a, w, h, /*fromWm=*/false);
-}

-// SDL_WINDOWEVENT_SIZE_CHANGED: the actual window size changed (our SDL_SetWindowSize, a user drag, or a

-                     a.requestedH, (int)a.wmControlled, (int)a.sizeHonored);
-    applyWindowSize(a, w, h, /*fromWm=*/true);
-}
````

the split added or the anonymous namespace removed. The prototype's numbers are 1683 non-blank lines of `main.cpp` at
Task 3's tree and 1680 of them present in exactly one of the six files.

leg exits 0 and its `sdl` leg runs the app). The prototype also attempted a `c++ -fsyntax-only` per unit as a cheaper

execute 'd21'` (the five `/tmp/f5bpro/s4f-s2b-cc-*.log` record it), so no log backs a `-fsyntax-only` pass. The build
is the proof that stands. **The design's as-built text claims the opposite, and that claim is UNBACKED.** Section 13.1
says the five units "also pass `c++ -fsyntax-only`", and the S2b paragraphs of sections 8 and 10 make the same claim

records the wrapper's failure, not a pass. This plan quotes the design's diff unchanged in Task 6 (it is the
prototype's blob, and a quoted file is never edited), so the false sentence stays in the quoted text here; the final
review's follow-up corrects the design document itself.

normalisation would be guessing); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the

### Task 5: config sections, and the audio and MIDI settings as packages

Design section 6 (6.1 to 6.8) and the design's stage S3. `config.json` gets what F5a gave a project: a contribution
shape (`definePackage({ configSections })`, the same `ProjectSection` type), a generated registry, per-section stamps
with refuse-newer at section scope, and a generic `config` host group (`section` / `setSection`) replacing
`ConfigHost.controlSurface`. Three rules make the file safe to share between builds of different ages, and each is a
case: a key with no contributor is kept verbatim, a contributed block this session did not set is written back as the
file carried it, and an absent key is not invented. A write keeps today's re-read, and now computes the stamp check, the
merge and the refusal INSIDE the re-read (over the file on disk), so two processes can share the file and a newer
build's block is never overwritten.

The audio settings become the `audio` section (`backend`, `driver`, `device`, `sampleRate`, `blockSize`, `outChannels`;
render-ahead stays a flag); the MIDI selection becomes the project's `midi` section (`inputs: [{ name }]`, `allInputs`,
`outputs`, `clockBpm`), the clock tempo moving there from `audio.json`. `portMatch` resolves a saved name against a fresh
listing in TIERS (exact; ALSA's `<client>:<port>` stripped; RtMidi's trailing WinMM index stripped), each of which must
find exactly one port. The rows move into their packages over `settings.audio` and the `settings.midi` container the
shell keeps, with the `instance.clock` slot; the two host groups are OPTIONAL on `UiHost`, so the plugin and the DPF
standalone hide the rows as before. The startup rendezvous widens to wait for TS's first audio apply (or 500 ms), and the
native `__rp_audioApply` RECORDS the request: the device opens at the app's old point, after `midi.open()` and the
providers' restore. `ProjectHost.revision()` and `MenuBuilder.onOpen` are the edges the MIDI service re-resolves on - never
a render, which the whole-prototype review found costing 60 applies in 60 frames.

One record moves: the recorded menu matrix's three audio/MIDI seam cases, re-recorded with
`RP_MENU_MATRIX_UPDATE=standalone-start,standalone-instance,standalone-scan`.

- Modify (63 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 5 under `packages/retroplug/test-ui/`; 5 under `packages/retroplug/test/menu/`; 4 under `packages/native/sdl/`; 4 under `packages/retroplug/src/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/test/config/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/ui/host/` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 3: The shell's side: `configSections.ts`, the model, and the re-read write**

`src/configSections.ts` is new: `CORE_CONFIG_KEYS` (derived from `userConfigSchema`'s shape plus `schemaVersion`, so
nothing hand-keeps a second list), the entry and contributor lookups, `assertConfigSectionKey` (a core key and
`__proto__` refused), `parseConfigSection` / `serializeConfigSection` (the stamp rules), `readableConfigSection`
(defaults for a missing key; defaults for a block stamped NEWER), `parseConfigSections`, `serializeConfigSectionValue`
and `defaultConfigSections`. `userConfig.ts` loses the `controlSurface` schema and carries `ConfigModel { core,
sections, raw, written }`; `userConfigSerialization.ts` writes the shell's fields in the order the file always had and
then each section under its key, an untouched block from `raw` verbatim and only a session-set key from its parsed
value; and `userConfigStore.ts`'s `section` / `setSection` run the stamp check, the refused-warning and the
contributor's `merge` inside the store's apply callback over the RE-READ model, so a refusal writes nothing.
`projectStore.ts` bumps `revision()` in `newProject` and `commit`.

Create `packages/retroplug/src/configSections.ts`:

````ts
// config.json's sections (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 6.1): a package owns a root key of the user
// config, exactly as it owns a block of a project's `settings` (projectConfig.ts's sections). The shell keeps every
// non-core root key it does not know verbatim, so the plugin - which lists none of the audio or MIDI packages - writes
// a standalone's `audio` block back instead of erasing it; a section stamped newer than this build's contributor is
// kept verbatim and read as its defaults, refused at the section's own scope; and a write still re-reads the file,
// because two processes (the plugin and a standalone) may share it.
//
// This module is the model plus the parse/serialize half; UserConfigStore owns the file.
import type { ProjectSection } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { migrateRaw, type RawObject } from "./migrate";
import { readSectionVersion } from "./projectConfig";
import { CONFIG_SECTIONS } from "./generated/packages";
import { CORE_CONFIG_KEYS } from "./userConfig";

// The shell's own root keys are derived from its schema (userConfig.ts), so the list a contributor may not take is the
// schema's shape and nothing else. Re-exported here because this is the module the sections' rules live in.
export { CORE_CONFIG_KEYS };

/** A section's contributor and the package that declares it: the generated registry's entry, and the unit a warning
 *  names when the contributor's own code throws. */
export interface ConfigSectionEntry {
  readonly pkg: string;
  readonly section: ProjectSection;
}

/** The package's section under `key`, or undefined for a root key no package of this product contributes (its value is
 *  then kept verbatim). */
export function configSectionEntryOf(
  key: string,
  sections: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): ConfigSectionEntry | undefined {
  return sections.find((entry) => entry.section.key === key);
}

/** The section a package contributes under `key`, or undefined for a key no package of this product contributes. */
export function configSectionOf(
  key: string,
  sections: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): ProjectSection | undefined {
  return configSectionEntryOf(key, sections)?.section;
}

/** Warning keys already reported: a contributor's throw is one package's fault, so it is reported once per package and
 *  key, not once per load or per write. */
const warnedSections = new Set<string>();

function warnSectionOnce(entry: ConfigSectionEntry, doing: string, error: unknown): void {
  const key = `${entry.pkg}\u0000${entry.section.key}`;
  if (warnedSections.has(key)) return;
  warnedSections.add(key);
  console.warn(
    `[config] the ${entry.pkg} package's section ${entry.section.key} threw while ${doing}: ${String(error)}. ` +
      "Reading its defaults instead; the rest of config.json is unchanged.",
  );
}

/** A contributor's defaults, or `{}` when even those throw: a package's own breakage must not stop the config from
 *  loading, and there is nothing better to read than an empty block. */
export function configSectionDefaults(entry: ConfigSectionEntry): unknown {
  try {
    return entry.section.defaults();
  } catch (e) {
    warnSectionOnce(entry, "reading its defaults", e);
    return {};
  }
}

/** Every contributor's defaults, by key: what a config that never set a section reads, and what a fresh file starts
 *  with. */
export function defaultConfigSections(
  sections: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const entry of sections) out[entry.section.key] = configSectionDefaults(entry);
  return out;
}

/** A raw section carried up to its contributor's version and parsed, or kept verbatim. Kept verbatim when it is stamped
 *  NEWER than its contributor reads: the refuse-newer rule at section scope, so the rest of the file loads and this one
 *  block is neither read nor (see serializeConfigSection / UserConfigStore.setSection) written. */
export function parseConfigSection(contributor: ProjectSection, raw: unknown): unknown {
  const block = raw && typeof raw === "object" && !Array.isArray(raw) ? (raw as RawObject) : {};
  const version = contributor.version;
  // An additive-only section declares no version: nothing is stamped in it, so nothing needs migrating, and a stray
  // stamp in the file is just data its schema drops.
  if (version === undefined) return contributor.schema.parse(block);
  const stamped = readSectionVersion(block);
  if (stamped > version) return raw;
  return contributor.schema.parse(migrateRaw(block, stamped, version, contributor.migrations ?? {}));
}

/** A section as config.json writes it: a contributor that declares a version stamps its own, and a block this build
 *  kept verbatim because it is stamped newer is written back exactly as it came. */
export function serializeConfigSection(contributor: ProjectSection, value: unknown): unknown {
  const version = contributor.version;
  if (version === undefined) return value;
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) return value;
  const block = value as RawObject;
  if (readSectionVersion(block) > version) return value;
  return { ...block, schemaVersion: version };
}

/** Refuse a root key that is not a section a host may read or write: one of the shell's own fields (whose value in the
 *  file would become an object the next load clamps back to the default), or `__proto__`, which a plain assignment
 *  treats as a prototype rather than as a value. The generated registry refuses a contributor of the shell's keys;
 *  `__proto__` it cannot refuse (a manifest's member of that name is not its JSON's to declare), so this is the one
 *  gate for it. */
export function assertConfigSectionKey(key: string): void {
  if (CORE_CONFIG_KEYS.includes(key)) {
    throw new Error(`${key} is one of the shell's own config keys, not a config section`);
  }
  if (key === "__proto__") throw new Error("__proto__ is not a config section: it names a prototype");
}

/** What a READER of a section gets: its contributor's parsed value, or its defaults when the block is stamped newer
 *  than this build reads (the refuse-newer rule at section scope). Only the writer keeps the raw block: a reader handed
 *  a block it cannot parse would be typed `T` and hold something else. */
export function readableConfigSection<T = unknown>(
  sections: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
  key: string,
  contributors: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): T {
  const entry = configSectionEntryOf(key, contributors);
  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sections, key)) {
    // A section this product contributes but the file has never carried reads as its contributor's defaults. The shell
    // does NOT write that block out until the section is set: a file written by an older build round-trips byte for
    // byte, which is what lets the plugin (no audio section) write a standalone's config without inventing one.
    return (entry ? configSectionDefaults(entry) : undefined) as T;
  }
  const raw = sections[key];
  if (entry?.section.version !== undefined && raw !== null && typeof raw === "object" && !Array.isArray(raw)) {
    if (readSectionVersion(raw as RawObject) > entry.section.version) return configSectionDefaults(entry) as T;
  }
  return raw as T;
}

/** Store a section by key as an own, enumerable property. `Object.defineProperty` rather than assignment, because a
 *  hand-edited `__proto__` key is data the shell keeps: assigning it would set this object's prototype and drop the key
 *  on the next save. */
export function putConfigSection(sections: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, value: unknown): void {
  Object.defineProperty(sections, key, { value, enumerable: true, writable: true, configurable: true });
}

/** The sections of a raw config root exactly as the file carried them: every root key the shell does not own, its
 *  value untouched. A block this session does not set is written back from here (the verbatim-keep rule), which is what
 *  preserves a field a newer build added. */
export function rawConfigSections(raw: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> {
  const sections: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(raw)) {
    if (CORE_CONFIG_KEYS.includes(key)) continue;
    putConfigSection(sections, key, value);
  }
  return sections;
}

/** The sections of a raw config root: every root key the shell does not own, through its contributor (or kept
 *  verbatim). A contributor's key the file does not have is ABSENT here, not filled: `readableConfigSection` answers
 *  its defaults, and a write of the file leaves the file as it was rather than stamping a block nobody set. */
export function parseConfigSections(
  raw: Record<string, unknown>,
  contributors: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const sections: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(raw)) {
    if (CORE_CONFIG_KEYS.includes(key)) continue;
    const entry = configSectionEntryOf(key, contributors);
    let parsed = value;
    if (entry) {
      try {
        parsed = parseConfigSection(entry.section, value);
      } catch (e) {
        warnSectionOnce(entry, "parsing its saved block", e);
        parsed = configSectionDefaults(entry);
      }
    }
    putConfigSection(sections, key, parsed);
  }
  return sections;
}

/** A section by key as config.json writes it: its contributor's stamping, or the raw value unchanged. */
export function serializeConfigSectionValue(
  key: string,
  value: unknown,
  contributors: readonly ConfigSectionEntry[] = CONFIG_SECTIONS,
): unknown {
  const contributor = configSectionOf(key, contributors);
  return contributor ? serializeConfigSection(contributor, value) : value;
}
````
