````ts
// Port-name matching (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 6.3): a project saves the ports it opened, and the
// same rig on another machine, or the same machine after other clients came and went, lists them under names with
// volatile parts. The table below is the whole point of the module: real ALSA, WinMM and CoreMIDI names, and the rule
// that a normalised match has to be UNIQUE.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { foldPortName, resolvePort, resolvePorts } from "../portMatch";

/** The names a real machine lists, by platform: ALSA's "<client>:<port> <client#>:<port#>" (RtMidi's form), WinMM's
 *  "<name> <index>" suffix (deps/rtmidi appends the port number to every Windows name), and CoreMIDI's own spelling.
 *
 *  The WinMM and CoreMIDI rows are UNVERIFIED: no Windows or macOS machine has listed its ports for this table yet
 *  (design section 11). The WinMM form is the vendored RtMidi's own (deps/rtmidi/RtMidi.cpp's getPortName), and the
 *  CoreMIDI rows are the spellings the Launchpad pack's tests carry; the agents replace them with real listings. */
const ALSA = [
  "LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 24:0",
  "Launchpad Pro MK3:Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI 28:0",
  "Midi Through:Midi Through Port-0 14:0",
  "Arturia KeyStep 32:Arturia KeyStep 32 MIDI 1 20:0",
  // A two-port interface: both names end in a number of their own, and only the client:port suffix is volatile.
  "MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 1 28:0",
  "MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 2 28:1",
];
const WINMM = ["Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth 0", "MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A 1", "MIDISPORT 2x2 Port B 2"];
const COREMIDI = ["Launchpad Pro MK3", "IAC Driver Bus 1", "Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI"];

test("an exact name wins, and needs no normalising", () => {
  expect(resolvePort("IAC Driver Bus 1", COREMIDI)).toBe("IAC Driver Bus 1");
  expect(resolvePort("Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth 0", WINMM)).toBe("Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth 0");
});

test("ALSA's client:port numbers move, and the saved name still finds its port", () => {
  // The same interface, listed after another client came and went: the saved 24:0 is 28:0 now, and 26:0 is not in the
  // list at all.
  expect(resolvePort("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 26:0", ALSA)).toBe("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 24:0");
  expect(resolvePort("Launchpad Pro MK3:Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI 26:0", ALSA)).toBe(
    "Launchpad Pro MK3:Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI 28:0",
  );
  expect(resolvePort("Midi Through:Midi Through Port-0 99:0", ALSA)).toBe("Midi Through:Midi Through Port-0 14:0");
});

test("WinMM's trailing index moves, and the saved name still finds its port", () => {
  // A driver reinstalled (or another device added) renumbers the list, not the name (RtMidi's own suffix form).
  expect(resolvePort("MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A 9", WINMM)).toBe("MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A 1");
  expect(resolvePort("MIDISPORT 2x2 Port B 4", WINMM)).toBe("MIDISPORT 2x2 Port B 2");
  expect(resolvePort("Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth 0", WINMM)).toBe("Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth 0"); // exact
  // A name that already ended in a number on a platform that does not append one still matches exactly first.
  expect(resolvePort("IAC Driver Bus 1", COREMIDI)).toBe("IAC Driver Bus 1");
});

test("CoreMIDI's repeated device name folds to one, in both directions", () => {
  expect(resolvePort("Launchpad Pro MK3 Launchpad Pro MK3", COREMIDI)).toBe("Launchpad Pro MK3");
  expect(resolvePort("Launchpad Pro MK3", ["Launchpad Pro MK3 Launchpad Pro MK3"]))
    .toBe("Launchpad Pro MK3 Launchpad Pro MK3");
  // The port name that carries the device name and its own does NOT fold the same way: ".. MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI" is not a
  // repeat, so it stays itself rather than colliding with the bare device name.
  expect(foldPortName("Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI")).toBe("Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI");
});

test("ALSA's multi-port interface keeps its two ports apart when the client renumbers", () => {
  // The case the ALSA rule exists for, on an interface whose port names END in a number: with the index rule applied
  // to every name, "MIDI 1 24:0" and "MIDI 2 28:1" both folded to "... MIDI", so the saved entry matched two ports (or
  // none) and the row said "(missing)" after every renumber. Only the trailing client:port may move.
  expect(resolvePort("MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 1 24:0", ALSA))
    .toBe("MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 1 28:0");
  expect(resolvePort("MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 2 24:1", ALSA))
    .toBe("MIDISPORT 2x2:MIDISPORT 2x2 MIDI 2 28:1");
});

test("spacing is the machine's punctuation, not the device's name", () => {
  expect(resolvePort("Arturia  KeyStep 32 ", ["Arturia KeyStep 32"])).toBe("Arturia KeyStep 32");
  expect(resolvePort("Arturia KeyStep 32", [" Arturia  KeyStep 32 "])).toBe(" Arturia  KeyStep 32 ");
});

test("two candidates resolve to nothing; so does none", () => {
  // Two identical interfaces: the stem matches both, and guessing would silently drive the wrong one.
  const two = ["LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 24:0", "LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 30:0"];
  expect(resolvePort("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 26:0", two)).toBe(null);
  // Nothing present matches the saved name at all.
  expect(resolvePort("Some Synth", ALSA)).toBe(null);
  expect(resolvePort("", COREMIDI)).toBe(null);
  // A name that normalises away entirely names nothing.
  expect(resolvePort("   ", COREMIDI)).toBe(null);
});

test("a whole saved list resolves in order, dropping what opened nothing", () => {
  const saved = ["Launchpad Pro MK3", "Gone Synth", "IAC Driver Bus 1", "Launchpad Pro MK3"];
  expect(resolvePorts(saved, COREMIDI)).toEqual(["Launchpad Pro MK3", "IAC Driver Bus 1"]);
});
````

````ts
// A fake MIDI stream for the menu and UI tests: the two globals (and the transport trio) the SDL host binds, over port
// lists the test owns. Nothing opens a port - the real stream is proved by retroplug-midi-test over the fake backend -
// so a test machine's MIDI gear is never listed or touched (the Zoom L6 rule and the port filter's).
import type { MidiDescription, MidiSelection, TransportState } from "@retroplug/core/host";

interface MidiHooks {
  __rp_midiDescribe?: () => MidiDescription | null;
  __rp_midiApply?: (selection: MidiSelection, mode: "diff" | "reopen") => void;
  __rp_getTransport?: () => Partial<TransportState>;
  __rp_setTransport?: (playing: boolean) => void;
  __rp_setClockBpm?: (bpm: number) => void;
}

const globals = globalThis as unknown as MidiHooks;

export interface FakeMidiDeviceOptions {
  inputs?: string[];
  outputs?: string[];
  supportsVirtual?: boolean;
  reserved?: { input: string; output: string };
  /** What the stream "opened", which is what the "(missing)" rows read. Defaults to every listed port. */
  openedInputs?: string[];
  openedOutputs?: string[];
  transport?: Partial<TransportState>;
}

export class FakeMidiDevice {
  description: MidiDescription;
  transportState: TransportState;
  /** Every selection applied, in order, with its mode. */
  readonly applied: { selection: MidiSelection; mode: string }[] = [];
  readonly tempos: number[] = [];
  readonly transports: boolean[] = [];
  private open: boolean;

  constructor(options: FakeMidiDeviceOptions = {}) {
    const inputs = options.inputs ?? ["Launchpad Pro MK3", "Arturia KeyStep 32"];
    const outputs = options.outputs ?? ["Deluge"];
    this.description = {
      inputs,
      outputs,
      openedInputs: options.openedInputs ?? inputs,
      openedOutputs: options.openedOutputs ?? outputs,
      supportsVirtual: options.supportsVirtual ?? true,
      reserved: options.reserved ?? { input: "", output: "" },
    };
    const t = options.transport ?? {};
    this.transportState = {
      playing: t.playing ?? false,
      external: t.external ?? false,
      bpm: t.bpm ?? 120,
      localBpm: t.localBpm ?? 120,
    };
    this.open = true;
  }

  install(): this {
    globals.__rp_midiDescribe = () => (this.open ? this.description : null);
    globals.__rp_midiApply = (selection, mode) => {
      this.applied.push({
        selection: { ...selection, inputs: [...selection.inputs], outputs: [...selection.outputs] },
        mode,
      });
      // What the stream does: what it resolved and the reservation let through is what opened.
      this.description = {
        ...this.description,
        openedInputs: selection.allInputs
          ? this.description.inputs.filter((n) => n !== this.description.reserved.input)
          : selection.inputs.filter(
            (n) => this.description.inputs.includes(n) && n !== this.description.reserved.input,
          ),
        openedOutputs: selection.outputs.filter(
          (n) => this.description.outputs.includes(n) && n !== this.description.reserved.output,
        ),
      };
    };
    globals.__rp_getTransport = () => ({ ...this.transportState });
    globals.__rp_setTransport = (playing) => {
      this.transports.push(playing);
      this.transportState = { ...this.transportState, playing };
    };
    globals.__rp_setClockBpm = (bpm) => {
      this.tempos.push(bpm);
      this.transportState = { ...this.transportState, localBpm: bpm, ...(this.transportState.external ? {} : { bpm }) };
    };
    return this;
  }

  uninstall(): void {
    delete globals.__rp_midiDescribe;
    delete globals.__rp_midiApply;
    delete globals.__rp_getTransport;
    delete globals.__rp_setTransport;
    delete globals.__rp_setClockBpm;
  }

  /** An external clock master starts, stops or retempos: the rows follow it without anyone touching the menu. */
  setExternal(external: boolean, bpm = this.transportState.bpm): void {
    this.transportState = { ...this.transportState, external, bpm, ...(external ? { playing: true } : {}) };
  }
}
````

````diff
+/** A port the control surface holds: never openable by the stream, so it is marked and never offered as a pick or as
+ *  "(missing)" - it IS here, and it is held. */
+function reservedRow(id: string, name: string): MenuItem {
+  return infoRow(id, `[ ] ${name} (control surface)`);
+}
+
+function midiSettingsChildren(host: UiHost): MenuItem[] {
+  const dev = host.midiDevice;
+  if (!dev) return []; // no MIDI stream on this host (a DAW routes MIDI): the container is empty
+  const described = currentDescription(dev);
+  if (!described) return []; // a stream that cannot describe itself shows no picker
+  const section = host.project.section<MidiSection>(MIDI_SECTION_KEY);
+  const { missingInputs, missingOutputs } = resolveSelection(section, described);
+  const write = (patch: Record<string, unknown>) => host.project.setSection(MIDI_SECTION_KEY, patch);
+
+  /** Toggle one port in one direction. A checked row is open (or every input is wanted): taking it out removes every
+   *  entry that resolves to it and turns All devices off, so the tap always does something real. An unchecked row adds
+   *  the name; one that is already saved but did not open is a RETRY (a reopen), which is what the exclusive-port case
+   *  on Windows needs. */
+  const toggle = (direction: "inputs" | "outputs", port: string, checked: boolean): void => {
+    const entries = direction === "inputs" ? section.inputs : section.outputs;
+    const named = entriesFor(entries, direction === "inputs" ? described.inputs : described.outputs, port);
+    if (checked) {
+      write({
+        [direction]: entries.filter((entry) => !named.includes(entry)),
+        ...(direction === "inputs" ? { allInputs: false } : {}),
+      });
+    } else if (named.length > 0) {
+      applySection(dev, section, "reopen", described); // saved, resolved, refused: try it again
+    } else {
+      write({ [direction]: [...entries, { name: port }] });
+    }
+  };
+
+  const reservedIn = described.reserved.input;
+  const reservedOut = described.reserved.output;
+  const inputRows = described.inputs
+    .filter((name) => name !== reservedIn)
+    .map((name, i) => {
+      const saved = entriesFor(section.inputs, described.inputs, name).length > 0;
+      const checked = described.openedInputs.includes(name) && (section.allInputs || saved);
+      return portRow(`midi-input-${i}`, name, checked, () => toggle("inputs", name, checked));
+    });
+  const outputRows = described.outputs
+    .filter((name) => name !== reservedOut)
+    .map((name, i) => {
+      const checked =
+        described.openedOutputs.includes(name) &&
+        entriesFor(section.outputs, described.outputs, name).length > 0;
+      return portRow(`midi-output-${i}`, name, checked, () => toggle("outputs", name, checked));
+    });
+  return [
+    infoRow("midi-project", "Saved with this project"),
+    // Every hardware input at once, an explicit choice rather than the default: opening them all makes anything
+    // plugged in a MIDI source, so a control surface's free-running clock would drive the host tempo.
+    action("midi-all-inputs", `${section.allInputs ? "[x]" : "[ ]"} All devices`,
+      () => write({ allInputs: !section.allInputs })),
+    ...inputRows,
+    ...(reservedIn ? [reservedRow("midi-reserved-in", reservedIn)] : []),
+    ...missingInputs.map((entry, i) => infoRow(`midi-missing-in-${i}`, `${entry.name} (missing)`)),
+    separator("midi-sep-outputs"),
+    ...outputRows,
+    ...(reservedOut ? [reservedRow("midi-reserved-out", reservedOut)] : []),
+    ...missingOutputs.map((entry, i) => infoRow(`midi-missing-out-${i}`, `${entry.name} (missing)`)),
+    separator("midi-sep-rescan"),
+    // Re-resolve the saved names against a fresh listing and reopen every port: the one remedy for a device that was
+    // unplugged and plugged back in (there is no hotplug watch). A click, so the fresh read is this row's own.
+    {
+      ...action("midi-rescan", "Rescan", () => {
+        const fresh = dev.describe();
+        if (!fresh) return;
+        listing = { dev, value: fresh };
+        applySection(dev, section, "reopen", fresh);
+      }),
+      keepOpen: true,
+    },
+  ];
+}
+
+/** Settings > MIDI's rows, in the shell's MIDI container. Opening that container is one of the two moments the design
+ *  names for a re-resolve (the other is a project load), and the shell's open hook is how a package hears it: the
+ *  service re-reads the machine and diffs once, and no render touches a device. */
+const midiMenu: MenuBuilder = {
+  placement: "settings.midi",
+  build: (host) => midiSettingsChildren(host),
+  onOpen: () => requestReapply(),
+};
+
+/** The MIDI Clock submenu (Instance menu > MIDI Clock): a clock control, not a cosmetic one, because while the
+ *  transport runs the LSDj / risa sync roles turn it into link-port clock for the cart. The tempo is the project's now;
+ *  the transport starts stopped at every launch and is never saved. While an external master is running it owns both
+ *  values, so the rows show ITS state and go inert. */
+function clockChildren(host: UiHost, t: NonNullable<ReturnType<MidiDeviceHost["transport"]>>, bpm: number): MenuItem[] {
+  if (t.external) {
+    return [
+      infoRow("inst-clock-source", "Source: External MIDI clock"),
+      infoRow("inst-clock-transport", `Transport: ${t.playing ? "Playing" : "Stopped"}`),
+      infoRow("inst-clock-tempo", `Tempo: ${Math.round(t.bpm)} BPM`),
+    ];
+  }
+  const step = (delta: number) =>
+    host.project.setSection(MIDI_SECTION_KEY, {
+      clockBpm: Math.min(CLOCK_BPM_MAX, Math.max(CLOCK_BPM_MIN, Math.round(bpm + delta))),
+    });
+  return [
+    cycler("inst-clock-transport", "Transport", ["Stopped", "Playing"], t.playing ? 1 : 0, (n) =>
+      host.midiDevice?.setTransport(n === 1),
+    ),
+    {
+      // Not a `cycler`: the tempo is a range, not a list of options. Same keys though - Left/Right step by one,
+      // PageUp/PageDown by ten (onCoarseStep, as the render-duration row uses), Enter nudges up.
+      id: "inst-clock-tempo",
+      label: `Tempo: ${Math.round(t.localBpm)} BPM`,
+      kind: "cycler",
+      keepOpen: true,
+      onSelect: () => step(CLOCK_BPM_STEP),
+      onCycle: (dir) => step(dir * CLOCK_BPM_STEP),
+      onCoarseStep: (dir) => step(dir * CLOCK_BPM_COARSE_STEP),
+    },
+  ];
+}
+
+function clockRow(host: UiHost): MenuItem[] {
+  const dev = host.midiDevice;
+  const t = dev?.transport();
+  if (!dev || !t) return [];
+  const bpm = host.project.section<MidiSection>(MIDI_SECTION_KEY).clockBpm;
+  const state = t.playing ? `${Math.round(t.bpm)} BPM` : "Stopped";
+  return [separator("inst-sep-transport"), submenu("inst-clock", `MIDI Clock: ${state}`, clockChildren(host, t, bpm))];
+}
+
+/** The host-transport block, between the instance's own groups. */
+const clockMenu: MenuBuilder = {
+  placement: "instance.clock",
+  build: (host) => clockRow(host),
+};
+
+/** The listing the rows render from, the section the last apply resolved, and what the rows printed last: the latches a
+ *  mount puts back, and what makes the poll report a change once rather than every frame. */
+let lastSection = "";
+let lastClock = Number.NaN;
+let lastRevision = Number.NaN;
+let lastRows = "";
+/** A re-resolve is due: the shell's Settings > MIDI container was opened, and the list a project was resolved against may
+ *  be older than the machine (a device plugged in since). */
+let reapplyRequested = false;
+
+/** Ask the service to re-read and diff once on its next poll (the container opened). */
+function requestReapply(): void {
+  reapplyRequested = true;
+}
+
+/** The MIDI service: watches the project's `midi` section and applies it (a project load, a row's pick, a Rescan), drives
+ *  the clock tempo, and repaints the rows when what they show moves.
+ *
+ *  It re-resolves on the edges only, never on a render: the mount, a section or project change, the container opening,
+ *  and a listing that is not the one the last apply resolved against. That last one is what "a device plugged in since"
+ *  means - there is no hotplug watch, so the machine is read when one of the other edges makes it worth reading.
+ *
+ *  The FIRST apply lands on the first poll, not on start: the services start in product order and the Launchpad's
+ *  restore (a claim) comes after this package's, so a hardware port the claim holds is never opened first and then
+ *  taken away - on Windows that would be a refused open, everywhere else a pad heard twice for a frame. The same
+ *  ordering is why the AUDIO service applies on its first poll too. */
+const midiService: UiService = {
+  id: "midi-ports",
+  start: () => {
+    listing = null;
+    lastSection = "";
+    lastClock = Number.NaN;
+    lastRevision = Number.NaN;
+    lastRows = "";
+    reapplyRequested = false;
+  },
+  poll: {
+    frames: 1,
+    run: (host) => {
+      const dev = host.midiDevice;
+      if (!dev) return false;
+      const section = host.project.section<MidiSection>(MIDI_SECTION_KEY);
+      // The tempo is applied on its own below: a clock-only change must not reopen the ports.
+      const key = JSON.stringify({ inputs: section.inputs, allInputs: section.allInputs, outputs: section.outputs });
+      // A project load re-resolves even when the new project saved the same names (another machine's ports may be the
+      // ones that are here now).
+      const revision = host.project.revision();
+      if (listing?.dev !== dev || reapplyRequested || key !== lastSection || revision !== lastRevision) {
+        // The fresh listing is what the saved names are resolved against, so a port that came or went since the last
+        // apply (the machine's list changed, not the project's) is exactly what this read picks up.
+        const fresh = dev.describe();
+        if (fresh) {
+          lastSection = key;
+          lastRevision = revision;
+          reapplyRequested = false;
+          applySection(dev, section, "diff", fresh);
+          // What the apply opened, so the checkboxes follow a pick without waiting for another edge.
+          listing = { dev, value: dev.describe() ?? fresh };
+        }
+      }
+      const bpm = section.clockBpm || DEFAULT_CLOCK_BPM;
+      if (bpm !== lastClock) {
+        lastClock = bpm;
+        dev.setClockBpm(bpm);
+      }
+      // The rows follow the listing, the section and the transport: a poll repaints only when one of them moved.
+      const rows = rowsKey(listing?.value ?? null, section, dev.transport());
+      const moved = rows !== lastRows;
+      lastRows = rows;
+      return moved;
+    },
+  },
+};
+
+export default defineUi({
+  menus: [midiMenu, clockMenu],
+  services: [midiService],
+});
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The shell's UI host and menus**

`ui/host/uiHost.ts` builds the generic `config` group and the two device groups over the six hooks, absent where the
hooks do not exist (so the plugin and the DPF standalone hide the rows); `nativeHooks.ts` declares them;
`menuContributions.ts` gains `menuPlacementOpen(placement, host)`, which collects the placement's open hooks so the
shell's container rows can call them without naming a package; `menuDefs.ts`'s `container()` helper passes one to the
Settings > Audio and Settings > MIDI rows and the audio/MIDI/clock rows themselves move out; `Menu.tsx`'s `activate`
runs a submenu's `onOpen` when it OPENS (never on a render, never on a close); `App.tsx` starts the services in
product order and pumps UI frames in the rendezvous.

````diff
+    apply: (selection, mode = "diff") => native.__rp_midiApply?.(selection, mode),
+    transport: () => {
+      const t = native.__rp_getTransport?.();
+      if (!t) return null;
+      // The tempo a clock master is driving is the one the row shows; our own comes back when it leaves. A host that
+      // cannot say reads the free-run defaults, as the menu always did.
+      const bpm = typeof t.bpm === "number" && t.bpm > 0 ? t.bpm : 120;
+      return {
+        playing: t.playing === true,
+        external: t.external === true,
+        bpm,
+        localBpm: typeof t.localBpm === "number" && t.localBpm > 0 ? t.localBpm : bpm,
+      };
     },
+    setTransport: (playing) => native.__rp_setTransport?.(playing),
+    setClockBpm: (bpm) => native.__rp_setClockBpm?.(bpm),
   };
 }
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The Launchpad's `controlSurface` as a config section**

The pack owns `ControlSurfaceSettings` and its section under the SAME root key `controlSurface` with the same four
fields, so an existing `config.json`'s bytes do not move (E8); the pack's app module contributes it, and
`launchpadDevices.ts` reads and writes it through `host.config.section("controlSurface")` / `setSection`.

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/control/configSection.ts`:

````ts
// The control surface's config section (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md sections 6.1 and 6.2): the machine's
// port pair, where it lives in config.json. The key, its four fields and their order are the ones config.json always
// carried, so the pack, not the shell, decides what a control surface's stored state is.
//
// HOST state rather than project state: port names belong to the machine, and one process holds one device for every
// project it has open. The port names are opaque - often an interface's, not the device's, since a Launchpad also
// speaks TRS/DIN - and `device` is what a scan read off the hardware ("" = never scanned), shown and never
// interpreted.
//
// The parse is written out rather than made of zod fields, as the pack's project section is: the section contract asks
// only for a `parse`, and junk snaps to the default instead of failing the whole file.
import type { ProjectSection } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";

export interface ControlSurfaceSettings {
  input: string; // "" = none chosen
  output: string;
  enabled: boolean; // the user's Connect: claim the pair now, and again at the next launch
  device: string;
}

/** The section's root key in config.json, which is also what the shell's `config` host group reads it by. */
export const CONTROL_SURFACE_SECTION_KEY = "controlSurface";

const isObject = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> =>
  v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);

const stringOf = (v: unknown): string => (typeof v === "string" ? v : "");

function parseControlSurface(raw: unknown): ControlSurfaceSettings {
  const block = isObject(raw) ? raw : {};
  return {
    input: stringOf(block.input),
    output: stringOf(block.output),
    enabled: block.enabled === true,
    device: stringOf(block.device),
  };
}

/** The section the generated registry hands the shell: no `version` (nothing about it has needed a migration), so its
 *  bytes are what they always were and a block this build does not understand is kept as it came. */
export const controlSurfaceSection: ProjectSection<ControlSurfaceSettings> = {
  key: CONTROL_SURFACE_SECTION_KEY,
  schema: { parse: parseControlSurface },
  defaults: () => parseControlSurface({}),
};
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The native side: the six hooks, the recorded apply, and the rendezvous**

`hooks.cpp`'s eight old globals become six: `__rp_audioDescribe` (with `overrides`, what this run's flags pin),
`__rp_audioBackendDrivers(id)` (`[]` while a run pins a backend), `__rp_audioApply(choice)` (which RECORDS the request
while the host has not reached its own point and only sets `audioApplied`, the rendezvous' word), `__rp_audioStatus`
(with `live`), `__rp_midiDescribe` (with `openedInputs` / `openedOutputs`) and `__rp_midiApply(sel, mode)`. A hook
call that omits a field reads it as `""` (`readString` once turned a missing `driver` into the string "undefined" and
muted the run), `apply` validates the channels (2, 4, 6, 8) and a positive rate and block, and `__rp_setClockBpm` no
longer persists. `audioLoop.cpp` loses the `audio.json` and `midi.json` shims and renames `restoreControlSurface` to
`waitForUiStartup`, which waits on the control surface's `restored()` and on `audioApplied`, bounded at 500 ms,
printing `audio: the UI did not apply its settings; starting on the defaults` at the bound; `main.cpp` opens the
device at its one old point, after `midi.open()` and `rp_restore_providers`, with the recorded request or the
defaults, and then sets `a.audioDeviceReady` so a UI apply is live.

- [ ] **Step 10: The tests that move with the rows, and the matrix's three seam cases DERIVED**

Every existing test that read the old seam is re-pointed in this commit (the typecheck RED above is the record that
each is a named edge): the config, project, graph, hosts, menu, services, scanner and `test-ui` files, and
`test-native/launchpad-devices` over the generic config group. None of them changes a case's meaning, and the `test`
leg's file and case counts below are the run's.

````diff
+test("building the menus never enumerates a sibling audio backend", async () => {
+  // C1 of the F5b S3 review: a builder that asks every backend for its drivers initialises PortAudio and SDL audio at
+  // launch (and on every menu render) whatever the run pinned. The fake describes only the backend IN FORCE and counts
+  // every backendDrivers call, so this is the same path the native hook takes.
+  const fake = new FakeAudioDevice().install();
+  const g = globalThis as { __rp_isStandalone?: boolean };
+  g.__rp_isStandalone = true;
+  const { resetAudioDraft } = await import("@retroplug/audio/ui");
+  resetAudioDraft();
+  try {
+    const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
+    const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be, notify: () => {} });
+    const startItems = buildStartMenu(ctxOf(stores)).items;
+    // The Settings children are built EAGERLY as part of the menu (that was the leak's path), and so is the instance
+    // menu's copy.
+    const settings = submenuChildren(startItems, "start-settings");
+    expect(settings.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    be.seed("/roms/a.gb", gbRom());
+    const id = stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
+    const sys = stores.project.systems.view().find((s) => s.id === id)!;
+    buildInstanceMenu({ ...ctxOf(stores), system: sys });
+    // Opening Settings > Audio is a menu build too, and asks for nothing by itself.
+    const audioItems = submenuChildren(settings, "set-audio");
+    expect(audioItems.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    expect(fake.backendDriversCalls).toEqual([]);
+
+    // Only the explicit step on the Driver row enumerates a sibling, once, and its drivers then read.
+    expect(findItem(audioItems, "audio-drivers-more")).toBeTruthy();
+    findItem(audioItems, "audio-drivers-more")!.onSelect!();
+    expect(fake.backendDriversCalls).toEqual(["sdl"]);
+    const audioRows = () => submenuChildren(submenuChildren(buildStartMenu(ctxOf(stores)).items, "start-settings"), "set-audio");
+    // The fetched backend's drivers are in the row now: Auto -> PortAudio's two -> SDL's one.
+    findItem(audioRows(), "audio-driver")!.onCycle!(1);
+    findItem(audioRows(), "audio-driver")!.onCycle!(1);
+    findItem(audioRows(), "audio-driver")!.onCycle!(1);
+    const last = audioRows();
+    expect(findItem(last, "audio-driver")!.label).toBe("Driver: SDL: pipewire");
+    // The second backend is the only sibling, so the row is gone once it has been asked for.
+    expect(findItem(last, "audio-drivers-more")).toBe(undefined);
+  } finally {
+    resetAudioDraft();
+    fake.uninstall();
+    delete g.__rp_isStandalone;
+  }
+});
+
+test("a muted device keeps Apply live, and the audio service repaints when the status moves", async () => {
+  const fake = new FakeAudioDevice().install();
+  const g = globalThis as { __rp_isStandalone?: boolean };
+  g.__rp_isStandalone = true;
+  const { resetAudioDraft, default: audioUi } = await import("@retroplug/audio/ui");
+  const { createUiHost } = await import("../../ui/host/uiHost");
+  resetAudioDraft();
+  try {
+    const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: new MockBackend("/cfg"), notify: () => {} });
+    const host = createUiHost(stores, { views: { open: () => {} }, beginImport: () => {} });
+    fake.mute("the device went away");
+    const items = submenuChildren(submenuChildren(buildStartMenu(ctxOf(stores)).items, "start-settings"), "set-audio");
+    // The status row says why, and Apply - though the draft is clean - is the retry.
+    expect(findItem(items, "audio-status")!.label).toBe("Muted: the device went away");
+    expect(findItem(items, "audio-apply")!.disabled).toBeFalsy();
+
+    // The service's first poll applies the saved section (clearing the mute), and a later move repaints once.
+    const svc = audioUi.services!.find((s) => s.id === "audio-device")!;
+    svc.start!(host);
+    expect(svc.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
+    expect(svc.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
+    fake.mute("lost again");
+    expect(svc.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
+  } finally {
+    resetAudioDraft();
+    fake.uninstall();
+    delete g.__rp_isStandalone;
+  }
+});
````

`sdl:controller` is rewritten around the project section: its three `midi.json` writes become autoloaded projects with
a `midi` section (`all-inputs.rplg`, `scan-project.rplg`), and its leg 2's ordering assertion becomes "the claim
precedes `] running ` and the claimed port is NEVER opened as a hardware input by the stream" (it would have failed
under the old rule, because the virtual ports open first now). `sdl:smoke`'s audio-hook leg reads `__rp_audioDescribe`
and the status an Apply adopted, its transport leg loads a project whose `midi.clockBpm` is 140 (so E7 is proved), it
gains the E12 leg (a saved section at 512 with `--block-size 256`) and the startup-order leg; both harnesses assert
the negative `audio: the UI did not apply its settings`. `check-doc-links.mjs` reports a dead link inside a
`*-plan.md` RECORD as a warning rather than editing the record (which is why `docs/launchpad-plan.md` stays
byte-identical although the pack's rows moved out of the shell).

````diff

+                // can see what was proposed; it is never edited, so a file it cites may since have moved. Reported, not
+                // failed: the record is right and the tree moved, and the fix belongs to whoever reads the plan.
+                if (/-plan\.md$/.test(file)) warnings.push(`${where}  dead link in a plan record  ${href}`);

 wait "$OTHER_PID" || { cat "$TMP/first.log" >&2; fail "first run exited non-zero"; }
 OTHER_PID=""
 # The refusal is SAID (a silent second process - one that never even tried - must not pass), and the pair is
diff --git a/tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh b/tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh
index 61d48ecd5..5058e777f 100755
--- a/tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh
+++ b/tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh
@@ -62,11 +62,15 @@ run() {
     fi
 }
 want() { grep -qE "$2" "$1" || { cat "$1" >&2; fail "$3"; }; }
+# A line the run MUST NOT print: the rendezvous's own failure report. It means the audio service never applied the
+# `audio` section, so the app started on the defaults after the half-second bound.
+refuse() { ! grep -qF "audio: the UI did not apply its settings" "$1" || { cat "$1" >&2; fail "$2"; }; }
 
 # 1) Boot + render: the UI must actually draw (RETROPLUG_SDL_REQUIRE_NONBLANK exits non-zero on a flat frame),
 #    not merely boot. This is the standalone analogue of the jack `screenshot` check, minus Xvfb.
 run boot 90 RETROPLUG_SDL_REQUIRE_NONBLANK=1 RETROPLUG_SDL_SCREENSHOT="$TMP/frame.png"
 want "$LOG" "running " "boot: no 'running' banner"
+refuse "$LOG" "boot: the audio service never applied its settings"
 [ -s "$TMP/frame.png" ] || fail "boot: no screenshot written"
 echo "  ok: boot + non-blank render"
 
@@ -77,11 +81,13 @@ want "$LOG" "afterStop=0" "clock: 0xFC stop did not clear transport"
 # ...and with no clock master, the host's own transport is STOPPED at boot. That default is what keeps a
 # SYNC=MIDI cart from being clocked by a standalone nobody has pressed play on (Instance menu > MIDI Clock).
 want "$LOG" "live=0" "clock: the host transport is running at boot (should start stopped)"
-# ...and the MIDI Clock submenu's controls actually reach it: this drives __rp_setTransport/__rp_setClockBpm
-# through the JS globals those rows call, so a missing bind reads back the default instead of quietly
-# dropping the submenu from the menu.
-run transport 30 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_TRANSPORT=1
+# ...and the MIDI Clock submenu's controls actually reach it: this starts the transport through the JS global the row
+# calls and loads a project whose `midi.clockBpm` is 140 (the tempo is the PROJECT's now, applied by the midi package's
+# service), so a missing bind reads back the default instead of quietly dropping the submenu from the menu.
+printf '{"schemaVersion":"4","settings":{"midi":{"clockBpm":140}},"systems":[]}\n' >"$TMP/tempo.rplg"
+run transport 30 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_TRANSPORT=1 RETROPLUG_AUTOLOAD_PROJECT="$TMP/tempo.rplg"
 want "$LOG" "transport self-test: playing=1 bpm=140" "transport: the MIDI Clock seam did not start/retempo the clock"
+refuse "$LOG" "transport: the audio service never applied its settings"
 echo "  ok: MIDI-clock transport + stopped at boot + menu play/stop"
 
 # 3) Multi-output audio (P5): an 8-channel device opens with 8 planar buffers.
@@ -112,19 +118,33 @@ want "$LOG" "wheel: notches=\(0\.00,-3\.00\) at \([1-9][0-9]*,[1-9][0-9]*\)" \
      "wheel: SDL_MOUSEWHEEL did not reach the handler at the tracked cursor"
 echo "  ok: mouse wheel"
 
-# 5b) Settings > Audio through the JS seam: the Apply row's own call, with the arguments audioDraft.ts builds - a driver
-#     LABEL from the getter's list, and the chosen device. The hook behind it read that label as a BACKEND id once, so
-#     every Apply resolved to a backend that does not exist and muted the run; this reads the getter back and holds the
-#     old shape (drivers, driver, devicesByDriver, defaultByDriver, autoDriver, device) and an unmuted status.
+# 5b) Settings > Audio through the JS seam: the Apply row's own call, with an `audio` section's fields, then the
+#     description read back. The hooks answer what the rows read: the backends, and the status the device adopted (the
+#     rate and block an Apply asked for), with the null fallback this run is pinned to and no mute.
 run audio-hook 20 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_AUDIO_HOOK=1
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"drivers":\["Auto"' "audio hooks: the getter lost the drivers list"
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"driver":"Auto"' "audio hooks: the selected driver is not the Auto label"
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"devicesByDriver":{' "audio hooks: the getter lost devicesByDriver"
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"defaultByDriver":{' "audio hooks: the getter lost defaultByDriver"
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"autoDriver":' "audio hooks: the getter lost autoDriver"
-want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"muted":false' "audio hooks: an Apply muted the run"
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"backends":\[\{"id":"portaudio"' "audio hooks: the description lost the backends"
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"backend":"null"' "audio hooks: the null backend pin did not hold"
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"sampleRate":44100' "audio hooks: an Apply did not adopt the rate"
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"blockFrames":256' "audio hooks: an Apply did not adopt the block"
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-hook: .*"error":""' "audio hooks: an Apply muted the run"
 echo "  ok: Settings > Audio through the JS seam"
 
+# 5c) `--block-size` over the section (E12): the file asks for 512, the flag for 256, and the device the service
+#     applied runs at the flag's block. A launch script's quantum must win over the saved choice without being saved.
+SAVED_CFG="$RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR/config.json"
+printf '{"schemaVersion":3,"audio":{"backend":"null","driver":"","device":"","sampleRate":48000,"blockSize":512,"outChannels":2}}\n' >"$SAVED_CFG"
+run block-saved 30 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_AUDIO_STATUS=1
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-status: .*"blockFrames":512' "block override: the saved section did not open at its block"
+LOG="$TMP/block-flag.log"
+if ! env RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_AUDIO_STATUS=1 RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=30 "$BIN" --block-size 256 >"$LOG" 2>&1; then
+    cat "$LOG" >&2; fail "block override: binary exited non-zero"
+fi
+want "$LOG" 'post-audio-status: .*"blockFrames":256' "block override: --block-size did not win over the section"
+rm -f "$SAVED_CFG"
+echo "  ok: --block-size overrides the audio section"
+printf '{"schemaVersion":3,"audio":{"backend":"null","driver":"","device":"","sampleRate":48000,"blockSize":512,"outChannels":2}}\n' \
+    >"$RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR/config.json"
+
 # 6) Close guard (P6): an OS close on a clean project isn't vetoed → exits well before the 120-frame budget.
 run quit 120 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_QUIT=1
 want "$LOG" "close-guard test: exited at frame ([0-9]|[1-9][0-9])$" "quit: close guard did not exit early"
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), a fixed-length string.
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` replaces that string (`Mmm dd yyyy`) with `Nov  4 2026` before hashing, and this
plan's command does the same with `sed` and additionally COUNTS the string first (it must be exactly one, or the
normalisation would be guessing); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
feat(settings): config sections, and the audio and MIDI settings as packages

The TypeScript half of the standalone's audio and MIDI (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 6): config.json
gains package-owned sections, the Launchpad's controlSurface moves into its pack, and the Settings > Audio and
Settings > MIDI rows, the MIDI Clock submenu and the startup rendezvous move into the audio and midi packages.

Config sections. definePackage gains configSections, the same shape a project's sections use (key, schema, defaults,
optional version and migrations, merge), and a section is a non-core ROOT key of config.json. The shell keeps a key no
package of its product contributes verbatim - parseUserConfigResult carries the raw blocks beside the typed value and
serializeUserConfig writes the contributors' keys in product order, then the unknown ones in the order they were read -
so the plugin (which lists neither package) writes a standalone's blocks back instead of erasing them, and a config.json
written before this phase round-trips byte for byte. A block this session did not set is written back as the file
carried it, whatever wrote it: a shell field's write keeps the contributed blocks' raw bytes beside their parsed values,
so an additive field a newer build wrote survives. A block stamped newer than its contributor reads is kept, read as the
contributor's defaults and refused by setSection with one warning. Every write is computed over the file ON DISK (the
store re-reads inside its apply callback), so another process's change to a shared file survives and a newer build's
block is refused, not overwritten. The generic config host group (section / setSection) replaces
ConfigHost.controlSurface, and the Launchpad's controlSurface is its config section under the same root key with the
same four fields, so an existing file's bytes do not move. CORE_CONFIG_KEYS is derived from the schema's shape plus
schemaVersion, and a test holds the generator's refusal list to it.

The audio section (packages/audio). { backend, driver, device, sampleRate, blockSize, outChannels } with the defaults
the SDL app opened with, ids rather than a library's numbers, and render-ahead left a run's flag. The Settings > Audio
rows moved out of the shell's menuDefs.ts and audioDraft.ts into the package's ts/ui, at a new settings.audio placement
inside the shell's container: one Driver row naming the backend ("Auto (PortAudio: PipeWire)", "PortAudio: ALSA", "SDL:
pipewire"), Output Device, Rate, Block, Out Channels, Apply (the draft model kept), a "More drivers..." step that is the
only thing that enumerates a sibling backend (once per visit, and not offered at all while a run pins one), a Muted row
with the reason, and a row naming a run's flag overrides. The audioDevice host group (describe, backendDrivers, apply,
status) is offered only where the SDL hooks exist, so the plugin and the DPF standalone draw no row; the hooks replace
__rp_getAudioConfig/__rp_setAudioConfig and native no longer reads or writes audio.json. The service applies the saved
section on its FIRST POLL (after the Launchpad's restore), watches status() so a mute or a recovery repaints the Muted
row, and keeps Apply live while the status carries an error as the retry.

The midi section (packages/midi). { inputs: [{ name }], allInputs, outputs: [{ name }], clockBpm } under a project's
settings, distinct from the shell's midiRouting; portMatch.ts resolves a saved name in TIERS - exactly, then with
ALSA's volatile client:port numbers stripped, then with the index RtMidi appends to every WinMM name stripped - and each
tier has to match exactly one present port, so a two-port interface keeps its ports apart across a renumber and two
identical devices resolve to nothing (the WinMM and CoreMIDI table rows are UNVERIFIED until the Windows/macOS agents
list real ports). Settings > MIDI's rows are the project's: a checklist per direction plus "All devices", the entries
that resolve to nothing as "(missing)", a control surface's held port as "(control surface)", and a Rescan row. Each
present port maps to the saved entries that resolve to it, so a renumbered port reads checked and one tap removes every
entry naming it; a saved port that resolved but did not open is unchecked and its tap retries it. The MIDI Clock
submenu moved to a new instance.clock placement, its tempo saved in the section. A UI service watches
project.section("midi") and applies it with Apply::Diff on a section change, a project load (the store's new revision
counter) and opening the container - which is a MenuBuilder.onOpen hook the shell's Settings > MIDI row runs, so a
render never touches a device: the rows read the port listing the service last read, the service re-reads it on those
edges only, and the poll reports a repaint only when what the rows show moves. midi.json is no longer read or written,
and the Launchpad's rematchPorts uses the same matcher.

Startup (decision 23). The rendezvous widens: it waits for TypeScript's first audioDevice.apply from the audio section,
which RECORDS the request, or for the 500 ms bound - and native then opens the device at the point it always has, after
the MIDI stream and the providers' restore, so the order stays the claim, then MIDI, then audio last and no new edge
appears. The engine is built before any device is open and re-rated once at prepare. The virtual MIDI ports open at
once; hardware ports open when a project's section is applied. --audio-backend, --block-size and --render-ahead
override the saved choice for the run, and a backend pin keeps a same-backend driver and device.

Harnesses. sdl:controller's midi.json writes become autoloaded projects with a midi section, and its leg 2 holds the
new ordering rule: the claim precedes "] running " and the claimed port is never opened as a hardware input by the
stream. Both SDL harnesses keep RETROPLUG_SDL_AUDIO_BACKEND=null pinned and assert the rendezvous's audio half never
reports a miss. sdl:smoke's audio-hook leg and its transport leg read the new seam (the tempo comes from a project's
midi.clockBpm, and the hook no longer sets it), and a new leg proves --block-size over the section (E12). Both harness
scripts and the kit's SDL legs run under the /dev/snd guard, whose NOSND_LOG records refusals and audio-library
dlopens (it counts only a library NOT already loaded, so a null-pinned run's log is empty).

Re-recorded: the recorded menu matrix's three audio/MIDI seam cases, with RP_MENU_MATRIX_UPDATE=<the three case
names> (pnpm test menu/recorded-trees; the recipe takes a named case list). The Driver row lists only the backend in
force (SDL's entries arrive through "More drivers..."), so the record gains that row and loses the SDL cycler step.
Every other case holds. No parity, kit, render, registration, role-golden, protocol, edio or device-image baseline
moved.

Tests changed with the design's edges and named in the stage report: theme-config/format, user-config, watcher, services,
menu/launchpad, menu/leaves (the audio rows and the MIDI Clock), menu/recorded-cases, menu/recorded-trees,
test-native/launchpad-devices, test-ui/audio-device, audio-driver, midi-settings, midi-clock, ui-services,
hosts/host-groups, project/sections and project/tolerance (a fresh project gains the midi block), and
graph/plugin-product (E9's case). New: config/config-sections, midi/portMatch, midi/midiService, midi/configSection,
audio/configSection, audio/audioDraft. retroplug-audio-host-test loses its AudioChoice case with the helper the shell
no longer maps labels through.
EOF
````

### Task 6: the SDL-audio leg, the linkage check, the guard and the docs

Design section 7 and the design's stage S4. Four pieces, and the phase's last commit:

- **`sdl:pipewire` is rewritten** to write a stamped `config.json` `audio` block (no `audio.json`, no numeric
  `hostApi`) and to drive each leg with `--audio-backend`, which overrides the backend for the run and keeps a saved
  driver and device when the section names the same backend (E12), so every leg stays expressible. It gains an AUTO leg
  (no flag, `backend: "auto"`, the state a user's file is in, expecting PortAudio's PipeWire on the session default),
  the SDL-audio MODE (the same selection cases over SDL's PipeWire driver, wide output, and a LIVE-MENU leg that drives

- [ ] **Step 1: The guard, as tracked source**

`nosnd.c` is an `LD_PRELOAD` shim over `open` / `openat` / `openat64`: it refuses a `/dev/snd` path that is not `seq`
or `timer` before the syscall (returning `ENOENT`), and it counts each refusal and each audio-library `dlopen` that
was not already in the process (the lookup state goes through `dl_iterate_phdr`'s `data` struct, not process globals;
libasound's own config loader re-`dlopen`s libasound on every `snd_seq_open`, which is why an already-loaded library
is not counted). `build-guard.sh` builds it with the system `cc` (Linux only) into the caller's directory;
`guard-env.sh` sources the guard into a harness's own scratch directory, prepends it to `LD_PRELOAD` unless a copy is
already there (two guards would double every count) and exports `NOSND_LOG`. The first version of this was an
untracked `.superpowers/verify/nosnd.so` that two tracked docs and a tracked harness depended on: this step is that
file, tracked, with one source and no drift.

Create `tools/sdl-audio-guard/nosnd.c`:

````cpp
// The LD_PRELOAD guard every audio-capable harness runs under (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md section 7):
// refuse every ALSA device node but the sequencer and the timer, so a run on a machine whose default card is a real one
// can never open it - PortAudio's ALSA backend probes every card at Pa_Initialize, and SDL's PipeWire driver reaches the
// card through its ALSA monitor. Built by tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh and prepended to LD_PRELOAD by
// tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh, tools/run-sdl-controller.sh and tools/run-sdl-pipewire.sh.
//
// A refusal happens HERE, before the syscall, which is why the log is the proof: strace cannot see a call that was never
// made. Both the refusal and a look at the subsystems being touched are therefore the same compile, and this header is
// the whole of it.
//
// NOSND_LOG=<file>: append one line per refused path and per dlopen of an audio client library that was NOT already
// loaded, so a run can prove what it reached. A library's own dlopen is not a new audio dependency coming up: libasound
// is linked by rtmidi and SDL, and its config loader dlopens itself on every snd_seq_open, which made a null-pinned
// run's log non-empty for the MIDI client it is entitled to. Only a library that was NOT already loaded is logged, and
// that is the rule the counts in a harness's summary mean.
#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <link.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>

// NOSND_LOG=<file>: append one line per refused path and per audio-library dlopen. O_APPEND on every line, so threads
// that refuse at the same moment cannot interleave inside one line.
static void note(const char* what, const char* p) {
    const char* log = getenv("NOSND_LOG");
    if (!log || !*log) return;
    FILE* f = fopen(log, "a");
    if (!f) return;
    fprintf(f, "%d %s %s\n", (int)getpid(), what, p ? p : "(null)");
    fclose(f);
}

static int refused(const char* p) {
    if (!p || strncmp(p, "/dev/snd/", 9) != 0) return 0;
    if (strcmp(p + 9, "seq") == 0 || strcmp(p + 9, "timer") == 0) return 0;
    note("refused", p);
    return 1;
}

// Whether a library is ALREADY loaded when the dlopen runs (DT_NEEDED, or an earlier dlopen of it): then this is not a
// new audio dependency coming up. Searched per call, through dl_iterate_phdr's own `data` - the callback runs inside that
// call on the caller's thread, so nothing here is shared between two threads' dlopens.
struct Lookup {
    const char* want;  // the basename being looked for
    int         found;
};

static int phdr_cb(struct dl_phdr_info* info, size_t size, void* data) {
    (void)size;
    struct Lookup* look = data;
    if (!info->dlpi_name || !*info->dlpi_name) return 0;
    const char* base = strrchr(info->dlpi_name, '/');
    base = base ? base + 1 : info->dlpi_name;
    if (strcmp(base, look->want) == 0) {
        look->found = 1;
        return 1;  // stop walking
    }
    return 0;
}

static int already_loaded(const char* name) {
    if (!name) return 0;
    const char* base = strrchr(name, '/');
    struct Lookup look = {base ? base + 1 : name, 0};
    dl_iterate_phdr(phdr_cb, &look);
    return look.found;
}

void* dlopen(const char* name, int flags) {
    static void* (*real)(const char*, int);
    if (!real) real = (void* (*)(const char*, int))dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "dlopen");
    if (name && (strstr(name, "jack") || strstr(name, "pipewire") || strstr(name, "pulse") || strstr(name, "asound") ||
                 strstr(name, "portaudio")) &&
        !already_loaded(name))
        note("dlopen", name);
    return real(name, flags);
}

#define WRAP(name, ...)                                                                              \
    int name(const char* p, int f, ...) {                                                            \
        static int (*real)(const char*, int, ...);                                                   \
        if (!real) real = (int (*)(const char*, int, ...))dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, #name);                   \
        if (refused(p)) { errno = ENOENT; return -1; }                                               \
        mode_t m = 0;                                                                                \
        if (f & (O_CREAT | O_TMPFILE)) { va_list a; va_start(a, f); m = va_arg(a, mode_t); va_end(a); } \
        return real(p, f, m);                                                                        \
    }
WRAP(open)
WRAP(open64)

#define WRAPAT(name)                                                                                 \
    int name(int d, const char* p, int f, ...) {                                                     \
        static int (*real)(int, const char*, int, ...);                                              \
        if (!real) real = (int (*)(int, const char*, int, ...))dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, #name);              \
        if (refused(p)) { errno = ENOENT; return -1; }                                               \
        mode_t m = 0;                                                                                \
        if (f & (O_CREAT | O_TMPFILE)) { va_list a; va_start(a, f); m = va_arg(a, mode_t); va_end(a); } \
        return real(d, p, f, m);                                                                     \
    }
WRAPAT(openat)
WRAPAT(openat64)

// The _FORTIFY_SOURCE entry points a caller compiled with fortification reaches instead of open/openat.
int __open_2(const char* p, int f) { return open(p, f); }
int __open64_2(const char* p, int f) { return open64(p, f); }
int __openat_2(int d, const char* p, int f) { return openat(d, p, f); }
int __openat64_2(int d, const char* p, int f) { return openat64(d, p, f); }
````

Create `tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build the /dev/snd guard a harness prepends to LD_PRELOAD: nosnd.c beside this script, as a shared object in the
# caller's scratch directory, printed on stdout so a script can do `GUARD=$(tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh "$TMP")`.
#
# It is built rather than shipped because a .so in a repository is an artifact (and a binary one), and because the
# harnesses already own a scratch directory per run. Linux only: the guard wraps open/__open_2, which is how ALSA's
# legacy (non-sequencer) device layer opens /dev/snd/*; macOS and Windows have no /dev/snd to guard.
#
# Usage: tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh <output-dir>    (CC overrides the compiler)
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <output-dir>" >&2
    exit 2
fi

case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux) : ;;
    *) echo "error: the /dev/snd guard is a Linux facility (this is $(uname -s))" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
OUT="$1"
[ -f "$HERE/nosnd.c" ] || { echo "error: $HERE/nosnd.c is missing" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"
"${CC:-cc}" -shared -fPIC -O2 -o "$OUT/nosnd.so" "$HERE/nosnd.c" -ldl
echo "$OUT/nosnd.so"
````

Create `tools/sdl-audio-guard/guard-env.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Source this from a harness that could reach a real sound card: it builds the /dev/snd guard from the tracked source
# beside it into the caller's scratch directory and puts it in FRONT of LD_PRELOAD, so every /dev/snd node but the
# sequencer and the timer is refused before the syscall (nosnd.c says why). A caller that already has the guard in
# LD_PRELOAD keeps its own: the verification kit prepends one for the whole run, and loading a second copy would only
# count every audio-library dlopen twice.
#
# Usage, after `TMP="$(mktemp -d)"`:
#     . "$REPO_DIR/tools/sdl-audio-guard/guard-env.sh" "$TMP/guard"
#     export NOSND_LOG="${NOSND_LOG:-$TMP/nosnd.log}"      (optional: the log of what the run refused and loaded)
#
# REPO_DIR must be set by the caller.
GUARD_DIR="${1:?guard-env.sh needs a scratch directory for the built guard}"
GUARD="$("$REPO_DIR/tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh" "$GUARD_DIR")" || exit 1
case "${LD_PRELOAD:-}" in
    *nosnd.so*) : ;;  # already guarded (the kit's copy, or an outer harness's)
    *) export LD_PRELOAD="$GUARD${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}" ;;
esac
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The linkage check**

`check-audio-linkage.sh` fails on a symbol table it could not read (an empty table must not pass vacuously), then
holds the products: no `Pa_*` symbol and no backend factory (`rp_portaudio_backend`, `rp_sdl_backend`) in
`retroplug-cli`, `retroplug-host` or the Node addon, and no audio-library `DT_NEEDED` beyond what the product already
had (SDL2's presence proves nothing: a product with no audio backend may still need SDL2 for its window). It is a
standing kit leg (`audiolink`).

Create `tools/check-audio-linkage.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The audio backends' product wiring, checked on the binaries themselves (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md
# section 5.7(4)). A product names its audio backends in AUDIO_BACKENDS, and a product that names none must link neither
# PortAudio nor SDL audio: the backends are static libraries, so the proof is that the binary carries neither backend's
# FACTORY symbol and no audio library dependency.
#
#   retroplug-cli, retroplug-host, build/node/retroplug.node   no rp_portaudio_backend / rp_sdl_backend symbol, no
#                                                              portaudio/SDL-audio/pulse/jack/pipewire DT_NEEDED (or
#                                                              otool entry)
#   retroplug-sdl                                              names `AUDIO_BACKENDS portaudio sdl`, so both factories and
#                                                              the Pa_* symbols are expected; PortAudio must not be a
#                                                              DYNAMIC dependency (the static library is linked in),
#                                                              and this script prints the counts so a build that named
#                                                              one backend shows zero for the other
#
# The factory symbols are the check, not SDL2: a product that links NO audio backend may still need libSDL2 for its
# window, so a DT_NEEDED on SDL2 says nothing either way - the two factories do.
#
# A binary with an EMPTY symbol table proves nothing (stripped, or a static archive that dropped what the script greps
# for), so that fails rather than passing vacuously.
#
# Run by the verification kit (the `audiolink` leg). Linux reads DT_NEEDED with readelf and symbols with nm; macOS uses
# otool -L and nm -gU. Anything else reports SKIPPED (CI builds these two platforms).
#
# Usage: tools/check-audio-linkage.sh [binary ...]     (defaults: the four above, under build/)
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BINS=("$@")
if [ "${#BINS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    BINS=(
        "$ROOT/build/bin/retroplug-cli"
        "$ROOT/build/bin/retroplug-host"
        "$ROOT/build/node/retroplug.node"
        "$ROOT/build/bin/retroplug-sdl"
    )
fi

case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux)
        deps() { readelf -d "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
        syms() { nm -g "$1" 2>/dev/null || nm -D "$1" 2>/dev/null; } ;;
    Darwin)
        deps() { otool -L "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
        syms() { nm -gU "$1" 2>/dev/null; } ;;
    *) echo "audio linkage: SKIPPED (no dt-needed/otool reader for $(uname -s))"; exit 0 ;;
esac

FAIL=0
for bin in "${BINS[@]}"; do
    if [ ! -f "$bin" ]; then
        echo "  FAIL: $bin is missing (the kit builds it first)"; FAIL=1; continue
    fi
    name=$(basename "$bin")
    needs=$(deps "$bin")
    table=$(syms "$bin")
    if [ -z "$table" ]; then
        echo "  FAIL: $name has an empty symbol table: nothing here is proved"; FAIL=1; continue
    fi
    pa_symbols=$(printf '%s\n' "$table" | grep -cE ' Pa_[A-Za-z]' || true)
    factories=$(printf '%s\n' "$table" | grep -cE 'rp_(portaudio|sdl)_backend' || true)
    audio_dep=$(printf '%s\n' "$needs" | grep -ciE 'portaudio|libpulse|libjack|libpipewire' || true)
    case "$name" in
        retroplug-sdl)
            sdl_dep=$(printf '%s\n' "$needs" | grep -ci 'libSDL2' || true)
            if [ "$audio_dep" -eq 0 ] && [ "$sdl_dep" -gt 0 ] && [ "$factories" -gt 0 ]; then
                echo "  ok: $name keeps its backends static (SDL2 dependency only, $factories backend factory"
                echo "      symbol(s) and $pa_symbols Pa_* symbol(s) linked in)"
            else
                echo "  FAIL: $name links an audio library dynamically, has no SDL2 dependency, or names no backend"
                printf '%s\n' "$needs" | grep -iE 'portaudio|pulse|jack|pipewire' >&2
                FAIL=1
            fi ;;
        *)
            if [ "$audio_dep" -eq 0 ] && [ "$factories" -eq 0 ] && [ "$pa_symbols" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "  ok: $name names no audio backend (no factory symbol, no Pa_*, no audio dependency)"
            else
                echo "  FAIL: $name names an audio backend ($factories factory symbol(s), $pa_symbols Pa_*)" >&2
                printf '%s\n' "$needs" | grep -iE 'portaudio|pulse|jack|pipewire' >&2
                FAIL=1
            fi ;;
    esac
done

if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then echo "audio linkage clean"; else echo "audio linkage FAILED"; fi
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
````

- [ ] **Step 3: `sdl:pipewire` in both modes**

The script writes `{"schemaVersion":3,"audio":{...}}` into a scratch config dir and runs the app with
`--audio-backend` per leg; the AUTO leg runs first with no flag. The selection, wide-output and menu legs start
wireplumber on a private dbus (SDL's PipeWire driver needs the session graph) and are counted as SKIPPED when it is
missing, so the summary says how many ran. The SDL stream's node is read from the graph with the test sinks and their
monitor ports excluded (the alphabetically-first output node could be `rp-decoy`'s monitor), its name prefix read from
the run (SDL names its PipeWire node from its app-name hints), and the wide leg asserts the API's 8 channels and pair
1 linked, not 8 graph ports (SDL 2.30's node is a stereo stream: design R11). The ALSA-fallback leg holds the CLEAN
degradation in this container (exit 0, a `null` device with a status, no `/dev/snd/pcm` attempted, the private
config's default the null PCM) and says so.

````diff
+# The standalone's own PipeWire node. Read from the graph and DISCRIMINATED against this server's own objects: every
+# sink in the private server exports monitor ports, so "the first output node alphabetically" can be rp-decoy's monitor
+# (a sink's) or the graph's MIDI bridge, and the leg would then count the wrong node's ports. The test sinks and their
+# monitors are excluded by name, which leaves the client's stream. A node name can carry spaces ("Audio Stream"), so the
+# port is split off at its LAST colon and the two are joined with a delimiter awk can rely on.

+    pw-link -o 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^\(.*\):\([^:]*\)$/\1|\2/p' \

+    RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO=1 RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=240 \
+        timeout -k 5 90 "$BIN" --audio-backend sdl >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
+    APP_PID=$!
+    for _ in $(seq 60); do grep -q "running " "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.25; done
+    sleep 3
+    SDL_NODE=$(stream_node)
+    SDL_PORTS=$([ -n "$SDL_NODE" ] && port_count "$SDL_NODE" || echo 0)
+    SDL_LINKED=$(linked_pair1 "$SDL_NODE")
+    wait "$APP_PID"; RC=$?
+    CHOSE=$(sed -n "s/.*audio: SDL \[\(.*\)\] '\(.*\)' [0-9]* Hz.*/\1|\2/p" "$LOG" | head -1)
+    check "SDL opens 8 channels against a stereo sink" "pipewire|RetroPlug Low Priority"
+    grep -q "audio: SDL .*512 frames, 8 ch" "$LOG" \
+        && { echo "  ok: SDL reports 8 channels"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: SDL did not report 8 channels"; cat "$LOG" >&2; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
+    # SDL 2.30's PipeWire driver takes the 8-channel request at the API (the host renders 8, and SDL accepts 8) but its
+    # graph node is a STEREO stream: SDL mixes the extra channels into the first pair inside itself, so the node has 2
+    # output ports (design R11; the backend warns about it at open). What must hold either way is that the stream exists
+    # and its first pair reaches the sink.
+    [ "$SDL_PORTS" -ge 2 ] \
+        && { printf '  ok: the SDL stream has its ports (node %s, %s - its PipeWire node is stereo)\n' \
+                    "$SDL_NODE" "$SDL_PORTS"
+             PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: the SDL stream has no output ports (node '$SDL_NODE')"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
+    [ "$SDL_LINKED" -ge 2 ] \
+        && { echo "  ok: SDL pair 1 is linked to the sink"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: SDL pair 1 is not linked to the sink (found $SDL_LINKED links)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
+
+    # A live stream survives a menu build (S2 review C2): the Settings > Audio rows ask the SDL backend for its device
+    # list, and a listing must never switch the driver (SDL_AudioQuit closes every open device). The hook drives the
+    # real menu to Settings > Audio from the SDL queue; the leg holds the stream OPEN across it, the same node/ports
+    # before and after, and exactly one open line.
+    writecfg sdl "pipewire" "RetroPlug Low Priority" 48000 512 2
+    LOG="$TMP/sdl-menu.log"
+    RETROPLUG_DEBUG_AUDIO=1 RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=150 RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_MENU=40 \
+        timeout -k 5 90 "$BIN" --audio-backend sdl >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
+    APP_PID=$!
+    for _ in $(seq 60); do grep -q "running " "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.25; done
+    sleep 1
+    NODE_BEFORE=$(stream_node)
+    PORTS_BEFORE=$([ -n "$NODE_BEFORE" ] && port_count "$NODE_BEFORE" || true)
+    wait "$APP_PID"; RC=$?
+    grep -q "menu test: settings open, audio live=1 backend=sdl" "$LOG" \
+        && { echo "  ok: Settings > Audio opened with the SDL stream running, and it is still live"
+             PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: Settings > Audio did not open over a live SDL stream"; cat "$LOG" >&2; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
+    OPENS=$(grep -c "audio: SDL \[" "$LOG")
+    [ "$OPENS" -eq 1 ] \
+        && { echo "  ok: the stream was opened exactly once (the menu did not reopen it)"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: the SDL stream opened $OPENS times (a menu build disturbed it)"; cat "$LOG" >&2
+             FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
+    [ "$PORTS_BEFORE" -ge 2 ] \
+        && { echo "  ok: the stream was linked before the menu opened ($PORTS_BEFORE ports)"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); } \
+        || { echo "  FAIL: the SDL stream had no linked ports before the menu ($PORTS_BEFORE)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
 else
-    echo "  SKIPPED: wide-output checks need wireplumber + dbus-daemon (not installed, or it would not start)"
+    SKIP=$SDL_LEGS
+    echo "  SKIP: $SKIP SDL-audio legs need wireplumber + dbus-daemon (not installed, or it would not start)"
 fi
 
-echo "SDL PipeWire check: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
+REFUSED=$(refused_count)
+DLOPENS=$(dlopen_count)
+echo "  guard: $REFUSED refused /dev/snd path(s), $DLOPENS audio-library dlopen(s) (see $NOSND_LOG)"
+echo "SDL PipeWire check: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed, $SKIP skipped"
 [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
````

````diff
+  `priority.session` and is never the default, so "followed the default" can't pass by accident. The SDL selection legs,
+  the wide-output legs and the menu leg need wireplumber and dbus-daemon (SDL's PipeWire driver connects through the
+  session graph, and ports only materialise once something links the stream); that part starts wireplumber with its
+  bluetooth context dropped, because that context's logind module has no `/run/systemd` in a container and takes the
+  daemon down with it, and on a private `dbus-daemon`, without which it quits at startup whenever the shell has no
+  session bus. SDL legs skipped for a missing wireplumber are counted and reported as SKIP. **Every run goes under the
+  `/dev/snd` guard, whose source is tracked (`tools/sdl-audio-guard/nosnd.c`, built by
+  `tools/sdl-audio-guard/build-guard.sh` into the harness's own scratch directory): via `LD_PRELOAD`, every `/dev/snd`
+  node but `seq`/`timer` is refused before the syscall, and `NOSND_LOG` records each refusal and each dlopen of an audio
+  client library that was not already loaded, so the run PROVES no real sound card was opened (an strace cannot see a
+  refusal). The three SDL harnesses (`sdl:smoke`, `sdl:controller`, `sdl:pipewire`) put it in front of `LD_PRELOAD`
+  themselves through `tools/sdl-audio-guard/guard-env.sh`, so a bare `pnpm sdl:controller` is guarded; the kit prepends

+  legitimately logs refused card control nodes, and the ALSA-fallback leg holds only that no card's PLAYBACK node is
+  opened (it falls back to `null` with a status here, since a container's PortAudio cannot enumerate a private null
+  PCM). An Auto leg runs with no backend pinned, which is the state a user's config is in. Not in CI (the runners have
+  no PipeWire); the devcontainer ships one for it. The kit runs it as the guarded `pipewire` leg.
   **It ships in the `build.yml` artifact for every platform but is deliberately kept OUT
   of releases** — `release.yml`'s four packaging steps are explicit allowlists, and
   `retroplug-sdl` is not on any of them (each carries a comment saying so). Don't add it

-  `setOnLinkChanged` and `setOnScanBusy` callbacks in `sdl/main.cpp` stop and restart the stream to

-  that disappears (USB unplug, PipeWire node removed, suspend) freezes everything; nothing watches stream

-  `Pa_StopStream` return values are ignored, so a failed restart leaves a live-looking app with a dead

-  `openAudio` mutes on every launch with no fallback to defaults, and `__rp_getAudioConfig` has no
-  status field, so the UI can't say the device failed to open. Retry with defaults; expose
-  open/muted/error to Settings > Audio.
-- [ ] **RT tuning applies once per process** (*audit*). `paCallback`'s `static std::atomic<bool> tuned`
-  latches on the first stream. On ALSA (the handheld) each `StartStream` spawns a new thread, and because
-  of the stop/start lock above that now happens in ordinary use, so the audio thread loses SCHED_FIFO +
-  core pinning. On PipeWire the same call sets SCHED_FIFO 80 and pins PipeWire's shared data-loop thread,
-  overriding rtkit. Re-tune per callback thread (compare `pthread_self()`), and only on ALSA.
+- [x] **Pa_StopStream / Pa_StartStream used as a lock.** *Fixed in F5b: a MIDI change no longer stops audio at
+  all. `MidiStream`'s outputs are an immutable set swapped through an epoch handshake (the audio thread brackets
+  its sends with a counter the control thread waits out), an input's port cancels its own callback as it closes,
+  and `reconfigureMidi` / the Launchpad callbacks are gone. Only a real device change (`AudioHost::apply`) stops
+  and restarts the stream, once. See [modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f5b-design.md) 4.3
+  and edge E5.*
+- [x] **Dead audio device = frozen app.** *Fixed in F5b: `AudioHost` owns a backend-neutral no-pull watchdog (a
+  started device that runs no pull for a few block durations, never under 250 ms, falls to the `null` device with
+  a status Settings shows), each backend reports its own `lost()`, and a stream that opens but will not start is
+  an open failure that falls back. The false-trip hazard a permanent mute once had is gone too: while the status
+  carries an error, Settings > Audio's Apply stays live as the retry.*
+- [x] **Bad persisted audio config = muted forever.** *Fixed in F5b: the `audio` section is a stamped
+  config.json section whose parse clamps junk to defaults per field; a failed open falls to the `null` device with
+  `AudioHost`'s status carrying the reason, which Settings > Audio renders as "Muted: why"; and Apply is the
+  live retry while it does.*
+- [x] **RT tuning applies once per process** (*audit*). *Fixed in F5b: `AudioHost` tunes PER THREAD (a
+  `thread_local` latch, so a re-opened stream's callback asks once for itself), on the callback thread only (the
+  null pump and a test's hand-cranked pull are left alone), with the renderer at 80 and the callback at 85 under
+  render-ahead. The "only on ALSA" suggestion is not taken: the pin is best effort and a failure is ignored, as it
+  always was; PipeWire's data-loop thread is still the one tuned, which the muOS run is to watch.*
````

````diff
+The outputs are an immutable `OutputSet` (the virtual output's pointer and the hardware ports it NAMES; the control
+thread owns the ports) reached through one atomic pointer. A change builds the new set, publishes it (an exchange),
+waits for the send in flight, then frees the old one. The wait is an epoch handshake: `send` brackets its use of the set
+with a counter the audio thread increments to an odd value on entry and an even one on exit (two atomic increments, no
+lock and no allocation on the audio path); the control thread reads the counter after publishing and, if it read an odd
+value, waits until the counter has CHANGED. Waiting until it is merely even is unbounded under back-to-back sends (the
+review's probe: 556 ms on a 32-thread box, never returning when pinned to one core); waiting for a change is the one
+send in flight.
+
+**All four operations on the two locations are `seq_cst`**: the entry increment and the pointer load in `send`, the
+exchange and the epoch load in `retire`. The shape is store-buffering, each side writes one location and then reads the
+other, and with relaxed or acquire/release orders AArch64 (the handheld and Raspberry Pi builds) may let the sender read
+the OLD set while the control thread reads the epoch as even, so the old set would be freed under a send. No test can
+hold that: ThreadSanitizer checks happens-before, not weak-memory reorderings, and x86's locked increment is a full
+fence, so the comment in `MidiStream.cpp` says why. The wait yields a few times and then sleeps in 100 us steps, so a
+170 ms WinMM bulk SysEx is not a spinning UI thread. `send()` is the AUDIO THREAD's alone: the entry asserts it in a
+Debug build (`NDEBUG` is defined in `build/` and in both sanitizer trees, so the rule is held by the argument and a case,
+not by a run), and `AudioHost` must never let two threads render at once, a watchdog takeover included.
+
+A block runs at most one `send` per pending message, sequentially, so the wait is at most the one send in flight: none
+when audio is not running (the counter is even). A port send that blocks (a WinMM bulk SysEx blocks about 170 ms, which
+is why the Launchpad writes on its own thread) makes the wait that long, and `MidiStream::send` runs every selected
+hardware output's send INLINE on the audio thread, so a SysEx the engine emits to a selected WinMM output blocks the
+audio callback itself that long (as `MidiIo` always did; the Launchpad's own link is not in the stream). A retire list
+drained from the frame loop is the alternative that never blocks the UI (report item 19: built as approved; it is added
+only if the Windows run shows a stall, section 12).

 ### 6.6 Startup
 
 The SDL app's rendezvous holds audio and MIDI until TS's `restored()` or 500 ms (`restoreControlSurface`,
 `main.cpp:1000-1011`, which today waits only when the product started the Launchpad provider). It widens to a second
-condition: TS's first `audioDevice.apply`, issued from the `audio` section by the UI's mount. Native therefore opens
-audio after that apply or, at the 500 ms bound, with defaults (Auto), so a missing or broken `config.json` can never
-keep the app silent (the rule `restoreControlSurface` states). `setupSdl` no longer opens a device (`:1437-1441` goes):
-it initialises video and the game controller, and the audio backends initialise their libraries at first use. The
-virtual MIDI ports open at once (nothing in the file chooses them); the hardware ports open when a project's section is
-applied, which is after the autoload (`:1670`) and the UI mount; the control surface's claim, reserved from TS's
-`restored()`, still precedes any hardware open of that port, which is what `sdl:controller` leg 2 holds (section 9).
+condition: TS's first `audioDevice.apply`, issued from the `audio` section by the audio service's first poll (the
+rendezvous pumps UI frames, so those polls run). `setupSdl` no longer opens a device (`:1437-1441` goes): it initialises
+video and the game controller, and the audio backends initialise their libraries at first use. The virtual MIDI ports
+open at once (nothing in the file chooses them); the hardware ports open when a project's section is applied, which is
+after the autoload (`:1670`) and the UI mount; the control surface's claim, reserved from TS's `restored()`, still
+precedes any hardware open of that port, which is what `sdl:controller` leg 2 holds (section 9).
+
+**As built the audio device does NOT open inside the rendezvous.** The design said "native opens audio after TS's first
+apply", and the first S3 pass did exactly that, so the device opened and started on the audio service's first poll,
+before `app.midi.open()` and before `rp_restore_providers` (the N8's reconnect ran with the audio thread live, unproved
+and unlisted). The whole-prototype review's I3 held that the app's order is claim, MIDI, providers' restore, audio last,
+and no new edge was wanted, so the native `__rp_audioApply` only RECORDS the request (`AppState`'s `req*` fields) and
+sets `audioApplied`, the word the rendezvous waits on; `main.cpp` opens the device at its one old point, after
+`app.midi.open()` and `rp_restore_providers`, with the recorded request (or the defaults when TS never applied), and
+`audioDeviceReady` then makes a UI apply live, as before. `waitForUiStartup` (the renamed `restoreControlSurface`)
+waits on the control surface's `restored()` where the product started the Launchpad provider and on `audioApplied`, and
+prints "audio: the UI did not apply its settings; starting on the defaults" at the bound. `sdl:smoke`'s order leg holds
+the order off the log ("the MIDI stream opens before the audio device"), and the startup line for a pinned run says
+"on the null device (pinned by --audio-backend null)", not that no device chose it. A TS apply the host receives in the
+rendezvous is therefore never followed by a second open with a shim's config, and the old sentence "audio last" stays
+true.
 
 Two consequences the order carries, both found in verification: the engine is constructed before any device is open, so
 `bootControlPlane`'s `engine.setSampleRate(a.sampleRate)` (`:1335`) reads the default 48000 rather than an obtained
 rate, and a configuration that differs gets one in-place re-rate at `prepare` (`Engine::setSampleRate`,
````
